#763. Coles investigates cyber-attack and apologises to customers

📅 16 Nov 2026

Coles investigates cyber-attack and apologises to customers

Tanggal: 16 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/16/coles-cyber-attack-incident-data

Supermarket giant says no customer, team or supplier data compromised but recommends updating passwords as a precaution.

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.

Australia’s second-largest retailer has been targeted in a cyber-attack, though it is still too early to tell whether any of its data has been stolen or compromised.

Coles revealed the threat on Monday morning, saying it was investigating with support from the Australian Cyber Security Centre and global security experts.

“Coles Group Limited is currently investigating a cyber security incident,” the company said in a statement to the stock exchange.

“We have not identified any evidence that customer, team or supplier data has been compromised or removed from Coles’ systems.

Diungkapkan bahwa “operations continue and customers are able to shop as normal with coles in stores and online. ”.

Coles apologised to its customers for any concerns they might have at “a time of increasing cyber incidents in Australia and around the world”.

“We have security measures in place to protect customer and supplier accounts and are continuing to closely monitor our system,” it said.

Berdasarkan laporan, “we recommend you regularly update your password with a strong, unique password for your account and not reuse the same password across multiple services. ”.

Coles also warned customers to be cautious if they received unexpected emails or SMS messages purporting to be from the retailer, and not to click any links.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in a separate and unrelated incident, woolworths said it was aware of reports from customers who purchased compromised e-gift cards. The ABC first reported on Monday some customers had lost hundreds of dollars after buying the company’s Everyday WISH gift cards through its rewards website or app, only to find the sums loaded on to them had been spent by someone else.

Some customers told the national broadcaster they had lost up to $500, with transactions showing up at stores in different states to where they purchased the cards.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we are aware of reports of an issue affecting a number of customer e-gift cards and are looking into the matter as a priority,” a woolworths spokesperson said in a statement. We encourage any customer who notices a transaction they don’t recognise to contact our Gift Card Support team. “We recognise the concern this has caused affected customers and we apologise to customers impacted. ”.

The company says it is working through all reported issues and will look into replacing affected e-gift cards.

#764. Tech failure forces hundreds of University of Melbourne students to abandon final exams mid-test

📅 16 Nov 2026

Tech failure forces hundreds of University of Melbourne students to abandon final exams mid-test

Tanggal: 16 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/nov/16/university-of-melbourne-students-exams-cancelled-tech-issue

Students left in limbo after digital platform fails during exams, with university saying ‘third-party technical partners’ likely to blame for issue.

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.

Hundreds of students at the University of Melbourne were forced to abandon their final exams on Monday morning after many were unable to access the digital platform needed to begin them.

Diungkapkan bahwa jol scobie, a first-year student at the university, was set to take his australian politics exam on monday after preparing for weeks. He had initially been told earlier in the year it was going to be a hand-written essay before instructors changed the test to a digital platform.

Diungkapkan bahwa the subject was one of several holding exams at the royal exhibition building in carlton, with hundreds of students in attendance on monday. About half were able to log on to the digital system and begin, Scobie said, but many others were left sitting at their desks, staring at a blank screen for about 50 minutes.

Students undertaking the Australian politics exam were meant to complete two 1,000-word essays over two hours.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “the [exam coordinators] said: ‘listen, we can’t get it to work. It’s time for everyone to leave,’” Scobie said. “We were sort of standing there watching hundreds and hundreds of students pour out of the building. ”.

A university spokesperson confirmed technical issues caused the cancellation of a “small number” of exams on both 11 and 16 November.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “early indications are that the issue relates to third-party technical partners involved in the delivery of our digital exams,” the spokesperson said. “Our teams are following established contingency processes to resolve the issue and communicate alternative arrangements for the students affected.

Diungkapkan bahwa “we understand exam disruptions can be stressful for our students, and have support services available to assist students as needed. ”.

The university did not immediately reply to questions about how many students were affected, and if they would be able to sit makeup examinations before Friday.

Berdasarkan laporan, millie mountford, another first-year student, said there had been limited communication about when a makeup exam would be held and when students and the university would be able to fit them in during an already busy week. Thousands of other students will be sitting their own tests in the coming days, with Mountford herself having another scheduled for tomorrow.

She does not know if it will go forward without any issues.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i’m just kind of demotivated to study when i don’t even know if it will actually be worth it,” she said. “It’s just majorly inconvenient. ”.

Charlotte Wickham said the cancelled exam could snarl her travel plans to see her family in Tasmania over the holiday break due to the high cost and limited ability to change flights at the last minute.

Berdasarkan laporan, “the stress really comes from not knowing if they are going to reschedule [the exams for] the supplementary period,” she said. “We have these questions that we’ve specifically studied for and now we have such a long period of waiting. We’ve planned our lives, and we have to keep these at the back of our minds. Do we have to restudy because the questions are different?”.

Berdasarkan laporan, the issues come after the national tertiary education union organised a 24-hour strike and four-day teaching ban in october amid concerns from members about academic workloads, ai protections and fair pay. Members voted to approve a proposed new enterprise agreement to address some of those concerns earlier in November.

Last week, the Age reported the University of Melbourne was planning to cut almost 180 jobs across mainly non-academic staff after “disappointing” financial results.

#765. Australia’s national medical research body advises conditional use of puberty blockers for transgender children

📅 16 Nov 2026

Australia’s national medical research body advises conditional use of puberty blockers for transgender children

Tanggal: 16 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/nov/16/australias-national-medical-research-body-advises-conditional-use-of-puberty-blockers-for-transgender-children

New National Health and Medical Research Council guidelines at odds with public hospital bans in Queensland and NT.

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.

Australia’s largest medical research organisation has advised puberty blockers are appropriate for the gender-affirming care of children in certain circumstances, after a year-long review of international evidence.

The federal government last year commissioned the commonwealth-funded National Health and Medical Research Council (NHMRC) to develop the advice in response to bans in Queensland and Northern Territory public hospitals imposed by their governments.

The New Zealand government later followed suit despite widespread opposition in the health sector and warnings that the bans would harm children.

The council explicitly rejected alternative approaches to gender-affirming care proposed by opponents of the approach – such as the “wait and see” model – as a form of withholding care for children which it stated “can affect the young person’s physical and mental health, wellbeing, and ability to function”.

The NHMRC’s interim national clinical practice guidelines released on Monday, which advise conditional use of puberty suppressants for children, could put pressure on state and territory governments to consider their positions.

“Trans and gender-diverse young people experience unjust and avoidable health disparities arising from stigma, discrimination, and barriers to accessing health care,” it said.

Puberty blockers are a class of drugs used to stop the body producing oestrogen and testosterone.

They are covered by the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme for cisgender patients, and have been used for decades.

The new NHMRC guidelines do not require a child to be distressed to be treated for gender incongruence and recommend a multi-disciplinary team “should be determined on a case-by-case basis”.

Doctors should “prioritise the best interest and wellbeing of the young person and provide care that respects their autonomy”, the advice reads.

The guidelines describe gender incongruence as the clinical term for a difference between a person’s gender and their sex recorded at birth.

“It is not a mental health disorder,” it states.

The preliminary agreement at UN climate talks in Turkey calls for a rapid reduction of planet-warming emissions and at least $120 billion to help countries adapt to climate change.

COP31 co-host Australia has kicked off the second week of climate talks in Antalya with a draft political deal calling for an "immediate transition away from fossil fuels" and a "tripling" of finance for climate adaptation measures in developing countries to at least $120 billion (€109 billion).

Diungkapkan bahwa the goal of co-host turkey to increase electrification of the world's economies to 35% by 2035 also features in the text. The draft emphasizes clean energy but notes that "electrification can provide co-benefits regardless of the electricity mix" — an approach that has proved divisive at the talks, with many insisting that electrification be strictly tied to renewable energy.

Language around a faster phaseout of oil, coal and gas is important because fossil-fuel producing nations have repeatedly pushed back against stronger wording in previous COP decisions.

Diungkapkan bahwa "the new negotiating text contains all the necessary building blocks for a successful outcome to the conference: from the goal of climate neutrality for all industrialized countries by 2030 to a work program that can keep the 1. 5-degree limit in place," said Greenpeace Germany head Martin Kaiser on Monday.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Berdasarkan laporan, the draft expressed "deep concern" that the 1. 5 Celsius (2. It stressed the need for "accelerating action to minimize both the magnitude and duration of any temperature overshoot and to return global warming to below 1. 7 Fahrenheit) temperature threshold agreed at the 2015 COP in Paris to avoid runaway climate change was now out of reach. 5C as soon as possible. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, however, kaiser criticized the lack of binding commitments in the draft's resolutions. He added that Europe should work with China and the most climate-vulnerable countries to keep oil-producing nations, including Russia and countries in the Middle East, from "undermining the conference's decisions and turning them into a free pass for the oil and gas industry. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, cosima cassel, an expert at climate think tank e3g, was also cautiously pleased with the draft's "ambitious language" but said it appeared the broad deal would now leave negotiators to "fight for trade-offs. ".

"The test will be whether the final decision keeps the core elements once that process plays out: ambition on overshoot, defense of the science, clean electrification and forward progress on adaptation finance," she said in a statement.

Disagreements over financing largely relate to who should bear the costs of international climate action, whether financial support should be provided through grants or loans, and how funding for developing countries can be increased.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, at 18 pages and 144 items, the draft deal will be the focus of lengthy negotiations in the coming days as delegates try to come to an agreement by friday. But Chris Bowen, chief of negotiations and Australia's minister for climate change and energy, appeared optimistic.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "the general tenor and tone [of the talks] has been very constructive," he told reporters. "Parties have come to me with strong views about various things, as you'd expect […] [but] they've also come in the spirit of cooperation, the spirit of respect and a spirit where parties have said to me that they want to help get an outcome. ".

Motoko Rich, the Rome bureau chief, has been traveling with Pope Leo XIV through Uruguay, Argentina and Peru.

Flying with Pope Leo XIV over the Andes, halfway through the pontiff’s 12-day trip to South America, the journalists traveling at the back of the plane suspected something was amiss.

Berdasarkan laporan, they had expected the pope to come out from behind the business-class curtain and take questions, as he had on previous papal flights. Instead, Vatican officials abruptly told the press corps that the pope would not be speaking with them on the nearly five-hour flight from Argentina to Peru.

Was the pope, who had been diagnosed with lung cancer less than a month earlier, feeling ill? Was he too exhausted to talk? Was he taking a nap?.

Berdasarkan laporan, “it’s evident he’s well,” said maria montserrat alvarado, who heads the vatican’s communications department, when asked why the pope wasn’t taking questions. “He’s running circles around us. ”.

It was perhaps inevitable that Leo’s every action on this journey, so soon after surgery to remove a lobe of his right lung, would be scrutinized for signs of fatigue or illness, particularly as the Vatican is not known for its transparency.

The three-country trip, which began in Uruguay and concludes in Peru on Monday, involves a grueling schedule of 12 flights, two helicopter rides, nine Masses, 36 speeches and numerous meetings with local bishops and community members.

#793. Five EU countries expected to announce migrant deportation centre in Rwanda

📅 16 Nov 2026

Five EU countries expected to announce migrant deportation centre in Rwanda

Tanggal: 16 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cw987343352go?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Dinghys in the Mediterranean (file pic) are often overcrowded.

Five EU countries are expected to announce the creation of a migrant deportation centre in the landlocked African country Rwanda, according to diplomatic sources, part of a broader push to boost deportations and curb irregular migration.

Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands said in September they were working towards a deal with a non-EU country to host "return hubs".

In August, Rwanda said it had begun "preliminary discussions" with several European states.

It is understood the scheme would only apply to asylum seekers who had exhausted legal avenues to remain in the EU, unlike a scrapped British deal that envisaged sending people to Rwanda to have their claims processed.

Legal challenges meant the UK deal never took off, and it was eventually junked by the incoming Labour government in 2024.

The five EU countries say the plan to send migrants abroad is in line with EU and international law, but human rights bodies say it could violate migrant rights.

The deal follows a recent EU reform that allowed for the creation of hubs outside of the bloc.

Diungkapkan bahwa details are expected to be announced on monday in vienna. Diplomatic sources told the AFP news agency the hub in the east-central African nation is expected to initially run as a pilot, hosting about 100 people, with each of the five nations possibly sending about 20 migrants.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the eu countries reportedly expressed hope that a centre would be running in 2027. The United Nations' International Organisation for Migration (IOM) could play an ancillary role.

"IOM has a long history of providing assistance to migrants in situations of transit, including in complex contexts," an IOM spokesperson said, adding the agency was in discussions with some EU countries "on plans for the establishment of return hubs or similar mechanisms".

With elections approaching in several EU nations, administrations have been under pressure to show they can control migration.

Concerns around security, struggling economies and disillusionment with governing parties have all had a major role in shaping attitudes towards people leaving their home countries.

Human Rights Watch's senior Africa researcher Clementine de Montjoye said the choice of Rwanda would be a cause of concern as it had a "well-established record of repression of dissent, arbitrary detention, ill-treatment in detention" and support for armed rebels in the neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "paying kigali to host a deportation programme would not only cause suffering and harm to those deported, it would finance and provide political leverage to a government responsible for serious human rights abuses at home and abroad. ".

The independent EU Agency for Fundamental Rights argued any third country hosting a return hub should "respect fundamental rights", including that people should not be sent to a country where they face serious risk of persecution.

Unaccompanied children should not be sent to a return hub, the agency said.

According to the European Border and Coast Guard Agency, there were almost 110,000 irregular border crossings into the EU in the first 10 months of 2026, which represents a 29% decrease compared to the previous year.

In October, about 18,100 crossings were detected, which is about 6% less than October 2025 but 22% more than in September "largely because of a sharp rise in arrivals on the Western African route to the Canary Islands".

Diungkapkan bahwa china says presidents xi, trump and putin are going to have "in-depth discussions on global peace. " Ukraine, Iran and denuclearization could also feature in the talks.

Beijing said on Monday the leaders of the US, Russia and China will discuss "world peace" in their first trilateral summit in China this week.

Presidents Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin are due to meet in the southern Chinese city Shenzhen on Thursday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit.

Sebagaimana diketahui, china provided few details about the talks, but said they would involve "in-depth discussions on preserving global peace and promoting stability in relations. ".

"It will be of ground-breaking significance," foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning told a news briefing on Monday, hours after Beijing confirmed the meeting.

Berdasarkan laporan, us president donald trump has previously said the meeting will be "interesting. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, "we'll talk a lot of things, including denuclearization, but we'll be talking a lot of things. We're trying to end the war in Iran," he told reporters at a Florida airport on November 8.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In his brief remarks Trump avoided mentioning Russia's war in Ukraine.

According to a report published by the Wall Street Journal last month, Putin wanted the talks to broker a Ukraine peace agreement that would serve Moscow's interests.

US officials say Trump is not expected to raise the issue, AFP news agency reported.

Following his visit to China, German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier told public broadcaster ARD that Xi appeared irritated when asked whether the trilateral talks would cover Ukraine.

"He explicitly pointed out that this is a European conflict, in which the Europeans must also be at the table," Steinmeier told ARD earlier this month.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Friday asked Trump to not make any "surprises" on Ukraine with Putin during the talks.

Berdasarkan laporan, "please, no surprises. Continue to ‌play as part of 'Team Europe' and 'Team Ukraine'," he said.

Washington wants China included in future nuclear arms control deals, but Beijing insists the US and Russia must first reduce their arsenals.

China previously rejected Trump's proposal for broader disarmament talks following the expiration of a US-Russia nuclear treaty in February.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but according to the us state department, in a call this week, top diplomats wang yi and marco rubio "agreed on the importance of meaningful leader-level conversations to advance goals such as peace and denuclearization. ".

The Iran war, which began with US and Israeli strikes on February 28, is currently undergoing some de-escalation although major issues remain unresolved.

#797. Eurovision organisers criticise Malaysian removal of LGBT+ footage in first Asian contest

📅 16 Nov 2026

Eurovision organisers criticise Malaysian removal of LGBT+ footage in first Asian contest

Tanggal: 16 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2026/nov/16/eurovision-organisers-malaysia-removal-lgbt-footage-first-asian-contest

Broadcaster TV3 appears to cut footage of Thai drag performers and gay Philippine jury spokesperson.

Eurovision’s organisers have said they are “surprised and disappointed” that the first Eurovision Asia was altered when it was broadcast in Malaysia, apparently removing LGBTQ+ imagery and people from the show.

The European Broadcasting Union (EBU), the alliance of public broadcasters that owns Eurovision, said it would write to Voxovation, the company producing the Asian contest under licence, and ask it to establish with the Malaysian broadcaster TV3 why it happened.

Footage circulating online of the contest, which was won by the Philippines’ Carmelle, showed the first of two cuts during the voting in Saturday’s final in Bangkok, when the Philippines’ spokesperson, Vice Ganda, awarded the Philippine jury’s points.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, vice ganda is gay and identifies as non-binary. The comedian is among the biggest stars on Philippine television, has fronted the country’s most watched daytime show, and has campaigned for LGBTQ+ acceptance at home.

Diungkapkan bahwa announcing a national jury’s points is one of the most visible roles in a eurovision final. Each country’s spokesperson appears in turn to reveal how their jury has ranked the other entries.

While the international feed showed Vice Ganda announcing that the Philippine jury had given its 12 points, the maximum, to the Malaysian entrant, Aina Abdul, TV3 viewers saw only the scoreboard.

Separate footage shows part of the show’s opening number showcasing Thai culture, in which drag performers appeared on street food carts, replaced with a wide shot taken from rehearsals.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, eurovision fans accused the channel of “censorship”. The Guardian has not been able to review TV3’s broadcast independently as its livestream is no longer available online.

Martin Green, the director of the Eurovision song contest, said: “We are surprised and disappointed to learn that the broadcast of Eurovision song contest Asia was altered in Malaysia.

“We take this matter seriously and will be writing to Voxovation, the producers of the show, to seek clarification and ask them to establish with Malaysian broadcaster TV3 why this happened.

Diungkapkan bahwa “this appears to be isolated to the malaysian broadcast of the show, and all other transmissions were not altered. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, voxovation said in a statement that it was aware of the concerns raised and was “looking into the matter with the broadcaster to establish the circumstances … we are working with the malaysian broadcaster to make sure this doesn’t happen again. ”.

Neither the EBU nor Voxovation said whether the contest’s participation agreement required broadcasters to carry the show unedited or what the consequences would be if one did not.

The Guardian has asked Media Prima, Malaysia’s largest media group and TV3’s owner, for comment.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this is not the first time the wider eurovision song contest has faced allegations of censorship. In May 2018 the EBU terminated its partnership with the Chinese streaming service Mango TV after it dropped the Irish and Albanian entries and blurred a rainbow flag in the audience, saying such censorship was not in line with its “values of universality and inclusivity”.

Asked before Saturday’s final how the EBU’s commitment to its values squared with the laws in Malaysia and Bangladesh, the other competing country where same-sex relations are criminalised, the EBU’s head of communications, Dave Goodman, said the contest’s values were “non-negotiable”.

Malaysia has some of the harshest anti-LGBTQ+ laws in Asia, with oral and anal sex being punishable by up to 20 years in prison.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, rights groups have warned of a hardening climate. In November last year, authorities raided a men-only spa in Kuala Lumpur and detained more than 200 men, though no charges followed. And in 2022, police raided an LGBTQ+ Halloween party in the capital and arrested 20 people.

In 2023, a festival appearance by the British band the 1975, whose singer criticised the country’s homophobic laws and kissed a male bandmate on stage, led to the event being cancelled and prompted tighter entry rules for foreign performers.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, tv3 has faced pressure over lgbtq+ visibility before. In February 2025, it apologised after male guests arrived at a red carpet event in clothing resembling women’s dress.

#798. Man sentenced over 'horrific' attempted murder of three children

📅 16 Nov 2026

Man sentenced over 'horrific' attempted murder of three children

Tanggal: 16 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cr0qj0nzwj34o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

In July Riad Bouchaker was found guilty of the eight charges he faced.

A 52-year-old man has been sentenced to life in prison for the attempted murder of three children outside a primary school in Dublin's Parnell Square in November 2023.

Riad Bouchaker, of no fixed address, was also found guilty of assault causing serious harm to creche worker Leanne Flynn, and of assaulting two other children and a teenager.

On Monday, Judge Tony Hunt imposed the overall sentence of life imprisonment in Dublin's Central Criminal Court.

Rioting across many parts of Dublin following the attack led to the deployment of the most riot police in Irish history.

Bouchaker was originally from Algeria but had lived in Ireland for 25 years prior to the attack, and he had Irish citizenship.

He was assisted by an Arabic interpreter and a speech-and-language expert during the trial, who were present in court for the sentencing.

The attack took place outside a primary school on Parnell Square East.

The attack took place outside Gaelscoil CholÃ¡iste Mhuire in Parnell Square, shortly after 13:40 local time on 23 November.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a group of 13 children, aged five and six, were lined up on parnell square waiting to go to their afterschool provision. Childcare worker Leanne Flynn was helping a little boy zip up his jacket when Bouchaker pulled his knife on the children.

A five-year-old girl was left with a lifelong brain injury after being stabbed in the heart.

Now eight, she is non-verbal and can only communicate by blinking, uses a wheelchair and has to be fed through a tube in her stomach as she cannot swallow safely by herself.

The judge said the child will never live independently and that her life, and the lives of her family, had been permanently altered.

He also noted that Flynn suffered life-threatening injuries, including a collapsed lung and the loss of a spleen, as well as profound psychological consequences and her services not being available to children.

The judge said she had acted fearlessly to protect the children and hoped she could return to work in the future, but said the possibility of such remains an unanswered question.

Speaking outside court Garda (Irish police) Det Supt Colm Murphy acknowledged the actions of those "who immediately reacted the to the situation as it unfolded, in particular to Leanne Flynn â her actions on the day saved lives".

Murphy, who was the senior investigating officer in charge added: "To those who intervened and stopped the attack again, their actions saved lives".

He also gave praise to medical personnel on the ground and hospital staff, saying that they too "saved lives".

Murphy also acknowledged the principal of Gaelscoil CholÃ¡iste Mhuire, "for the way he and the staff at the school reacted on the day", and also to the parents who had to endure such a traumatic incident".

Judge Hunt said this was an unprecedented, highly unusual case involving a sudden, ferocious, sustained attack on young children and their childcare worker.

He said he had to mark the exceptional gravity of the offending against very young children and their carer, with a lethal weapon leading to consequences of the utmost gravity.

He said the circumstances were uniquely horrific and marked a profound assault on the most fundamental values protected by the criminal law.

The judge said the children happened to be selected because they were there and he was not yet sure what inference could be drawn from how Bouchaker found himself at their collection point.

At an earlier hearing, the court heard he received brain surgery in 2021 and a portion of his skull was removed, leaving a part of his brain vulnerable.

He suffered a head injury when members of the public intervened during the Parnell Square attack, after which he received hospital treatment for a month.

His defence team, which the judge ordered cannot be named due to safety concerns, said Bouchaker's cognitive function, memory, concentration, communication and decision-making were affected as a result of the impairment.

The most riot police in Irish state history were deployed to deal with the rioting following the attack.

The attack was followed by riots across much of Dublin.

The most riot police in Irish state history were deployed to deal with the unrest.

Within hours of the attack, rioters destroyed 11 police vehicles, while 13 shops were badly damaged and more were looted during clashes with riot police.

Three buses and a tram were also destroyed and several police officers were injured during three hours of sustained violence.

Ireland's police chief at the time, Drew Harris blamed the rioting on a "lunatic, hooligan faction driven by a far-right ideology".

A group of five EU member states, including Germany, was set to announce a new scheme on Monday to deport rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda.

A plan to set up so-called return hubs in a non-EU country had been announced by the group — which also includes Austria, the Netherlands, Greece and Denmark — had been announced back in September.

Monday's expected announcement comes after the EU introduced new regulations to speed up deportations and allow the establishment of hubs outside of the bloc.

Rwanda was not officially named as the chosen country, but people who had been briefed on the ongoing negotiations spoke to Reuters and AFP news agencies.

The central African country had also acknowledged being in "preliminary discussions" with the group of states.

Rwanda had also been the intended destination for a similar plan set up under the UK's former Conservative government that subsequently collapsed in UK courts.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

However, the new EU scheme differs from the British one in that it is only intended for migrants who have exhausted all other legal avenues within the European Union.

Migration hubs have been seen by governments as a means to visibly show that they are taking action on migration amid surging anti-migrant sentiment and rising support for the far right.

While the leaders of the five countries said the scheme would comply with EU law, that has not protected them from criticism, especially over the plan to send migrants to a country with which they have no connection.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the council of europe, a pan-european human rights body, said in july that return hubs posed "considerable human rights risks. ".

Claims that the scheme is meant as a deterrence have been rejected by researchers who say there is no evidence that deterrence works.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "enforcement changes how people travel, not whether they travel. Some pause or ⁠change ​route, and smugglers adapt and raise their prices," said Roberto Forin of the Mixed Migration Centre, a ​research institute that collects data along migration routes.

The choice to pick Rwanda has also been controversial, with the government President Paul Kagame in particular being accused of suppressing dissent and supporting the M23 rebel group in the neighboring Democratic Republic of Congo.

"Paying Kigali to host a deportation program would not only cause suffering and harm to those deported, it would finance and provide political leverage to a government responsible for serious human rights abuses at home and abroad," said Human Rights Watch's senior Africa researcher, Clementine de Montjoye.

#805. Trump to embark on Asia trip in apparent foreign policy push before end of term

📅 16 Nov 2026

Trump to embark on Asia trip in apparent foreign policy push before end of term

Tanggal: 16 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/16/trump-asia-foreign-domestic-policy

Experts say US president may lean toward global affairs after domestic influence curtailed in midterm elections.

Donald Trump is embarking on his first overseas trip since his Republican party’s thumping midterm repudiation by US voters, in what may herald a renewed focus on foreign policy for the remainder of his presidency.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the us president will meet his chinese and russian counterparts, xi jinping and vladimir putin, for their first trilateral summit, on the sidelines of the asia-pacific economic cooperation (apec) forum in the chinese city of shenzhen. Before that, he will land in Manila in the Philippines on Tuesday for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit.

At the Asean summit, Trump is expected to sign a trade agreement with Thailand, push deals with other countries and lobby fellow leaders to favour the US over China on artificial intelligence.

He will also take part in the first leaders’ meeting of the Quad partnership – consisting of the US, Japan, India and Australia – since he returned to the White House in January 2025.

Diungkapkan bahwa white house officials said the president would be accompanied to apec by elon musk, the tesla and spacex entrepreneur who spent almost $500m (£380m) unsuccessfully supporting republican candidates in this month’s midterms. The reason for Musk’s presence has not been explained.

The China leg of the trip will take place amid the continuing fallout from the Nvidia spying scandal, which prompted the company’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, to resign amid revelations he had had an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

Trump is under pressure to raise the matter with Xi when they hold a bilateral meeting on the sidelines of Apec.

The US president has said he does not plan to bring up the subject; administration officials insist he will not do so and that the meeting will be dedicated to implementing a trade agreement between the two superpowers.

Huang persuaded the Trump administration to lift restrictions on the sale of Nvidia’s AI chips to China that had been imposed during Joe Biden’s presidency.

Mao Ning, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson, told reporters on Monday that at the trilateral summit, Xi, Trump and Putin “will exchange views in depth on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations, which is of groundbreaking significance”.

Some analysts have characterised the meeting as a “big three” gathering echoing the 1945 Yalta meeting of Winston Churchill, Franklin D Roosevelt and Joseph Stalin that in effect carved up postwar Europe, between a communist-ruled east and a democratic, capitalist west.

Such a prospect has alarmed Ukraine, which fears that Putin – who initially suggested the trilateral meeting – will use it to persuade Trump and Xi to agree to a settlement of the war with Russia on Moscow’s terms.

However, Trump has said Ukraine will not be up for debate at the meeting and that its main purpose will be to discuss ending the US’s war with Iran and “denuclearisation” – shorthand for a deal among the three powers to limit nuclear arms.

That is believed to be unpalatable to China, which has been increasing its nuclear arsenal, and has signalled an unwillingness to enter into reduction agreements until it is closer to parity with the US and Russia.

Our US morning briefing breaks down the key stories of the day, telling you what’s happening and why it matters.

Analysts say the main beneficiary of the three-way meeting is likely to be Putin, whose standing will be boosted by being treated on an equal footing by two other leaders whose countries are, in reality, much more powerful.

Expectations of a substantial agreement are low.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, lyle goldstein, an international affairs fellow and china specialist at brown university in the us, said the trump-xi-putin meeting would not have a substantive result. “There will be no ‘Yalta’, as many have feared,” he said.

Jonathan Czin, the Michael Armacost chair in foreign policy studies at the Brookings Institution, said Trump’s lame duck status would deter Xi and Putin from trying to reach long-term arrangements with the US.

Diungkapkan bahwa “both men know trump’s time is expiring even more quickly than his leverage – and that he will be irrelevant in a mere 26 months [when his term expires],” czin told an online brookings forum. “Why would either man make a deal with a leader whose time and leverage are waning? They will only do it if they think they can pilfer more from Trump diplomatically than they will be able to gain from the next American president. ”.

Nevertheless, Goldstein – who took soundings on Chinese expectations for the summit in a visit to Shenzhen last week – predicted Trump would follow the pattern of previous presidents by turning increasingly to global affairs while he faces the prospect of his influence on the domestic front being curtailed after the Democrats’ victories in the House of Representatives and the Senate.

Berdasarkan laporan, “the president has been badly damaged by the election and will have limited prospects for the next two years,” he said. It would not surprise me if Trump is ready to go all-out to make some further splash in foreign policy. “That may cause him to be more active in foreign policy since he can act in that domain with fewer constraints. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, with the risks of reigniting the war with iran high and the russia-ukraine war still resistant to a diplomatic resolution despite white house efforts, goldstein suggested trump could attempt “a dramatic foreign policy flourish in asia”, such as an agreement with kim jong-un, the north korean dictator with whom he has frequently boasted of having a close relationship. Kim is not expected to attend the Apec gathering, although there have been rumours he may appear.

#808. Proposed NSW laws to allow coalmine to increase production pose ‘serious corruption risk’

📅 16 Nov 2026

Proposed NSW laws to allow coalmine to increase production pose ‘serious corruption risk’

Tanggal: 16 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/nov/17/proposed-nsw-laws-to-allow-coalmine-to-increase-production-pose-serious-corruption-risk

Bill to authorise expansion at Mount Pleasant coalmine, subject to a landmark high court decision, will be debated this week.

Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast.

A New South Wales government bill to increase coal production at a Hunter Valley coalmine creates a “serious corruption risk” for the state due to a clause that would give the resources minister “king-like” powers, the barrister and anti-corruption campaigner Geoffrey Watson says.

Diungkapkan bahwa the state parliament will this week debate legislation to allow mach energy to increase coal production at the mount pleasant mine in muswellbrook by 32% to 16. 5m tonnes per year.

Diungkapkan bahwa the minns government announced the bill last month after the high court ruled that an expansion of the mine was invalidly approved. The government has said the legislation is necessary to prevent 400 job losses at the site before Christmas.

Watson, the Greens and some members of the crossbench have raised concerns that a clause in the bill would give the resources minister of the day “unusually broad” powers to override other state laws.

Known as a Henry VIII clause, it would allow the minister to make regulations that could modify laws of the state as they apply to the Mount Pleasant development.

Henry VIII provisions are sometimes used by parliaments and draw their name from King Henry VIII and his style of governing by royal proclamation.

Watson is a director of the Centre for Public Integrity and Grata Fund and a former counsel assisting the NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption (Icac).

In a legal analysis of the bill, he raised concerns that Clause 17 “explicitly places” wide powers to “make new laws (or to repeal or modify existing laws) in the hands of one person – the mining minister – and for a single coal mine owner”.

“There are real problems with this as it is known that the concentration of this kind of power in the hands of one person creates a serious corruption risk,” he wrote.

Berdasarkan laporan, he said the risk was “heightened” because the mount pleasant bill had been created for a single private company. He wrote that while he imputed “no bad faith at all to the current mining minister”, past experience in the state “has shown that not all ministers have acted in a manner free from improper motives”.

“Historically, we’ve seen this concentration of power into the hands of a single decision maker as posing a serious risk of corruption,” Watson told Guardian Australia.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “now, corruption in that sense may not mean money passing hands. It also includes undue influence, decisions made in [circumstances] other than the public interest. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa elaine johnson is the director of johnson legal, which represented the denman aberdeen muswellbrook scone healthy environment group (dams heg) in the high court proceedings. In a separate legal opinion, she raised similar concerns there was “a very obvious corruption risk arising from Clause 17”.

She wrote that the clause gave the resources minister of the day “unfettered power to make regulations to change the application of any law of the state” to the mine, and said it could potentially affect many laws that applied to the mine, such as those that regulate noise and dust or worker safety.

Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here.

Diungkapkan bahwa the lower house is expected to debate the legislation on tuesday, followed by the upper house later this week. The Minns government is hoping to pass the bill in what is likely to be the final sitting week before the March 2027 election.

Both Labor and Coalition lower house seats are under pressure from One Nation in the Hunter, where the mine is located.

One Nation’s NSW leader and candidate for Cessnock, Mike Newman, has described the Minns government’s bill to increase production limits at Mount Pleasant as a “Band-Aid on a bullet-wound”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the coalition resources spokesperson and nationals mp for upper hunter, dave layzell, said the opposition would not oppose labor’s legislation “in any way”. Asked about the Henry VIII clause, he said the Coalition would follow advice on the bill from the parliament’s legislation review committee which is expected on Tuesday.

Our political team brings you up to speed on the stories that really matter and what they mean for you.

“We recognise [Labor’s] argument about the need to protect the number of jobs they are quoting.

“We agree that it is important that we fix the situation with the Mount Pleasant Mine extension.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “we cannot allow green environmental lawfare to continue to delay projects that have the support of the majority of the community, and are approved on a technical basis by the planning system. ”.

The Greens climate spokesperson Sue Higginson said it was “the broadest” Henry VIII clause she had seen during the current parliament and the party would seek to remove it from the bill or limit its scope.

“Placing that much power in the hands of a single minister is a corruption risk the Labor government should know well,” she said.

Diungkapkan bahwa “a tightly limited henry viii provision can be necessary to give effect to parliament’s decision over time, as with the recent great koala national park bill, where it allowed more land to be permanently protected in the public interest as it becomes available. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, a spokesperson for the resources minister, courtney houssos, said the government had been clear that the purpose of its bill was to protect all permanent workers at mount pleasant. They said the bill had been presented transparently to parliament.

“We welcome constructive engagement on the Bill from crossbenchers and will engage with good-faith amendments as we always do,” they said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “any proposed regulation would be submitted to the executive council for approval and published transparently in the usual manner, and also subject to disallowance in the usual manner. ”.

They added that Henry VIII provisions had been “routinely” used in legislation for decades, including in bills the Greens had supported in this term of parliament.

The independent MP Alex Greenwich, who intends to oppose the bill as a whole, said the provision was “dangerously broad and quite unprecedented”.

“It’s especially concerning, given parliament won’t sit for six months, meaning regulations issued during that time won’t be able to be disallowed,” he said.

#809. Landmark Crimea bridge hit as Russia reports biggest Ukrainian drone attack of war

Landmark Crimea bridge hit as Russia reports biggest Ukrainian drone attack of war

Tanggal: 16 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ckx27v6dpjz0o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

The Kerch bridge was built in 2018 and is one of President Putin's signature infrastructure projects (file photo).

Russia says it has recorded the biggest Ukrainian drone attack since the war began, in which a landmark bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea sustained minor damage and several oil refineries were hit.

Berdasarkan laporan, the russian military intercepted and destroyed 2,049 drones and four flamingo long-distance missiles over 24 hours, officials said. Around 600 flew towards capital alone, Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin added.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, kyiv, meanwhile, came under a record 17 air raid alerts in a single day. At least seven people were killed by Russian strikes and attacks on energy infrastructure caused blackouts for 50,000 people.

The intense strikes come days after US, Ukrainian and Russian envoys held talks aimed at ending the war.

The war in Ukraine began with Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022.

The Moscow-installed head of Crimea, Sergei Aksyonov, confirmed that drones had struck the Crimean Bridge connecting Russia's mainland with the annexed peninsula, leading to traffic restrictions.

Diungkapkan bahwa the structure - also known as kerch bridge - was built by russia after it invaded and annexed the peninsula in 2014. It was inaugurated by Russian President Vladimir Putin to great fanfare in 2018 and is carefully protected with multiple layers of aerial and maritime defences.

Berdasarkan laporan, russian pro-war military commentators said on telegram that rather than a direct attack, the bridge had suffered from the impact of drone warhead debris. Neither Ukraine's domestic security service nor its main military intelligence directorate has responded to a BBC request for comment.

Atesh, a partisan Ukrainian group operating inside Russian-held territory, said on social media that authorities in Crimea were "bracing for further strikes" on the Kerch Bridge and that they felt Moscow did not appreciate the seriousness of the situation.

Ukrainian drones also hit several energy facilities, including an oil refinery in Ilsky, in the southern Krasnodar region, where falling drone debris sparked a fire and injured six people, including children.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, last week, president volodymyr zelensky accused russia of carrying out a concerted operation against ukraine's bridges in order to "divide ukraine. and make life as difficult as possible for people" on both sides of the Dnipro River which cuts across the country.

Despite the high-level diplomacy and visits by US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff to both Putin and Zelensky, peace remains a distant prospect.

Moscow is uncompromising on its demands for Ukraine to cede territory and measures to ensure Kyiv's neutrality.

The Kremlin has now also started to talk about the need to rethink Europe's "security architecture", often intended by Moscow to mean a scaled-down Nato presence in countries close to Russia.

The apparent willingness of the US to engage in this conversation has set off alarm bells among Ukraine's European partners, which are concerned their continent's security could be redrawn by Washington and Moscow without their involvement.

A team of six - Britain, France, Germany, Italy, Poland and a representative of the EU institutions - will represent Europe in future talks with Russia, Ukraine and the US.

But the Kremlin continues to be dismissive of European input.

Diungkapkan bahwa "we have also said more than once we need to understand. how much their position will help the peace process," said spokesman Dmitri Peskov.

EU representatives kept pushing for "unconditional support" for Ukraine and "enhanced pressure" on Russia, Peskov said, adding that "this sort of wording rather suggests their reluctance to facilitate the peace process".

Rosenberg: Uncompromising Putin ups demands for peace with Ukraine.

US has floated Ukraine ceding Donbas for Nato membership, Zelensky says.

Russia's mega-rich are already imagining a future after Putin.

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.

The Minns government has mothballed laws intended to protect homebuyers from underquoting after the premier said real estate agents in his Sydney electorate had raised concerns about their effect amid a housing market downturn.

Changes due to come into effect on Tuesday would have banned agents in New South Wales from lowering the advertised price of a property beneath a written offer previously rejected by a seller, with fines of up to $110,000 or three times an agent’s commission, whichever was greater.

But the laws and fines will be paused for up to a year after a last-minute intervention by the premier, Chris Minns, who flagged on Monday morning that concerns had been raised by agents in his south Sydney electorate of Kogarah.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “it has come across my desk from real estate agents in my electorate,” he told reporters, after he was asked about fears the laws could prevent sellers from advertising at a lower rate now that the market has fallen. Home values in Sydney have dropped by 10. 1% from their 2026 peak, according to data from Cotality.

“I do think it’s [an] unforeseen [consequence], but it is something we’re going to have to deal with because it’s not the seller or the agent’s fault if the price of real estate is dropping, and the legislation at least intuitively believed that the prices would always rise,” said Minns.

Diungkapkan bahwa the changes, which were passed in june, were modelled on laws already in effect in victoria. Under additional transparency measures which came into effect in Victoria last month, sellers must reveal their reserve price at least one week before a sale, and agents must publish sale prices after a transaction is completed.

The decision is a potential embarrassment for NSW fair trading and corrections minister, Anoulack Chanthivong, who has previously been overruled by Minns on rental and prison reforms.

The minister faces a preselection battle in his seat of Macquarie Fields, but Minns would not say on Monday if he would intervene on Chanthivong’s behalf.

As recently as 1 November, Chanthivong had praised the laws as “important reforms to put the hammer down on underquoting and stop homebuyers being taken for a ride”.

On Monday afternoon, a spokesperson for the Minns government provided a statement from Chanthivong, who said the laws had been passed “at a different time and in a different economic and housing market”.

“We introduced these laws to crack down on underquoting, protect homebuyers from misleading practices and ensure a fair and transparent property market for buyers and sellers,” he said.

“People are already doing it tough, and the last thing we want is for laws designed to protect homebuyers to inadvertently make it harder for them to buy a home.

Diungkapkan bahwa “that’s why the government has made the decision not to proceed with the implementation of these changes today. ”.

It is the latest of several reversals in recent weeks by the government, under pressure ahead of the March state election from One Nation and the Coalition, with the cost of living and pressures on small businesses among the key issues.

Last month, the government dropped parts of plastics legislation which would have required cafes to offer customers who dine in the option of mugs and glasses instead of takeaway cups.

Sebagaimana diketahui, polling conducted internally by the labor party has suggested that one nation could win more than 20 seats in the lower house. The party was polling at 26% of the primary vote in NSW according to a Sydney Morning Herald Resolve poll in October, behind Labor on 30%, but ahead of the Coalition on 23%.

One Nation announced four more candidates on its six-person upper house ticket on Sunday, but has so far only announced one lower house candidate, NSW party leader Mike Newman.

The Estonian government says it will shut the crossings after accusing Russia of directing an alleged sabotage attack on a drone manufacturer.

Estonia has said it will close border crossings into Russia from 1 December after accusing Moscow of being behind an attempted arson attack at a drone factory.

Prime Minister Kristen Michal said the break-in on Saturday at a facility north of the capital Tallinn was part of what he called Russia's "broader hybrid war against Europe".

The alleged attackers were arrested, Michal said, with local media reporting the suspects are Latvian.

They are said to have broken into the factory and attempted to set fire to it using flammable liquids.

On Monday, Moscow said the accusation was "baseless" and accused the Estonian government of "building a wall" between the neighbouring countries.

The facility targeted is operated by Threod Systems and produces attack and reconnaissance drones, with Ukraine and Nato member states listed as customers on its website.

Foreign minister Margus Tsahkna said on Sunday that "closing the border crossings will reduce Russia's ability to conduct hostile activities in Estonia".

Michal said "extensive damage was averted thanks to heightened security measures" at the factory, while the head of Estonia's internal security service labelled the incident attempted Russian sabotage.

The decision to close border crossings is expected to be finalised next week, according to local media.

Diungkapkan bahwa estonia shares a border of around 220 miles (338 km) with russia that spans both sea and land. Three road crossings are in operation but are already subject to restrictions.

Diungkapkan bahwa one of them is located at narva, estonia's third biggest city. It sits on the western bank of the River Narva that flows into the Baltic Sea; on the eastern bank is Russia. Closures will complicate life for families which live either side of the border.

Sebagaimana diketahui, kremlin spokesman dimitry peskov said: "estonia is building a wall. Many countries, as history demonstrates, have built walls that have brought nothing good to those who erect such walls. ".

Russia has been repeatedly accused by European leaders of targeting national infrastructure and resources destined for Ukraine since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022.

Tanggal: 16 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/16/world/europe/russia-ukraine-winter-campaign.html

Even as it talks peace, Russia has opened a bombing campaign intended to strip Kyiv and other cities of heat, running water and sanitation this winter.

When American-led talks to end the war in Ukraine resumed last week in Abu Dhabi, the overriding question was whether Russia intended to give any ground after a nine-month lull in negotiations.

Berdasarkan laporan, but russian missiles and drones had already done the talking for moscow, analysts said. Weeks earlier than expected, Russia has opened an intense bombing campaign against the infrastructure that keeps Ukrainians alive and functioning in the winter. Daily waves of strikes against Ukraine’s energy system have raised fears that the capital, Kyiv, a city of three million people, could become all but uninhabitable in the coming months.

Berdasarkan laporan, in the abu dhabi talks, an emboldened russia outlined hard-line demands that stood little chance of gaining acceptance by ukraine and its european allies. That unbending stance indicated that Russia had no real interest in discussing peace now, because Moscow believes that the winter bombing campaign will strengthen its negotiating position entering the spring.

“They want to come to the table holding our energy system hostage,” President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine said after a recent Russian attack.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the abu dhabi talks will be followed by a meeting on thursday between president trump, president vladimir v. Putin of Russia and the Chinese leader, Xi Jinping, at a summit in Shenzhen, China. It was unclear whether the three leaders would discuss the war in Ukraine.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, assaulting infrastructure has become moscow’s strategy for victory as it has failed for nearly five years to achieve its major objectives in ukraine. While Russia has tried each winter to knock out the country’s power system and freeze its people into submission, Ukrainian cities are now in their most precarious position of the war. The grid is more fragile after years of strikes, and the Ukrainian military is struggling to protect the system because of dwindling air defenses.

Gun violence remains a persistent problem in South Africa, where about 60 people are murdered every day, according to police (file photo).

South African police are investigating the murders of 17 people in two separate shootings on Sunday night.

Berdasarkan laporan, eight men were fatally shot in a minibus in kwazulu-natal province. Police declared them dead when they arrived at the scene. Hours later, nine people were found shot dead inside a shack in western Pretoria.

Diungkapkan bahwa police say the two incidents are unrelated. The motive for the shootings has not yet been established.

Sebagaimana diketahui, south africa is struggling to contain violent crime, including gang-related killings. The country has one of the world's highest murder rates.

Police say they responded to reports of a shooting â outside Pietermaritzburg town in KwaZulu-Natal and found a white seven-seater vehicle riddled with bullet holes.

Inside were eight men with multiple gunshot wounds.

"It has not been established how the incident happened, and police are collecting pieces of evidence to determine the possible motive of the killings and the identity of the suspects," police spokesperson Robert Netshiunda said.

The police have launched a manhunt for the suspects.

In a separate shooting in the Jeffsville informal settlement in Atteridgeville, west of Pretoria, police found the bodies of six men and three women.

Berdasarkan laporan, they are believed to have been killed inside a four-room shack between 22:00 and 23:00 on sunday. The bodies were scattered across the rooms, with several spent cartridges discovered outside the shack.

Community members initially mistook the gunshots for thunder and lightning.

"The provincial commissioner of police in Gauteng [province, which includes Pretoria] has mobilized the necessary resources, including the crime intelligence and the deputy provincial commissioner tracking team to search for the suspect," police spokesperson Brigadier Brenda Muridili said.

Berdasarkan laporan, it's not the first mass shooting in the area. In January, five men were shot dead outside a local shop in broad daylight.

Illegal firearms are widespread in South Africa, where gun violence remains a persistent problem, increasingly involving mass shootings.

In September, 28 people were killed in two separate cases.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, eighteen people were killed when eight gunmen stormed a bar near johannesburg and opened fire on 25 september. Fourteen others were injured.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in a separate shooting the following day, 10 people were killed outside an entertainment venue in a township near cape town. A further 11 were injured.

Much of the violence has been linked to turf wars between gangs involved in drug trafficking and illegal mining.

In February, President Cyril Ramaphosa described organised crime as "the most immediate threat to our democracy, our society and our economic development".

Earlier this year, the military was deployed alongside police to five provinces with the highest murder rates, including Gauteng, in an effort to tackle armed violence.

Berdasarkan laporan, according to the latest police statistics, 5,427 people were murdered nationwide between april and june 2026, an average of about 60 killings a day. This was a 6% decline compared with the same period a year earlier.

#830. Gérard Depardieu drops appeal against sexual assault conviction

📅 16 Nov 2026

Gérard Depardieu drops appeal against sexual assault conviction

Tanggal: 16 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/nov/16/gerard-depardieu-drops-appeal-against-sexual-assault-conviction

French actor apologises to two women he was convicted of assaulting on a film set in 2021.

The French actor Gérard Depardieu has dropped his appeal against a conviction for sexually assaulting two women on a film set, and has for the first time apologised to the victims.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i was found guilty. “I address my deep and sincere apologies to those who suffered. I hear it and I accept this conviction,” Depardieu, 77, said in a written statement. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the actor, who has made more than 200 films and tv series, wrote: “for a long time on film sets, i hid behind provocation and ribald humour. ”.

He said he accepted that remarks and “some of my gestures” were not “without consequences”, particularly because he held a powerful position in the entertainment industry.

Depardieu said he had never intended to hurt the women he encountered but had “come to understand that intention changes nothing about the harm caused”.

He said times had changed and that he belonged “to a world that no longer exists”.

At a trial last year, Depardieu was found guilty of sexually assaulting a 55-year-old set dresser and a 35-year-old assistant director during the shooting of the feature film Les Volets Verts (The Green Shutters) in Paris in September 2021.

His suspended sentence will now stand and his name must be added to France’s sex offender register.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the set dresser, named in the media as amélie, said outside the paris appeal court on monday: “i waited for years for this apology. ” She said she would have preferred if Depardieu had attended court to deliver it in person.

Diungkapkan bahwa the assistant director, named in the media as sarah, said: “the monster of cinema has fallen. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, depardieu’s conviction last year was a turning point for the #metoo movement in france. He became the biggest figure in the French film industry to be convicted of sexual assault after years of criticism of the country’s reluctance to take women’s claims of abuse seriously.

Diungkapkan bahwa depardieu had previously denied all allegations of sexual assault. He told last year’s trial that the media had used allegations against him to damage his reputation.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, he attacked the #metoo movement as well as women who had staged protests outside venues during his concert tour at the time of the allegations. “This movement is going to become a terror,” he said.

The trial also set an important legal precedent when the judge ruled that Depardieu’s defence lawyer, Jérémie Assous, had been “excessively harsh” to the two women in court, saying they were not real victims and were liars.

Assous had said the women were working for the cause of “rabid feminism” and called their lawyers hysterical, “abject and stupid” and described them as having an “unbearable voice”.

The judge awarded the complainants compensation for being further victimised by Depardieu’s defence during the trial, ordering Depardieu to pay each woman €1,000 (£835).

The court had heard there was a “system of impunity” around Depardieu, with film industry insiders staying silent to keep cashing in on his name.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, depardieu has appealed against a separate decision requiring him to face trial on charges of raping and sexually assaulting the actor charlotte arnould at his paris home in 2018. Appeal judges will rule this month on whether to uphold his appeal or allow the trial to go ahead next year.

Diungkapkan bahwa in an open letter to le figaro in october 2023, depardieu denied all allegations and said any encounter with arnould had been consensual. “Never, ever, have I abused a woman,” he wrote.

In December 2023, when Depardieu was under formal investigation for rape and sexual assault in the Arnould case and also facing scrutiny over sexist comments revealed in a TV documentary, the French president defended him, saying “he makes France proud”.

Berdasarkan laporan, asked at the time about stripping depardieu of a state award, emmanuel macron said: “you will never see me participate in a manhunt … i hate that type of thing. ”.

#832. ‘It’s like the 16th-century version of doomscrolling’: the Book of Miracles may fetch £1m at auction

📅 16 Nov 2026

‘It’s like the 16th-century version of doomscrolling’: the Book of Miracles may fetch £1m at auction

Tanggal: 16 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/books/2026/nov/16/book-of-miracles-apocalyptic-weather-visions-auction

Exclusive: Public institutions get first chance to bid for rare ‘wonderbook’ of apocalyptic visions and extreme weather.

Berdasarkan laporan, in one illustration, five suns blaze down on leipzig in 1551. In another, blood rain falls on Rome in 1456. In a third scene, dated 1552, monstrous hailstones batter the Dutch city of Dordrecht during a storm so fierce people feared Judgment Day had come.

Created during the mid-16th century, when earthquakes, storms, floods and other extreme weather events were often interpreted as ominous warnings from God, the Book of Miracles contains 167 paintings of apocalyptic visions, celestial wonders and meteorological phenomena.

Diungkapkan bahwa it is the only known copy. To this day, no one is sure why it was created.

Berdasarkan laporan, now, public institutions will have their first chance to bid for the book of miracles since scholars learned it existed. It is expected to fetch between £700,000 and £1m when it is auctioned in London on 10 December, as the star lot of the Christie’s valuable books and manuscripts sale.

Members of the public will also have a rare opportunity to see it in person for six days before it goes under the hammer.

Berdasarkan laporan, for nearly half a millennium, scholars were unaware of its existence. Found in the library of a small baroque castle in southern Germany nearly 20 years ago, the manuscript, which is from 1550s Augsburg, was put up for auction alongside the castle’s furniture, carpets and tankards in 2008 and sold for just over £100,000.

Shortly after the sale, the manuscript entered the private collection of Mickey Cartin, one of Connecticut’s biggest contemporary art collectors.

Eugenio Donadoni, Christie’s international specialist in medieval and Renaissance manuscripts, said the book was an “exceptionally rare” German wonderbook.

Diungkapkan bahwa “german wonderbooks functioned as the sensationalist mass media of their day,” he said. They mark a shift from medieval to Enlightenment. “They were used by Lutheran theologians such as Martin Luther and Philip Melanchthon to further their Protestant eschatology, but crucially – with all the depictions of comets, cosmological events, natural disasters, all verified by witnesses, with exact dates and geographic coordinates – they laid early foundations for empirical observation and reporting. ”.

He expects the sale will attract collectors of both historic and modern art because some of the scenes, which are painted in watercolour and gouache, are “super surrealist … almost Dalí-esque”.

“If it weren’t for the little captions, which are obviously 16th-century German, some of them look so vividly modern … it’s really jaw-dropping,” Donadoni said.

The scenes depicted include a plague of locusts arriving in Poland on a “terrible wind” in 1527 and the North Sea flooding the coast of Frisia – in what is now the Netherlands and Germany – in 1230.

Other pictures are of fiery comets and eclipses, while scholars think an illustration of “wondrous dragons” flying across the sky over Bavaria in 1533 depicts the northern lights.

Underneath each scene, a German picture caption describes what is happening and where and when the event took place.

Your weekly art world round-up, sketching out all the biggest stories, scandals and exhibitions.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “all of these events are portentous,” said donadoni. “The artists of the Book of Miracles, relying on contemporary broadsheets, chronicles and histories, have condensed into pictorial form the concerns of an age that was gripped by an anxiety – and learned curiosity – about the future. ”.

The book records how uneasy people felt about climatic anomalies at a time of doctrinal disunity, when there was growing interest in documenting and cataloguing visible, tangible scientific phenomena, he said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “it’s really fascinating … it is a window into how europeans were dealing with the impending end of the world, political uncertainty and extreme – and strange – weather events. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the five suns over leipzig, for example, is thought to depict the optical illusion of a parhelion, more commonly known as a sun dog. “You see in the sky various different rings of light and it looks like suns,” Donadoni said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “blood rain” occurs when high concentrations of red-coloured dust particles, usually from the sahara, mix with water droplets in rain clouds. “Many of these things have actual rational scientific explanations to them,” Donadoni said.

Diungkapkan bahwa he said he imagined that leafing through the pages of the book in the 1550s was similar to bingeing on bad news on social media today: “i think it could be a little like the 16th-century version of doomscrolling. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in this way, the book straddles a momentous turning point in history. “We’re right at that period where the superstition of the middle ages turns into the age of scientific discovery,” Donadoni said.

Berdasarkan laporan, till-holger borchert, the director of the suermondt ludwig museum in aachen, has studied the manuscript and said the first time he saw it, his reaction was: “wow”. “It’s one of a kind,” he said. “It grabs you by your heart or your soul or your belly. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, he said he thought £1m was a “very conservative estimate” of its value. “It [the final price] could possibly be much more,” he said.

Diungkapkan bahwa a facsimile of the manuscript was published in 2013 that got people “really excited” about it, borchert added, and since then the book of miracles has become “a kind of icon for people who are interested in apocalyptic things”. It would be wrong to value it merely as an historical document: “It’s more than that. It speaks to us, to our generation. ”.

The remains of writer and diplomat Miguel Ãngel Asturias have been buried in his native Guatemala 52 years after he died in exile.

His ashes were brought to Guatemala from Paris, where he had lived before his death from cancer in the Spanish capital, Madrid, in 1974.

Asturias was awarded the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1967 for his vivid writings, which drew on the experiences of indigenous Guatemalans.

The urn containing his ashes was placed in soil gathered from different parts of Guatemala at a cultural centre named after him in Guatemala City.

Sebagaimana diketahui, his son, whose name is also miguel ãngel asturias, said at the ceremony on sunday: "i can tell you, old man, that you are with us, you are in your homeland, you will sleep beneath your own skies. ".

Asturias, who was born in 1899, first moved to Paris in the 1920s to study ethnology.

Influenced by the surrealists, he wrote his first major work, Legends of Guatemala, a retelling of Maya origin legends and mythological tales, while in France.

Subsequent works, such as the 1946 novel The President and his Banana Trilogy, denounced the terrors of dictatorship in Latin America and the exploitation indigenous workers suffered on banana plantations.

Arguably his most famous novel was Men of Maize, published in 1949, which explores the struggles of indigenous communities as the world around them quickly changes and modernises.

Nobel Peace Prize laureate Rigoberta MenchÃº (centre) attended a ceremony to welcome the ashes of Asturias back to Guatemala alongside the writer's son (right).

Between 1944 and 1954, a period known as "Guatemala's 10 Years of Spring", he served in several diplomatic posts in Central and South America and continued writing.

But when the democratically elected Guatemalan President Jacobo Ãrbenz GuzmÃ¡n was deposed in a CIA-backed coup in 1954, Asturias was stripped of his Guatemalan citizenship, his books were banned and he had to go into exile.

At Sunday's burial ceremony, Asturias's son said that the writer had "always wanted to be in Guatemala" but "political conditions did not allow him to".

The family only agreed to have the ashes moved from PÃ¨re Lachaise cemetery in Paris to Guatemala after the current progressive president of Guatemala, Bernardo ArÃ©valo, was elected in 2023.

ArÃ©valo praised Asturias at the interment ceremony as "our voice in the world".

"He deserved to rest in the land he named and reinvented in his pages," said ArÃ©valo, whose father Juan JosÃ© appointed Asturias to the diplomatic service when the older ArÃ©valo served as president during the 10 Year Spring.

Andy Burnham will say on Monday that Brexit “has not worked” and that he will sign a new deal with the EU.

It is the latest in a string of comments by the prime minister criticising Brexit, after he told the Welsh Labour conference on Saturday that the UK has “lost more than we gained” through leaving the EU.

Is consistent with the Labour manifesto and the government’s red lines.
