Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cr868wd2qg18o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

The attack on Bilkis Bano and her family was one of the most horrific crimes during the Gujarat riots.

The article has details that some readers may find disturbing.

A pregnant Muslim woman who was gang-raped and saw 14 family members murdered during the 2002 Gujarat riots has spoken of her "pain, shock and disbelief" after two of her rapists were recently granted bail.

Bilkis Bano said in a statement that she heard about the top court order through press reports and vowed to fight back.

The freed men are from a group of 11 convicts - part of a Hindu mob - serving life terms for the attack on Bano.

Diungkapkan bahwa all the men were also freed in 2022 after a gujarat government order. That decision, and the celebrations as they left prison, caused global outrage. In 2024, the Supreme Court overturned the order.

In a short three-page order dated 28 October, the Supreme Court granted bail to Bipinchand Kanaiyalal Joshi and Pradip Ramanlal Modhiya and suspended their sentences while their petition challenging a 2017 Bombay High Court order is being heard.

The judges explained that the early release was because the two convicts "have been under incarceration for a period of more than 17 years" and "that one of the appellants has a severe handicap".

On Tuesday, Bano's lawyer Shobha Gupta told the BBC that the news of Joshi and Modhiya's release had left "Bilkis heartbroken".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "she has to restart her battle for justice. What is troubling for us is that every time something like this happens, we worry that it could affect her faith in judiciary. She had no information that this case was coming up in the Supreme Court. ".

The riots began after a fire on a passenger train in Godhra town killed 60 Hindu pilgrims.

Gupta said it was difficult to understand why the convicts were being released because "it's not a routine criminal case, it's a case that shocks the conscience of the world, of entire humanity".

The attack on Bano and her family was one of the most horrific crimes during the Gujarat riots, which began after 60 Hindu pilgrims were killed in a fire on a passenger train in the town of Godhra.

Diungkapkan bahwa hindu mobs attacked muslim neighbourhoods, blaming them for starting the fire. The riots continued for three days and more than 1,000 people died, most of them Muslims.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when rioters attacked bano's village and started setting muslim homes on fire, she and 16 relatives went on the run. She was 19, had a three-year-old daughter and was pregnant with her second child.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, they were attacked on the morning of 3 march 2002 by a group of men "with swords and sticks", she told me in 2017. Her three-year-old daughter, she said, was snatched from her lap and killed.

How a Gujarat riot victim stood up to her rapists.

India Supreme Court cancels release of 2002 riots rapists.

India PM Modi's government okayed rapists' release.

Berdasarkan laporan, her attackers were her neighbours, men she had seen almost daily while growing up. They tore off her clothes and several of them raped her, ignoring her pleas for mercy.

Her cousin, who had given birth two days earlier, was raped and murdered and her newborn baby was killed too.

Diungkapkan bahwa bano survived only because she lost consciousness and her attackers left, believing she was dead. Two boys - seven and four - were the only other survivors of the massacre.

The riots continued for three days and more than 1,000 people died, most of them Muslims.

Berdasarkan laporan, her fight for justice has been long and nightmarish. The first arrests were made only in 2004 after the Supreme Court called in federal investigators and transferred her case to Mumbai, saying that courts in Gujarat could not deliver justice to her.

In her statement released on Monday night, Bano spoke of "fresh tears of pain, shock and disbelief".

"I still cannot believe that once again, for the second time, an order has been passed by the Supreme Court without calling me up and without hearing me," she said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "for 24 long years, i have stood up to fight for justice. again and again. And I am scared of losing faith in justice, yet again. Yet today, I find myself losing the very justice I had fought so hard to win. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa bano vowed to "fight this order. for my children, who do not deserve to live haunted by fears and scars for the rest of their lives".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "i do this for my three-year-old saleha who deserved to live and whose memory demands justice. Because no woman, no survivor, no citizen should have to endure this eternal test of belonging and equality, and fight for justice for the rest of her life. I do this for women everywhere. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa prime minister narendra modi was gujarat chief minister at the time of the riots, and was criticised for not doing enough to prevent the carnage. He has always denied wrongdoing and has not apologised for the riots.

Berdasarkan laporan, in 2013, a supreme court panel also said that there was insufficient evidence to prosecute him. But critics have continued to blame him for the riots happening on his watch.

#961. Paul Kelly pleads for Albanese to ‘show some backbone’ over AI as creatives campaign for copyright protections

Paul Kelly pleads for Albanese to ‘show some backbone’ over AI as creatives campaign for copyright protections

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/18/paul-kelly-albanese-ai-copyright-protections-creatives-campaign

Music legend is joined by Jimmy Barnes and Peter Garrett in backing Not AI’s To Take campaign ahead of Aria awards.

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.

Australia’s creative community has launched a major campaign pleading with the Albanese government not to water down copyright law amid furious lobbying from AI companies, ahead of Wednesday night’s Aria awards.

Music legends Jimmy Barnes, Paul Kelly and Peter Garrett are among those backing the Not AI’s To Take campaign, supported by dozens of creative groups representing the recording, writing, publishing, film, television and media industries.

While the government maintains it will not undermine copyright law, the industry minister, Tim Ayres, said on Tuesday “the status quo is no good” for the creative sector, ahead of a package of AI legislation expected by early 2027.

But creatives have pushed back on such claims, arguing copyright law doesn’t need updating – just better enforcement, and that changes could put the $70bn creative industry and its 600,000 workers at risk.

Diungkapkan bahwa “[ai platforms] haven’t made one phone call yet. They haven’t called us. They haven’t called anybody,” said Dean Ormston, CEO of music rights organisation Apra Amcos.

Berdasarkan laporan, “there’s nothing wrong with the copyright framework. The problem is getting somebody to sit at the table and have a discussion with us. ”.

Not AI’s To Take is backed by the likes of Aria, the Copyright Agency, the Australian Directors’ Guild, Screen Producers Australia, the Australian Society of Authors, the Australian Writers’ Guild, and media organisations including Foxtel, Free TV, Nine, Seven and Guardian Australia.

Australian musicians including Montaigne and KLP have backed the campaign online, while Guardian Australia understands Barnes, Kelly and Garrett – some of Anthony Albanese’s favourite musicians – will also feature.

“Our government has been a huge supporter of Australian music and creativity, and now we’re asking them to continue that support by standing firm on copyright and making sure big tech doesn’t get to rewrite the rules at the expense of creators,” said KLP, real name Kristy Lee Peters.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in quotes shared on the campaign’s website, barnes said: “i think that these companies should go and f. k themselves. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, kelly is quoted as saying: “australia has had some of the best copyright laws, something to be proud of. Now is the time for our government to show some backbone. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa although albanese has declared it would be “theft” if creatives weren’t paid for their work, some ai companies have argued it is too difficult to make individual licensing deals under existing copyright law. AI companies have said they need legal certainty on the copyright issue before investing and training models in Australia, with Anthropic putting forward an “opt-out” model to scrape creative works unless a rightsholder objected.

Diungkapkan bahwa however anthropic told a senate committee it would “provide ongoing access to frontier models to eligible australian entities, regardless of whether training is permitted. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the government is expected to unveil a long-awaited legislative package on ai in late 2026 or early 2027, with proposals around datacentres, online safety, productivity and copyright. Albanese said last week that artists “need to be compensated if their work is used”. But the creative community is concerned that lobbying from big tech may sway government decisions.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “this isn’t a smear campaign. We’re just making some noise out in the open, where tech companies are doing it in the shadows,” said Patrizia Di Biase-Dyson, CEO of the Australian Publishers Association.

Berdasarkan laporan, “everything is at stake. We have to do as much as possible to educate everyone. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa ormston said creative industries welcomed the investment and opportunities of ai, and had applauded both labor’s rebuffing of a text and data mining exemption and albanese’s public support. But he said artists were worried about potential changes.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “our very clear message to the government has been: hold firm. You are absolutely saying the right thing. You are absolutely right in the fact that while we want AI in this country, we want it on Australia’s terms,” Ormston said.

Asked about the campaign on Tuesday, Ayres said “nothing has changed in terms of the government’s approach” to copyright.

Diungkapkan bahwa “i understand the anxiety, though. Their work is currently being appropriated, today, offshore. For those workers, the status quo is no good for them. We have set out a program for a scheme of legislation that would protect those rights, make sure that artificial intelligence investment in Australia is on Australia’s terms.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “we’re not about undermining copyright here. That commitment has been made so many times now. ”.

A spokesperson for the attorney general, Michelle Rowland, said the government was “committed to supporting” creatives, and pledged any copyright changes would “deliver meaningful control and fair compensation”.

But independent senator David Pocock urged caution around any moves, warning that copyright changes could create a legal “loophole” to make Australia a global “data laundering hotspot”.

“There are more than 100 court cases on foot involving copyright and AI training in the US and we should wait for these to play out before making any changes given the risks of getting it wrong are so high,” he said.

The E1 area east of Jerusalem is a strategically important part of the occupied West Bank.

The UK has sanctioned companies it said were involved in building settlements in the occupied West Bank, in the first package of measures since the government announced a tougher approach to Israeli actions in the territory.

The government said the sanctions against eight construction and property development firms would disrupt their flows of finance and ability to support building in the West Bank.

Settlements are illegal under international law, and there has been a rise in violence towards Palestinians in the West Bank by settlers in recent months.

It comes two days before the deadline for bids for construction tenders in the E1 area east of Jerusalem.

The plans, which have been condemned internationally, would in effect divide the West Bank in two and isolate East Jerusalem.

UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has said the E1 development would render a two-state solution "unviable" by "cutting through the heart of Palestine".

The sanctions also target Tzav 9, an Israeli activist movement which the UK government says has organised and carried out blockades to prevent aid entering Gaza.

It comes after the UK expanded its human rights sanctions regime last month, enabling the government to sanction individuals and companies involved in violations of international humanitarian law anywhere in the world.

The government is also developing separate legislation to ban the import of settlement goods and the provision of advertising services for settlement properties in the UK.

Miliband said: "Protecting the two-state solution is the North Star of this government's approach.

"That is why my message on E1 is clear: do not bid, do not build, and do not profit from the destruction of the two-state solution.

"The status quo in the West Bank and Gaza is unacceptable.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "we are committed to working productively with a new israeli government and the palestinian authority to advance lasting peace and security for israelis and palestinians alike. ".

UK announces sanctions on West Bank settlements prompting furious Israeli response.

Israel opens up bids for highly sensitive West Bank settlement project.

In September, the UK government announced that it would ban the import of goods from Israeli settlements, as well as acting against companies and individuals providing services for settlement expansion.

At the time, Miliband said the move marked the "beginning of a new approach" to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, which "not only calls out injustice and suffering but acts".

The announcement prompted a furious reaction from Israel.

Sebagaimana diketahui, israel has built about 160 settlements housing 700,000 jews since it occupied the west bank and east jerusalem during the 1967 middle east war. An estimated 3. 3 million Palestinians live alongside them.

There has been a surge in attacks by settlers on Palestinians and their property in the West Bank since the start of the Gaza war, which was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023.

#965. Chris Minns’ backflips are adding up. Is he ‘clearing the runway’ or panicking?

📅 17 Nov 2026

Chris Minns’ backflips are adding up. Is he ‘clearing the runway’ or panicking?

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/nov/18/chris-minns-labor-backflips-are-adding-up-is-he-clearing-the-runway-or-panicking-nsw-state-election

From train timetables to coffee cups and property underquoting, the NSW premier is making policy reversals well ahead of the March election.

Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast.

Diungkapkan bahwa if recent coverage is to be believed, the new south wales premier, chris minns, is a talented gymnast. A last-minute intervention by the premier on Monday afternoon, the day before a suite of reforms on underquoting were due to take effect, marks a quadruple or quintuple policy “backflip” by Minns in recent weeks, depending on who you ask.

The laws banning real estate agents from lowering the advertised price of a property beneath a previously rejected written offer have been shelved for up to a year, after the premier flagged on Monday morning he had received concerns from estate agents in his own electorate about their effect amid a housing market downturn.

The NSW opposition leader, Kellie Sloane, said the move was “government by 2GB”, referencing the Sydney talkback radio station which had also raised the issue on Monday morning.

“But this isn’t the first time” she told presenter Ben Fordham on Tuesday.

First, the government backed down last month from implementing changes to several local and regional rail line timetables after criticism from commuters.

Next, after a social media post by Sloane, it changed gender-neutral language of “carer” and “lactating parents” in a new parliamentary breastfeeding policy to reflect what Minns said was “commonsense language like ‘mother’ and ‘breastfeeding’”.

After the Daily Telegraph ran a “Nup to the Cup” campaign against plastics legislation, which included requiring cafes to offer dine-in customers mugs and glasses instead of takeaway cups, the government dropped the changes, which would not have been implemented until 2028.

Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here.

This weekend, it made an election promise of a two-year funding guarantee for community preschools after the opposition had warned the sector was facing a $150m annual cut from January.

But Eamonn Fitzpatrick, a lobbyist and former communications and campaign advisor to federal and state Labor governments, says the reversals are more about “clear air” than pre-campaign jitters as the government enters the final sitting days before the March election.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “that is the job of this final sitting week, let’s not forget you go into summer. It’s a dead period,” says Fitzpatrick, who worked alongside Minns in the office of former Labor premier Morris Iemma.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “what you’re seeking to do, actually, in either putting things on hold, changing your minds, revising policies, you’re actually just minimising distraction … clearing the runway. ”.

Fitzpatrick says interventions are part of Minns’ brand as a strong leader, but insists his style is no more top-down than previous premiers.

Minns has consistently polled ahead of Sloane as preferred premier but he has made no secret about the threat from One Nation, whom he and his ministers have started to refer to as the state’s unofficial opposition.

Peter Lewis, the non-executive chair of strategic communications company Essential, which undertook qualitative research for Labor in the last federal election, said recent polling suggested voting intention in November in NSW was at 27% for Labor, 26% for One Nation and 23% for the Coalition.

Lewis says he thinks the threat of One Nation in NSW is being “used to push the political debate towards the right and could be used as an excuse for the government not to embrace more progressive policies”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i wonder if there is a bit of a mistake in that. One Nation voters are being driven by dissatisfaction with the status quo and so governments that are seen as actually addressing issues probably have a better case to answer. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, defending its underquoting backflip, labor has said it is protecting buyers from being shut out of sales at lower prices amid a downturn which has seen home values in sydney drop by 10. 1% from their 2026 peak, according to data from Cotality.

In question time, the fair trading minister, Anoulack Chanthivong, whose department was responsible for the reforms and who has now been overruled for a third time by Minns on policy, said the market had changed and the government had responded.

Both he and Minns pointed out that Sloane and the opposition had supported the underquoting laws at the time, which were conceived for a “rising hot market”.

But, Lewis says “there is a cost in being seen to change a position” – and points to Peter Dutton’s 2025 federal election campaign as an example.

“Maybe Minns has done this early enough in the cycle for it not to be an issue, but as you get close to the election it changes, particularly when they’re walking back commitments that have been made to benefit people.

Penry Buckley is Guardian Australia’s NSW state reporter.

#966. Carney eyes 'other options' for embattled Canadian auto sector on China trip

📅 17 Nov 2026

Carney eyes 'other options' for embattled Canadian auto sector on China trip

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cq98xlz09ye0o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Carney eyes 'other options' for embattled Canadian auto sector on China trip.

The plight of Canada's car industry has become one of the clearest stress tests of Ottawa's effort to weather US tariffs and chart a path forward.

The past year and a half has been tough on the sector since US President Donald Trump imposed a 25% tariff on non-American-made vehicles, upending decades of free trade and automotive integration with Canada.

Now Prime Minister Mark Carney has signalled that he is looking to China, where he is on a visit for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit (Apec), as part of the solution.

But that avenue is not without controversy, and is once again drawing the ire of those close to Trump.

While in Cambodia earlier this week, Carney told reporters that Canada could turn to European and Asian carmakers to save its auto manufacturing sector if a trade deal with the US could not be reached.

Diungkapkan bahwa "look - great auto workers, important market, real assets in canada," he said. "If they're not fully utilised in a North American context, that provides other opportunities.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "canada's going to move forward either way. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, he went on to meet chinese president xi jinping in china on tuesday for their second head-to-head in less than a year. The two talked afterwards of the importance of developing their relations, and Carney said they had agreed to further tariff cuts.

Neither side mentioned vehicles specifically, though analysts suggest the issue will have been prominent in their minds.

Carney and Xi met on Tuesday to discuss cooperation and trade ahead of this week's Apec summit.

In January, Carney said that opening the door to China's electric vehicles, external (EV) could result in investment into Canadian-owned companies and the creation of manufacturing jobs in the sector.

American tariffs on imports of Canadian-made vehicles have led to thousands of job losses in Canada and anxiety over the future, as 90% of cars made in Canada are shipped to and sold in the US.

Berdasarkan laporan, at the same time, china has been eyeing canada as a potential entry-point to the north american ev market. Earlier this year, Canada announced that it would let in 49,000 EVs from China at a low tariff rate, with plans to raise that quota gradually to 70,000 by 2030.

The move was a significant break from the US, which has tariffed Chinese EVs heavily since the presidency of Joe Biden to protect domestic manufacturing.

Chinese EV manufacturers like BYD and Chery have already been lobbying the Canadian government for access.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, last week, canada's minister of international trade maninder sidhu toured a chery plant in china, external to discuss their potential entry to the canadian market. He told reporters afterwards that Canadians could expect to see affordable Chinese electric vehicles for sale in Canada by early 2027.

Canada's international trade minister Maninder Sidhu toured a Chinese EV plant earlier this month.

These moves come as the toll of US tariffs on Canada's auto sector has become harder to ignore.

Stellantis, an American car manufacturer that made models like the Dodge Challenger and the Chrysler 300 in Canada, recently announced it would sell its assembly plant in Brampton, Ontario - a move that Carney characterised as a "betrayal" of the plant's 2,200 workers.

The facility had been idle since 2023 for a planned retooling, but what was supposed to be a temporary shutdown became permanent after Trump's tariffs, leading the company to shift some manufacturing to Illinois in the US.

Stellantis said it would sell part of its Brampton plant to Roshel, a Canadian defence contractor and manufacturer of armoured vehicles.

The Canadian auto workers' union has expressed concern about the deal, calling it "underhanded" and warned that Canada would lose thousands of high-paying jobs as a result.

The deal has also led to speculation that a Chinese EV manufacturer could move into the facility, after Canadian media outlet CTV News reported, external, citing anonymous sources, that Stellantis was planning to lease back 25% of its plant to assemble "affordable" EVs.

Canada's deal with China signals it is serious about shift from US.

How China made electric vehicles mainstream.

There are prominent voices who oppose any such move, including within Canadian politics.

In a letter to Carney, Ontario Premier Doug Ford warned against opening the door for Chinese EV kits to be assembled in Canada at the Brampton plant.

China overwhelmingly builds its cars at home and ships them whole - or to be assembled in kits - overseas.

Lynette Ong, director of the China Governance Lab at the University of Toronto, said introducing Chinese auto manufacturing in Canada would be "controversial" due to fears that Canadian jobs could be lost and that the North American auto manufacturing industry could be eroded.

"We want to make sure they're hiring Canadian workers, that they are helping train Canadian workers and that they are transferring the technology over," Ong said.

She argued that Canada should also be wary of making itself vulnerable to potential security breaches and foreign interference from China, as well as risking the ire of the Trump administration.

Sebagaimana diketahui, that already appears to be happening. Peter Navarro, Trump's senior counsel for trade and manufacturing, warned Carney against cosying up to China in a post on X, external.

Diungkapkan bahwa "are u really threatening to play china off the u. ? This is offensive in the extreme," he wrote on Monday. S. "You should be far more worried China is going to eat Canada alive. ".

His comments were reposted by Pete Hoekstra, the US ambassador to Canada.

Berdasarkan laporan, canadians' views of china have grown more positive since trump's return to the white house. An Angus Reid poll released on Tuesday, external suggests many are open to Chinese investment in the EV sector, but with additional security or restrictions.

The Carney government has set terms for China's entry to Canada's auto market, including that any venture should be jointly-owned by a Canadian company, that it must follow Canadian labour standards and that the cars should be built using Canadian-made parts.

Ahead of his meeting with Xi on Tuesday, Carney also noted there are "clear guardrails" in how Canada deals with China, including barring work on sensitive matters like artificial intelligence and critical minerals.

Sebagaimana diketahui, canada has also eyed other partnerships. It is notably pursuing associate member status with the EU, and had signed a free trade deal with the Philippines earlier this week.

Just how much Canada is willing to embrace Chinese manufacturing, however, still depends on the outcome of ongoing US-Canada trade talks.

Berdasarkan laporan, progress has been made in negotiations with the us, carney recently said, but differences remain. It is unclear if Trump and Carney will speak on the sidelines of the Apec summit later this week.

#968. Australia’s gender pay gap falls below 20% for first time

📅 17 Nov 2026

Australia’s gender pay gap falls below 20% for first time

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/australia-gender-pay-gap-falls-below-20-percent-for-first-time

Men still dominate top-paid positions but businesses’ ‘deliberate’ decisions have narrowed gap, workplace gender equality agency report finds.

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.

Australian women earn 80c for every $1 men earn, on average, after Australia’s gender pay gap fell below 20% for the first time in 2025-26.

The workplace gender equality agency’s (WGEA) report on Wednesday showed men still dominated top-paid positions but businesses’ decisions have narrowed the gap.

WGEA chief Christine Castley said most Australian employers were ignoring backlash to diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) and improving their hiring and promotion to ensure women reached senior positions.

“Employers are actually thinking in a very deliberate way about what’s going on with workplace gender equality and then taking action,” Castley told Guardian Australia.

Berdasarkan laporan, the overall wgea pay gap was 19. 7% for the year, with the 2025-26 survey including federal government public sector employers for the first time.

Diungkapkan bahwa the figure has improved significantly in the last decade, from 26. 3% in 2015-16. Coverage has also increased, now covering more than 6m employees across 9,096 employers.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the private sector’s pay gap fell from 21. 1% last year to 20. 3% this year, as women accounted for a growing share of full-time management and leadership roles.

Bigger pay rises in female-dominated industries, including retail, aged care and childcare, also helped narrow the gap.

Sebagaimana diketahui, however, women-dominated industries and occupations were still typically paid less than those dominated by men. The average woman still earned $27,467 less per year than the average man, WGEA found.

Diungkapkan bahwa the survey accounted not only for wages but all earnings, including penalty rates, superannuation, bonuses and overtime. Average total remuneration in the survey was $125,568.

Diungkapkan bahwa the overall distribution of pay did not improve from 2024-25. Women make up about half of Australia’s workforce but men remained overrepresented in the highest-paid positions.

Berdasarkan laporan, every level of management was dominated by men, wgea found. The disparity was greatest at the chief executive level, where three in four CEOs were men and the gender pay gap widened to 27. 6%.

Sebagaimana diketahui, women accounted for just 36% of employees in the top pay quartile in the private sector. In the commonwealth public sector, women’s representation in the top quartile was 46% and the gender pay gap was just 7. 8%.

Promotion rates are similar between genders but women are less represented at higher levels, likely because they resign or take time off for care and domestic responsibilities, previous WGEA work has found.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, wednesday’s report found just 7% of manager roles are part-time, but 29% of women work part-time compared with 12% of men. WGEA called for workplaces to redesign roles to allow more part-time work.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in the financial services sector, which has the worst pay gap at 26. 7%, men would be more likely to be promoted or get bonuses as they took on more visible work, Castley said.

“[It’s] the person who can attend the client functions [and] can be available 24/7, the person who’s most visible to the leadership of the organisation, versus, perhaps, the person [doing] the work that’s behind the scenes,” Castley said.

Berdasarkan laporan, superannuation provider rest was an outlier in the finance industry. Its pay gap has fallen to 9. 4%, from 20. 1% in 2022.

Rest’s chief people officer, Amy Murrell, said the improvements had been helped by extending paid parental leave to all permanent staff, regardless of gender, time of arrival or primary or secondary carer classification.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “it’s not going to happen naturally,” murrell said. “I think you have to prioritise it for it to make sense. ”.

The firm had also increased representation after setting targets for at least 40% of employees to be women and 40% men at every level of its business, from its board to its investment team.

Castley said some Australian business leaders had taken on an “anti-DEI” narrative, amid global backlash to diversity, equity and inclusion measures, but most businesses were “getting on with the job”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, wgea asked businesses to set new targets for the first time in 2026. The most popular goals included improving gender balance at junior and managerial levels and consulting employees on gender equality efforts.

“These are the real issues that need to be tackled … and it’s actually very reassuring that those are the targets that employers have picked because it demonstrates, I think, a very real commitment to actually taking action,” Castley said.

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/nov/17/voldemort-gotham-city-greens-liberal-labor-one-nation-victorian-election-leaders-debate-ntwnfb

Ben Carroll, Jess Wilson, Ellen Sandell and Warren Pickering grilled by undecided voters – and each other – as state prepares to head to the polls.

For a brief moment on Tuesday night, the Victorian election looked like it might actually get interesting.

Berdasarkan laporan, two weeks into the offical campaign, with early voting opening on wednesday, the contest has been pretty short on excitement. The Labor government has continued to slide in the polls, while the Coalition opposition has largely been focused on not getting in its own way for long enough to cruise to victory.

Berdasarkan laporan, but the only debate of the campaign offered a welcome jolt of life. Dubbed the “People’s Forum” by hosts News24 and the Herald Sun, Tuesday evening’s showdown delivered a few moments of political theatre.

There was the moment the opposition leader, Jess Wilson, mocked the premier, Ben Carroll, for refusing to say the names of his predecessors, Daniel Andrews and Jacinta Allan, telling the Labor leader they’re “not Voldemort”.

“I can say their name just as you can say Jeff Kennett’s name,” Carroll responded.

“Jeff Kennett,” Wilson immediately retorted.

(For all the back-and-forth, Carroll never did say their names).

Diungkapkan bahwa or wilson’s apparent “julia gillard moment”, according to the herald sun, when she told carroll she “would not be lectured” by him on the costings of her policies. The premier had claimed the Liberal plans didn’t “stack up” and would require cuts to healthcare funding to pay down debt.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i like to see these scare campaigns that you run,” wilson said. “But Ben, I won’t be lectured by you or your government on costings when you have racked up $200bn worth of debt in this state. ”.

Then there was One Nation’s Victorian leader, Warren Pickering, who said the state resembled “Gotham City” because of rising crime and vowed to lock up more offenders – even if that meant sending them interstate.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i don’t give a damn if our prisons are full. They’re bringing in a supermax in New South Wales. You’ve broken the law. You’re going to jail. That’s where you’re bloody going,” he said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the only person to receive rousing applause was billy, a bearded schoolteacher who asked how the leaders planned to rebuild trust in politics when, as he put it: “nobody believes a word you say any more – and it’s fundamental. No fun, and mostly mental. ”.

But many of the night’s most memorable moments came courtesy of Greens leader, Ellen Sandell, whose late inclusion on the panel followed a stoush between Carroll and Wilson over whether Pickering should be invited.

“Having four of us on the stage tonight tells you everything about how politics is changing,” Sandell told the 100 undecided voters gathered at the Sofitel in Melbourne.

In her green blazer, and unmistakably in enemy territory, Sandell spoke authentically and was the only leader willing to take all three other parties to task: Labor over donations from the gambling industry, the Liberals over money from property developers and One Nation for its links to billionaire Gina Rinehart, who she said is “writing [their] policy”.

“If you’re wondering why you can’t afford your groceries or your rent or to buy a home, just look at who is funding these three other parties,” Sandell said.

When offered the opportunity to ask any other leader a question, Sandell asked Carroll how he can claim to fight for working people given cuts to the public sector and fights with health workers, teachers, council workers and firefighters over wages.

Berdasarkan laporan, she also engaged in a back and forth with wilson on several issues. She wants to rip up renewable energy. She wants to make sigfniciant cuts to public service. Asked whether she would possibly support the Liberals with confidence and supply in the event of a hung parliament, she said the Greens values were “quite far apart” from the Coalition’s: “Jess Wilson wants to rip up treaty. ”.

Wilson relied on an often repeated line that treaty “goes far further than what the voice [to parliament] ever did” and “undermines our parliament”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, sandell’s response: “you know that’s not true though, you can’t lie to the victorian people like that. ”.

The pair also clashed over pro-Palestinian protests in Melbourne’s CBD, with Sandell defending the right to “peaceful protest”.

“There is a very clear difference between antisemitism, which is unacceptable, and actually standing up and calling out war crimes that are happening by the government of Israel,” she said.

Berdasarkan laporan, wilson responded: “at these protests, we have seen people throw rocks at police officers. That is not a peaceful protest.

Sandell responded that existing laws already dealt with such incidents and argued that protest permits were not the answer.

Diungkapkan bahwa “politicians shouldn’t be the ones deciding who gets to protest,” she said. “That is an authoritarian government move, and we do not want that. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, pickering agreed with sandell and said politicians should not be deciding who gets to protest. He described One Nation as a “flagbearer” for the principles of democracy, including freedom of speech.

“I don’t necessarily think the permits are the way to go,” he said.

Berdasarkan laporan, wilson, who holds a comfortable lead in the polls, arguably had the most to lose from the debate but held her own. She largely avoided taking the bait from the other leaders, including Pickering, who during his turn to ask a question, tried to pressure her on the Coalition’s position on legislated net zero targets. Wilson stuck to her line that she was governed by “practicality” and “not ideology”.

She was less definitive on the Suburban Rail Loop, leaving open the possibility of scrapping the multibillion-dollar project once the Coalition had “visibility” of the contracts that have been signed.

Sebagaimana diketahui, asked by moderator kieran gilbert if the coalition would be willing to scrap the project and move on, wilson said: “that’s exactly what the review is for. ”.

Carroll, meanwhile, acknowledged that Labor had made mistakes during its 12 years in government but leaned heavily on its record, including 121 new schools, record NAPLAN results, the highest-paid teachers in the country and 17,000 nurses.

He also repeatedly referred to his decision to call a royal commission into allegations of corruption on government construction sites, describing it as one of the “hardest” things he had done.

Victoria will not get another leaders debate, after Carroll and Wilson failed to agree on terms for one on free-to-air television.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the audience members were polled as they left the sofitel, with 39% saying wilson had won the debate, followed by sandell on 25% and pickering on 16%. Just 13% were undecided at the end of the night and only 7% picked Carroll.

It appears no matter what the premier has to say, many Victorians have stopped listening.

Benita Kolovos is Guardian Australia’s Victorian state correspondent.

Pakistan's jailed former PM Imran Khan has appealed for urgent medical treatment, saying that his and his wife's health has been deteriorating.

"At 74, this unrelenting state is taking me to a place from which I may not return alive," the cricket star-turned-politician wrote in a letter published by his lawyer Salman Safdar.

Authorities in Islamabad maintain that Khan gets seen weekly by doctors, who have assessed that he is of "satisfactory" health.

Sebagaimana diketahui, khan, who faces more than 100 charges, has been in prison since august 2023. His wife Bushra Bibi was jailed along with him last year. Khan argues the cases against them, ranging from corruption to selling state gifts, are politically motivated.

Concerns over Khan's health have grown louder in the past year, with his family claiming he has lost most of his vision in his right eye after prison authorities failed to take action.

In his letter, Khan wrote that doctors have told him he is "highly vulnerable to a brain haemorrhage and cardiac arrest", and that his heart has already "suffered damage".

Sebagaimana diketahui, he also expressed concern for bushra bibi, whom he says suffered a detached retina in april and underwent surgery in secrecy. Khan said he fears she may lose her sight without further surgery.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "i have fought impossible legal battles in countless cases, and i have not stopped. But the system has stopped giving me justice," he wrote.

He said that he is being held in solitary confinement for up to 22 hours a day, where he is allowed neither visits by his family nor access to books and television, and that this has "taken a heavy toll" on his mental health.

He also claimed he had only seen his lawyers four times over the past year.

"I will only remain able to prove my innocence if I stay alive," he wrote.

Pakistan's parliamentary affairs minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry disputed these claims, saying Khan is "provided with all facilities in prison, including food of his own choosing".

"[He] is currently the most well-accommodated prisoner in Pakistan," the minister told reporters.

Authorities also say Khan was taken to a government-run hospital for an eye injection a week ago, where doctors deemed him "clinically stable".

Khan, who previously captained the Pakistan national cricket team, served as Pakistan's prime minister from 2018 to 2022.

His arrest in May 2023 sparked large-scale, violent protests by supporters, who ransacked the corps commander's residence in Lahore, smashing chandeliers and making away with furniture, paintings, and even peacocks, among other things.

At least eight people died in the protests and the army were called in to quell the violence.

Even behind bars, Khan remains a force in Pakistani politics.

Diungkapkan bahwa thousands of his supporters took to the streets in early october in a dayslong march, demanding his release. Authorities later ordered a crackdown on protests and imposed a state of emergency in Khan's party stronghold, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

Former international cricket captains have made several appeals in recent months to Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, insisting that Khan be given proper medical care.

Crossbenchers say the proposals could allow an ‘uncapped amount of money’ to flow to major parties through investment funds.

Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast.

Independent MPs say the government’s last-minute changes to controversial election funding laws would allow “an uncapped amount of money” to flow to the major parties through investment funds.

The amendments to the incoming federal electoral laws, which the government describes as “technical”, were introduced on Tuesday afternoon and come weeks before they are set to begin operating.

Diungkapkan bahwa from january, political parties and candidates will face campaign spending limits and donation caps during federal elections. Disclosure thresholds for political gifts and donations will be lowered to $5,000, and public funding per vote received will be increased from $3. 35 to $5.

But crossbenchers, who have long criticised the changes as favouring major parties and incumbents, say the latest tweaks further enable a lop-sided system.

They take particular aim at changes to allow political parties to invest and grow their funds without the interest earned contributing to donation ceilings.

“The amendments would enable a federal account holder to continue to grow their capital in a competitive manner and when the federal account funds are not required for incurring electoral expenditure,” the bill’s explanatory statement said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “this would allow federal account holders a greater degree of flexibility to administer their financial assets as they wish, protecting the right to take part in the conduct of public affairs directly. ”.

Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here.

Berdasarkan laporan, major parties often set up investment arms to grow funds in time for election cycles. The Cormack Foundation in Victoria serves as a major financial backer for the Liberals, while Labor Services and Holding and Pilliwinks are Labor’s and the Nationals’ equivalents, respectively.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in 2024-25, cormack donated $4. 7m to the Liberals, while Labor Services and Holding donated $598,00.

The federal government intends to pass the eleventh-hour changes in both houses this sitting fortnight ahead of the electoral laws coming into effect from 1 January 2027.

The independent ACT senator, David Pocock, said the bill continues the “major party stitch-up” and enabled “an uncapped amount of money to flow from their huge investment vehicles into their political accounts”.

“They like to talk about taking money out of politics but they legislate to drive more in,” Pocock said.

Diungkapkan bahwa “and while the government is prioritising law changes that will line their own coffers, they’re failing to bring forward the overdue measures to strengthen our democracy like banning deepfakes in elections or legislating truth in political advertising. ”.

Independent Curtin MP, Kate Chaney, said the changes didn’t address the bill’s serious flaws, and instead included tweaks to protect the existing investment vehicles and assets of major parties.

“Rather than being a new act of bastardry, this bill tweaks the act of bastardry performed on Australian democracy last year,” Chaney said.

Berdasarkan laporan, “we don’t let coles and woolies make laws about supermarket competition, but this is what it looks like when major parties make laws about who can compete with them. ”.

The electoral laws overhaul is already being challenged in the high court by former parliamentarians, Zoe Daniel and Rex Patrick, on three grounds.

The two are arguing the $800,000 cap on spending in each electorate impinges on the implied right of political communication.

While the expenditure cap applies to all candidates, the former independents argue newcomers are at disadvantage because major parties can also tap into their national campaign budget, which is capped at $90m.

They also argue two other changes unfairly disadvantage candidates without political parties: the $50,000 cap on individual donations, aimed at preventing Clive Palmer-sized campaigns, and rules stopping a single donor, such as Climate 200, from giving to more than five candidates in a state or territory.

Daniel and Patrick said the latest amendments were not about getting big money out of politics but stopping competitive newcomers.

“Rather than trying to make this flawed law fair, the government is doing the opposite by introducing amendments that would entrench access to wealth for the ALP and the LNP through the enormous investment vehicles that only they have,” they said.

Diungkapkan bahwa “no new entrant could amass such wealth under the new laws. They are pulling up the drawbridge, and it is transparent to anyone who cares to look.

Berdasarkan laporan, “it is classic cartel behaviour akin to coles and woolies land-banking to prevent competition from newcomers. ”.

#980. Body of Melbourne Cup horse found dumped in Sydney skip

📅 17 Nov 2026

Body of Melbourne Cup horse found dumped in Sydney skip

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ck1ewl2zjqgzo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

So You Are competing in the Melbourne Cup at Flemington Racecourse on 3 November.

The body of a top Australian racehorse has been found dumped in a skip bin, hours after its trainer revealed the horse had died from colic.

In a video shared online, only two weeks after So You Are raced in the Melbourne Cup, the deceased racehorse appeared to be lying in a large metal bin surrounded by other household rubbish in Sydney.

Trainer Bjorn Baker - who shared news of the horse's death from colic on Monday - has said he was "deeply distressed" by the video, and called for a "full explanation".

Racing NSW, the state's industry regulator, said a preliminary investigation had found the horse was later properly buried, but called the way its body was handled "completely unacceptable".

"Like everyone who has seen the footage, I am deeply distressed by the handling of So You Are's remains," Baker said in an statement shared online.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "he was a much-loved horse, and he deserved to be treated with dignity and respect after his death. ".

So You Are had a successful run during spring, winning four times at respected races including the Rosehill, Randwick and the Bendigo Cup.

The five-year-old recently finished eight in the Melbourne Cup, which was won by Point of Law, a horse previously owned by King Charles III.

The racehorse had received urgent treatment after a severe bout of colic, but was "unfortunately unable to be saved" and was euthanised under anaesthesia, Racing NSW said.

"So You Are was then transported for burial, and was being held temporarily, awaiting burial, when these images were recorded," it said.

Burial at a licensed landfill is typically recommended for animals that die from euthanasia due to the chemicals involved in the process, according to the racing body.

"That burial, however, should have occurred in a timely and respectful manner," it added.

In a statement, REC Equine Specialists - the hospital where the horse died - said a contractor had been hired to dispose of the So You Are's body.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "we did not carry out the burial ourselves, but we chose the provider and the arrangements, and we take full responsibility for that. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, "we have spoken with so you are's owners and trainer to apologise personally. ".

The company added that it had stopped using the contractor, and was reviewing its processes to make sure they known exactly how horses are handled after leaving their hospital.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "no owner should have to go through what so you are's connections have experienced this week. We will make sure it does not happen again. ".

Jowett's video appeared to be filmed at a public rubbish drop-off and land facility called Lucas Heights, in Sutherland Shire, south of Sydney.

The waste management company that runs the landfill site said So You Are's body had been moved to a skip bin in a permitted area, the Australian Broadcasting Corporation has reported.

#983. Mozambique opposition leader goes on trial for terrorism over deadly election protests

📅 17 Nov 2026

Mozambique opposition leader goes on trial for terrorism over deadly election protests

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/crq5vl1l6z2po?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

VenÃ¢ncio Mondlane was the runner-up in the 2024 presidential election.

Mozambique's opposition leader VenÃ¢ncio Mondlane has gone on trial for charges including incitement to terrorism and civil disobedience over deadly protests that followed the country's disputed 2024 elections.

He denies any wrongdoing, while his party has described the trial as politically motivated.

Ahead of Mondlane's appearance at the Supreme Court, security was tight, with authorities fearing a fresh wave of demonstrations by his supporters.

Police have appealed to citizens to follow the proceedings calmly and avoid actions that could threaten public order.

Mondlane arrived at the Supreme Court early on Tuesday with "great peace of mind", and was greeted by dozens of supporters.

"As you can see, I arrive calm, confident in the work of my legal team," he told journalists gathered outside court, amid a heavy police presence.

The trial is widely seen as a major test of Mozambique's political stability, nearly two years after disputed elections triggered some of the country's deadliest political unrest in decades.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "the trial is a real test for mozambique. It is is an important opportunity to demonstrate that the rule of law applies equally to everyone," said Luis Nhachote, a political analyst.

Mondlane, who challenged the presidential election results that declared Daniel Chapo of the ruling Frelimo party the winner, accused the authorities of widespread electoral fraud and called for nationwide protests and work stoppages.

Children shot dead after joining pot-banging protests in Mozambique.

The demonstrations continued for months, with rights groups accusing security forces of using excessive force against protesters.

Amnesty International, citing local civil society organisations, said more than 300 people were killed during the unrest, which was one of the country's worst post-election crises since independence.

Mozambican police put the death toll at 96, including 17 police officers.

European Union election observers also reported irregularities in the October 2024 vote, raising questions about the credibility of the results.

About 96 people died during the 2024 protests, according to police.

Prosecutors accuse Mondlane of encouraging demonstrations that disrupted public services, damaged property and threatened public security.

The charges include publicly glorifying criminal acts, incitement to collective disobedience, public instigation to commit crimes and offences linked to terrorism.

He could face up to 24 years in prison if convicted of the most serious charge.

Mondlane has rejected the accusations, insisting that his calls for demonstrations were aimed at demanding electoral transparency rather than encouraging violence.

A heavy deployment of police patrolled outside the Supreme Court and major streets in Maputo before the trial began.

In a statement issued on Monday, Mozambique's police appealed to citizens to "preserve tolerance and peaceful coexistence," adding that the right to demonstrate must be exercised strictly within the limits of the law.

Police also pledged to protect people and property while acting preventively and proportionately in accordance with the rule of law.

The court has only granted access to selected media organisations, sparking criticism from journalists and press freedom campaigners.

Court officials say the restrictions are necessary because of limited seating capacity in the courtroom, but critics argue they undermine transparency in a case of significant public interest.

Live broadcasts of the trial have been banned by the authorities, citing the fear of unrest.

The proceedings were expected to be heard by five judges, with witnesses called by both the prosecution and defence.

Political observers warn that the trial could reignite tensions in a country still struggling to recover from the violence and deep political divisions that followed the 2024 elections.

#988. Ukraine hails attack on vital Kerch bridge linking Russia and Crimea – Europe live

📅 17 Nov 2026

Ukraine hails attack on vital Kerch bridge linking Russia and Crimea – Europe live

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/nov/17/europe-ukraine-russia-crimea-kerch-bridge-attack-latest-news-updates

Zelenskyy praises ‘unprecedented attack’ as the Kremlin says bridge will be restored and will be ‘better than ever’ following strike.

Ukraine has critically damaged the Kerch bridge linking occupied Crimea with Russia in an overnight missile attack, in what Ukrainian officials say is a symbolic blow to the Kremlin.

Diungkapkan bahwa photos suggest that a 227-metre road arch span has fallen into the kerch strait, which connects the sea of azov with the black sea. The adjacent railway arch span has also sustained damage.

Diungkapkan bahwa ukrainian commentators say the massive steel arch cannot easily be replaced. The closure of the bridge means that traffic from Crimea can travel out of the peninsula only via a land corridor through occupied southern Ukraine, vulnerable to Ukrainian drones.

But Russian officials, quoted by Reuters, insisted that damage was only minor, and would be quick to sort out.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we have already gathered together the resources, designers, and builders ‌for repair work. We are sorting out logistics issues with the regional leadership,” Russian deputy prime minister Marat Khusnullin wrote on Telegram.

The bridge has in the past been a key supply route for Russian forces in Ukraine ​and is widely viewed as one of Russian president Vladimir Putin’s signature infrastructure projects.

The overnight strike followed ‌an intensification of ​Russian attacks in the ​past few months on bridges in Ukraine, including in the capital Kyiv.

Elsewhere, EU defence ministers are meeting in Brussels this morning for their latest discussions on Ukraine, followed by the Ukraine defence contact group.

Meanwhile, Germany’s chancellor Friedrich Merz is hosting Finland’s influential Alexander Stubb, two days before a major meeting of the coalition of the willing in Berlin.

Diungkapkan bahwa they will no doubt offer their reaction to today’s events in ukraine. I will bring you all the latest.

It’s Tuesday, 17 November 2026, it’s Jakub Krupa here, and this is Europe Live.

The Speaker of the Riksdag, Andreas Norlén, has said granted Ulf Kristersson’s request for more time for coalition talks (15:50) but that he wants to have clarity for the Swedish public by Christmas.

He said he would give parties one more week before he calls in the party leaders to decide what will happen next, but that he is determined to get to the end of this process soon so that by Christmas, Sweden will either have a new government or can prepare to go back to the polls with a second election.

Diungkapkan bahwa “my opinion is that this formation of government needs to come to an end in good time before christmas. I want that when the Swedish people celebrate Christmas they will know that Sweden either has a new government or are preparing themselves for another election. ”.

Sticking to the Swedish theme for a moment, Sweden’s defence minister Pål Jonson is the latest leader to stop by the journalists upon his arrival at today’s Ukraine Defence Contact Group in Brussels.

Diungkapkan bahwa in his comments, he said the meeting was “timely” as “the situation in ukraine is very challenging due to the fact that russia scaled up its production, both of ballistic missiles and also drones and glide bombs. ”.

Sweden will spend €4bn on helping Ukraine in 2027, Jonson said, noting cross-party backing across the parliament.

The minister also said that Sweden signed a letter of intent with Ukraine and the UK on the upcoming delivery of Gripen fighter jets for Ukraine.

Responding to questions from reporters, Jonson also said that the US undersecretary of defence Colby did not say “specific” information on the ongoing review of the US posture in Europe.

Berdasarkan laporan, “we are expecting it to come by the end of the year,” he said, adding that “the message is clear that europe is going to shouldering the lion’s share of conventional deterrence by 2028. ”.

Asked about the peace negotiations with Russia, the Swedish minister said he “has not seen any serious intent from the Russian side” on ending the war in Ukraine, stressing the need to keep supporting Kyiv in the meantime.

Jonson pointedly disagreed with Finland’s president, Alexander Stubb, who has repeatedly called for direct talks with Russia’s Vladimir Putin.

Diungkapkan bahwa asked if he sees any merit in that approach, he said:“not quite, because we do not see any serious commitment from the russian side to making any kind of compromise. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i know there’s all kinds of ideas drifting around that we should also have a discussion about the european security architecture. We do not welcome that. ”.

In other news, after 65 days without a government, Moderates leader Ulf Kristersson has asked for more time before parliament votes on whether they want him as prime minister.

Two weeks after he was given the task to attempt to form a “middle” coalition government by the Speaker, he said on Tuesday afternoon that he had requested a few more days.

The Speaker will hold a press conference later this afternoon when he is expected to respond to the former prime minister’s request.

His announcement comes after the Centre party leader, Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist, asked Kristersson and the Social Democrats leader Magdalena Andersson to present a “total package” for her party to choose between after talks between the left-leaning parties failed to produce a result.

Berdasarkan laporan, she has already said yes to andersson’s proposal of a coalition between the social democrats, green party and the centre party with cooperation with the left party. But the Left party has since continued to demand ministerial posts, which the Centre party has refused to accept.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “a majority government that cannot agree does not work, so nothing would get done. A few more days are needed before a vote takes place, so that the Centre party can have a complete basis for decision making which is needed to take a position. ”.

If the vote on Kristersson does not lead to a government, parties have just one more attempt before another election will be automatically called.

Kristersson said he does not want another election, but is “totally prepared” for one and already has a team of people preparing in case.

Berdasarkan laporan, meanwhile, ukraine’s volodymyr zelenskyy has said kyiv is working on a prisoner of war exchange with russia, “one of the most important agreements reached at the trilateral meeting in abu dhabi. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, he said ukraine would submit its proposals to the us, and could “deliver results in the coming weeks. ”.

“The timeline for implementing this agreement depends on how quickly the Russian side acts and on the American team’s communication with them,” he said.

Acting on the success of the humanitarian operations in Oleshky, Ukraine will also propose 10 other areas in the occupied parts of Kherson and Zaporizhzhia regions where similar actions are needed, Zelenskyy said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, arriving earlier, uk defence secretary wes streeting – who co-chairs the group - said the meeting comes “at a critical time for the war in ukraine” in what he argued “has been a terrible year for vladimir putin. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “russian casualties are [at] intolerably high levels as a direct result of his illegal and unnecessary war. The frontline isn’t moving, and Ukraine continues to show extraordinary resilience, courage and ingenuity. The economic costs on his economy and his own people have been catastrophic. And all of those lives and all of those, economic costs are coming with little to no gain. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, streeting said the meeting was focused on “mobilising the support for allies … to see ukraine through what will inevitably be a challenging winter. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “we’re all invested in the, attempt to negotiate a peace, and an end to this conflict that has to be on terms that are acceptable to ukraine. There can be no decision about Ukraine without Ukraine. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i think we’ve just seen another example of ukrainian ingenuity and ukraine’s absolute determination to defend itself against russian aggression. We stand with Ukraine, as they do that. ”.

Just like Rutte, he said he expected “a number” of announcements from Ukraine’s allies to help Kyiv in the coming months today.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, over in brussels, the ukraine defence contact group is about to meet for their latest talks on ukraine, including the us undersecretary of defence, elbridge a. Colby.

Diungkapkan bahwa nato’s secretary general mark rutte just arrived and chatted with reporters, telling them he is “relatively optimistic” ahead of the meeting, hoping for “some good announcements this afternoon. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “a lot of people are working very hard to bring peace to ukraine. But in the meantime, we have to make sure that they have what they need to get through winter, that they have what they need to be as strong as possible in the peace negotiations. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, on the kerch bridge, rutte said that “it’s important that ukraine defends itself. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, “and that means also hitting out at logistical nodes; it’s unavoidable that they do that. … We have to see, of course, what exactly happened but at least [from] the media footage, it seems that they were successful. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, rutte declined to comment on the peace negotiations, saying merely that “the us is playing a crucial part here. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa “i think it’s good that europe is now at a table – that was one of the outcomes of abu dhabi – i think the europeans have organised themselves now quite well. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa asked about the renewed starshield restrictions affecting ukraine, he said that “relevant parties are working very hard to make sure that as soon as possible, things are back to normal. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i know that anyone who can be helpful here is working on this. ”.

Back to Ukraine, the Swedish armed forces have taken to social media with a post that appears to mock Russia following the overnight attack on the Kerch Bridge.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “bridges enable military mobility. Equally important is the protection of these important land corridors to avoid having to take the long way round. A strategic necessity in all operations, creating the preconditions for logistics, reinforcement and sustainment of forces. ”.

North Macedonia’s security agency said it had foiled a “terrorist” assassination plot targeting a person in neighbouring Greece and dismantled an Iranian-linked network, AFP reported.

The National Security Agency (ANB) said it had busted “a wide network of proxy actors” linked to Iranian Edris Jahangiri Mavaneh, who was a “collaborator of the Iranian security and intelligence services”.

The network, “under the direct instructions of the Iranian national, undertook preparatory logistical activities to carry out a terrorist act/assassination against a person in Greece”, the agency said.

The operation was led in cooperation with the Greek national intelligence agency, it added.

Four suspects have been remanded in custody and another placed under house arrest, interior ministry official Aleksandar Janev told local media.

Meanwhile, Slovakia looks set to host another round of governmental ⁠consultations with Russia in 2027, foreign ministry documents scrutinised by Reuters showed, ⁠continuing the ⁠direct talks ​held last month for the first time since Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine.

The latest round of talks in October centred on discussions over Russian energy supplies, as ⁠well as culture and agriculture, and resumed ​a process suspended ‌in 2022, Reuters noted.

Slovakia’s prime minister Robert Fico is a fairly regular guest in Moscow and has often faced criticism for his pro-Russian views and repeated call for engagement with Moscow, despite the continuing invasion of Ukraine.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the 140 successful candidates from serbia’s student list have just been sworn in as mps at the national assembly in belgrade. They took the oath en masse, alongside members of the long-governing Serbian Progressive Party (SNS), which now finds itself in opposition for the first time in 14 years.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it follows the spectacular triumph of the student list in last month’s parliamentary elections. It comfortably defeated the SNS and its populist leader Aleksandar Vučić with a slate of candidates drawn from academia, athletics and economics, among other disciplines. None of the new MPs have any political experience.

Berdasarkan laporan, before the parliamentary session, student list supporters gathered outside the national assembly to cheer their representatives. Some of them performed the traditional kolo circle dance in celebration.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, meanwhile, there were jeers and whistles for arrivals from vučić’s party. A woman in the crowd poured a bottle of drinking yoghurt over the head of SNS candidate Lidija Vukićević, who said she felt “very bad” about the “primitivism and vulgarity” of Student List supporters.

Berdasarkan laporan, now the mps have been sworn in, the next task is to elect a parliamentary speaker. Whoever it is become the acting president of Serbia – because Vučić resigned as head of state to make his unsuccessful attempt to become prime minister.

Separately, former US president Joe Biden’s memoir, Promise Me, America, got published today, and it features some interesting lines on European affairs.

Just skimming the book for now, there is a bit of interesting background on the US response to the Russian invasion of Ukraine, and his secret visit to Kyiv in February 2023, as well as some of Biden’s unfiltered views on Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

Diungkapkan bahwa “but i must admit that it could be difficult to work with zelensky[y]. As brave as he and the Ukrainians were, they tested our patience on many occasions, demanding more armaments and money. ….

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, zelensky[y] could be moody and stubborn in our private conversations, and not as grateful as i would have expected. That could be frustrating, and I let him know that in no uncertain terms. Still, I refused to cut and run on the Ukrainians, who possessed a tremendous fighting spirit. And so did Zelensky[y]. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, in longer paragraphs on ukraine, biden writes he was “not blind to ukraine’s faults,” including “too much corruption” in the country’s judicial system, “where the rich and powerful were often free to buy their way out of accountability. ” “Ukraine would have to deal with these challenges if they wanted genuine integration with Europe and the West. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “but i had also seen the inner strength of the ukrainian people. If they could create a real democracy, with checks and balances, and fair elections, they could be a bulwark in the region, and an inspiration to peoples everywhere who were trying to claw their way out of a history of repression. They deserved a fighting chance. ”.

He also reveals that Donald Trump’s transition team after the 2024 elections wanted to get a permission to immediately start negotiations with Russia’s Vladimir Putin.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “during the transition, donald trump’s team had asked me to sign a letter empowering them to negotiate directly with putin, even before he took office. But I refused, unwilling to give them carte blanche for what I expected would be a kind of surrender, at Ukraine’s expense. ”.

Elsewhere, Biden also writes about his relationships with other leaders, including first foreign trip as president, to attend a G7 summit in Cornwall in 2021, noting his “bittersweet” feelings about “saying goodbye to an old friend, Angela Merkel,” while remarking how “impressed” he was by France’s Emmanuel Macron.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “[he] enthusiastically welcomed me into the group, but he asked hard questions about the rise of populism in the united states and how it might affect our long-term foreign policy. ”.

double quotation mark“When I said, ‘America’s back,’ he responded, ‘For how long?’”.

Diungkapkan bahwa writing about brexit, biden – who is of irish heritage on his mother’s side – expresses his frustration that the withdrawal from the eu was “threatening to undermine the good friday agreement of 1998, which had done so much good in bringing peace to northern ireland. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i also disapproved of brexit for its ultranationalist claims, and for making many promises that could not possibly be kept. I believed that the populist leaders and opportunists who backed Brexit had sold the British people a false bill of goods. ”.

Finland’s Alexander Stubb just addressed reporters in Berlin, after meeting Germany’s president Frank-Walter Steinmeier.

Stubb said the upcoming meeting of the coalition of the willing in Berlin on Thursday will be “very important” for the peace process.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i think it’s important that we get a structure and order in the negotiations, which basically means that there’s a clear timetable and that there’s a clear agenda. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa “the process is not going to be fast, but i think it should be well structured. You cannot speak about security without Europe. … I think the key here is that you cannot speak about territory without Ukraine. ”.

Stubb also explained his approach to engagement with Russia, rooted in three key issues: geography, diplomacy and military.

Diungkapkan bahwa “we need diplomacy. If you don’t talk about peace, you will never get peace. And in order to be able to get peace, you need to have dialogue and conversation and diplomacy. … We believe that in order for you to have a diplomatic say in the geographic situation that you are in, you have to back it up with something. ”.

In Kyiv, Russian ballistic missiles hit the Northern and Southern bridges – two major transport arteries that cross the Dnipro river.

Traffic was also suspended, causing gridlock early on Tuesday morning.

Russia’s army confirmed it had hit both bridges in a “massive attack” on Ukraine’s infrastructure, AFP reported.

Hungary will suspend rail traffic between Hungary and Ukraine for two days after a Russian drone struck just hundreds of meters from a railway station in western Ukraine, Hungarian prime minister Péter Magyar said.

“Recently, in Transcarpathia, a Russian drone struck 300 meters from the Mukachevo railway station.

The Hungarian crew of the train arriving from Hungary has been taken off the train.

Sebagaimana diketahui, we are suspending rail traffic between hungary and ukraine for today and tomorrow. ”.

Mukachevo is just across the Hungarian-Ukrainian border on the Ukrainian side, in an area inhabited by many ethnic Hungarians.

Hungary’s foreign minister Anita Orbán – no link with that Orbán – offered a bit more detail on the incident.

“At around 10am Hungarian time, Russian Geran-2 drones attacked Transcarpathia in three waves, primarily targeting the areas around Mukachevo and Uzhhorod.

Sebagaimana diketahui, ukrainian air defence forces responded effectively and shot down several of the attacking drones. Unfortunately, reports have also come in of multiple drone strikes, and the extent of the damage is currently being assessed.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this is not the first air attack against transcarpathia, and unfortunately it is unlikely to be the last. As Russia intensifies its attacks against Ukraine’s civilian population, we can expect further attacks of this kind against Transcarpathia as well, which until now has been relatively protected due to its geographical location.

Sebagaimana diketahui, ukraine’s civilian population is likely to face the most difficult winter of the war so far. The electricity grid and district heating systems are already in critical condition, particularly in Kyiv, Kharkiv and southern Ukraine. Russia is expected to intensify its attacks on power generation. Without electricity, water supplies in cities are also disrupted, millions of people are left without heating and power, and everyday life becomes increasingly difficult.

Berdasarkan laporan, i express my solidarity with the hungarian community in transcarpathia and with the entire ukrainian people, who have now had to face the horrors of war every day for nearly five years and are making extraordinary efforts simply to get through daily life. ”.

Let’s quickly go back to Ukraine for some news from Hungary’s prime minister, Péter Magyar.

Diungkapkan bahwa en el tribunal, sanon, vestido de traje y corbata, tiene el porte de un estadista. Pero los fiscales dicen que el haitiano-estadounidense de 67 años no era más que un estafador.

El elocuente residente de Florida está acusado de asociarse con una empresa de seguridad del sur de Florida y un escuadrón de sicarios compuesto por excomandos militares colombianos, quienes irrumpieron en la residencia presidencial de Moïse por la noche y le dispararon a quemarropa.
