Scammed migrant workers in UK to be considered possible victims of modern slavery

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/nov/17/scammed-migrant-workers-modern-slavery-home-office

Home Office changes policy after legal challenge over case of care worker scammed out of £22,000.

Migrant workers who are financially exploited can now be considered victims of modern slavery, after a legal challenge by a care worker who was scammed out of £22,000 to pay an agent for a job in the UK that did not exist.

Diungkapkan bahwa the care worker, ali*, from pakistan, was put in contact with an agent who told him he could organise a certificate of sponsorship for him to work in a uk care home. The agent was recommended by a friend who said he had been helped to secure a UK care job.

After handing over £22,000 and obtaining what he thought was a genuine certificate of sponsorship and a health and care skilled worker visa from the Home Office, he, his wife and their two young children moved to the UK in October 2023, excited about their new start.

He was keen to begin work as soon as possible as he had incurred heavy debts owed to family members from whom he had borrowed money to cover the cost of obtaining the documents.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, after he arrived in the uk, he kept calling the number he had been given to find out when he could start work. Eventually, he was told to go to a car showroom where he met a man who told him he had been scammed, as he had encountered others in a similar situation who had been sent to him too.

Sebagaimana diketahui, ali was devastated to learn he had lost all the money to a scam. The friend who had recommended the agent told him no job had been forthcoming for him either and so he had returned to Pakistan.

Diungkapkan bahwa “at that moment i felt like my whole life had just started to cave in,” ali said in a witness statement about his case. “We had invested everything we had and got into very heavy debts on the basis of this care worker job. I feel trapped by my debts and my family’s needs. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, he and his family were left destitute as a result of the scam. He said that as a result of the extreme stress, his hair turned white and he lost two stone in weight.

Berdasarkan laporan, luke piper, the head of immigration at work rights centre, said the charity had come across many other cases of migrant workers being subjected to financial exploitation. In a recent survey of more than 100 migrant care workers conducted by the charity, nearly three-quarters (74%) had experienced some form of financial exploitation.

“There is a worrying disconnect between those experiencing modern slavery and those getting help,” Piper said.

Diungkapkan bahwa ali was referred to the national referral mechanism for potential victims of trafficking and modern slavery and was initially found not to qualify as a potential victim of modern slavery. Supported by Work Rights Centre and Central England Law Centre, he challenged the home secretary for not including financial exploitation in the list of forms of modern slavery.

A judicial review was issued earlier this year and the decision was then reversed so that the Home Office will consider his case as one of potential human trafficking.

The Home Office has admitted in a court order that it previously “adopted an unduly narrow approach to the concept of exploitation” and said it would recognise financial exploitation as a form of modern slavery and trafficking.

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/17/chloe-moffat-policy-parents-treasury-worker-employers

Exclusive: Parents of Chloe Moffat urge employers to treat staff facing allegations in a kinder, more human way.

The parents of a Treasury worker who took her own life last year have launched a policy that directs employers to treat staff in a kinder and more commonsense way, and are asking HR departments across the country to adopt it.

Chloe Moffat’s parents also said the government department plans to plant a memorial garden in her honour at its Horse Guards Road offices.

Sebagaimana diketahui, moffat, a 26-year-old personal assistant, took her own life the day after she was called into a surprise disciplinary meeting about anonymous complaints alleging she had disclosed sensitive information at work, which she denied. A coroner found in August that the Treasury had “materially contributed” to her death.

Berdasarkan laporan, she had been convinced she would lose her job, the coroner heard, despite that not being a likely outcome. Moffat’s managers declined to allow her to bring a colleague to the “informal” meeting, did not give her any advance notice of it and refused to tell her whether she was likely to lose her job. They also removed access to her director’s email and changed her work responsibilities.

She had worked at the Treasury for almost three years, loved her job and had an exemplary employment record, the coroner heard.

Berdasarkan laporan, her parents, anne and david moffat, have been working with the global kindness institute, an ngo, to come up with “chloe’s policy” for hr departments to adopt to prevent such tragic incidents from happening in future. They are calling on organisations across the country to help develop and take on the policy.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “all we want is for nobody else to go through this,” anne moffat said. “If it goes through HR departments, even people considering making allegations, everybody can hopefully follow the Chloe policy and ask if this is really necessary.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “so many people are so policy driven and so into disciplinaries and making people accountable when it may not be necessary. People aren’t being treated in a commonsense, human way. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the policy calls on hr departments to consider the harms of disciplinary processes to those subjected to them, particularly when complaints are anonymous or unverified. It emphasises prioritising psychological safety and supporting those going through any disciplinary process, as well as minimising these processes in the first place by considering alternatives. It also calls on HR departments to provide clarity to those going through disciplinary processes, including letting people know if their role is safe.

Sebagaimana diketahui, david moffat said: “it’s a powerful leadership standard. If it raises the profile of the process that Chloe went through and avoids it happening to anyone else, that is good enough for me. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the treasury’s response to the coroner’s prevention of future deaths report acknowledged the department’s role in her death and committed to safeguards. A review of the civil service by the Cabinet Office found that the conditions to which Moffat was subjected had been replicated in other disciplinary meetings.

Anne Moffat said: “If you think about what happened to Chloe, if HR had thought ‘we know that she was very well thought of, nothing else had ever happened, these were the first ever allegations, they were anonymous,’ was this process necessary?”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the prevention of future deaths report issued by the coroner last month found there was still a risk at the civil service due to its disciplinary procedures. The civil service has put in place multiple safeguards to address these issues. This guidance includes allowing staff to have a supporter in disciplinary meetings, giving proper notice of any such meeting, and informing staff if a dismissal is not likely. The Treasury is also hiring an on-site occupational therapist to support staff wellbeing.

Berdasarkan laporan, the moffats met james bowler, the permanent secretary at the treasury, at the end of last month. David said: “We felt listened to, and as part of their response to the coroner as well we felt reassured that change was being implemented. It was a very emotional meeting. If the changes they have put forward to the coroner had already been in place, we certainly feel that Chloe would be with us today. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa anne added: “it is the first time we felt that the treasury had been compassionate to us and it wasn’t defensive or legal speak. They are looking at how to remember Chloe, and looking at the possibility of a memorial garden within the building and marking the garden with a plaque. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, david said: “we feel that chloe is finally being acknowledged and remembered. ”.

A Treasury spokesperson said: “The Treasury’s deepest sympathies continue to be with Chloe’s friends and family, and the department continues to mourn our colleague.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “our response to the coroner’s prevention of future deaths report sets out the action we have taken following this tragic case. An independent review found staff acted in good faith and with a duty of care throughout. ”.

#1027. Jensen Huang’s departure as Nvidia CEO becomes a political proxy war

Jensen Huang’s departure as Nvidia CEO becomes a political proxy war

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/global/2026/nov/16/jensen-huang-nvidia-ceo-china

Huang’s exit sharpens debate over US stance towards Beijing; and as outages increase, do you get the feeling nothing works?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this was originally published in techscape, a newsletter about how technology shapes our lives. Sign up to receive it here.

Berdasarkan laporan, hello, and welcome to techscape. I’m your host, Blake Montgomery, US tech editor at the Guardian, writing to you from a plane back from Web Summit in Lisbon. Today in tech, we’re discussing the implications of Jensen Huang’s ouster, and the recent spate of failures in critical infrastructure in everything from Microsoft Outlook accounts to air traffic control to copper wires in routers.

Berdasarkan laporan, the chief executive officer of what once was the most valuable company in the world resigned on thursday. It may cost the world economy much more. Jensen Huang’s departure from chipmaker Nvidia after news broke he had at least three affairs – one with an executive at the datacenter firm Megaspeed, whom US intelligence has investigated for spying for China; others with his own employees – has already cost his company hundreds of billions in stock market value. Nvidia is central to the AI boom both as chipmaker and lender.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, we’ll know more about the company’s path forward later on tuesday when it reports its quarterly earnings. Executives, especially interim CEO Colette Kress, will face investors’ questions about the post-Huang era.

Diungkapkan bahwa the scandal has highlighted divisions among two heavyweights within the trump administration, each fighting for the us to take their preferred stance toward china. The treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, is accusing the commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick, of failing to curb sales by Nvidia that contravened export controls.

Sebagaimana diketahui, here’s how the business of megaspeed worked, which is what the two secretaries are warring over. Megaspeed, where alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang worked, would buy Nvidia chips from its base in south-east Asia, installing them in datacenters in Singapore, Malaysia, and Indonesia. Nvidia is barred from selling advanced chips to China. From there, it would lease or sell them to Chinese clients.

Diungkapkan bahwa lutnick has pushed to allow more trade with china, particularly where his family business, cantor fitzgerald, is concerned. Bessent argues for a more hawkish posture and more restrictions.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the question is what will happen next. I think the scandal will result in harsher export controls on China, given that Megaspeed facilitated about $12bn in chip sales in contravention of US export controls. Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/17/business/economy/global-debt-economy-world-bank.html

Sebagaimana diketahui, the debt load of developing countries jumped to $9. 4 trillion as high interest rates and other global shocks batter their economies.

Patricia Cohen covers the global economy and reported this story from Bangkok and London.

It’s hard to find a government these days that is not struggling with crushing public debt.

Berdasarkan laporan, the financial problems of wealthier nations have been monopolizing the spotlight. The United States, Britain, France, Italy, China and Japan are all facing record or near-record debt levels. The fallout has been painfully visible in France, where anger at rising costs and crumbling public facilities and services helped provoke violent protests and a general strike in recent weeks.

But rich countries’ fiscal problems do not just pool at home; they trickle down to amplify the financial pressures on low and middle-income countries.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the result is that less-well off nations are borrowing more and paying more for their loans. Their combined debt surged last year to $9. 4 trillion, according to a World Bank report this month.

The poorest of the poor countries fare the worst: They are facing interest rates not seen since the late 1980s.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, many of the causes are beyond their control. A series of crises, beginning with the Covid-19 pandemic, and continuing with energy shocks, supply chain disruptions and rising prices stemming from the wars in Ukraine and Iran have strained national budgets and pumped up debts.

#1059. How the attack on Crimean Bridge unfolded

📅 17 Nov 2026

How the attack on Crimean Bridge unfolded

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/crz9dgz28zwdo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Footage shows Ukrainian missile approach Crimea bridge.

Stretching across the Kerch Strait in the Black Sea, the Crimean Bridge was always a symbol: for Russia, a prestige project cementing its claim to sovereign Ukrainian territory, and for Ukraine, a hated piece of infrastructure emblematic of Moscow's occupation of the Crimean Peninsula.

A key section of the double-arched, 12-mile-long bridge now lies on the seabed, brought down by an arsenal of Ukrainian long-range weaponry in a seven-stage operation culminating in a dramatic collapse.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov has said that the bridge "will be rebuilt, and it will be even better than before".

But eight years after its unveiling, the bridge has now become material proof of Kyiv's ability to pierce through Moscow's military defences to hit even its most treasured and protected structures.

The attack on the strategic Crimean Bridge was carried out gradually to cut across several layers of defence, Kyiv confirmed on Tuesday.

For several weeks Ukraine's Security Service and its General Staff gradually destroyed air defence systems, radars, electronic warfare assets, and other designated targets, President Volodymyr Zelensky said.

Berdasarkan laporan, a significant strike had already been reported on 16 november, when drones hit the bridge at night. Traffic was paused briefly then reinstated, and although the arch over the road section was visibly damaged, the structure remained standing.

But that hit turned out to have been only the penultimate stage of a complex attack.

In the early hours of 17 November, the final strikes dealt a fatal blow to the weakened arch structure.

One verified video - filmed from a camera on board a Ukrainian-made Flamingo missile - shows the weapon approaching the main span of the bridge and heading towards the steel arches, with the footage freezing just before impact.

The Flamingo had potentially been modified to be controlled remotely, which improved its accuracy enough to strike the bridge supports, munitions expert Justin Bronk, from the Royal United Services Institute said.

The missile's "very heavy warhead" made it "more suitable" for attacking the bridge's reinforced concrete spans and supports, Bronk added.

Zelensky later confirmed that several types of missiles and drones had been employed in the attack, which led the massive road arch - weighing thousands of tonnes and measuring about 227m in length - to collapse into the strait.

Daylight images taken from the shores of Crimea to the north show a section about 200m (660ft) long of the tarmac was too dragged below into the sea.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this is clearly critical damage to the crossing. Far from just being a decorative feature of the bridge, the arch played a structural role, transferring loads and supporting the span and helping to ensure the stability of the entire structure.

Diungkapkan bahwa the parallel arch supporting the railway section has remained standing, although it may also have been damaged. All traffic on the bridge was initially suspended, though trains were later allowed to resume running.

Diungkapkan bahwa but the damage to the bridge's main span is "catastrophic", colin capriani, a structural engineer from monash university in melbourne, australia, told bbc verify. It was "very hard to envisage" how the bridge could be rebuilt given it is clearly well within range of Ukrainian weaponry, Capriani added.

Major attacks in 2022 and 2023 had already caused serious damage to the road spans of the bridge, but the structure survived.

The difference this time is "the most critical and vulnerable part of the bridge has been hit", said David MacKenzie of engineering consultancy COWI, adding that "although the wreckage of the bridge can be cleared fairly quickly, reinstating full road traffic will take over a year".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, moscow uses crimea as a military base, with airbases, troop concentrations, training grounds and artillery stockpiles. From there it also carries out strikes on the rest of the country and resupplies its troops in southern Ukraine.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the attack comes after a summer of frequent strikes on crimea, dictated by ukraine's stated goal of cutting the peninsula off from russia. At the time, Kyiv vowed to turn the Crimean Peninsula "into an island".

Now - although it is too early to speak of a complete blockade of Crimea â the risk of a serious transport and logistics crisis has increased significantly.

Diungkapkan bahwa there is still a land corridor running through the occupied parts of the zaporizhzhia and kherson regions. However, Ukraine has been systematically striking transport routes across northern Crimea, as well as bridges and other crossings in the area around Chongar, which has already caused problems with the delivery of fuel and other supplies, including military cargo.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, moscow can also still utilise the ferry crossing across the kerch strait. It could partly compensate for the loss of the bridge, but its capacity is very limited - and anything on the Black Sea has become vulnerable to attack. Resupplying Crimea by sea is risky, as Ukrainian naval and aerial drones operate extensively in the area.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in addition, debris from the crimean bridge - particularly its enormous arch - may have blocked the shipping channel. This would make it harder for larger vessels to pass through and create further problems for ports in the Sea of Azov, including the occupied cities of Mariupol and Berdyansk.

Away from the operational value of the damage to the bridge, the symbolic significance remains.

Diungkapkan bahwa in 2018, putin triumphantly drove over the bridge representing the unification of russia and crimea in a russian-made truck. That section of the road now lies on the seabed.

Nearly five years since he launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Putin continues to wreak destruction on Ukraine's civilian population, but his most prized symbols of power are increasingly threatened by Kyiv's reach.

Jensen Huang and Nvidia's interim CEO, Colette Kress.

Diungkapkan bahwa in the company's first results since huang's dramatic exit, interim chief executive colette kress said it is "business as usual" and told investors: "we've got this. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, the company's quarterly sales doubled from a year earlier, reaching $115. 8bn (Â£86. 9bn), with shares in the company jumping by almost 4% in after-hours trading.

Diungkapkan bahwa she added that nvidia's leadership team has "stood up very strongly over the last week. working seamlessly in all of their departments and projects".

Sebagaimana diketahui, "our momentum is real. Our supply is growing. " Kress said before leaving the analyst call. "We've got this. Our customers and our partners are with us, and employees are committed. Our demand is accelerating. ".

The rise and fall of Jensen Huang - how the tech superstar became mired in scandal.

Jensen Huang says he would be 'honoured' to return as Nvidia CEO if board asked him.

St Kitts and Nevis to wind down citizenship-by-investment program after EU warns of end to visa-free access.

The decision by St Kitts and Nevis to end a lucrative programme offering citizenship to wealthy foreigners in exchange for investment threatens its economy and ability to support people in need, the premier of the island of Nevis has warned.

On Friday, Terrance Drew, the prime minister of the twin-island Caribbean nation, announced he would wind down the citizenship-by-investment (CBI) programme, after the European Union threatened to end visa-free access for St Kitts and Nevis.

Mark Brantley, the premier of Nevis, which has autonomous self-governance in some aspects, said he understood that the “country was given very little choice”, but did not “support the winding down of the program”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the 42-year-old cbi programme, which st kitts and nevis pioneered, allows wealthy foreigners to obtain citizenship and ultimately a passport by investing in infrastructure and other development projects. It has brought billions of dollars into the country and in some years accounted for the largest share of government revenue.

Diungkapkan bahwa in june, the european commission wrote to the five caribbean nations that currently operate cbi programmes: st kitts and nevis, dominica, antigua and barbuda, grenada and st lucia. It warned that countries may lose visa-free access to its 29-country Schengen area if they did not phase out CBI.

In Friday’s statement, Drew blamed concerns over the programme on mismanagement by previous administrations, including years of underselling to undercut other countries, a controversial prison project, weak escrow protections and investment sums not being properly paid into the citizenship unit.

Diungkapkan bahwa he said his government had led major reforms to the caribbean’s programmes with international partners, including the us treasury, but argued that continuing the programme risked visa-free travel to parts of europe and access to international banking. That could disrupt services allowing visitors to use overseas cards and families abroad to send money home.

Brantley, however, argued it was unfair for the EU to force St Kitts and Nevis to make a move without offering assistance to navigate the transition to other industries.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i have not yet seen from the eu any corresponding suggestions of assistance. And we have to realise that these citizenship-by-investment programs, not only in St Kitts and Nevis, but … smaller countries of the Caribbean, have contributed significantly to our gross domestic product and also to ensuring that our people … can get adequate access to water and to education, to healthcare and the like,” he said.

Brantley described the 1 June 2028 deadline the EU gave the country to phase out the lucrative programme as “frankly ludicrous”.

In his statement, Drew said the CBI programme “did a lot of good, but it also created a danger”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “when one source pays for half or more of everything, you are at its mercy. If it stops, everything stops. That is putting all of your eggs in one basket,” he added.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the prime minister said the government aimed to diversify its economy by strengthening tourism, yachting, and digital and creative industries, among others. He added that the sale of clean, geothermal energy was “at the heart of it” with drilling and exploration already planned.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i will not pretend that the road is easy. We will. Our plan is to make this change by growing our economy. Less CBI money means we must spend wisely and plan carefully. Raising taxes is not part of that plan,” Drew said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, antigua and barbuda has also expressed willingness to end the programme, though it is trying to negotiate a longer transition period. The five Caribbean governments have taken differing positions on the EU demand. According to local media, Grenada has indicated it wants its programme to continue until 2032, while Dominica and St Lucia have responded to Brussels without publicly committing to ending their programmes.

Indigenous Awá people of Amazon make contact with villagers and accept food to take back to territory.

About 20 Indigenous people emerged from isolation in Brazil’s Amazon rainforest, several organizations reported on Tuesday, raising the alarm about increased invasions into the tribe’s territory.

According to the NGO Survival International, members of the Awá people, who live in voluntary isolation, arrived on Monday in a village and made contact with a government team in a “historic encounter”.

The village they entered was within the Arariboia Indigenous territory in the north-eastern state of Maranhão, home to the Guajajara ethnic group.

Local community leaders said the villagers offered food to the group.

“They asked for yams and took them back into their forest,” said Survival International.

Diungkapkan bahwa the ngo explained that the awá typically subsist on hunting and gathering. However, they have faced increased incursions from illegal loggers, hunters and cattle ranchers.

A video of the encounter, filmed by Guajajara villagers and released by Survival International, shows a group of men, women and children at the edge of the forest.

Diungkapkan bahwa partially concealed by vegetation, they appear naked and are wearing necklaces. The men carry bows and long arrows.

“The physical condition of some members, particularly the children and the elderly, caused concern among the villagers, who noted clear signs of severe emaciation,” warned Coapima, an organization representing Indigenous groups in Maranhão.

Coapima highlighted the risks that unplanned contact poses to such groups, noting that they are particularly “exposed to diseases” against which they have little to no immunity.

Funai, the public agency responsible for Indigenous affairs, said in a statement sent to AFP that its technical teams were closely monitoring the situation and analyzing available information regarding the group’s health.

Survival International’s director, Caroline Pearce, said the group’s choice to emerge from isolation was a “troubling indication of how the continued invasion of uncontacted peoples’ forests puts otherwise self-sufficient Indigenous people in real danger”.

She said the Awá were being driven into “an ever-smaller island of the Amazon rainforest, surrounded by destruction”.

According to the NGO, about 196 “uncontacted” peoples and groups, who choose to live in isolation, have been identified across 10 countries.

More than 90% of such groups live in the Amazon rainforest, primarily in Brazil, with others in Indonesia and India.

The Forest Guardians – a group of Guajajara people who have battled illegal invasions for years – warned in comments in the Survival International statement that “climate change, fires, deforestation and land encroachment” were affecting the Awá’s way of life.

According to Survival International, many of the guardians have lost their lives trying to protect the territory they share with the Awá.

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cq7825234lgmo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Masha was in her kitchen when she heard the explosions blast through the city.

Berdasarkan laporan, the alarms warning of a ballistic missile threat went off just before 23:30 on monday in kyiv. Moments later came the boom of explosions.

Once again, the main bridges over the broad River Dnipro that cuts through the city were the target and this time the Russian missiles hit what they wanted.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, close to one end of the pivnichnyi (northern) bridge there is a large crater and in the pouring rain, water now rushes through it to the river below. Chunks of tarmac and metal are scattered around.

At its broadest point, the jagged hole is about eight metres wide.

Diungkapkan bahwa the crossing is closed to all traffic apart from the occasional fire engine or police car passing at high speed. By contrast, nearby roads are jammed with cars and trucks, forced to take long detours.

Berdasarkan laporan, anyone in a hurry to move around this city has to walk, or cycle, across the bridge, picking their way through the wreckage. In the miserable weather, that also means getting very wet.

Masha and her family moved to a flat next to the bridge because they had been living by a power plant that kept getting hit by Russian missiles.

Diungkapkan bahwa last night, she was in the kitchen of their new place when the russians struck the bridge. She thought her windows would be blown out of their frames by the explosions.

Diungkapkan bahwa "it was really scary. We had no idea they'd hit here so much. It's like we're cursed," Masha told me, describing grabbing her child and running into the corridor for protection.

But somehow, she still managed to sound cheerful.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "it's difficult, but we're used to it. And we try to take the positive from everything. Like: we survived today! So we can be happy about that. ".

The Northern Bridge crossing is closed to traffic while emergency response teams work to clear the debris.

From the damage, it looks like Russia targeted the same spot on the bridge with a volley of three missiles, aiming to keep the road closed for as long as possible.

Berdasarkan laporan, a major recovery operation is under way, with firefighters and engineers in fluorescent overalls working to evaluate the extent of the damage. But it looks like the disruption will continue for some time.

Further along the Dnipro River, the Pivdennyi (Southern) bridge was also hit on Monday night, with four missiles.

Berdasarkan laporan, the metro line across it was suspended for a while, although by mid-afternoon it had been restored. The mayor, Vitali Klitschko, said road transport in one direction was also being partially restored.

Diungkapkan bahwa on the pivnichnyi bridge, a man with a bag of tennis rackets on his back was gazing at the crater in front of him. He was heading home from the courts after he had travelled on foot to the left bank.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "it is upsetting," anatolii told us. "Then when you read the news of what our side did to the Crimea bridge, you do feel a bit better. ".

The main bridges over the River Dnipro - that cuts through Kyiv - were the target of Russian strikes.

That is because there was a battle of the bridges overnight.

Sebagaimana diketahui, ukrainian missiles hit the one russia had built to occupied crimea, and caused serious damage. That bridge is prized by Russian President Vladimir Putin personally, a symbol of his illegal 2014 takeover.

Ukrainians loathe it for the same reason and now a section has collapsed into the sea, along with its towering arch.

To many here, the timing feels significant: a blow to Putin's image, just as he wants to seem most powerful at this week's summit with the US and China.

But for Kyiv resident Antonina, today is just another challenge to overcome.

The 67-year-old, who we met pulling a shopping trolley through the debris on a bridge in the Ukrainian capital, was heading to see her son on the right bank, but taxi drivers were charging a fortune to go round, so she decided to walk.

Diungkapkan bahwa "it was a very scary night. We will get through this, but I just wish the war would end. It felt like something exploded right over my head. ".

A Russian military transport plane has crashed in Siberia, killing all 19 people on board, the country's defence ministry said, according to state-run media.

The An-12 aircraft went down during a "scheduled flight" in an "uninhabited area" in the Kemerovo region, the ministry said in a statement.

Seredyuk, who visited the crash site, said "a helicopter and medical facilities have been put on standby".

He also posted a video showing firefighters combing through what looked like the crash debris, with a number of ambulances also seen standing nearby.

Berdasarkan laporan, cctv footage posted on social media appeared to show the moment the plane crashed, with a lighted object falling through the sky in the distance. An explosion then lit up the sky, but the crash was too far away to be seen.

The BBC and Reuters news agency verified the time and date of the footage, while Reuters also verified the location based on features of the scenery that matched satellite imagery of the area.

It was not immediately known whether the crashed aircraft had any cargo on board.

An-12 planes are widely used by the Russian military to transport weaponry and personnel, and also for search and rescue operations.

#1081. US loses measles elimination status after 26 years amid record case numbers

📅 17 Nov 2026

US loses measles elimination status after 26 years amid record case numbers

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c977p71jx0xxo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

BBC's Madeline Halpert explains why the US lost its measles elimination status and what it could mean.

After more than two decades, the US has lost its measles-free status, following two years of record case numbers and deaths.

The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), a specialised service of the United Nations, determined the US has had uninterrupted transmission of the same strain of measles for more than 12 months.

Dr Jarbas Barbosa, director of PAHO, announced that Mexico and Bolivia have also lost their measles elimination status, attributing the resurgence in the region to persistent "gaps in vaccination".

The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said it was committed to "regaining measles elimination status" by expanding access to vaccines.

The US has seen 5,400 cases of measles this year alone, with 10 measles-related deaths, the most the country has seen since the 1990s.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the measles virus - with its signature blotchy red rash - used to infect millions of children a year before a vaccine was invented. The extremely contagious virus can be fatal, and some patients can experience long-term complications including encephalitis and immune amnesia, which resets the immune system, leaving it with only limited ability to respond to new infections.

The US recommends two measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) shots for children between ages one and six, which is 97% effective in protecting against the illness.

PAHO, a group within the World Health Organization, revoked the US's measles-elimination after determining that the virus had circulated nonstop for more than a year.

Berdasarkan laporan, "these figures are a serious warning for our region," paho's director barbosa said at a news conference on tuesday. "Measles is resurging globally amid persistent gaps in vaccination. ".

He added that Canada, which lost its status of having eliminated measles last year after seeing several large outbreaks, has made strides this year to interrupt transmission.

Daniel Salas, the executive manager of immunisations at PAHO, said that the US and others who lost elimination status would be required to submit corrective action plans outlining how they would attempt to improve vaccination rates.

Berdasarkan laporan, us health secretary robert f kennedy jr kennedy has attempted to make a series of sweeping changes to us vaccine recommendations and policies. The vaccine sceptic has also frequently cast doubt on the safety of MMR shot, as vaccination rates have declined across the US in recent years.

Kennedy has argued that the rise in measles cases started before he took the helm at HHS and that neighbouring countries have also seen more infections.

Responding to Tuesday's announcement, the CDC said the agency and its partners were "committed to stopping measles outbreaks, protecting Americans, and regaining measles elimination status".

"Together, we will encourage MMR vaccination, expand access to vaccines, and help communities close gaps in protection," the agency said.

CDC Director Erica Schwartz said the measles elimination designation was not what protected Americans.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "vaccination does," she said. "We know where transmission is occurring and we've invested $100 million in state and local health departments to reach those communities. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in a post on social media, kennedy said: "i continue to recommend mmr vaccination as the most effective way to prevent measles. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, "we are working to close vaccination gaps and rebuild public trust," he also said. "We will answer families' questions honestly about vaccine benefits and risks and work with trusted health care providers and community leaders to prevent measles, limit its spread, and support timely treatment. ".

The UK, Spain and Austria were among European nations that lost their measles-free status earlier this year, along with countries including Russia, Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan.

Nuwan Gunawardhana, an assistant professor of medicine with Columbia University Irving Medical Center, said the US losing its elimination status was "a huge leap backwards".

The US was the first country to eliminate measles in the Americas thanks to vaccination campaigns, noted William Moss, a paediatric infectious disease specialist at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health.

Dr Gunawardhana said it took massive efforts from public health officials and clinicians to build trust with patients to increase uptake of the MMR vaccine, leading to decades in the US with few infections and deaths.

But that trust has been steadily eroding since the Covid-19 pandemic, when Dr Gunawardhana said patients were confronted with misinformation about the safety of vaccines and lost even more trust in public health systems.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the vaccination rate for mmr across the us has fallen to 92. 4%, below the 95% level that provides herd immunity, which limits the spread of measles and protects those who cannot get vaccinated, including newborns.

Diungkapkan bahwa the vaccination rate for mmr across the us has fallen to 92. 4%, below the 95% level that provides herd immunity - which limits the spread of measles.

An outbreak in Pennsylvania has infected over 1,400 people - likely a large underestimate - and killed seven people, according to state officials.

Kennedy, the health secretary, has sparred with Pennsylvania officials over how it is counting the measles deaths, with CDC declining for now to record some of the deaths in its database.

Last year, the health secretary fired all the members of a top vaccine advisory panel and replaced them with his own appointees, some of whom were vaccine critics.

The panel recommended a number of vaccine changes - including no longer requiring the Hepatitis B vaccine for all newborns - but those recommendations were blocked by a federal judge.

President Donald Trump this year also cast doubt on the safety of the MMR vaccine, issuing an executive order for the shot to be split into three separate immunisations for measles, mumps and rubella, a move public health experts say is costly and could sow confusion about an already safe vaccine.

Doctors and public health officials say the misinformation from Kennedy and Trump has played a major role in falling vaccination rates.

Diungkapkan bahwa "it's confusing patients. It's confusing families," Dr Gunawardhana said. "We need a clear message from the top. ".

The federal government's vaccine manoeuvres have left public health officials and states to fill in the gaps, offering their own separate recommendations upholding decades-long practices.

In this US county, measles starts to feel like next pandemic.

In Amish country, nurses go door to door to stop deadly spread of measles.

An eight-year-old Haitian boy who was put into restraints and detained by immigration agents in San Diego on 4 November and transferred to a facility in Texas has been reunited with his family in California.

Berdasarkan laporan, “an eight-year-old child belongs in a classroom, on a playground, and surrounded by love – not in immigration detention. A spokesperson for the homeland security department said ICE took the child into custody “out of an abundance of caution and to ensure the child’s safety”.

American soldier arrested by UK police on suspicion of spying taken into US military custody

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6x284ez38vdo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Lt Col Brandon Carroll Tyner was arrested on 10 November.

A US Army officer arrested in the UK on suspicion of spying for Russia earlier this month has been taken into US military custody, British counter-terror police have said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the serviceman has been identified as lt col brandon carroll tyner, bbc news understands. The 41-year-old - who served in the US Army since 2008 - was arrested near Gloucester last week by British counter-terror police.

Tyner was based at Imjin Barracks in Innsworth, Gloucestershire, the headquarters of Nato's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps.

Diungkapkan bahwa counter terrorism policing said he is now in us custody over suspected national security and espionage allegations. At the time of his arrest, Russia said it had "nothing to do with it".

British police previously said he was being held in London after he was arrested under section one and section three of the National Security Act 2023, which relate to obtaining or disclosing protected information, and assisting a foreign intelligence service.

The day after Tyner's arrest on 10 November, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said he was "unaware" of what it was connected to.

"We have nothing to do with it, and it has nothing to do with us," he told reporters in Moscow.

The US serviceman is understood to have been based at Imjin Barracks in Gloucestershire.

Sebagaimana diketahui, on tuesday, assistant commissioner laurence taylor, head of counter terrorism policing, said: "subsequently, a decision was made to pass the investigation to them [their american partners] to progress. ".

"These are extremely serious allegations, and our collective response should send a strong message that we will act swiftly and robustly where we suspect this kind of espionage activity taking place," he added.

Tyner's arrest was the result of a long-running operation by MI5 - the UK's domestic intelligence and security agency - in collaboration with the FBI, the BBC understands.

He had previously served in Afghanistan and Iraq, but at the time of his arrest was working with NATO's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps near Gloucester - where he was said to be entrusted with sensitive information which would have been extremely damaging if leaked to Russia.

Berdasarkan laporan, detectives sent the crown prosecution service a file on the senior us soldier's alleged spying for consideration - allegations described by the head of counter terrorism policing as "extremely serious. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, but at that stage the attorney general's office in london got involved. As did the US authorities.

And now the decision has been taken that Lieutenant Colonel Tyner should be taken into custody by the US Military.

It means he will not stand trial in the UK, but under US Uniform Code of Military Justice.

FBI director Kash Patel said an army officer was in custody "as the result of an espionage investigation and the close cooperation" between the bureau, US Army and various UK partners.

"Together we worked to identify a potential threat to national security and take swift action," he said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "this fbi has zero tolerance for anyone who betrays their oath to the united states or puts our national security at risk. ".

US Brig Gen Sean Stinchon said the case should serve as a "stark warning to any service member suspected of violating the oath" they all take.

"Whenever we suspect somebody of betraying the trust of their fellow soldiers and jeopardising our collective defence, we will identify you, and we will ensure justice is served," he added.

The Costa Rican journalist Camilo Rodríguez, who gained prominence for publishing allegations against ⁠suspected drug traffickers and politicians, was shot dead on Monday, authorities said.

The first known killing of a journalist ⁠in Costa Rica in ⁠25 years, ​Rodriguez’s death comes as the country grapples with a surge in drug violence driven by international trafficking groups, despite long ⁠being regarded as one of Central America’s most peaceful and stable democracies.

Diungkapkan bahwa rodriguez, 51, was attacked at about 3. 20pm local ⁠time amid heavy traffic on a main highway on the outskirts of the capital ​San José, the Red Cross ‌reported.

President Laura Fernández condemned ‌the attack in a video message.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i am filled with indignation and outrage over ‌the cowardly murder of communicator camilo rodríguez. Regardless of the content of his communications, what happened today in our country is a stain on freedom of expression,” Fernández said.

Berdasarkan laporan, the attorney general, carlo díaz, told the local news outlet extra noticias that investigators found multiple bullet impacts and a crime scene resembling a contract ‌killing, probably linked to the allegations rodríguez had published. He gave no further evidence and did not name suspects.

“We know he ​was a communicator who publicly identified people for alleged links to drug trafficking,” Díaz said, adding that Rodríguez had previously reported threats but had declined protection.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “silencing someone who reports on drug trafficking or corruption, in this case a communicator, is a ⁠signal we cannot tolerate in a democratic society. “.

Díaz pledged efforts to ​hold those responsible ​for the murder accountable.

The last such ​attack on a media worker happened in July 2001 when the radio ​producer Parmenio ‌Medina was gunned ​down on a ​Santo Domingo highway, in roughly the same area as Rodríguez’s attack took place.

Costa Rica’s homicide rate doubled between 2013 and 2023 and has only eased slightly since then.

William and Kate celebrate Earthshot Prize winners in Mumbai

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cqlykve012d1o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Watch: William and Catherine walk green carpet in Mumbai for Earthshot Prize.

The Prince and Princess of Wales have said environmental innovators are changing the lives of future generations as they celebrated this year's winners of the Earthshot Prize.

Five award-winners were named at a ceremony in Mumbai, India, and will each receive Â£1m to scale up their projects.

One of the winners was a country - with Bhutan being recognised for its environmental policies that help to safeguard water supplies for nearly a fifth of the world's population.

Indian cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar, actor Rami Malek and Bollywood stars Alia Bhatt and Sonam Kapoor were among those who attended the ceremony, which saw performances from Take That and Bridgerton's Simone Ashley.

The annual event, founded by Prince William and now in its sixth year, was hosted by Karan Johar, presenter of The Traitors India and one of the country's most well-known film makers.

Berdasarkan laporan, prince william was joined by catherine at the ceremony as the royal couple continued their first official overseas trip together in four years. Catherine's cancer treatment has limited the amount she has travelled internationally.

They arrived on the event's green carpet wearing outfits celebrating Indian fashion.

Prince William wore a bespoke Bandhgala, a classic Indian formal jacket, while Catherine was dressed in an Anarkali dress by Mahima Mahajan made from handwoven silk Georgette with traditional Banarasi gold detailing.

During his speech, Prince William said this decade was the moment when positive change becomes irreversible" and remarked that history was "not written by challenges alone", but also by those who rose to meet them.

He added that "around the world, we are witnessing human ingenuity on a remarkable scale".

Separately, Catherine highlighted the "hope" represented by entrepreneurs, organisations and scientists tackling the environmental crisis.

The princess, who presented an award, also said: "Just as the natural world finds ways to adapt and flourish, so too can we, when we nurture new ideas and give them the opportunity to grow.

Diungkapkan bahwa "the people we're celebrating tonight are a huge part of that story. Their work will inspire and create seismic change that will improve lives for generations to come. ".

William and Catherine talk with guests during the awards ceremony in Mumbai.

The royal couple also spoke to those performing, which included Take That.

There are five Earthshots, or goals, for which an award is given: Protect and Restore Nature; Clean Our Air; Revive Our Oceans; Build a Waste-Free World; and Fix Our Climate.

Five winners were chosen from a list of 15 finalists who attended Tuesday's awards ceremony.

Sebagaimana diketahui, protect and restore nature: bhutan, the country that helps to protect the water security of 1. 6 billion people across South Asia and has a national nature coalition that aims to revive forests and rivers by restoring 50,000 hectares of damaged land.

Build a Waste-Free World: PFAS-Free France, a national campaign that helped secure landmark legislation banning 'forever chemicals' in France by 2030, and hopes to extend the ban to more major countries.

Revive Our Oceans: Niue Ocean Wide Trust, the Pacific island's scheme that has safeguarded marine life by investing in conservation to fund the long-term protection of its vast waters.

Clean Our Air: Mahindra Last Mile Mobility, a scheme rolling out up to one million electric rickshaws across India with the aim to drasitically cut one of the world's largest sources of on-road air pollution.

Fix Our Climate: Ãrsted, a global energy company that has cut its direct carbon emissions by more than 98% by transforming from being highly coal-intensive to a leader in offshore wind.

Indian actor Sonam Kapoor was among the famous guests invited to attend the annual awards night.

Indian cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar (right) also appeared alongside his wife Anjali (second right), daughter Sara (second left) and daughter-in-law Saaniya (left).

The Earthshot prize, first held in 2020, was inspired by former US President John F Kennedy's Moonshot project, which challenged scientists to get astronauts to the Moon and back safely.

Tuesday's event also saw appearances on stage from Earthshot ambassadors Robert Irwin, the Australian conservationist, and Nomzamo Mbatha, the South African actor.

As well as Take That, there were also musical performances from a number of Indian artists including Shreya Ghoshal, composer and pianist Merlin D'Souza and all-female hip hop collective Wild Wild Women.

The dazzling awards night was brought to a close by musician and composer Shashwat Sachdev.

After driving an electric rickshaw, William said he would've liked a longer promenade so he could "see what the top speed was".

Earlier on Tuesday, William and Catherine drove in an electric rickshaw to meet the 15 finalists.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as william stepped from the vehicle, which is manufactured by prize winner mahindra last mile mobility and has a top speed of 55mph, he said: "it was quite good fun, really good fun. ".

The couple arrived in India on Monday for the three-day visit, which is expected to also include a meeting with India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday.

Their first engagement saw them play a game of street - or "gully" cricket - in Mumbai alongside Tendulkar.

US President Donald Trump has arrived in the Philippines' capital on the first leg of a trip to Asia, which will end in a meeting in China with its President Xi Jinping and his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a red carpet was rolled out for trump as he walked off air force one in manila. A band played one of his favourite songs, Y. C. M. A. , before he was whisked away by helicopter to a hotel.

Trump's first meeting at the Asean Summit was with US partners in the Quad - India's Narendra Modi, whom he described as a "very tough man", Japan's Sanae Takaichi, who "may be even tougher", and Australia's Anthony Albanese.

"Our countries are the four corners of the free, open, stable, prosperous Indo-Pacific," the US president said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "we have outstanding relationships and co-ordinate closely. my phone is always open," Trump added.

Many countries in South East Asia have been hit hard by Trump's tariffs and his war on Iran - but their exports to the US rose 30% last year thanks to the AI boom for which the region manufactures many of the components.

The US is hoping to draw more countries here into its "Pax Silica" tech and AI ecosystem, and away from China.

But China's huge influence in this region cannot easily be challenged, and certainly not in the few hours Trump is in the Philippines.

Later on Tuesday, Trump signed a trade deal with Thailand alongside the country's Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul.

The US is Thailand's largest export market, accounting for 24% of its total shipments this year.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, trump then joined south east asia leaders at a dinner, telling those gathered: "this is one of the world's most vibrant and productive regions filled with the tremendous potential. ".

After an overnight stay in Manila, the US president will fly to Shenzhen in China to attend a summit of Asia Pacific leaders and have nuclear talks with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.

Asked if he would also be open to a one-on-one meeting with Putin, Trump said: "If it's available, I would".

#1108. As Trump and Xi meet, China's AI dreams face an unexpected hurdle: the Nvidia spy scandal

📅 17 Nov 2026

As Trump and Xi meet, China's AI dreams face an unexpected hurdle: the Nvidia spy scandal

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c5vg23g92rj4o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Jensen Huang is out but his shadow looms over the upcoming meeting between US President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping this week.

For Beijing, the former Nvidia CEO's dramatic fall is a major challenge - and not just because of claims that a Chinese spy may have honey-trapped Huang, one of the artificial intelligence industry's most influential figures.

Rather, the allegations surrounding Huang and his affair with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang are turning into a new flashpoint in an already fragile US-China relationship.

US intelligence reports claim she had ties to Beijing's intelligence apparatus - in particular the Ministry of State Security, China's main civilian spy agency.

The claim remains unproven, but it has already reignited debate in Washington over exports of advanced chips to China and whether the Trump administration has been too willing to ease restrictions.

For years now, advanced computer chips have been a key battleground in the US-China rivalry because they are essential for AI, supercomputing and military technology.

Chinese officials are worried this scandal could strengthen voices in Washington who argue in favour of further limiting Chinese access to cutting-edge American tech.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, just this week, the trump administration introduced new export restrictions on chinese firms that access advanced us chips in third countries such as malaysia, thailand or brazil. They typically do this by renting computing power in data centres abroad to train their AI models. But some of the firms, like the one Alice Huang worked for, are also accused of smuggling chips to China, although they have denied this.

Diungkapkan bahwa until now, this controversy appeared to be a sideshow in us-china relations. But with Beijing calling the new rules "economic coercion" on the eve of Trump arriving in Shenzhen, there is a growing risk it could become something much bigger.

Watch: Jensen Huang speaks to the BBC's Faisal Islam in 2025.

Diungkapkan bahwa democrats, who will control congress come january, have made their position clear. Last Wednesday top Democrat Ted Lieu told Politico the Trump administration had been "1,000%" too deferential to Nvidia, putting national security at risk, while fellow Democrat Zoe Lofgren suggested Congress would now be more likely to restrict sales of AI chips to China.

The BBC has approached the White House for comment.

Beijing's foreign ministry had described the spy claims as a "smear against China".

"The US should stop fabricating so-called espionage narratives to find pretexts for imposing technological blockades," spokesperson Mao Ning said last week.

The ministry also seemed keen to keep the meeting on track, saying the two countries had kept "close communication regarding interactions between the two heads of state".

For the last year, Trump and Xi have been seeking to stabilise relations after a damaging tariff war that almost brought trade between the two countries to a standstill.

The Trump administration's decision to permit sales of advanced Nvidia H200 chips to China in late 2025 was seen as evidence that both sides were searching for areas of co-operation, even while competition intensified.

It was a rare move given Washington had spent years trying to limit China's access to the most advanced chips.

Berdasarkan laporan, many in the us have long viewed these chips as a national security issue, arguing they could strengthen china's military and surveillance capabilities. Jensen Huang, who rejects that claim, advocated lifting bans on the export of high-performing chips to China. Beijing argues the restrictions are an attempt to contain its rise.

History has taught Beijing and Washington that spy scandals rarely remain confined to the intelligence world.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, analysts in china already see echoes of an incident in 2023 when a suspected surveillance balloon drifted through the skies over the us before an american fighter jet shot it down. Beijing insisted it was a civilian meteorological airship that had strayed off course.

The suspected Chinese spy balloon was shot down days after it was spotted over the US.

But a planned trip by then US Secretary of State Antony Blinken was cancelled and communication between the two governments deteriorated sharply.

The incident showed how quickly a security dispute could overwhelm diplomatic efforts and push relations into a deep freeze.

"The mere passage of a balloon sent American public opinion and politicians into a state of high alert, as if a "Chinese threat" were looming directly overhead," said the state media outlet, the Global Times this week as it made a direct comparison with the Nvidia scandal.

"No-one on the US side has ever apologised or taken responsibility for the genuine damage this caused to US-China relations," it added.

The state-run outlet also questioned why the Nvidia story had emerged so soon after "the hard-won detente" between Beijing and Washington, following a meeting between the two countries' leaders in September.

"Is someone behind the scenes pushing an agenda and stirring up confrontation?" it asked.

Both Trump and Xi have significant incentives to keep talking.

Sebagaimana diketahui, china's economy remains under pressure and is increasingly reliant on exports. Xi needs trade to keep flowing and this meeting is a key stepping stone to replacing the current trade truce that is due to expire in January.

Meanwhile Trump has repeatedly touted his close relationship with Xi and argued that maintaining dialogue is essential to managing competition between the two powers.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the us president is in his last two years and faces an uphill struggle to pass domestic legislation after the midterms. To counter this, he could be looking for some foreign policy wins.

He may also hope for Xi's help to end the war in the Middle East.

Neither side will want to be discussing intelligence concerns and technology controls instead of trade, investment and economic co-operation.

The summit is also being carefully choreographed by Beijing to show off its technological prowess in Shenzhen - a deeply symbolic choice of city.

It's home to some of the country's biggest tech companies and has become a showcase for Beijing's ambitions in AI and advanced manufacturing.

Also, given Washington's tighter restrictions on advanced chips, Beijing has options for retaliation.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, one of its most powerful tools is its dominance of key rare earth minerals. China processes much of the world's supply for materials that are used in everything from electric vehicles and smartphones to military equipment.

Analysts have long warned that technological restrictions can trigger a cycle of retaliation in which each side reaches for its strongest economic leverage.

That would shift the current trend of US-China relations from engagement back towards mutual suspicion.

Actors, authors and musicians sign open letter urging Murray Watt to reject the fossil fuel company’s plan to drill for gas in Browse basin off Kimberley coast.

Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here.

More than 150 Australian artists, including Hugh Jackman, Rebel Wilson and Jessica Mauboy, have backed a Greenpeace-led campaign against Woodside Energy’s proposal to develop the Browse basin, about 300km off the Kimberley coast.

Sebagaimana diketahui, woodside, the country’s largest fossil fuel company, describes browse as “australia’s biggest undeveloped offshore gas resource”. The oil and gas giant is hoping to win federal government approval to drill more than 50 gas wells about 3km from the Scott Reef area, which is home to more than 1,500 species, including endangered pygmy blue whales.

Actors Jackman, Wilson, Richard Roxburgh and Mia Wasikowska are among prominent Australians who oppose the Browse development on the basis that the proposed gasfield could damage the unique reef ecosystem.

They join musicians Jimmy Barnes, Paul Kelly, Tame Impala’s Kevin Parker, Tina Arena, Jessica Mauboy, G Flip, Vance Joy, Missy Higgins and Baker Boy in signing an open letter calling on the federal environment minister, Murray Watt, not to approve the development.

The letter – which says the Browse project “would turn Scott Reef into an industrial gas zone with decades of deafening seismic blasting [and] carbon dumping beneath the ocean floor” – was also signed by authors JM Coetzee, Helen Garner, Anna Funder and Diana Reid.

Sign up to get climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s Clear Air column as a free newsletter.

“Drilling at Scott Reef could cause an oil spill up to 30 times bigger than the 2009 Montara disaster, polluting Scott Reef with oil condensate, impacting the Kimberley coastline and even reaching as far as Indonesia,” it continued.

The open letter comes after a supergroup of more than 20 Australian artists – including King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard, Barnes, John Butler and Montaigne – last Monday released If Not Now, a musical call to arms about the reef.

The song, a reimagining of King Gizzard’s 2020 track, If Not Now, Then When?, is a collaboration between Greenpeace Australia Pacific, Green Music Australia and p(doom) Records.

Browse, first proposed by Woodside in 2018, would see gas piped about 900km to its ageing North West Shelf gas export plant, which is adjacent to the world heritage-listed Murujuga rock art.

Last month, Guardian Australia revealed that WA’s independent environmental watchdog had sharply criticised the proposal, saying that plans to protect turtles and blue whales near Scott Reef would be ineffective.

A draft letter from the Environmental Protection Authority, written in 2023, advised that it may be impossible to reduce the risk of an oil spill to an acceptable level.

Greenpeace last month nominated Scott Reef for national heritage listing, based on its ecological and scientific values.

Sebagaimana diketahui, modelling by the institute for energy economics and financial analysis suggests that browse would generate up to 6. 9% and 3. 8m tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions yearly at peak production, accounting for between 2. 7% of Australia’s emissions in 2035.

“Browse gas is likely four times more expensive than existing domestic gas,” the institute found last year, adding that the project “is unlikely to be competitive either domestically or internationally, based on IEEFA cost estimates”.

Matt Roberts, executive director of the Conservation Council of Western Australia, earlier this month described Woodside’s proposal as “extremely concerning”.

Diungkapkan bahwa “at the end of the day, we don’t need browse gas. Western Australia has enough gas available to support us through the transition to a renewable future and regional demand for LNG is declining.

Berdasarkan laporan, “the federal and state governments have enough evidence to reject this disastrous proposal and save scott reef, and we expect them to do just that. ”.

A spokesperson for the national EPA has told Guardian Australia the development was being assessed under the national Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act, and the “decision clock” had been paused while the agency waited on “further technical advice”.

A Woodside spokesperson said the proposed development “remains subject to a detailed, public and transparent assessment by state and Commonwealth regulators”.

Feedback had helped reduce “the infrastructure footprint around environmentally sensitive areas like Scott Reef – which will not be built on, drilled or mined”, they said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “browse is a natural gas and condensate development, not an oil development. References to a potential ‘oil spill’ from Browse are inaccurate. ” The spokesperson added that the “longest credible duration of a potential well blowout, while still highly unlikely”, was around 12 hours.

#1119. David Jones: what went wrong and what happens next? Five takeaways from first creditors meeting

📅 17 Nov 2026

David Jones: what went wrong and what happens next? Five takeaways from first creditors meeting

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/17/david-jones-creditors-meeting-debt-administrators

Upmarket retailer, which recorded a net loss of $228m last financial year, has total debt over $400m including $11m owed to staff.

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.

Upmarket retailer David Jones owed hundreds of millions of dollars when it collapsed into administration, after accelerating financial losses and reputational damage threatened its ability to stock shelves for Christmas.

About 500 creditors attended its first meeting on Tuesday, where administrators McGrathNicol started to break down who is owed what, when those left out of pocket will know where they stand, and what ultimately went wrong.

David Jones collapsed early this month owing in excess of $400m to an assortment of creditors, including $180m of debts to trade creditors, mainly consisting of the brands that stocked its shelves.

There are also outstanding employee entitlements, such as annual and long-service leave, worth about $11m, and about $33m in unredeemed gift cards, which the retailer is still accepting.

The rest is owed to large secured creditors, led by the retailer’s main financier, Hilco, which has a controlling hand over the current process and even has its own representatives in the 19 stores marked for closure.

Taken together, the debts are well over $400m, but that total is almost certain to climb as landlords tally up their losses.

On top of unpaid rent up to the appointment of administrators, shopping centre owners will also claim for broken leases after the chain’s receivers moved to close half of its 38-store network.

What, if any, money suppliers get back hinges on whether a buyer steps in and how much they are willing to pay, or whether the chain ends up liquidated, as well as how much cash David Jones can bring in through the crucial Christmas trading period.

Because product suppliers sit near the bottom of the creditor priority list, they won’t receive any money until secured lenders and employees are paid out.

Given the size of the outstanding debts, and poor financial state of the department chain, many suppliers are bracing for a near total loss of outstanding amounts.

Shaun Fraser, a founding partner at McGrathNicol, told creditors there were “too many variables” to indicate how much, if any, suppliers would receive.

“We haven’t yet got to a point where we’re engaged enough with bidders to have a sense of what value might be there,” Fraser said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we haven’t reached a point in the sale process where people are talking value or price. ”.

Store closures mean at least 1,689 jobs will go, plus those from brands with in-store concessions, the Shop, Distributive and Allied Employees Association (SDA) said Tuesday.

Diungkapkan bahwa bernie smith, the sda national vice-president, said staff were stressed and did not know when they would be paid their entitlements. Only 170 staff were set to be redeployed, with offers to go out by Monday, he said.

Out-of-pocket suppliers are particularly frustrated, though the modern practice of holding meetings online kept any real anger contained behind muted microphones.

There were questions over whether there had been preferential treatment to some suppliers, and if the retailer had been trading insolvent before the appointment of administrators.

McGrathNicol said it would investigate when the company might have been insolvent, and if preferential payments were made.

One brand representative said they had also repeatedly asked for stock lists and weekly sales figures without response.

The administrators provided updated financials at the meeting that showed the poor state of affairs at David Jones.

The 188-year-old retailer recorded a net loss of $228m in 2025-26, before losing a further $69m in the first four months of the new financial year leading up to the administration.

Creditors were told that the funding pressures it was facing, coupled with reputational damage, was affecting its ability to get stock for the Christmas trading period.

David Jones ultimately got tipped into administration when negotiations with its main landlord, Westfield owner Scentre Group, broke down.

The retailer’s private equity owner, Anchorage Capital, wanted to radically reduce store numbers – something that is now happening during receivership – to rid the network of underperforming suburban stores.

The directors of David Jones listed several causes of the retailer’s problems, including everything from cost-of-living pressures and soft luxury demand to fierce online competition.

Fraser said there was also “clearly a business model problem” with the retailer.

Under a dual appointment, receivers FTI Consulting have taken day-to-day control of the business while administrators McGrathNicol hunt for a buyer, having called for “non-binding indicative offers” for the retailer by the end of the month.

That will trigger a process that could see formal bids lodged either late this year or early in 2027, giving some clarity to employees and suppliers ahead of the next creditors’ meeting, due by March.

The road ahead is, however, complicated by the breakdown in relations between Anchorage and the Westfield owner, which is threatening the retailer’s ability to operate at any of its complexes.

The Scentre Group chief executive, Elliott Rusanow, told Guardian Australia the landlord now had a “unique opportunity to facilitate the entry and growth of businesses that are more relevant to customers today and into the future”.

“That is the opportunity we will pursue at each of the 17 destinations with a David Jones store,” Rusanow said.

‘Heads should roll’: owner of Melbourne Cup horse found dumped in skip bin demands investigation

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/nov/18/stuart-ramsey-calls-for-investigation-so-you-are-melbourne-cup-horse-found-skip-bin-ntwnfb

Stuart Ramsey says it is a ‘bloody disgrace’ the gelding was left in the skip bin while awaiting burial.

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.

So You Are’s owner-breeder has demanded a full investigation after the Melbourne Cup runner’s body was found in a skip at a Sydney tip, insisting “heads have got to roll”.

Stuart Ramsey says it is a “bloody disgrace” the gelding was left in the skip bin while awaiting burial at Sydney’s Cleanaway Lucas Heights Resource Recovery Centre.

The grisly sight was uncovered by a Sydney man, with online footage outraging industry participants and anti-horse racing activists alike.

New South Wales premier Chris Minns said on Wednesday the incident “obviously needs to be investigated” but “we expect to get to the bottom of it”.

“We do need better ways of disposing of horses,” Minns said.

Bjorn Baker’s promising stayer took ill at a spelling farm after finishing eighth in Australia’s most famous race on 3 November.

He was rushed to the REC Equine Specialists veterinary clinic at Horsley Park in Sydney’s west after showing signs of colic on Monday morning.

Surgery could not save the horse and he was euthanised under anaesthesia.

Racing NSW said its ongoing investigations found So You Are was being held temporarily awaiting burial when the footage was recorded.

It is common practice for vets to dispose of equine remains at landfill sites licensed to deal with horse carcasses, and is recommended by the NSW Department of Primary Industries in most cases.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for safe disposal, the carcass should be covered during transportation and buried under at least two metres of soil and a safe distance from water sources. The drugs used for euthanasia are slow to break down and poisonous to other animals, and can persist in the tissue of the dead animal for years and leach into the surrounding soil.

Sebagaimana diketahui, while the equine veterinary clinic has apologised, renowned breeder ramsey of boutique hunter valley farm turangga stud, wants answers and accountability over the disposal of the five-year-old, who earned $1. 4m from eight career wins.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “there should be a full investigation. Heads have got to roll – simple as that,” Ramsey said.

Diungkapkan bahwa “he was more than just a racehorse. He brought our family together, and to think of the stress the family are under now because of this – it’s a bloody disgrace.

Diungkapkan bahwa “we took 30-odd people down to melbourne for the race. So You Are brought us all together, as only a horse can do.

REC’s managing partner, Jonathan Lumsden, said the centre had spoken with So You Are’s owners and trainers to apologise.

He pointed out the veterinary practice did not carry out the burial but took “full responsibility” for choosing the service provider and arrangements.

“He should have been promptly and respectfully buried,” Lumsden said in a statement.

Ramsey, who said he hadn’t been contacted by REC, isn’t satisfied with their explanation.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “so they should take responsibility. It wasn’t the contractor’s fault; it was their fault. They were in charge of the horse,” he said.

“They didn’t even give us the option of burying him up at Turangga … they should all be out – gone.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i don’t mean everyone, but the bosses and the people who’ve made the decisions. ”.

Ramsey declared racehorses among the best-looked-after animals in the world and spoke of his affinity for So You Are.

A review into a similar incident in New Zealand, where a horse’s body was dumped at a tip, led to the establishment of a dedicated equine crematorium run by a charitable trust, which opened in 2025.

The treatment of So You Are’s remains has sparked strong criticism from animal welfare groups.

“There is always the option to bury the horse or have the horse cremated,” the Coalition for the Protection of Racehorses campaign director, Elio Celotto, said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “however, it is more expedient to dump the horse at a local tip. This is business as usual for an industry where profit is always more important than sentiment. ”.

Victorian Animal Justice party MP Georgie Purcell said the tragic case should force the industry to confront serious questions about duty of care.

“The racing industry breeds these horses and profits from them but fails the most basic obligation to treat them with dignity after death,” she said.

Racing NSW said “appropriate action” would be taken if any wrongdoing was discovered in its ongoing investigation.

“Under NSW Department of Primary Industries guidelines, a licensed landfill is the preferred option for animals who have died via euthanasia due to the chemicals involved in the process,” it said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “that burial, however, should have occurred in a timely and respectful manner. ”.

Baker said he was also left deeply distressed by the handling of the much-loved horse’s remains, adding they deserved to be treated with dignity and respect.
