Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/australia-sanctions-construction-company-west-bank-settlement-expansion-ntwnfb

Foreign affairs minister Penny Wong says rapid expansion of settlements and settler violence are ‘extinguishing the possibility of a two-state solution’.

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.

Australia has announced another tranche of sanctions on individuals and organisations involved in “illegal settlement expansion and human rights abuses against Palestinians” in the West Bank.

In a statement, the foreign affairs minister, Penny Wong, said it was the first time Australian sanctions had targeted a construction company involved in the building of settlements.

The sanctions prohibit Australians and Australian businesses from trading with or providing financial or other support to three individuals and four organisations.

“We are taking these actions because the rapid expansion of settlements and settler violence are extinguishing the possibility of a two-state solution,” Wong’s statement said.

Diungkapkan bahwa “this includes the e1 settlement where demolitions and the displacement of palestinians have occurred in recent weeks. Israeli settlements in the West Bank are illegal under international law. ”.

Among those sanctioned is Daniella Weiss and her Israeli settler organisation, the Nachala movement, which the government said has provided support for outposts and settlements that have perpetrated serious human rights abuses.

Weiss is known as the “godmother” of the settler movement and was sanctioned by the UK in May 2025, shortly after she appeared on a Louis Theroux’s documentary The Settlers.

Prominent West Bank settler Eliav Libi has also been sanctioned, as well as the Eyal Hari Yehuda construction company which has helped develop settlements and outposts and demolished Palestinian structures in the West Bank.

Wong said the sanctioned individuals and organisations had “actively participated in the planning, coordination and establishment of new settlements, including raising funds, recruitment of volunteers and providing support to violent settlers”.

Speaking on ABC radio on Wednesday morning, Wong said Australia had been coordinating with the UK on the sanctions.

“We thought it was very important to work with the United Kingdom to have a coordinated set of sanctions ahead of those decisions.

Berdasarkan laporan, “we urge israel to desist from proceeding with this settlement, which renders likely unviable the prospect of a palestinian state. ”.

Wong said she had spoken to her Israeli counterpart, Gideon Sa’ar, on Tuesday night when she “outlined” Australia’s position.

Diungkapkan bahwa “we’ve made clear we will continue to take action in respect of those involved in the settlement enterprise. The settlement enterprise is violent. ”.

Wong had signalled further sanctions in September, after the government ruled out an import ban on trade from illegal settlements in the West Bank.

On Wednesday, the foreign affairs minister said the government was still considering further action, but provided no detail.

“We’ll continue to look at targeted measures we can take to push back against what the current Israeli government is doing,” Wong told journalists.

When asked whether Wong was concerned Israel would respond to Australia sanctions with countermeasures, the minister said it had in the past.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we’ve seen the israeli government take action against australia, including asking our diplomats to leave ramallah. We’ve also seen the caretaker prime minister, Netanyahu, be very public in his criticism of Australia.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “so obviously, there is a reaction to australia acting, but we think this is the right thing to do. ”.

The analysis by the Climate Change Committee (CCC) suggests the policy would blow a hole in the plan for achieving net zero carbon emissions by 2050 – prompting concerns that Andy Burnham’s government will have to slash the UK’s carbon emissions reduction targets, known as the carbon budgets.

Carmakers must sell a bigger proportion of electric cars each year under the rules, known as the zero emission vehicle (ZEV) mandate, or face fines of £12,000 per vehicle.

Such cuts would, he said, “put the government’s commitment to tackling climate change at risk, miss an opportunity to reduce costs for a typical household by about £800 a year, increase the UK’s exposure to volatile oil markets by up to 15m barrels of oil a year in 2030, and damage long-term competitiveness as our main export markets rapidly transition to electric vehicles”.

The idea did not come to fruition though, with other cabinet ministers mostly opposed.

Diungkapkan bahwa the source said it was not clear if the proposal was still being discussed. A government source strongly denied that it was under consideration.

Fears are growing that the US could impose sanctions on judges at the international court of justice, including this year’s Nobel peace prize winner, Navi Pillay, if the court rules on Thursday that the Myanmar government committed genocide against the Rohingya.

The ICJ has never found a state responsible for committing genocide, and a significant factor in previous cases has been how to prove “intent” in a crime defined as acts committed with the “intent to destroy, in whole or in part” a national, ethnical, racial or religious group.

Lawyers representing Rohingya survivors say patterns of behaviour by Myanmar’s military, including killing people as they fled, show clear attempts to destroy the group during assaults on Rakhine state in 2016 and 2017.

The Foundation for Defense of Democracies, an influential thinktank close to the White House, has predicted a genocide ruling will lead to the US imposing sanctions on the ICJ.

The US and Israel fear the final judgment may clarify how to establish a government’s intent to commit a genocide, and so set a precedent that makes it more likely the court will later rule that Israel committed genocide in Gaza.

Myanmar, which has denied carrying out a genocide, claims its actions targeted a military uprising by insurgents.

The ICJ, sometimes described as the UN’s top court, is responsible for settling interstate disputes, unlike the international criminal court (ICC), which prosecutes individuals accused of war crimes and other international crimes.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the us has already imposed crippling sanctions on judges at the icc after the court issued arrest warrants against the israeli prime minister, benjamin netanyahu. Berdasarkan laporan, the gambia, as a litigant, was entitled to appoint an ad hoc judge in the case against myanmar and chose the south african lawyer pillay, who in october was awarded the nobel peace prize. She is required to act as a jurist and not an advocate for the Gambia.

Mike Waltz, the US ambassador to the UN, has sent a warning shot to Pillay and the 15 ICJ judges, saying Washington “will not allow globalist, faux judges to weaponise the law against our troops”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, waltz asserted last month: “the icj ad hoc judge navi pillay is tipping the scales on the icj’s current proceedings on myanmar, intending to lower the legal threshold for proving genocide so that weakened and false standard can later be weaponised against american and allied soldiers whenever they raise a finger against terrorists that hide behind civilians. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, in remarks addressed to pillay, he said: “we see your agenda and we’ll be watching the icj’s handling of these proceedings very closely. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa in a speech last friday, the us secretary of state, marco rubio, said: “for this global elite, international law … is an instrument to advance their interests under the pretence of universal principles. ”.

He warned the ICC against quoting laws to “men with swords”.

In the Myanmar case, a 24-page submission jointly filed by the UK and five other mainly European states, argued that the ICJ, in judging intent to commit genocide, should examine a range of “facts and circumstances” assessed “comprehensively and holistically”.

It also stressed that genocide was not solely defined by killings, and that the treatment of children, gender-based violence and forced displacement were also relevant.

The US until recently had taken a relatively more benign view of The Hague-based ICJ, and under Antony Blinken as US secretary of state determined that Myanmar had committed genocide.

Watch: BBC correspondents discuss historic Trump, Xi and Putin meeting.

Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin met for the first time in more than a year on Wednesday, as they prepared for landmark talks in China with Xi Jinping.

The US president was greeted off his plane by the Chinese leader as he arrived in Shenzhen for a summit of Asia-Pacific leaders, which will culminate in a closely-watched meeting between the pair and the Russian president.

After a carefully choreographed handshake and hug between Trump and Xi on the tarmac, the US president later greeted and exchanged pleasantries with Putin ahead of a reception.

Trump and Putin are expected to hold one-on-one talks on the sidelines of the summit on Thursday, in which the war in Ukraine could be discussed.

However the main focus during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum (Apec) will be on the US-China-Russia talks on Thursday - the first time the trio of leaders have met together in person.

A full agenda has not been made public but there have been various hints about what could be discussed, including the wars in Ukraine and Iran, nuclear proliferation, trade tensions and developments in artificial intelligence.

After a warm reception from Xi, the leaders of the US and Russia shook hands ahead of a reception.

It was not clear on Wednesday what form separate Trump-Putin talks would take, though a Kremlin spokesperson indicated short informal talks may happen without large delegations in the room.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has raised fears of a plan to end the war being discussed in the absence of representatives from Kyiv or Europe.

Wednesday's handshake was the first in-person meeting between Trump and Putin since August 2025, when the Russian leader travelled to Alaska for talks on the Ukraine war which failed to deliver a breakthrough.

Xi's personal reception for Trump at the airport mimicked a similar move by the US president when the Chinese leader visited Washington in September, a gesture Xi described as "special".

In Shenzhen, a red carpet was rolled out in front of Air Force One for Trump, with a cheering crowd, honour guard, military flyover and flowers presentation all in place to welcome him.

Chinese state-run news agency Xinhua quoted Xi as saying he wanted to pursue a "constructive strategic and stable relationship based on respect, fairness, and equality".

Xi's greeting will be seen as a diplomatic gesture designed to begin the week's talks with his American counterpart on a cordial note.

A lavish welcome ceremony was laid on for Trump's arrival.

The south-east Chinese city the Apec summit is being held in is a booming area for manufacturing and advanced tech.

It comes against the backdrop of the ousting of Nvidia chief executing Jensen Huang, who admitted to having an affair with a woman suspected by US intelligence of spying for Beijing - a claim dismissed as a "smear" by China.

Trump has pursued warmer relations with China but the incident points to ongoing tensions between the two powers.

Several hours before Trump's arrival, Putin landed in Shenzhen and held around two hours of talks with Xi, with whom he has pressed for closer economic and defence relations.

Xi said both countries would "move forward steadily and boldly" and that the relationship was "stable as a mountain, unshaken by storms".

Sebagaimana diketahui, leaked documents raise questions about claims egypt met welfare targets to qualify for €2. 5bn in loans.

The European Commission has been accused of sugarcoating figures to enable it to release funds to Egypt under a landmark pact with the authoritarian government of Abdel Fatah al-Sisi.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the charge relates to a €7. 4bn deal promised by Ursula von der Leyen, the European Commission president, to al-Sisi on a high-profile visit to Cairo in 2024. The three-year “strategic and comprehensive partnership” was intended to bolster Egypt’s shaky economy, deter migrants from coming to Europe and shore up a region reeling from the 7 October attacks and Israel’s war on Gaza.

The disclosure raises broader questions about the EU-Egypt relationship, as Egyptian authorities face scrutiny over shrinking press freedom following the jailing and alleged torture of six journalists, the entire newsroom of Matsadaash, a factchecking and investigative platform, and the closure last month of one of the country’s last independent news outlets and conviction of its high-profile editor, Lina Attalah.

Attalah is appealing against that conviction and will be in court this week as she seeks to overturn other charges including “publishing false news”, for which she was sentenced to a year in prison in absentia without her knowledge.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the spotlight is on €5bn in eu “soft” loans to egypt – lending with easy repayment terms, known as macro-financial assistance, that is meant to be available only to countries that respect human rights and democracy. While the EU conditions on democracy and rights are vague, the loans impose much more specific requirements on Egypt to carry out economic reforms.

Sebagaimana diketahui, separate data sources – from leaked eu documents and deleted from an egyptian government website – raise questions about the european commission’s claims that egypt met targets linked to social welfare programmes, which enabled the eu to release €2. 5bn in assistance.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in confidential documents, the commission told eu lawmakers that egypt had “broadly fulfilled” and then “fulfilled” two separate targets to increase the numbers of poor people on social welfare programmes between 2024 and 2026. But data points to a net reduction of 85,734 households as the Egyptian government removed people from its welfare programmes rather than expanded coverage.

Diungkapkan bahwa if egypt had expanded the programmes in line with the eu’s apparent conditions – and not removed any households – about 245,000 households, equivalent to roughly 909,000 people, would be getting these benefits. (The Guardian used World Bank data to make this rough calculation).

Berdasarkan laporan, according to the leaked documents, the commission wanted egypt to “further expand cash transfer programmes”, but despite a net reduction in beneficiaries it gave the green light anyway to two separate “soft” loans totalling €2. 5bn.

In response to the Guardian’s findings, one of the European parliament’s leading spokespeople on EU-Egypt relations, the Dutch MEP Tineke Strik, said she was introducing a question to the European Commission demanding clarification.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “the finding by this investigation that the commission is seemingly sugarcoating egypt’s performance is worrying,” strik said. “From the beginning, the commission has used macro-financial assistance primarily as a tool to lure Egypt into migration cooperation, while considering formal conditions and its reporting obligations towards parliament as an inconvenient formality. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa under the plan, egypt has so far received €3. 5bn in soft loans in three instalments, with a final payment of €1. 5bn expected before the end of 2027.

The charge of sugarcoating figures relates to two social welfare programmes: the Takaful and Karama cash transfer programmes for poor and vulnerable households.

Berdasarkan laporan, the takaful (solidarity) programme gives poor families cash payments as long as recipients have regular health visits and good attendance at school. The Karama (Dignity) programme gives unconditional cash payments to people living with a disability, older people, orphans and widows.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one of the eu conditions for egypt to gain the first €1bn loan was to increase the number of takaful and karama beneficiary households by 100,000 to 4. 7 million.

In a leaked report to lawmakers in the EU council of ministers and the European parliament, the commission described that requirement as “broadly fulfilled”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the data in that report, however, reveals a net fall of 62,281 households during this period, owing to what the eu officials describe as “a multi-annual recertification process”. Some beneficiaries were added to the list but a larger number were removed because they were deemed ineligible.

Berdasarkan laporan, in order to achieve a later instalment of €1. 5bn, Egypt was required to “further expand” the programmes, adding 60,000 households to the Takaful and Karama beneficiaries list. A second leaked report to EU lawmakers shows that the commission concluded the target was “fulfilled” because 442,118 families were added to the list.

Berdasarkan laporan, on this occasion, the commission did not report on numbers removed. The EU announced the release of the €1. Figures from Egypt’s ministry of social solidarity, however, show a net reduction of 23,453 beneficiaries to the programmes in the 11 months until June 2026, the period leading up to the release of that payment. 5bn payment in July 2026.

The data has since been deleted from the Egyptian ministry website but the Guardian has seen screenshots and archived webpages.

During a period from 2024 to 26 when the EU required Egypt to add 160,000 households to the rolls of the Karama and Takaful programmes, there was a net decline of 85,734 households.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, timothy kaldas, the deputy director of the tahrir institute for middle east policy, said the commission had generally “done a poor job of leveraging the funds of european taxpayers to support genuine stabilisation” on the other side of the mediterranean. “The strategic interest of Europe is seeing a more economically stable Egypt with a population that is less precarious,” he said.

Berdasarkan laporan, sandra gómez lópez, a spanish socialist mep who recently visited cairo to assess human rights in egypt, said the data presented by the guardian raised important questions. “The commission must explain transparently why it considers these commitments to have been fulfilled and demonstrate that European funding is genuinely contributing to improving social protection for the Egyptian population,” she said.

She stressed that the EU should not withdraw support, “but neither can we allow the country’s strategic importance to lead us to lower our standards when it comes to human rights”.

For critics, the questions about the EU’s willingness to hold Egypt accountable on very precise socioeconomic targets do not bode well for the broader but less defined goals for democracy and human rights.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, strik said: “the fact that egypt and the commission even seem to ignore the crystal-clear socioeconomic conditions doesn’t increase my expectation that they adhere to the vague precondition on democracy and the rule of law. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa claudio francavilla, an associate eu director at human rights watch, said: “without benchmarks, the eu has turned a human rights conditionality into a blank cheque for egypt’s authoritarianism. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in a statement to the guardian, the european commission said the policy target on takaful and karama referred to new beneficiary families “and not to its net increase”. The spokesperson said there was “no contradiction” between this statement and that in a confidential document that said Egypt was required to “further expand cash transfer programmes”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, asked about the release of the remaining €1. 5bn in promised loans, the commission said it “will be made once all conditions have been met”, referring to 24 economic policy conditions, keeping an IMF programme on track and “taking concrete and credible steps towards respecting effective democratic mechanisms, including a multiparty parliamentary system, and the rule of law, and guaranteeing respect for human rights”.

It added: “Compliance with the conditionality is examined thoroughly” by EU officials and diplomats based on “information provided by the Egyptian authorities and other relevant sources”.

Egypt’s mission to the EU in Brussels did not respond to a request for comment.

Sebagaimana diketahui, president vladimir v. Putin of Russia touched down in Asia in recent hours. So did two of his nuclear-capable bombers.

Sebagaimana diketahui, mr. Putin arrived early Wednesday in Shenzhen, China, for a regional economic meeting and a trilateral summit with President Trump and President Xi Jinping of China. Satellite images showed that two Russian Tu-95MS strategic nuclear bombers had landed on Tuesday at Da Nang Airport in nearby Vietnam alongside two long-range transport aircraft.

It was the first time that Russian strategic nuclear bombers had deployed to Vietnam since the Soviet era, a pointed demonstration of Russia’s nuclear might and global reach ahead of the high-level talks.

The surprise arrival of the Russian aircraft in the region caused a scramble among American allies in Asia.

Diungkapkan bahwa japan dispatched jets after russian planes were detected in japanese airspace near okinoshima, an island in the south of japan, and tokyo registered its discontent with the russian authorities. South Korea also deployed fighter jets; the authorities there said the Russian planes entered South Korea’s Air Defense Identification Zone, where Seoul closely monitors foreign aircraft, but not its sovereign airspace.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, russia lags both china and the united states significantly in economic output, technological innovation, population size and trade flows, making mr. Putin’s participation in the trilateral summit scheduled for Thursday to some degree conspicuous.

Berdasarkan laporan, but the one critical area where russia has retained its lead is in nuclear weapons. Putin has brandished as a reason the world must continue to accord Moscow a certain level of deference and respect. Russia boasts the world’s biggest nuclear arsenal, which Mr. Russia has also developed a range of new nuclear weapons systems in recent years.

Berdasarkan laporan, the tu-95ms is a nuclear-capable bomber with intercontinental range. Russia has also deployed the bombers in its war against Ukraine to launch conventional missiles.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, taiwan on tuesday said it detected two sorties of russian military aircraft flying in airspace east of the island. Gen. Huang Chih-wei, the Vice Chief of the Taiwanese military’s General Staff, said that “the actions of the Russian aircraft undermine regional peace and stability and are detrimental to maintaining the status quo of peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the russian and vietnamese authorities did not make any public statements about the arrival of the bombers. Putin met with Vietnam’s leader, To Lam, in Shenzhen on Wednesday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, which Mr. Mr. Trump and Mr. Xi are also attending.

Russia and Vietnam have a longstanding relationship that dates back to the Cold War, and Russia still supplies the vast majority of Vietnam’s military equipment.

Diungkapkan bahwa for vietnam, the decision to welcome the russian nuclear bombers shows china that vietnamese leaders have a range of possible military partners to push back against any aggressive moves by beijing. Vietnam has also deepened its ties with the United States in recent years.

But it is a careful balancing act for the Vietnamese.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, vietnam allowed russia to refuel its bombers from cam ranh bay in 2014 as they patrolled the area around guam, but the refueling was done midair and the bombers did not land on vietnamese soil. At the time, the United States protested the use of Cam Ranh Bay, a former American and then Soviet base, for the refueling.

Diungkapkan bahwa mr. Trump’s well-documented fondness for fast food. Marcos’s gesture was not only a matter of national pride, but also appeared to be a nod to Mr. Mr. Trump, a self-described germaphobe, has said that he favors fast food from chains like McDonald’s because of their speed, consistency and hygiene.

In April, he received two McDonald’s bags delivered by DoorDash to the Oval Office, in an event the White House had staged to promote a Trump administration initiative that removed taxes on overtime and tips.

Diungkapkan bahwa mr. Trump on Wednesday that Jollibee had surpassed Kentucky Fried Chicken in popularity in the United States. Trump replied: “Oh, wow, fantastic. The claim was dubious but Mr. Marcos told Mr. ”.

While KFC still has many more stores than Jollibee in the United States, the Filipino chain has promoted its fried chicken as America’s best since at least 2022, citing food critics’ rankings and three consecutive wins in a USA Today readers’ poll.

China warned on Tuesday that it could hit back after the Trump administration this week proposed a rule that would restrict China’s access to advanced chips through data centers outside its borders.

Under sunny skies with mild temperatures, a festive mood prevails in the city, which bears a strong resemblance to Miami — only much larger and with taller, newer high-rises.

Sebagaimana diketahui, schools in shenzhen have closed this week, many residents have left town and local authorities have instructed companies to allow those employees who are still here to work from home. Sebagaimana diketahui, youthful volunteers — mainly students at local universities — stand on street corners wearing bright red vests, having been offered academic credit in exchange for being trained as guides. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, at the same time, however, residents are aware of occasional hassles. “Many friends who live around here plan to travel outside the city because of the inconvenience of transportation — many roads will be closed to traffic,” said the resident, who gave only her family name, Zhang. Diungkapkan bahwa xiangmei road, located near the main summit venue and lined with some of china’s costliest condominium towers, was much quieter than usual on monday. South Korea has been gripped by revelations of AI-aided cheating, just days before more than half a million students are to sit high-stakes entrance exams.

The integrity of South Korea’s career-defining university entrance exam has been thrown into doubt after the top scorer in a recent professional exam admitted using a concealed camera and AI to cheat.

Sebagaimana diketahui, on thursday, more than half a million people, mostly school students, are due to sit the exam, known as the suneung, at 1,312 centres across the country. The exam runs for a gruelling eight hours over a single day and determines which university a candidate can attend and, in turn, their future prospects.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the country goes to great lengths to ensure the smooth running of the suneung. Aircraft take-offs and landings are rescheduled during the 25-minute English listening paper to minimise noise, while artillery fire and tank movements are suspended.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the stock market opens an hour late and cars are stopped 200 metres from every centre. Extra trains run from 6am, police drive latecomers to their exam halls, and tourist attractions open late to ease traffic. Offices are asked to open at 10am.

But in recent days, exam organisers have faced a renewed threat to the validity of the entire exercise, after the top scorer in this year’s tax accountancy exam- who got just one question wrong out of 160– admitted on Sunday he had cheated by using AI.

Prime minister Han Seong-sook told a cabinet meeting in Seoul on Tuesday that AI-assisted cheating was a “social evil” that the government would “root out”.

Diungkapkan bahwa “we will block outright the carrying of smart devices during the exam,” she said. The education ministry and other agencies should approach it “as if staking their jobs on it”, she added.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, han said smart devices must be turned off and handed in, while bags left in corridors would be checked for any devices that were still on. Exam officials would also inspect all candidates’ glasses and watches, as well as their collars, sleeves and buttons for concealed cameras.

The government will also send emergency alerts to every phone in the country, which sound at full volume and cannot be silenced, in the hope of catching out anyone who has not handed in their device.

More invigilators will be deployed, and the government said it was preparing to switch off school wifi inside exam centres and public wifi nearby, and that personal hotspots, which cannot be blocked, would be traced through connection records.

The weekend’s cheating revelation captured national headlines in South Korea, stoking concern about the security of the suneung.

Berdasarkan laporan, in a video posted to his lawyer’s youtube channel, the exam cheat said he had photographed the questions with a concealed microcamera, sent them to an ai system and read the answers from a smartphone. “I cheated in the tax accountant exam,” he said. “My top placing is not the result of legitimate effort. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, his lawyer handed police a camera, a laptop and a phone. No charges have been brought, and the prime minister has ordered procedures to begin that would void his result and bar him for five years.

Berdasarkan laporan, smart glasses have been banned in exams since the end of june. In October, several candidates were caught with them while sitting university-run admissions exams. At the suneung, wearing a pair counts as using one even when switched off.

Diungkapkan bahwa the education ministry looked at using radio-frequency equipment to detect the glasses in exam halls, but concluded conditions varied too much between venues for deployment this year. Checks will instead rely on visual inspection, with at least one dedicated official placed in each exam centre.

Diungkapkan bahwa to avoid facing scrutiny on exam day, some candidates are reportedly switching to contact lenses. An optician in Suwon, south of Seoul, said students who had never worn contacts were coming in to ask how to put them in.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “to anyone thinking of cheating as i did: i am going to tell the investigators everything, so please don’t think, ‘i won’t get caught. ’”.

#1164. Business Council of Australia more aligned with fossil fuel industry than its members’ values, analysis finds

📅 18 Nov 2026

Business Council of Australia more aligned with fossil fuel industry than its members’ values, analysis finds

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/nov/19/bca-policy-energy-companies-members-climate-concerns

Research by InfluenceMap raises questions about association’s policies and representation, particularly around advocacy for new gas supplies.

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.

The Business Council of Australia is lobbying for gas expansion policies that clash with the climate concerns of the majority of its own members, according to new research that raises questions about the sway of a handful of major companies.

The business association also does not publicly disclose who is on its energy and climate committee, prompting transparency concerns among researchers over how its policies are shaped and whose interests they represent.

Analysis by London-headquartered InfluenceMap found the BCA’s positions aligned more closely with energy companies Woodside, Santos and ConocoPhillips than with the majority of its corporate base, particularly on the energy transition where it has advocated for new gas supplies over phasing down.

InfluenceMap’s Australia lead, Jack Herring, said major associations such as the BCA are an influential voice in government policymaking.

“These findings suggest the BCA’s climate policy engagement better reflects the narrow interests of members connected to the fossil fuel value chain than its wider membership,” Herring said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “advocacy for fossil gas expansion risks undermining australia’s climate targets and also threatens to create increased health risks and energy affordability and security concerns for everyday households, so this is an issue that affects us all. ”.

InfluenceMap’s analysis of company positions shows more than two-thirds of the members assessed, including Qantas, Woolworths, Coles, Atlassian, Fortescue and major banks CBA and NAB, advocate for stronger climate policies than the business council itself.

That support typically includes backing faster renewable energy rollout and advocating for more ambitious emission reduction targets.

For the study, the thinktank assessed 58 companies – a representative sample of the BCA’s more than 120 members – drawing on thousands of public statements, government submissions and regulatory filings.

Of those members assessed, 69% backed stronger climate policies than the BCA, a gap that widened to 78% on energy transition issues.

Herring said the BCA does not disclose who sits on its internal climate and energy committees, obscuring how its policy positions are formed.

“We obviously do know who’s on the association board, but beyond that, there’s no transparency around those internal committees,” he said.

A spokesperson for the BCA said the association supported the “national goal of achieving net zero by 2050 and the setting of interim targets, while also delivering reliable and affordable energy and ensuring we don’t undermine our international competitiveness along the way”.

“The BCA has long advocated for gas as an essential part of the net zero transition – ensuring grid stability – while we move to greater reliance on renewable energy,” the spokesperson said.

The BCA declined to comment on the makeup of its climate and energy committee.

The analysis comes as industry groups ramp up lobbying over the “safeguard mechanism”, Australia’s main policy for curbing emissions from its largest industrial facilities, which is under federal review.

While the BCA and most big resources companies publicly support the Paris agreement and Australia’s net zero 2050 carbon emissions target, they interpret what those commitments require in radically different ways to what is widely regarded as climate best practice.

Several oil and gas producer members, including Woodside, argue that increased gas supply is required to support the shift to renewables and enhance energy security in language that has been adopted by the BCA.

This rubs against those BCA members aligned with the findings of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, which found greenhouse gas emissions from existing fossil fuel infrastructure were more than enough to push the world beyond its climate goals.

InfluenceMap also found that the business council frequently lobbies for a “technology-neutral” or “technology agnostic” energy transition, which is the same language used by the fossil fuel sector designed to steer renewable energy funding toward gas.

Persephone Fraser, the ethical research and climate policy lead at fund manager Australian Ethical, said misaligned lobbying was a significant risk for companies and their shareholders, and a major risk to the economy.

“Companies must be scrutinising what is being advocated for in their name and actively correcting the record when it is inconsistent with their own positions, and interests,” Fraser said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “membership of an industry association cannot mean outsourcing responsibility for climate lobbying. ”.

The French-made Falcon 6X replaces the ageing presidential jet, officials say.

Ghana's government has defended its purchase of a new presidential jet amid criticism over its cost, as many citizens continue to struggle with the high cost of living.

The $60m (Â£46m) French-made Falcon 6X has sparked a political row, with opposition politicians accusing President John Mahama's administration of misplaced priorities.

But the government says the purchase is justified, arguing that Ghana's improving economy makes the aircraft affordable and is needed to replace an ageing presidential jet.

The controversy comes as Mahama's administration seeks to demonstrate an economic recovery after years of financial difficulties that forced Ghana to seek IMF assistance.

Can Ghana's new president meet the voters' high expectations?.

Manufactured by French aerospace company Dassault Aviation, the aircraft was delivered to the Ghana Air Force on Monday at a reported cost of $61m.

Parliament approved its purchase last December as part of a broader programme to modernise Ghana's military aviation fleet, which also includes four helicopters from Airbus.

The jet was welcomed with a water salute on Monday, but its arrival triggered criticism online and among opposition politicians over the cost and timing of the purchase.

While in the opposition, Mahama himself opposed buying a new presidential jet, prompting questions about why his administration has now gone head with the purchase.

Opposition MP Samuel Abu Jinapor questioned the government's priorities, saying the expenditure came at a time when many Ghanaians continue to struggle with the cost of living and youth unemployment remained alarmingly high.

"What was unacceptable in opposition cannot suddenly become acceptable in government merely because the occupants of power have changed," Jinapor added.

He accused the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) of hypocrisy, recalling how its senior figures had strongly opposed proposals for a new presidential aircraft when they were in opposition.

Jinapor also called for greater transparency over the procurement process, how the purchase was financed and the government's justification for the expenditure.

Defence Minister Kenneth Adjei welcomed and inspected the new jet on Monday.

The purchase has also prompted sharp criticism on social media, with some users arguing the money could have been spent on more pressing public needs.

"This money can employ over 100,000 nurses and 200,000 teachers," an X user posted.

But the government has rejected the criticism, saying Ghana's economic circumstances have changed considerably since the NDC opposed a similar purchase.

Peter Lanchene Toobu, chairman of parliament's defence committee, said the party had never opposed acquiring a presidential jet in principle.

Its objection, he said, had been on the timing when Ghana was experiencing severe economic difficulties.

"We agreed in principle that we needed to purchase a new presidential jet," he said.

He argued, however, that Ghana could not justify the expenditure at a time when it was seeking a $3bn bailout from the IMF.

"The strength and macroeconomic stability of this country have enhanced our status in the sense that imports have become cheaper, and this is the right time," he added.

Toobu said the government had purchased the aircraft without borrowing, citing a stronger Ghanaian currency and improved economic conditions.

Government spokesperson Kwakye Ofosu also dismissed suggestions that the purchase was a misplaced priority.

He pointed to falling prices of construction materials and lower borrowing costs as evidence of the country's improved economic situation.

Berdasarkan laporan, "when i was campaigning in 2024, and i was donating cement, it cost 115 cedis (â£7. 5) a bag. Today, for 80 cedis, you will get a bag of cement," he told JoyNews.

The controversy has also extended to the aircraft's interior, following claims that it has a dedicated bedroom and bathroom.

But Ofosu dismissed claims that the jet had such luxury facilities, saying the president has no intention of "bathing in the air".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "there certainly is no bathroom. President Mahama has no intention of bathing in the air," Ofosu said.

He explained that the jet has reclining seats that can be converted into sleeping arrangements but denied that it has a dedicated bedroom.

The government says the new jet will replace the 16-year-old Falcon 900EX, which has suffered recurring maintenance problems, including corrosion and leakages in its fuel tank.

The older jet was reportedly grounded in France for several months in 2025 while undergoing repairs.

Officials say the Falcon 6X has a longer flying range, reducing the need for refuelling stops on international trips and improving the reliability of presidential travel.

Professor Godfred Alufar Bokpin, an economist at the University of Ghana said that while the president's safety was paramount, the timing of the purchase was difficult to justify amid severe austerity measures, high unemployment and widespread infrastructure challenges.

"The timing makes it a bit difficult to understand," he told the BBC, adding that the government should provide a cost-benefit analysis explaining why buying the jet was preferable to leasing one and how the decision serves Ghana's interests.

#1169. ‘Phantom forests’ in Australia’s arid outback used to create carbon credits meant to offset emissions, report claims

‘Phantom forests’ in Australia’s arid outback used to create carbon credits meant to offset emissions, report claims

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/18/phantom-forests-in-australian-arid-outback-used-to-create-carbon-credits-meant-to-offset-emissions-report-claims

Carbon credit companies reject research that found only small increase in forest and canopy cover in regeneration areas despite wet conditions.

Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast.

A fight over the legitimacy of Australia’s climate change policy has reignited after researchers claimed “phantom forests” in the semi-arid outback are being used to create offsets that allow fossil fuel companies to keep pumping out pollution.

A group of academics, including professors from the Australian National University and the University of New South Wales, said they had examined 50 forest regeneration projects used to create carbon credits.

Led by Prof Andrew Macintosh, the former federal government carbon credit scheme integrity chair and the director of ANU’s Centre for Environmental Markets, the researchers said they found only a small increase in forest and tree crown cover in the areas over the past five years despite wet conditions.

They said the conclusions were consistent with their previous peer-reviewed studies that found Australia’s method for creating carbon credits from forest regeneration was doing little to nothing to help address the climate crisis.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the research was published in a report released on wednesday by the australian conservation foundation. Prof David Eldridge, one of the report’s authors and a former principal research scientist with the NSW environment department, said he was “gobsmacked” that “phantom forests” in outback areas north-west of the remote town of Bourke could earn carbon credits for forest regrowth.

“Some of these areas have never grown forests; they will never grow forests,” he said.

Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here.

Berdasarkan laporan, the findings were rejected by companies that manage what are known as human-induced regeneration projects in north-western nsw. “These are some of the most closely examined carbon projects in the country, and the evidence on the ground shows they are working,” a spokesperson for Green Collar, a business that manages carbon credit projects, said.

Each carbon credit is said to represent one tonne of emissions that has been removed from, or prevented from being released to, the atmosphere.

Their use is contentious, in part, because industrial-polluting companies that are required to cut emissions under a federal policy known as the safeguard mechanism are allowed to buy an unlimited number of credits to count as their own cuts while continuing to pollute.

Scientists have warned limiting the climate crisis requires rapid direct cuts in emissions and that carbon credits – also known as offsets – should be used sparingly.

The Australian Conservation Foundation said it showed coal and gas companies should be banned from claiming offsets as their own emissions cuts.

Adam Bandt, the foundation’s chief executive and a former Australian Greens leader, said the safeguard mechanism was meant to “cut climate pollution and protect us from big coal and gas threatening our lives and livelihoods, but it’s not working”.

Berdasarkan laporan, “putting more climate pollution into the atmosphere now could push us past dangerous tipping points. It can’t be offset, and the science tells us to keep coal and gas in the ground,” he said.

Macintosh said the evidence showed the projects were by and large not regenerating forest, but had created more than 60m carbon credits worth up to $2bn.

Our political team brings you up to speed on the stories that really matter and what they mean for you.

Diungkapkan bahwa the report said the safeguard mechanism was being “materially undermined” by poor-quality credits. It said a “flood of cheap, low integrity” credits was making it cheaper in many cases for big polluters to pay for offsets rather than make direct emissions cuts.

Berdasarkan laporan, there have been more than 430 human-induced regeneration projects in australia since 2013, covering an area of 38m hectares – larger than japan. The federal government is now reviewing the safeguard policy, as required under legislation.

A spokesperson for the Clean Energy Regulator, which manages the scheme, said it took allegations about the integrity or efficacy of carbon credit projects seriously, and had confidence in the forest regeneration method.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it said projects were required to demonstrate every five years that canopy cover was increasing, and it had rejected non-complying areas that could have received 6. 7m carbon credits.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, green collar said it stood “firmly behind the integrity of its human-induced regeneration projects” and expressed frustration that the report had not been publicly released or published in a peer-reviewed journal. It said the researchers had “judged these carbon projects with satellite pictures and a single field visit”.

Diungkapkan bahwa “carbon is stored in stems, branches, leaves, roots and dead timber. Satellite canopy products see leaves from above. They do not measure the wood and roots where most of that carbon sits,” its spokesperson said.

Skye Glenday, the chief executive of Climate Friendly, another carbon credit project developer, said the criticisms of the carbon credit projects were “at odds with the facts and the extensive independent scientific and regulatory scrutiny that is applied to all projects”.

“Debate about the use of offsets is legitimate, but let’s have that debate on its merits rather than undermining the carbon drawdown Australia also needs,” she said.

#1172. Democrats win Alaska Senate race two weeks after midterms counting began

📅 18 Nov 2026

Democrats win Alaska Senate race two weeks after midterms counting began

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cqev3v2ygzlvo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Mary Peltola defeated the state's Republican incumbent after a controversial race.

Democrat Mary Peltola has won Alaska's hard-fought Senate race, completing a sweeping victory for the party in the US upper house in the midterm elections.

The win gives the Democrats a 56th Senate seat following a tumultuous and controversial election in Alaska, which featured alleged spoiler recruitment efforts and unprecedented court battles.

It took two full weeks of counting to call a winner in the 3 November poll due to the logistical challenge of collecting ballots from across the state's remote expanse.

It is the ninth Senate seat the Democrats have taken from Republicans in the midterms, giving the party control of the US Congress for the last two years of Donald Trump's presidency.

The Democrats also won back the House of Representatives, the lower chamber.

Peltola defeated the incumbent Republican senator, Dan S Sullivan, who is yet to comment.

In her victory statement, Peltola said the "status quo in DC is not working for Alaska".

She recalled speaking to "elders in tears about empty fish racks" and to parents in rural Alaska choosing between heating their homes and putting food on the table.

Peltola is the first Alaska Native elected to the US Senate, and is the first Democrat to win a US Senate seat in Alaska since 2008.

Donald Trump won the state by 13 points in the 2024 presidential election, but defeat for the Republicans in this year's US Senate race in the state caps off a string of losses in the midterms for the president's party.

Many voters across the United States cited cost-of-living issues as a factor that affected how they cast their ballots.

Berdasarkan laporan, trump says alaska voters chose the wrong dan sullivan. What does the data show?.

Could Alaska's fishing industry tilt Washington's balance of power?.

Peltola's campaign had come under fire after the New York Times, external reported that her team worked with people who tried to recruit so-called spoiler candidates in an alleged attempt to confuse voters.

The alleged scheme led to a candidate named Daniel J Sullivan - a complete political unknown residing in a small coastal town who shared a name with the state's current US Senator and incumbent, Dan S Sullivan - contesting the race.

After legal challenges, state courts ruled that Daniel J Sullivan could remain on the ballot, and election officials distinguished them on election materials.

Peltola denied having knowledge of the alleged plot but her campaign swiftly came under fire, and both the US justice department and Alaska's Republican governor said they would launch investigations.

The Trump administration also filed a lawsuit attempting to stop the certification of the election results if the incumbent Republican Senator Sullivan lost.

A federal judge, though, dismissed the case, following legal challenges from Alaska election officials as well as the Peltola campaign and voting groups.

Due to Alaska's ranked-choice voting system, voters confused about which Dan Sullivan was the incumbent could have simply chosen both men, listing them as their first and second choices.

If they did so, after the first round of voting was complete, tabulation would have re-allocated any votes from Daniel J Sullivan - who stood little to no chance of winning - to Dan S Sullivan.

Experts told the BBC that this process made it difficult for any potential spoiler candidate to have any impact on the results.

An analysis by BBC Verify found that even if every vote for Daniel J Sullivan had gone to the incumbent, Dan S Sullivan, Peltola would still have won.

The Democratic win in Alaska cements the party's majority in the US Senate, as the party now has 56 seats to the Republicans' 44.

Diungkapkan bahwa the most senior democrat in the senate, chuck schumer, said peltola had run "a pitch-perfect campaign devoted to the issues alaskans care most about". Hailing the Democrats' final tally in the Senate, he said: "56 seats was an unimaginable result even just a few months ago. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa the alaska seat was initially one of several toss-up races that appeared as a must-win for democrats if they wanted to gain control of the us senate. But by the time Peltola was called the winner, they had seats to spare.

With 99% of ballots counted, Peltola had slightly more than 50% of the votes, while Sullivan trailed on less than 46%.

Sullivan, a former Alaska attorney general and an ally of Trump, campaigned on his record of delivering energy and military investment for the state.

Peltola promised Alaskans a more independent voice in Washington.

"As a lifelong Alaskan who has dedicated my life to serving our state, there is no greater honor than having Alaskans' support in our fight to take on corporate greed, lower costs, and put Alaska first," she said in her victory statement.

Diungkapkan bahwa "i will stand up to anyone to take on the rigged system in dc and deliver results for alaska's working families. ".

#1174. 'Coalition of the Willing' meets in Berlin: In an era of waning support, Europe remains committed to Ukraine

📅 18 Nov 2026

'Coalition of the Willing' meets in Berlin: In an era of waning support, Europe remains committed to Ukraine

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.dw.com/en/coalition-of-the-willing-meets-in-berlin-in-an-era-of-waning-support-europe-remains-committed-to-ukraine/a-79974996?maca=en-rss-en-all-1573-rdf

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the "coalition of the willing" supporting ukraine is gathering in berlin. One of the key issues under discussion is whether Europe will be able to play a role in future negotiations over the country's future.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, once again, berlin is rolling out the red carpet, and once again the focus is on ukraine: around 20 heads of state and government, primarily from across europe, are set to gather in the german capital on thursday (november 19). They will discuss the future of the Eastern European country that has been under attack from Russia since February 2022 and is now facing yet another harsh winter.

Berdasarkan laporan, extensive security measures have already been announced for berlin's government district, pointing to the presence of high-ranking participants. It remains unclear whether Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy will be among them. What does appear certain, however, is the attendance of chief US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, according to several media outlets.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the "coalition of the willing" is a group of 36 countries determined not to be deterred from supporting the nation under attack. Unlike other international forums, the group is focused not only on how to support Ukraine militarily and financially in the here and now.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Sebagaimana diketahui, led by germany, france, and the united kingdom, the coalition is also prepared, in principle, to help monitor a possible ceasefire within ukraine itself and to contribute to the complex security guarantees the country would then require, should such a scenario come to pass. The effort dates back to March 2025, when the countries involved first met in London. Now they are gathering in Berlin.

Diungkapkan bahwa but what can the coalition realistically achieve? stefan meister of the german council on foreign relations (dgap) is not overly optimistic. There is no plan outlining what security guarantees Europe would offer, what troops it would be prepared to deploy, what measures it could provide to safeguard a ceasefire, or where it would be willing to make compromises. In an interview with DW, he said: "The fundamental problem is that Europe has yet to put forward a proposal. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa nevertheless, the meeting comes at a moment when some observers believe there may finally be movement toward ending the war. During talks in Abu Dhabi in the United Arab Emirates a few days ago, Russia, Ukraine, and the US managed to agree only on a prisoner exchange. It was a modest step forward.

Further talks are planned, and it has been a long time since the prospects appeared as favorable as they do now for Europe to secure a role in future decisions on war and peace in Ukraine.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It has repeatedly been argued, both by US officials and by those in power in Russia, that Europe does not speak with a single voice.

Berdasarkan laporan, unsurprisingly, this has sparked a debate among eu heads of state and government over who, exactly, could represent europe in such talks. Germany has a seat at the table, that is absolutely clear. Could it be German Chancellor Friedrich Merz of the center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU)? After the EU summit in Dublin, Ireland, on Friday, he said: "For the first time, concrete peace talks are expected to take place in the coming weeks with Europe represented. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but what exactly did that mean? that germany alone would speak for all of europe? hardly. As was also made clear in Berlin on Monday, Europe would be represented by the E3 countries, namely Germany, France, and the non-EU member United Kingdom, joined by Poland and Italy. Official EU representatives, including European Council President António Costa, would also take part.

Berdasarkan laporan, stefan meister of the dgap believes the debate says a great deal about the pressures europe itself is under: "europe's positioning has more to do with domestic political considerations than with developments in the negotiations. Everyone needs to show that they are participating in the talks in some way. Elections will be held next year in France and Poland, and it is still unclear whether French support for Ukraine will continue in its current form after that. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa german deputy government spokesperson sebastian hille, meanwhile, sought to downplay the debate on monday over a possible role for friedrich merz as chief negotiator. What matters is that Putin finally understands that he must come to the negotiating table so that we have a chance of achieving peace in the first place. At the federal government's regular press briefing, he said: "This is not about discussing individuals. ".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Berdasarkan laporan, us negotiator jared kushner, the son-in-law of president donald trump, struck a rather different tone last week. Speaking in Abu Dhabi, he said: "If Europe could identify one person to speak on their behalf, that would be a bigger achievement than getting the Russians to include them in the negotiations. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa government spokesperson hille responded on monday: "europe's strength lies precisely in the unity and cohesion of many countries. " Hille emphasized that the situation remained unchanged: peace in Ukraine could only be achieved step by step. We should not allow ourselves to be drawn into debates that others want to frame around this question. Europe, too, would need stamina, perseverance, and a willingness to undertake the painstaking work required to bring it about.

Declining support for Ukraine in German polls.

Berdasarkan laporan, european supporters of ukraine are also under pressure as public opinion on the issue is shifting, including in germany. While a broad majority favored helping defend the country in the immediate aftermath of Russia's invasion in the spring of 2022, support has since fallen markedly.

Sebagaimana diketahui, according to the latest ard deutschlandtrend survey on the issue, conducted in september 2026, 52% of eligible voters still support weapons deliveries to ukraine, while 42% believe such support has gone too far. That is the highest level of opposition recorded since the start of the war.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a further study conducted for public broadcaster wdr in november 2026 found that support for ukraine has become a more polarizing issue in germany than immigration. According to the survey, 54% of respondents favor continued support for Ukraine, while just under 29% would prefer a rapprochement with Russia, despite its war of aggression against Ukraine.

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/nov/18/byron-bay-doula-left-newborn-to-inflate-jumping-castle-freebirth-inquest-ntwnfb

Inquest into deaths of four babies born in free births or at home in northern NSW between 2022 and 2024 hears ‘something was seriously wrong’.

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.

Sebagaimana diketahui, baby dh was born in an inflatable pool, in a candle-lit room in his parents’ home near byron bay, with no one medically trained present. There are two very different versions of what happened next.

Diungkapkan bahwa in the parents’ version, the doula reassured them baby dh was ok, then left to inflate a jumping castle while their newborn turned purple, became floppy, and struggled to breathe. In the doula’s version, everything seemed OK but she suggested they seek more help if they wanted to.

The New South Wales coroner’s court heard the two competing narratives on Wednesday as part of an ongoing inquest into the deaths of four babies born in free births or home births.

The babies died in NSW’s northern rivers region between 2022 and 2024.

“The evidence will be that from his first minutes of life, [Baby DH] showed signs that something was seriously wrong,” the Lismore courtroom heard.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “his parents saw those signs. They raised them again and again with their doula, who they had engaged to watch for exactly that. Their doula, in this case, was a woman named Amy Lou Smith.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “each time the parents raised their concerns, they were reassured by amy lou. An ambulance was not called until moments before [Baby DH] stopped breathing. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, his father described the baby as floppy after birth. “His colour, his whole body was purple with his hands and feet darker still,” the court heard, and Smith told them some purple in the hands and feet was normal.

“I didn’t notice his body being purple,” Smith told the court.

Berdasarkan laporan, told the baby’s colour wasn’t improving, smith said “as long as his abdomen isn’t purple”, according to evidence from the parents. 5C. His temperature was low, 34. His whole body had been purple all along. The mother was shocked. Smith suggested trying to get it up to 37C.

“I believed if they had real concerns, that they would call an ambulance and not be texting a non medically trained doula,” Smith told the court.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, smith, the inquest heard, described his laboured breathing as “cute little noises”. “I didn’t say that,” Smith told the court.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the court heard smith told the couple baby dh would have been put on oxygen if he was in hospital. But Smith later told the court she didn’t know what the hospital would have done.

Sebagaimana diketahui, he had strange lumps on his body, and wasn’t feeding. Smith suggested they get the lumps checked out, and warned that babies sometimes take a while to latch on to the breast, according to the parents’ evidence.

Berdasarkan laporan, the court heard smith left to set up a jumping castle for her son’s birthday. She sent the couple a picture of the castle later, as they were trying to contact a doctor, the court heard.

Smith told the court the castle was already set up, and the couple was happy for her to leave.

“Everything felt like it was OK,” she said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, eventually, the parents spoke to the gp they had tried to contact earlier. They did, and did CPR until the paramedics got there. The GP told them to call triple zero. But Baby DH was declared dead at the hospital.

After the father had made the emergency call, Smith also told them to call an ambulance, and sent them instructions on infant CPR.

Throughout the hearing, Smith denied that any of her advice or comments constituted clinical advice.

Diungkapkan bahwa neonatologist dr paul evans, the court heard, had found baby dh had a complex heart defect, one that would have shown up on an x-ray. The baby could have been treated, and a birth plan with proximity to a major hospital and specialist cardiac care prepared, the court heard.

The child’s death was not inevitable, Evans found.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, while pregnant, baby dh’s mother decided to rely on a doula. She first approached a woman the court heard was likely to be Sita Tara Kali, a self-described birth keeper who was also involved in the care of another baby previously mentioned during the inquest. But Kali didn’t feel she could help, so they turned to Smith.

Diungkapkan bahwa the court heard the couple paid for an online “sovereign birth course” for smith and was reassured that she had enough experience. They agreed on an emergency plan.

Smith, who became a birth doula in 2020, was quizzed on her experience in court.

She has a degree in fine art and has worked as a social worker and a youth worker.

Diungkapkan bahwa she told the court she is not medically trained in any way but did an online “full-spectrum doula course”. She learned CPR but was not familiar with how to apply it to a newborn – she denied she had given the parents the impression she was.

She had no training about a newborn’s colour, breathing, or feeding, but she did go to a retreat where she learned about referring a woman to more support if needed.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, she had been present at 15 births over four years, nine alongside a midwife, and conceded she didn’t know what a low-risk birth would look like. She had read a couple of books about birthing, but they were more “spiritual”, the court heard.

She agreed that she now believes the best model of care for a home birth is for a clinically trained midwife to work alongside a doula.

#1178. Bancroft sandpaper claims heap pressure on Cummins

📅 18 Nov 2026

Bancroft sandpaper claims heap pressure on Cummins

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/articles/cmqlqdevgl9ro?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Cameron Bancroft and Steve Smith were banned for their part in the sandpaper plot.

Cameron Bancroft has claimed the whole Australia team knew about the 2018 sandpaper plot in explosive revelations that will heap pressure on current captain Pat Cummins.

In a detailed testimony, published by the West Australian,, external batter Bancroft - the player caught with the sandpaper during the Test match against South Africa - has given arguably the most complete account of the events in Cape Town eight years ago.

Diungkapkan bahwa "in 2018 not the entire truth was told," said bancroft. "I have never been completely honest about what happened. ".

For the past two weeks, Australian cricket has been embroiled in a debate over the ball-tampering saga following the publication of Usman Khawaja's autobiography.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, khawaja wrote that the whole australia team knew of the plot, claims supported by david warner and chadd sayers. Cummins described Khawaja's account as "wrong" and "nonsense".

On the day Cricket Australia announced a forum into the sandpaper episode, Bancroft published his account, explaining he was motivated by the news conference given by Cummins.

"The final straw for me to write this account was Australian cricket captain Pat Cummins' press conference," said Bancroft.

"It made me feel angry, betrayed and alone.

Berdasarkan laporan, "what i saw, experienced and lived with - not only him, but everyone else on that tour in south africa - is not the public account he gave in his press conference and in the years previously when he has spoken on this time. ".

Opener Bancroft was given a nine-month ban for his part in the plot.

Diungkapkan bahwa steve smith was stripped of the australia captaincy and given a year-long ban, the same suspension given to vice-captain warner. No other players or coaches were punished.

In his more than 4,000-word piece, Bancroft has claimed:.

Sandpaper was first used during the second Test against South Africa â the match before Bancroft was caught.

Bancroft had conversations with the Australia seamers â Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Marsh about whether the ball was "swinging enough".

Before the third day of the second Test, the entire playing group and staff had "celebrations" about the effect of the sandpaper.

When Bancroft was caught during the third Test, then Australia coach Darren Lehmann told 12th man Peter Handscomb to "get the sandpaper off Bangers now".

Bancroft found the publication of a joint-statement by the Australia bowlers in 2021 "deeply painful".

Khawaja's autobiography and the subsequent claims made by Warner and seamer Sayers have reopened old wounds related to the sandpaper saga.

Still, those connected have remained true to the accounts they have presented during the intervening eight years.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the most significant denial came from cummins, who rebuffed khawaja's account in an extraordinary 68-minute address to the media in sydney. Lehmann and Starc have also reiterated their denials.

Now, it is the extensive detail provided by Bancroft that could shed a whole new light on the controversy and lead to further questions for Cummins, Lehmann and Cricket Australia.

Cummins is due to lead Australia in the first Test against New Zealand on 9 December.

Diungkapkan bahwa a statement released on behalf of cummins said: "whilst we feel for cam and everything he's been through there's nothing in the statement that hasn't been answered by pat in his press conference. ".

A Cricket Australia statement said: "We respect that Cameron Bancroft has told his story, and we will take time to consider his comments.

"We expect that there will be many dimensions to the events of 2018, which is why we have established the forum for individuals to give their version of events.

Berdasarkan laporan, "we are finalising the terms of reference and will commence the process as soon as possible. ".

In his account, Bancroft said: "I have spent eight years speaking about accountability, honesty and the lessons I learned from one of Australian cricket's darkest moments.

Berdasarkan laporan, "however, in 2018 not the entire truth was told. I have never been completely honest about what happened.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "it was not just the three of us â steve smith, david warner and i â who knew about me using sandpaper on the ball in south africa. It was the whole team.

"When I was questioned during Cricket Australia's investigation, I did not give a complete and truthful account.

"I withheld important details, including when the use of sandpaper began, how long it went on for, and the involvement and awareness of others.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "i did this to protect cricket australia's investigation and not implicate others around me. ".

'No way in a million years' the whole team didn't know - Vaughan on sandpaper scandal.

Sebagaimana diketahui, bancroft said his actions were "discussed" and "acknowledged" by the entire playing group at the end of the second day and before the beginning of the third day. He said he was encouraged by Saker, who has since worked as a consultant with England.

The only person within the camp to express unease at the ball-tampering, according to Bancroft, was media manager Kate Hutchison.

"I received wraps and encouragement from members of the playing and coaching staff, especially David Saker," said Bancroft.

"Our media manager, Kate Hutchison, expressed her objection to what was happening.

"I recall her making it clear that she believed it was wrong, that she wanted nothing to do with it, and walking away from the discussion.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "i will never forget that. Somebody had spoken up.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "somebody had demonstrated that being part of the team did not mean having to accept everything the team was doing. And I ignored it. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, bancroft identifies saker as the coach khawaja claimed encouraged him to work harder on the ball during the third test in cape town. The 33-year-old said he took "feedback" from all the bowlers and wicketkeeper Tim Paine, who took over the captaincy when Smith was sacked.

Berdasarkan laporan, in cape town, bancroft was confronted by the umpires when tv cameras showed him concealing the sandpaper in his trousers. He claimed Lehmann sent a message to him via Handscomb.

"Peter Handscomb ran out at the drinks break after I'd been caught and shoved the sandpaper down my pants," wrote Bancroft.

Berdasarkan laporan, "he said to me: 'i think it's time i take that off you now. ' And Pete was doing his job after Boof [Lehmanm] shouted to him on the walkie talkie "get the sandpaper off Bangers [Bancroft] now".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "if he didn't know he wouldn't have said that. And if it wasn't clear enough before, then it was obvious now. ".

In 2021, Bancroft was playing county cricket with Durham and gave an interview to The Guardian in which he said the bowlers' involvement in the plot was "self-explantory".

In response, Cummins, Starc, Hazlewood and spinner Nathan Lyon released a joint-statement denying any knowledge that ball-tampering had taken place.

"Reading that statement was deeply painful," said Bancroft.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "i had memories of conversations on the field in port elizabeth and newlands, feedback about the ball and shared celebrations that made the statement difficult for me to digest. ".

'Cricket Australia didn't get it right' - Gillespie.

For almost two weeks, Australian cricket has been at war with itself over the revelations in Usman Khawaja's autobiography.

Diungkapkan bahwa but there has been an absence of a smoking gun. Without tangible, new, hard evidence, all that was left was claim and counter-claim.

Naturally, the spotlight fell on Pat Cummins because of his role as a bowler in Cape Town and his elevation to Australia captain in the years since.

Berdasarkan laporan, his performance last week in front of the media, on live television, was extraordinary. For 68 minutes he took all questions and appeared plausible in his answers.

In being so robust in his denial of Khawaja's account - Cummins called it "nonsense" - the skipper also left himself open to the consequences if it was later revealed he was not telling the truth.

Crucially, it was Cummins' press conference that compelled Cameron Bancroft to speak out.

It must be stressed that Bancroft's account is not the open-and-shut evidence that convicts Cummins or anyone else in the dressing room at Newlands in 2018.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but it is certainly the most complete account we have heard from anyone involved, walking step-by-step through the genesis of the plot, the execution and the fallout. Bancroft has named names: Cummins, the other bowlers, Tim Paine, coach Darren Lehmann and assistant coach David Saker. It is, potentially, the decisive intervention that shifts this whole saga in a new direction.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, whether by accident or design, it came on the day cricket australia (ca) announced its forum for evidence into the sandpaper controversy. Before Bancroft's account CA's action felt an unsatisfactory halfway house - not an investigation, with no guarantee outcomes will be published.

What now? Will CA go further? How will those implicated by Bancroft respond? How can Cummins lead Australia in the first Test against New Zealand? Could Steve Smith break a silence he has held since the publication of Khawaja's book?.

Diungkapkan bahwa throughout the past fortnight, there has been a sense that australian cricket hoped the sandpaper debate would eventually go away. Cummins even said he never wanted to speak about it again.

Instead of fading, the thirst for the truth grows, now fuelled by Bancroft's extraordinary story.
