#1179. Bikie ‘not surprised’ if he used fake $20,000 souvlaki invoice to pocket thousands on Big Build site, inquiry hears

📅 18 Nov 2026

Bikie ‘not surprised’ if he used fake $20,000 souvlaki invoice to pocket thousands on Big Build site, inquiry hears

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/nov/18/bandidos-bikie-joel-leavitt-cfmeu-big-build-inquiry-ntwnfb

Royal commission sees text message where Bandidos member Joel Leavitt says ‘just make up a quote that hits 20K’ while working on site for CFMEU.

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.

A Bandidos gang member says it is possible he used a fake $20,000 invoice for souvlaki to pocket thousands of dollars while employed on a Big Build site.

The former CFMEU member and bikie Joel Leavitt faced a second day of examination by the royal commission into alleged corruption across Victoria’s construction sector on Wednesday.

In 2023, while employed as site health and safety representatives, Leavitt and another man, Charles Farrugia, exchanged messages which were shown to the commission.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “just make up a quote that hits 20k and we will get the other nine off the subbies,” leavitt wrote. “Which will mean five each. ”.

The commission viewed a genuine receipt for roughly $9,000 for souvlaki catering, and another allegedly fake invoice for $20,000 which was sent by Leavitt to the site superintendent, Tim Alford, from the firm Acciona.

The commissioner, Chris Kourakis AC, said the evidence strongly suggested the two CFMEU health and safety representatives had organised a meal for workers to get a few souvlaki and had pocketed $5,000 each.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i’ll accept that,” leavitt said. “I’m not surprised that I could have. ”.

The commission also viewed messages between Leavitt and Alford in which the bikie appeared to direct who could and who couldn’t be hired to work on the site.

Diungkapkan bahwa in one message, alford appeared to address the arrangement, saying: “i don’t care bringing your mates on and putting them in spotting roles and finding homes. But they all need to do there jobs. ”.

The counsel assisting the commission Chris Carr SC asked Leavitt if he, on behalf of the CFMEU, was dictating who could work on the site, to which he replied he couldn’t recall.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i had my own demons at the time, so i may have dropped the ball on a few things,” leavitt said. “That’s my answer to that question, counsellor. ”.

Earlier on Wednesday, questioning returned to a $165,000 invoice paid to Leavitt’s now defunct company, JVL Consulting, by the union-aligned subcontractor BK Labour Hire in July 2025.

When shown a copy of the invoice Leavitt was unable to recall anything about it, or even give a clear answer as to what services his former company had provided.

Later on Wednesday, the BK Labour Hire director Bernard Kearney admitted he paid the invoice despite Leavitt not having done any work for the firm.

“I just decided to pay it and move on,” he said.

Carr said there were likely only a couple of reasons why BK Labour would have paid Leavitt, including a fear of violence or to suppress some information he had on them.

“Was it one or both of those two?” Carr asked.

BK Labour also received a succession of invoices from the senior CFMEU organiser Joe Myles totalling $256,000 over about a year.

Carr had earlier asked why Leavitt appeared to become uncomfortable when asked about the invoice.

Leavitt blamed his poor memory on having ADHD, as well as PTSD from being shot in May 2023.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “around that time i actually got told by gang squad that there was a contract on my life,” he said. “So it brought back some uncomfortable memories.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “that’s why i blocked out a lot of that time. ”.

Kourakis warned Leavitt it was an offence to fail to answer questions put to him by the commission, something he said could ultimately be tested in a courtroom.

“I’ve been shot … I’ve had drug issues … I am answering these to the best of my recollection,” Leavitt replied.

“How do you think you would act if you’d ever been shot?”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, after the commission briefly adjourned for leavitt to speak to his lawyers, the bikie returned to the stand and said jvl consulting had provided safety advice to companies. “Maybe helping them out with their procedures and policies and stuff like that,” he said.

The commission viewed a copy of Leavitt’s bank statement at the time which fluctuated between $0 and minus $20, before the $165,000 landed in his account.

“Everyone likes money – I’m sure all youse are on good money for this,” said Leavitt, addressing the bar table.

Kourakis informed Leavitt that the commission had evidence he did not do any work for BK Labour.

He said an inference that could be made was that Leavitt was “standing over” BK Labour for the payment because he needed money.

“If that’s the way you want to look at it, commissioner,” Leavitt replied.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, carr asked if leavitt knew something about bk labour that the company would have wanted to keep quiet. “Is the conclusion the commission should draw is that you just stood over them with some sort of explicit or implied threat of violence?” he asked.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, leavitt replied: “i’d like to talk to my counsel before i answer that. ”.

#1182. Grand Theft Auto 6 is a masterpiece, say critics

📅 18 Nov 2026

Grand Theft Auto 6 is a masterpiece, say critics

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cw8r75xm8v4po?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Review scores for GTA 6 are a fairytale ending after years of development.

After 13 years of waiting, record-breaking trailers and lengthy delays, critics have given their answer to one of the year's biggest questions.

Does Grand Theft Auto 6, surely the most anticipated game of all time, live up to the hype?.

According to the first reviews, it's a resounding yes.

Metacritic, which aggregates reviews from critics, averages it at 99 out of 100, external - tying with Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which has held the record since 1998.

Reviewers overwhelmingly agreed the open-world action game was an ambitious, ground-breaking title that was well worth the wait.

Sebagaimana diketahui, not everyone is enjoying the glowing praise - with some posters to online forums objecting to what one called "the ultra fan-boy hype. ".

But there is no question the reviewers have been effusive with their praise, with gaming website IGN, external branding GTA 6 "unprecedented", "unbelievable" and "unmissable".

Meanwhile in its five star review, Eurogamer said makers Rockstar had "pushed back the horizon of video games once again" with its graphics, storytelling and world building.

"The awe is all part of the point, of course, and GTA 6 is nothing if not truly awesome," reviewer Chris Tapsell wrote, external, but he added "there are also nits to pick".

For The New York Times, external one of those nits was whether the realism of the game might dull the fun chaos of its predecessors.

Reviewer Yussef Cole said GTA 6 had "matured beyond its memorable car crashes and stickups" with consequences to every action.

But "some of my favourite moments have been careening through streets with squad cars in hot pursuit," he wrote.

Critics say the relationship between Jason and Lucia is central to the game.

The graphics of the game were hotly anticipated and so far have not disappointed critics, with The Guardian, external describing Leonida, the setting inspired by Miami, as "so lifelike that at times it beggars belief".

And the relationship between the lead characters, Jason and Lucia, has also stunned critics.

"They feel like real people rather than puppets dancing to your whim," The Guardian's Keza MacDonald wrote, adding: "I found it impossible not to care for them".

Writing for Forbes, external, Paul Tassi said: "I can't say I've ever seen a better video game relationship than the one they share".

The Washington Post, external said GTA 6 "raises the bar at every level", while Bloomberg, external's Jason Schreier called it a "masterpiece" in his five star review.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "it's hard not to be astonished by what rockstar has done here," he wrote. "There's nothing else like it.

Diungkapkan bahwa "while playing this game, i often found myself wondering how it even exists. ".

Rockstar hasn't revealed the cost of the game, but some estimates put the figure north of $1bn (Â£760m).

GTA 6 is the most hotly anticipated videogame ever.

The Game Awards - the most watched ceremony of its kind in the industry - gave players a teaser of the critical reception when its 2026 nominations were revealed on Tuesday.

And despite having not released at the time, GTA 6 was the most-nominated title.

It will be up for eight prizes, including game of the year and best music.

The nomination of Manni L Perez in the best performance category confirmed wide speculation that she is the actress behind main character Lucia in GTA 6 - a fact Rockstar hadn't previously officially confirmed.

The jury for the event is largely made up of gaming journalists around the world, who would have received advanced copies for review.

Some, though, have questioned how a game that has just been released has garnered such positive reviews and award nominations.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there is a view in some online forums that the hype around the game has got out of control as, with one poster commenting: "i think everyone's tired of hearing about this game - i don't even want to play it anymore. ".

It appears so far, however, that is likely to be very much a minority view.

#1183. Has the 'Parthenon puzzle' been solved? The long quest to reassemble lost eastern pediment

📅 18 Nov 2026

Has the 'Parthenon puzzle' been solved? The long quest to reassemble lost eastern pediment

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.dw.com/en/has-the-parthenon-puzzle-been-solved-the-long-quest-to-reassemble-lost-eastern-pediment/a-79982098?maca=en-rss-en-all-1573-rdf

Berdasarkan laporan, the depiction of the birth of the goddess athena above the parthenon's entrance is considered a masterpiece of ancient art. Now, a German research team has pieced together all the surviving fragments.

The 2,500-year-old Parthenon is ancient Greece's most important temple and is regarded as one of the greatest masterpieces of the High Classical period of Greek art.

Dedicated to Athena, the city's patron goddess, it towers over Athens from its position on the Acropolis — a powerful symbol of the city's importance.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the parthenon had a lasting influence on western ideas of humanity and art. The sculptures adorning its pediments, created under the direction of the legendary sculptor Phidias, are considered unparalleled examples of proportion and grace. They have influenced artists from ancient Rome through Neoclassicism to the modern era.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the east pediment above the temple entrance depicted the birth of the goddess athena from the head of her father zeus, surrounded by the olympian gods. At its center stood a colossal Zeus figure, measuring 3. A total of 39 figures adorned the roughly 29-meter-long work of art. 8 meters in height.

For centuries, scholars have puzzled over exactly what the arrangement looked like, as the pediment was destroyed during the Christianization of Greece.

After decades of painstaking detective work and with the help of modern technology, archaeologist Vinzenz Brinkmann and his team have managed to piece together all the surviving fragments of the Parthenon's east pediment.

Berdasarkan laporan, brinkmann heads the antiquities and asia department at frankfurt's liebieghaus sculpture collection. "We're very, very confident that we've solved the mystery," he told DW.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the results are now on display in an exhibition at the liebieghaus titled "athena, the stage is yours: the parthenon puzzle. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, only around 20% of the original marble sculpture's volume is known to have survived. The fragments are scattered across various European museums, with most located in Athens. The British Museum also holds numerous pieces.

Brinkmann and his wife, Ulrike Koch-Brinkmann, have spent more than 40 years working on this ancient puzzle, with so many of its pieces missing.

And they were far from the first to attempt it: "Already in the 19th century, many scholars studied the subject and developed well-founded theories based on their deep knowledge of ancient sources," Brinkmann explains.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in 1910, a study documenting the many fragments held by the british museum was published. The research team was able to build on that earlier work, but progress remained slow for years.

Diungkapkan bahwa then, in 2014, a visit to the hermitage museum in st. Petersburg provided Brinkmann with a crucial clue. There, he encountered a Roman sarcophagus featuring a relief of Athena's birth. "That's when it suddenly clicked: They're all there!".

Sebagaimana diketahui, nine such sarcophagi are known to exist, almost all of them in rome. Each depicts a different section of the Parthenon's east pediment.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, brinkmann emphasizes that other scholars had already noticed this connection in the 19th century. "But we really seized on the idea and never let go. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa the researchers also benefited from 21st-century technology: 3d scanners and printers. Brinkmann and his team visited numerous destinations to examine around 60 original fragments at different locations — traveling light. An iPhone was all they needed to scan the pieces.

Sebagaimana diketahui, digitally fitting the fragments together led to another important discovery. "We know these figures we're putting together!" Brinkmann recalls thinking at the time.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the romans had repeatedly made individual copies of all the sculptures from the pediment. "These copies matched the fragments perfectly. Suddenly, we found ourselves surrounded by old acquaintances we had never suspected had come from the pediment. " This finally enabled the researchers to reconstruct all the figures and their original arrangement.

Berdasarkan laporan, using a 3d printer, the team created a 4-meter-long model at a scale of 1:7. For the exhibition, they also produced life-size 3D prints of the most important fragments and mounted them on panels depicting the complete figures at their original size. 7. An animation brings the reconstructed composition to life, digitally assembling the fragments to reveal how the east pediment once looked.

Sebagaimana diketahui, alongside works from the liebieghaus collection, the exhibition features loans from other institutions, including the vatican museums and the louvre. Objects from the Acropolis Museum in Athens had originally been expected as well. But Greece withdrew its participation after learning that the British Museum was also planning to lend fragments to the Frankfurt exhibition. The Liebieghaus ultimately decided to forgo the British-owned fragments, too.

Diungkapkan bahwa there is a reason for this controversy. Britain holds a substantial portion of the Parthenon frieze as well as fragments from both pediments.

Greek authorities have been campaigning for their return for decades.

In Britain, the 56 sections of the frieze are known as the "Elgin Marbles," named after Lord Elgin, the British ambassador to the Ottoman Empire in Constantinople.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in the early 19th century, elgin had sculptures removed from the exterior of the parthenon on the acropolis in athens. They were taken to Britain with the consent of the Ottoman Empire, which ruled Greece at the time.

Britain maintains that the sculptures were legally acquired.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for years, the dispute remained deadlocked. Since the Labour Party came to power in Britain, there has been some movement toward resolving it. But apparently not enough to persuade Greece to lend artworks to an exhibition in which the British Museum might also participate.

Berdasarkan laporan, the exhibition "athena, the stage is yours. The Parthenon Puzzle" runs through July 25, 2027, at the Liebieghaus in Frankfurt.

British hacker who stole $11m through text message scheme jailed for six years in US

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cm87987w1qz5o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Spanish police arrested Buchanan in Madrid.

Diungkapkan bahwa a british hacker has been sentenced to six years in a federal prison in the us for conspiring to hack into at least a dozen companies via text message phishing, and stealing more than $11. 6m (Â£8. 8m) in cryptocurrency from individual victims.

Tyler Buchanan, 24, from Dundee, started hacking as a teenager and was part of the collective of young hackers known as Scattered Spider, which has been blamed for a string of high profile cyber-crimes.

US prosecutors said the thefts had "severe, life-altering consequences" for victims and showed the growing threat posed by online crime groups.

The sentence brings to an end a years-long international investigation involving authorities in the UK, US, Spain and Canada.

Buchanan admitted taking part in a hacking campaign that began in 2021, when he was 19.

Working from his parents' home, he and other English-speaking hackers in the US and UK targeted employees at major technology and telecommunications companies.

It made them $8m in less than two years, according to US prosecutors.

Buchanan and his hacker gang sent out hundreds of SMS messages to the mobile phones of people who worked for large tech or telecoms companies.

The SMS phishing messages contained links to spoof websites designed to look like legitimate sites of victim companies.

The group used messages like "Hi, your account is due to expire - you need to log in to your work account here immediately or you will lose access to work apps".

The websites then lured the recipient into providing confidential information, including personal identifying information (PII), and account usernames and passwords.

The boys and young men did it on an industrial scale with Buchanan setting up a Telegram bot to collect all the victims' credentials as the duped workers unwittingly handed over their login details.

For some victim companies, subsequently stolen information included confidential work information, intellectual property, plus account access credentials, names, email addresses, and telephone numbers.

The group then used stolen information and SIM-swapping techniques to target cryptocurrency investors in the United States.

Diungkapkan bahwa in the largest single theft, prosecutors said one victim lost $1. 67m in December 2022.

Diungkapkan bahwa overall, authorities calculated that buchanan and his co-conspirators stole more than $11. 6m from victims.

Buchanan was also a victim of cyber-criminals.

In early 2023 his online identity and home address were leaked by rival hackers seeking access to his cryptocurrency.

Cyber security researchers and journalists reported that he was assaulted at his home and threatened with a blowtorch.

"TylerB and his group were highly sophisticated and organised but the violence he and others experienced was a sign of the troubling direction of these online communities of young hackers" says cyber security researcher Allison Nixon from Unit221B.

Buchanan then reportedly fled to Canada to escape further threats before returning home.

In April 2023, officers from Police Scotland searched Buchanan's bedroom after receiving a request from the FBI.

Investigators recovered a device containing the names and addresses of hacking victims, along with cryptocurrency seed phrases and account credentials belonging to at least one victim.

The following month, Buchanan left the UK again.

He was arrested on 31 May 2024 at Palma de Mallorca Airport in Spain while attempting to board a private flight to Naples.

After being extradited to the United States, he remained in custody before being sentenced this week.

In his November 2023 charge, Buchanan was named along with four American men and boys in their twenties and teens for alleged activity linked to the notorious cyber-criminal collective Scattered Spider.

They have all pleaded guilty too and are now serving time in jail.

Two other members of the Scattered Spider group were jailed in the UK in July for various cyber attacks including a disruptive one against Transport for London that caused Â£39m of damage.

A Spanish court is investigating the singer Julio Iglesias over complaints that he sexually abused and physically assaulted two female employees who worked at his properties in the Caribbean.

The announcement of the investigation by the Audiencia Nacional comes almost 11 months after Spanish prosecutors shelved the women’s complaints, arguing the country’s courts had no jurisdiction as the alleged offences took place outside Spain.

Berdasarkan laporan, but the human rights ngo women’s link worldwide, which is representing the women, has successfully argued that the audiencia nacional has jurisdiction over the case and iglesias’s spanish nationality provides sufficient grounds to try the case in spain. Sebagaimana diketahui, the allegations emerged in january this year after a three-year joint investigation by the spanish news site eldiario. es and the Spanish-language TV network Univision Noticias, which gathered testimony from 15 former employees who worked for the now 83-year-old singer between the late 1990s and 2023.

In a statement released on Wednesday, the Audiencia Nacional said it was investigating the women’s complaint, which accuses Iglesias of “offences against sexual freedom, as well as offences involving bodily harm and degrading treatment”.

The investigating judge, Antonio Piña, said preliminary evidence offered by one of the complainants was sufficient to launch an investigation.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “a photograph of the complainant shows a bruise on one of her arms, consistent with her having been gripped forcefully,” said piña. “In the same photograph, two marks are visible on one of her thighs – marks that could correspond to a human bite – which the complaint states are the result of her being forced to participate in sexual acts. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa however, piña rejected the women’s allegations of human trafficking and labour offences, and also noted that some of the alleged offences may have expired under the statute of limitations. The judge has called the two women to give evidence in person on 3 February next year.

Iglesias, who has sold more than 300m records during his six-decade career, has denied all the allegations and said he would defend himself against what he described as “a serious affront”.

Waymo has temporarily suspended its driverless vehicles from operating on all US freeways, the company has said.

The decision comes after California banned Waymo's driverless taxis from state freeways following a series of recent traffic incidents.

California's Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) cited an "imminent hazard to public safety" for the ban, noting an incident this month in which several driverless Waymo vehicles entered an active construction zone on US Route 101.

Waymo said it was working with state officials "diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations", adding that no injuries or collisions were reported following the incident on US Route 101 south of San Francisco.

California's DMV said Waymo's driverless taxis presented a risk "due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present".

In another incident earlier this month, footage widely seen on social media appeared to show a Waymo car trying to overtake patrol vehicles that were deliberately slowing the pace of traffic on a San Francisco highway.

The California ban, which came into effect on 11 November, would remain in place until Waymo "demonstrates to the department that it has taken effective corrective actions to address the deficiencies that precipitated the restrictions".

Berdasarkan laporan, a waymo spokesperson said: "in alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance. ".

Data on Waymo's website suggests that its cars, compared to human drivers, are involved in 95% fewer crashes resulting in serious injury.

Waymo currently operates driverless taxis in 15 US cities, but only offered freeway rides in a handful of those locations, including San Francisco, Los Angeles and Miami.

The company's driverless taxis can continue to operate on regular city streets.

In May, Waymo recalled thousands of its self-driving cars in the US over a software issue that could allow vehicles to drive into flooded roads.

In the same month, multiple Waymo cars were spotted driving around a cul-de-sac in Atlanta, Georgia, in the early hours of the morning.

#1198. EU proposes €45bn loan for Ukraine to avert cash crisis and boost defences

📅 18 Nov 2026

EU proposes €45bn loan for Ukraine to avert cash crisis and boost defences

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/eu-loan-ukraine-cash-crisis-defences-von-der-leyen-kyiv

Von der Leyen says she wants to give Kyiv ‘strong hand’ in talks and is confident all 27 member states will back idea.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the eu executive has proposed a €45bn (£37. 5bn) loan for Ukraine to help with a looming cash crisis and reinforce its defences, as Russia’s relentless bombardment continues.

Sebagaimana diketahui, announcing the plan to lend kyiv the money in 2027, the european commission president, ursula von der leyen, said: “we think this is the best way to give ukraine a strong hand at the negotiating table. And Ukraine only needs to repay once Russia pays for the damage it has caused in Ukraine. ”.

She expressed confidence all 27 member states would stand behind the loan, despite four central and eastern European countries having already ruled themselves out.

The Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said he hoped for the swift adoption of the loan and was counting on the support of all EU member states: “Strong support for Ukraine is the best signal to Russia that this war must end,” he wrote on X.

Diungkapkan bahwa zelenskyy convinced eu leaders last month that his country faced a €70bn funding gap in 2027. The EU pledged to cover €45bn and wants Ukraine’s other allies to cover the rest.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, only 11 months ago, the eu agreed a €90bn loan for ukraine, which was intended to cover two-thirds of kyiv’s military and civilian needs in 2026 and 2027. But as Russia’s attacks have escalated, the cost of Ukraine’s defence and the toll of economic disruption continue to rise.

Diungkapkan bahwa andrius kubilius, the eu defence commissioner, said ukraine’s military spending was increasingly dominated by drones. Ukraine, he told reporters, expected Russia to use 10m drones this year and 20m in 2027. “Ukraine with EU assistance needs to match – and will match,” he said.

The EU loan is split into two parts: €25bn for weapons and €20bn for civilian needs, including funding essential services, such as schools and hospitals.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, von der leyen expressed confidence that all member states would support the loan because “all 27 member states say very clearly that they want to support ukraine”. She said member states could choose to support Ukraine’s civilian needs, rather than military spending.

Slovakia, Czechia, Hungary and Bulgaria, however, have said they do not intend to take part in the latest funding round for Ukraine, prompting a warning from the German chancellor, Friedrich Merz, that he would block the EU’s seven-year budget unless all countries got onboard.

The four central and eastern countries are net beneficiaries of the EU budget, while Germany is the largest payer and Ukraine’s biggest EU donor.

The EU wants Ukraine’s non-EU allies – such as Norway, the UK and Canada – to find €25bn for Kyiv in 2027.

The most pressing stories and debates for Europeans – from identity to economics to the environment.

Diungkapkan bahwa the eu proposal included provisions “to help other countries to help us”, a senior commission official said. Brussels has proposed that G7 countries that provide new loans get guarantees that the borrowing can be repaid with future profits from Russia’s frozen assets.

The profits from the Russian assets are being used to repay a €45bn loan issued by the G7 to Ukraine in 2024.

Diungkapkan bahwa countries with a triple-a credit rating could opt to provide guarantees to the eu budget up to €5bn to expand european borrowing for ukraine on capital markets. The commission has identified six countries that fall into this category: Australia, Canada, Liechtenstein, Norway, Singapore and Switzerland.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, eu officials previously said the uk and other allies needed to do more to support ukraine in 2027, arguing that the eu was shouldering too much of the burden. The UK subsequently pledged a £10bn economic and military support package for Ukraine.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, zelenskyy said: “the uk, canada, japan, and norway have been helping tremendously in our defence of life, and establishing clear rules under which they can provide further aid in conjunction with the eu will help even more. ”.

#1200. Rubio says US not 'under systemic attack' after series of tech outages

📅 18 Nov 2026

Rubio says US not 'under systemic attack' after series of tech outages

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/crkgvxxwpwz2o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Watch: Marco Rubio says recent tech outages are 'completely unrelated' to one another.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has dismissed widespread concerns online that the series of recent tech outages in the past week are connected, telling reporters there was "zero evidence" of any link.

Rubio acknowledged that "people are fearful" the spate of outages, which included all flights being grounded in the US and widespread disruptions to banking, Apple and Microsoft services, could be linked or part of a plot.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "we are not under systemic attack," he said. "These events, one has nothing to do with the other, they are not inter-related. ".

Cyber-security experts have agreed that there is no evidence linking the outages, and many of the issues appear due to updates to old infrastructure.

In the past week, there has been a massive Microsoft outage, an apparent tech glitch which grounded all US flights for hours, and issues for the National Security Agency, outages affecting the biggest US banks and Apple.

Every affected company or agency has said the issue was not cyber-related and not the work of an outside actor.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, rubio's comments came hours after us director of national intelligence jay clayton also addressed the issue, telling fox news the outages were not the product of a cyber-attack. He explained "lots of institutions" are patching or upgrading systems, which has caused some disruption.

Rubio was asked whether the Trump administration was concerned public fears could lead to stockpiling or a run on the banks.

He said the best way to combat such fears was for the US government to share everything they know with the American people.

"Every indicator we have is that every single one of these events has an explanation or a cause that has nothing to do with a cyber-criminal, has nothing to do with a hostile actor or another country," he said.

Technology-related disruptions have happened almost daily since Thursday, when a Microsoft outage disrupted many of its services, including email.

Berdasarkan laporan, the next day, the us federal aviation administration halted flights across the us for more than four hours with a rare national ground stop. It was the longest halting of flights since the 11 September 2001 attacks on the US.

The US transport secretary said the issue was technical and caused by a copper wire upgrade and outdated equipment.

On Monday, a United Airlines technology failure delayed about 150 flights and a JPMorgan Chase software problem disrupted service at the biggest and most utilised banks in the US.

Both United and Chase said a software issue was behind the glitch.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, apple users were impacted by outages affecting icloud and apple pay on tuesday. The company said the cause was not a cyber-attack but the outage was triggered by an an internal update.

The same day, a highly classified network used by the US National Security Agency (NSA) for internal communications also went offline for a period of time.

Passengers wait to check in at Los Angeles International Airport as flights resume after being grounded for several hours on November 13 due to a major communications outage.

Cybersecurity experts say there is no evidence connecting the Microsoft, airline, and bank disruptions from the last five days.

Kris Beevers, CEO and co-founder of the network and infrastructure management company NetBox Labs, acknowledged the circulating theories on social media linking the barrage of outages.

"There is no conspiracy here," he told the BBC.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "there is something more ordinary, and more important to understand: the infrastructure that runs the world is changing faster than ever, and change is risk. Much of it is 30 to 40 years old, with decades of technical debt, and it's now being asked to change very quickly. ".

Beevers said AI is only part of the story.

"It's putting more strain on these legacy networks, and it's also creating real urgency around security," he said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "our customers are the amazing teams behind these networks at airlines, banking, energy, and retail who are essentially doing heart surgery on a global scale to get these networks back up and running quickly. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, vice president of threat intelligence for palo alto networks unit 42, sherrod degrippo, said: "what this week really underscores is how tightly coupled, and fragile, our core digital infrastructure is, where a single software bug or router failure can cascade nationwide. ".

#1203. Irishman charged with destroying US military aircraft with axe

Irishman charged with destroying US military aircraft with axe

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cwd01jjl5zzzo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

The military plane, seen above, was effectively destroyed by the vandalism.

US officials have charged an Irishman with destroying a $60m (Â£45m) American military aircraft after he allegedly sneaked onto the tarmac of an airport in Ireland.

Daithi O'Corrain, 48, is accused of doing extensive research before he allegedly used chemicals and various tools - including an axe - to damage a US Air National Guard C-130 Hercules parked at Shannon Airport near Limerick.

American prosecutors have charged him with destruction of government property, which carries a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison.

O'Corrain is not currently in US custody, according to the Associated Press news agency, and it is unclear whether he has a lawyer who could speak on his behalf.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in filings unsealed by prosecutors in new york on tuesday, agents from the fbi argued that the act jeopardised us national security. They say the plane was parked at the airport while en route to another country on a US military assignment.

"As alleged, Daithi O'Corrain carried out a deliberate, planned attack against a US military aircraft, causing tens of millions of dollars in damage and jeopardizing critical military operations," prosecutors said in a court filing.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "this was not an act of spontaneous vandalism," said fbi assistant director in charge james barnacle jr, explaining o'corrain "spent months researching the aircraft, acquiring tools and materials, and preparing to maximize the destruction he could inflict. ".

Officials say that the suspect planned extensively for the 11 April 2026 raid, and brought tools with him for the demolition, which took place over several hours.

He entered the plane by breaking a locking mechanism, officials say, then used straps to close the doors before covering the windows.

"O'Corrain then proceeded to inflict severe damage to the interior of the Aircraft by, among other things, cutting wire bundles and hydraulic lines within the Aircraft, crimping a liquid oxygen line within the Aircraft, destroying every gauge in the Aircraft's cockpit, and puncturing the Aircraft's air ducts," the US indictment says.

He also used gallium, a substance that can erode aluminum and steel, ball bearings which he poured in the fuel tank, and an axe which he used to puncture the exterior of the plane.

Sebagaimana diketahui, he was caught by airport crew, and filmed standing on top of the plane. He was arrested at the scene, and charged by Ireland's national police with causing criminal damages.

O'Corrain seen standing on the rear of the aircraft in a handout from the US Department of Justice.

The US charges say that he had planned well, because he avoided cutting a line that would have risked causing massive explosion.

Berdasarkan laporan, according to the limerick post, external, o'corrain is from cork city. Supporters have described him as an anti-war activist.

Diungkapkan bahwa shannon airport is a key hub for us military personnel, and is frequently the scene of anti-war protests. It was used by President Donald Trump in September for his visit to Ireland.

US prosecutors note that there have been several breaches there in recent years by protesters, including in May 2025 when three people drove a van through a perimeter fence, and then again later that month when a US airplane was sprayed with paint, making it temporarily inoperable.

#1205. Labour faces double blow over UK fossil fuel projects

📅 18 Nov 2026

Labour faces double blow over UK fossil fuel projects

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/18/sse-threatens-to-close-yorkshire-gas-storage-site-unless-ministers-intervene

Big North Sea operator EnQuest says it is quitting oil basin, while SSE threatens to close Yorkshire gas storage site.

The energy secretary has been dealt a double blow after two UK companies signalled plans to pull their investment from a series of major fossil fuel projects over government policies.

One of the North Sea’s biggest independent companies, EnQuest, said on Wednesday it was quitting the oil basin to focus on making better returns in Asia, blaming the “uncertain investment environment within the UK”.

Separately, the energy company SSE told investors that next summer it would close one of the country’s largest gas storage sites, which is on the North Sea coast, unless the government intervened to offer support amid weak market conditions.

The tacit criticism is expected to pile pressure on Miatta Fahnbulleh, who became the energy secretary in July, to clarify the government’s plan to secure the UK’s gas supplies as households face a rise in energy bills this winter because of soaring gas costs.

EnQuest set out plans to sell its entire portfolio of UK oilfields to the biggest North Sea producer, Neo Next+, for up to $960m (£730m), weeks after the company urged the chancellor, John Healey, to use his budget in November to reform the industry’s tax regime.

The UK oil and gas industry warned after the budget that the Treasury’s decision to leave its planned North Sea tax changes until the end of the decade was “continuing to drive energy investment abroad”.

The British oil company BP is also in the process of exiting the North Sea after announcing in the summer that it would end six decades of production from the basin by selling its entire business there.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the enquest deal marks “another significant company exiting the uk continental shelf”, according to james hosie, an equity analyst at shore capital. He said the company had opted to leave after 16 years as a leading independent operator in the basin “rather than hold out for an improvement in the UK regulatory and fiscal regime for upstream oil and gas”.

SSE told investors that while its Atwick gas storage site in the north of England had a “strategic importance” to the energy system as the North Sea’s domestic production declined, it was “increasingly clear that existing market arrangements do not support their continued operation”.

Berdasarkan laporan, closing the atwick facility, near hornsea on the east yorkshire coast, would remove about 309m cubic metres of gas, or about 1. 5 days’ worth of Great Britain’s gas usage, from the UK’s storage capacity.

The site makes up a fifth of the country’s onshore gas storage capacity, or 7% when including the storage tanks at the UK’s liquified natural gas terminals and the Rough site, also at risk of closure unless its owner, Centrica, the parent company of British Gas, can agree a long-term financial support deal with the government.

The renewed concerns over supplies emerged on the same day that the National Energy System Operator (Neso) warned in a second consecutive annual report that the UK was at risk of a gas supply crisis as the North Sea’s production winds down.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the report echoed concerns that while the uk has enough access to global gas markets to cover demand when weather is normal, if even a single piece of britain’s ageing gas infrastructure suffered an “unlikely” outage during a very cold spell, then supplies could fall short of demand. This would lead to emergency measures such as shutting off gas supplies to factories, power plants and – in extreme scenarios – homes.

Get set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morning.

Energy companies typically rely on stockpiling gas in their storage facilities during the summer, when prices are usually lower because of weaker demand, before selling the gas at a profit during winter when demand for energy usually lifts market prices.

However, the gas price increases triggered by the Iran conflict this year and by Russia’s war on Ukraine in 2022 has upended normal market patterns, leading to historic market price highs during the summer that have made it uneconomical to stockpile gas ahead of winter.

As a result, countries across Europe have entered the cooler months of the year with gas stores at their lowest level in more than a decade.

Diungkapkan bahwa britain already stores less gas than some of its european neighbours and is instead more reliant on liquefied natural gas imports. The closure of a storage facility such as Atwick could leave the UK even more exposed to price shocks on global markets.

Diungkapkan bahwa last month, fahnbulleh gave the final approval for the jackdaw gasfield, which began producing gas for the first time earlier this week. She is expected to make a decision on whether to consent to oil production from the Rosebank field before the end of the year.

The government was approached for comment.

David Lammy urges Andy Burnham to fight next election on rejoining EU

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/18/david-lammy-andy-burnham-campaign-rejoining-eu-election-brexit

Exclusive: Former business secretary calls for Labour manifesto commitment with referendum on final decision.

Andy Burnham should fight the next election on a promise to rejoin the EU, the former business secretary Peter Kyle has said, with voters given a referendum on the outcome of any deal.

The Labour MP, a key member of Keir Starmer’s cabinet, said the “only way through” the challenges of the domestic political debate was for the government to offer voters the choice to accept or reject any agreement.

His intervention comes as the prime minister prepares for a major UK-EU summit in Brussels on Friday, at which he hopes to secure agreements on food and farming and emissions trading.

Burnham has said there was “no rush” to decide on the UK’s longer-term relationship with the EU, as he came under pressure from his own party to press the brakes on the pace of the promised pursuit of closer ties.

Despite his suggestions at Labour conference, he is now not expected to set out the full options for a closer EU relationship until his 10-year plan in December – although he has denied he is “stepping back” from commitments.

Kyle is the latest senior Labour figure to publicly wade into the Brexit debate after the former foreign secretary David Lammy said the party should go into the next election clear that its intention was to rejoin.

Rachel Reeves, the former chancellor, has also argued Britain’s future should be back in the bloc, arguing that leaving had made the UK “poorer, weaker and less secure”.

Kyle, who was the author of a key amendment on a second vote during the original parliamentary battles over Brexit, said a “halfway option” such as joining the customs union or single market was a “non-starter”.

Writing on his Substack blog, he said: “The only way through I see is for Labour to have in its next manifesto a commitment to begin negotiations for rejoining the EU, alongside a promise that any final decision to rejoin would be subject to a referendum on the actual terms.

Berdasarkan laporan, “a campaign based on a complex halfway option, weighted with sovereignty implications, would be the worst of all worlds. It would be seen as a stepping stone to full membership which, for most supporters, it would be. So let’s get quickly to the real choice we face: in or out. Politically, it would be a non-starter. ”.

Kyle said his Labour manifesto proposal would, in contrast, give voters two distinct propositions, the status quo or the known terms of rejoining, “with an electorate informed and able to scrutinise both”.

Berdasarkan laporan, he criticised the new pro-brexit campaign group stay out, which was set up by architects of the vote leave campaign and has claimed rejoining the eu would cost britain £750m a week. Kyle accused it of “making random claims” about the cost of rejoining that were “as good as fictitious”.

The former minister urged his fellow pro-Europeans not to suggest that every problem the UK faced could be solved by rejoining, saying there was “an awful lot of fixing, building and potential” for the UK economy that wasn’t based on it.

“We must act with urgency on these [issues] and not be seduced into believing an easy route to growth can be found in the single market that avoids tough decisions now,” Kyle said.

Sign up for the Breaking News UK email to get newsletter alerts direct to your inbox.

Lammy, who served as deputy prime minister under Starmer, said Burnham’s Liverpool conference speech “blew the door wide open” on the issue.

Diungkapkan bahwa “burnham’s labour should go into the next election clear that its intention is to rejoin the eu,” lammy wrote in the times. “Forming the next government would give it the mandate to begin formal negotiations.

Berdasarkan laporan, “once a deal is agreed, this should be put to the people. Unlike the last referendum, the public should have the opportunity to decide between two clearly defined choices. ”.

On Tuesday, Burnham denied the debate on rejoining had become “toxic”, reiterating that he would stick to Labour’s red lines before the general election, but the public would be “in charge” of what came next.

Steve Rosenberg: Historic talks with Xi and Trump are a coup for Putin

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c9n70gd320mpo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Nearly five years after the full-scale invasion of Ukraine turned him into a pariah, Putin is back on the global stage.

But Thursday's mini summit of Vladimir Putin, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping already looks like a win for the Kremlin.

Sebagaimana diketahui, think back to 2022. After Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine President Putin was an international pariah. Western leaders were determined to isolate him and his country over the war in Ukraine.

Berdasarkan laporan, fast forward to 2026: vladimir putin has secured an historic meeting in shenzhen. For the first time in history, the leaders of China, Russia and the United States will sit down â just the three of them â for talks.

That puts Putin exactly where he wants to be: at the top table of global politics, rubbing shoulders with the leaders of the two great powers.

It allows him to boast that Western pressure on Russia has failed.

"We see such examples in the failed attempts to isolate our country, Russia, which has faced unprecedented sanctions pressure," Putin told a business forum of the Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation organisation.

That was followed by a meeting with Xi Jinping.

But the Kremlin says the "showstopper" event in Shenzhen will be Putin's trilateral with Xi and Trump.

It allows him to play global statesman, even as the Russian military continues to pound Ukrainian towns and cities, and the Kremlin continues to reject the idea of an unconditional, comprehensive ceasefire.

Diungkapkan bahwa one short meeting is unlikely to reshape the world. But it's the optics that are key. The photo-op. The picture. Three leaders, three big powers, discussing big issues.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in a way, vladimir putin will use this meeting to send a holiday postcard to the rest of the world. Instead of "Wish you were here", he'll sign it: "Look: I'm here. ".

But what of those who are not at the table?.

Among European leaders, and especially in Ukraine, there is concern that the three-way meeting might produce more than just a pretty picture, though not in a good way for Kyiv.

Diungkapkan bahwa donald trump has already said that in shenzhen he wants to discuss his "favourite subject" - the war in ukraine. The Kremlin would likely welcome an opportunity to argue its case to Trump and Xi without Ukrainian officials or European leaders in the room.

Berdasarkan laporan, last month ukraine's president volodymyr zelensky expressed concern that the putin-trump-xi meeting might resemble the yalta conference of 1945. That is when the leaders of the Soviet Union, Britain and the United States â Joseph Stalin, Winston Churchill and Franklin D Roosevelt - met to re-organise post-World War Two Europe.

"We really don't want this to turn into 'Yalta 2, 3, 4' with a redistribution of influence," said Zelensky.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it is unclear whether china would want the ukraine war on the agenda in shenzhen. In its official statements on the upcoming trilateral meeting, Beijing has talked more generally about the need to discuss "safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability".

Diungkapkan bahwa in shenzhen, russia will make the most of the optics. But a diplomatic victory is not the same as a military one.

Nearly five years after President Putin launched his so-called "special military operation", Russia is still struggling to win its war on Ukraine.

Over this time, it has suffered huge losses on the battlefield.

Sebagaimana diketahui, and the ukrainian strike on the road bridge linking russia to the crimean peninsula â carried out on the eve of the summit - was a blow to moscow's prestige. The attack severely damaged part of the multi-billion-dollar bridge built by Russia after it annexed Crimea from Ukraine.

The damage is not only a logistical headache for the Russian authorities.

It is a reminder that the Kremlin's "special operation" has not gone at all to plan.

The Shenzhen summit may give Vladimir Putin a big stage, and a bright spotlight.

It does not necessarily bring him closer to winning the war.

#1215. Can a US-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo?

📅 18 Nov 2026

Can a US-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo?

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cx053jrv9rz9o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

The Lobito Corridor links DR Congo's mineral-rich south to Angola's Atlantic coast through the Benguela Railway and the Port of Lobito.

As trains carrying thousands of tonnes of copper from the Democratic Republic of Congo roar through her community, 20-year-old Manuela Julia is not thinking about critical minerals or billion-dollar investments.

She is thinking about getting around more easily.

The railway runs through Catumbela, near the Angolan city of Lobito, on the Atlantic coast.

For Julia, it has made travelling cheaper and more convenient.

Diungkapkan bahwa "before, i had to use a taxi, which is much more expensive. Now it is cheaper and easier to travel," she says.

But the railway has ambitions far bigger than improving local transport.

It is part of the Lobito Corridor, a US-backed effort to secure access to Africa's critical minerals and promote regional economic cooperation, which Washington hopes will help bring peace to conflict-torn eastern DR Congo.

Under agreements brokered by US President Donald Trump, DR Congo and neighbouring Rwanda have committed to greater economic cooperation, including more transparent mineral supply chains and regional infrastructure development.

The wider plan envisages linking these initiatives to the railway, which transports minerals from Central Africa to Western markets via Angola, rather than east to China as most do currently.

The hope is that formalising the mineral trade and encouraging investment could help curb illicit markets that have helped finance armed groups and fuel instability.

Manuela Julia says the railway has made travelling around easier.

But can a railway built to move minerals to global markets also deliver peace and prosperity?.

The Lobito Corridor links DR Congo's mineral-rich south to Angola's Atlantic coast through the Benguela Railway and the Port of Lobito.

Its importance has grown as demand for copper and cobalt rises, driven partly by the global transition to cleaner energy, as both are critical ingredients for all kinds of electrical components.

"The timing matters," says Johannesburg-based political risk analyst Wellington Muzengeza.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "electrification and the energy transition have increased the strategic importance of copper, cobalt and reliable mineral supply chains. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, dr congo is the world's largest producer of cobalt and one of its biggest copper producers, along with neighbouring zambia. The US sees the corridor as a means to diversify mineral supplies and reduce reliance on China, which dominates much of the world's processing capacity.

A US-DR Congo strategic partnership identifies the route from the Congolese town of Sakania to Lobito as a priority for mineral exports, while the economic framework agreed by DR Congo and Rwanda envisages connecting regional infrastructure and trade initiatives to the corridor.

The project has attracted over $750m (Â£570m), including funding backed by the US International Development Finance Corporation and the Development Bank of Southern Africa to upgrade railway tracks, signalling systems and trains.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the railway, built in 1902 under portuguese colonial rule, was originally designed to transport goods and minerals from central africa to the atlantic coast. After years of disruption during Angola's civil war, it was rebuilt and fully reopened in 2015.

The US first got involved in the project under former President Joe Biden but backing has continued under Trump.

At Lobito's mineral terminal, the renewed ambitions are already visible.

Berdasarkan laporan, when the bbc visited, a train carrying about 12,000 tonnes of copper cathodes from dr congo had arrived. Workers moved the refined copper sheets into a warehouse before they were loaded on to ships bound for international markets, mostly the US.

The cargo is handled by Lobito Atlantic Railway (LAR), which has a 30-year concession to operate freight services along the corridor and manage the mineral terminal.

The Lobito Atlantic Railway has a 30-year concession to operate freight services along the corridor.

Chief operating officer Nicholas Gregoir says freight volumes have more than doubled since the company took over in January 2024.

LAR expects to transport about 200,000 tonnes of copper through the corridor in 2026.

For mining companies, the railway offers a shorter route to international markets.

"The Lobito Corridor is the shortest route for both Zambia and the DRC," to the Atlantic, says KÃ¡tila Vanessa Monteiro da Silva Neto, executive director of the Lobito Port Authority.

Zambia, Africa's second-largest copper producer, also plans to connect its Copperbelt to Lobito through a proposed 830km (515 mile)-railway.

But a more efficient route to market does not automatically translate into economic transformation.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "joining a corridor is not the same as industrialising," muzengeza says. It is whether that route helps build a stronger economy. "The test is not simply whether Zambia gains another route to the sea. ".

Some Angolans believe the railway's greatest value could lie in what it offers businesses and communities beyond mining.

"I call it a corridor of development," says businessman AdÃ©rito Areias.

The railway passes through some of Angola's most productive agricultural regions.

Better transport links could help farmers reach larger markets and reduce losses.

"If there isn't an artery carrying products from the interior to where there is demand, those products simply rot where they are produced," Areias says.

But the challenge is turning that ambition into reality.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the port of lobito handled about 1. Its mineral terminal can handle up to 3. 8 million tonnes of cargo in 2025, of which around 158,000 tonnes was minerals. 6 million tonnes annually.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "the port already has the capacity," says neto. "What we need now is sufficient railway capacity and rolling stock. ".

For residents along the route, the benefits have been immediate.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, state-owned railway operator caminho de ferro de benguela (cfb), which runs passenger services, carried a record 1. 6 million passengers in 2025.

LAR says it directly employs nearly 1,000 people, 98% of them Angolan.

"This job allows me to support my family," says Domingos Canhama, a father of four and a forklift operator at CFB.

"I can put food on the table, maintain a home and help support my father," he says.

Muzengeza argues that the bigger opportunity is developing local businesses in engineering, maintenance, warehousing and agricultural processing.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "businesses in angola need access to the railway, not just proximity to it. That means feeder roads, electricity, storage and predictable services," he says.

But can minerals and their movement along the railways line help deliver peace to eastern DR Congo, where the battle for control of mineral resources has fuelled decades of conflict?.

Domingos Canhama, a forklift operator at the Lobido railway company says the job has helped him support his family.

Most recently, this has seen the M23 rebel group seize control of many mineral-rich areas.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the congolese government says neighbouring rwanda is backing the m23 in order to gain access to dr congo's mineral wealth. Despite overwhelming evidence, Rwanda denies backing the M23.

The Trump-backed agreements between DR Congo and Rwanda seek to promote transparent mineral supply chains, cross-border investment and regional infrastructure, with the aim of ensuring mineral wealth does not finance armed groups.

"The US wants reliable access to minerals essential to defence, advanced technology and energy systems, while reducing dependence on supply chains in which China has substantial influence," says Muzengeza, the political risk analyst.

Diungkapkan bahwa "lobito is therefore more than a railway but an infrastructure that can reshape trade routes and commercial power. ".

At a meeting in Paris in November, DR Congo urged the US to turn its strategic partnership into tangible investments, arguing that success should be measured by completed projects rather than signed agreements.

"We want the partnership to support â local mineral processing, electricity access for households and businesses and peace in the east," said DR Congo's Economy Minister Daniel Mukoko Samba.

Even if more minerals move through formal channels, better infrastructure alone would not resolve the political and security tensions driving the conflict.

Diungkapkan bahwa there is also the question of who captures the wealth. Much of the copper and cobalt transported from DR Congo through Lobito is destined for processing and manufacturing outside Africa.

While Angola can earn transit fees and create logistics jobs, much of the higher-value activity takes place elsewhere.

"When you export raw materials, you are also exporting jobs and knowledge," Angola's Foreign Affairs Minister TÃ©te AntÃ³nio tells the BBC.

"We should not export lithium but export batteries," he says, arguing that the corridor should help develop local processing and manufacturing rather than simply accelerate raw material exports.

Back in Catumbela, such debates can feel distant from everyday life.

For Julia, the railway already means cheaper journeys and easier movement.

But its ultimate success will depend on whether it can deliver more than faster mineral exports.

Whether it can also help secure lasting peace in eastern DR Congo, where the minerals are mined, remains the bigger test.

#1216. India: Online censorship grows after 'Cockroach' protests

📅 18 Nov 2026

India: Online censorship grows after 'Cockroach' protests

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.dw.com/en/india-online-censorship-grows-after-cockroach-protests/a-79976982?maca=en-rss-en-all-1573-rdf

Since anti-government Cockroach protests erupted, journalists and creators say their content is increasingly being restricted on social media in India.

Berdasarkan laporan, a video showing a young girl crying as she spoke about alleged police brutality during the youth-led cockroach janata party (cjp) protests in july. A video examining the Hindu nationalist Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh's (RSS) contribution to the rise of India's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). A satirical cartoon criticizing Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government.

These are among the examples of content that have recently been restricted on social media in India.

Sebagaimana diketahui, content creator citysavitri describes herself as a "nobody" in the world of social media. She had started making videos just two months ago and had around 600 followers on Instagram.

Berdasarkan laporan, yet a video looking at the rss's role in the bjp's 2014 election victory was restricted in india within an hour of being posted. It was the first of three videos she posted that faced restrictions.

The experience made her feel that "anti-government commentary" was being monitored and curtailed.

"It is very plain and simple to understand," the content creator told DW.

Independent journalist Sadhika Tiwari was covering the CJP protest in New Delhi on July 20, when police used batons and tear gas against demonstrators.

Tiwari's video of a frightened young girl crying and speaking about police brutality garnered around 10 million views within hours, she said, before it was restricted in India.

Political cartoonist Satish Acharya has also faced repeated restrictions, with Instagram blocking his profile twice recently.

In May 2025, during the conflict between India and Pakistan, independent digital news outlet Maktoob Media's X account was withheld in India while it was reporting on the escalating crisis, its founder and editor Aslah Kayyalakkath told DW.

Diungkapkan bahwa "we received no official notice or email from either the government or x. It was our readers who first alerted us to the blocking," he said.

Berdasarkan laporan, maktoob media said it contacted indian officials and x but received no response. Access to the account was restored a few days later, again without an explanation.

Sebagaimana diketahui, kayyalakkath said maktoob's content from the july protest also faced restrictions. "Suppressing independent journalism undermines transparency, accountability and democratic values," he said.

Several of the content creators and journalists interviewed by DW said they received no prior notification or explanation for the restrictions.

Some users were not sure if their content had been blocked at the government's request or proactively by the social media platforms.

When asked for comment, Meta, the parent company of Facebook and Instagram, pointed DW to a website statement noting users can appeal content and account restrictions.

Berdasarkan laporan, at the heart of the debate are india's it rules, 2021, amended in february 2026. Section 79 of India's IT Act protects social media platforms and other intermediaries from liability for content posted by third parties, provided they meet certain legal conditions.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one such requirement, introduced through the february 2026 amendments, is to remove or disable access to specified unlawful content within three hours of receiving a valid court order or a reasoned government notice. The previous deadline was 36 hours.

Failure to comply can result in intermediaries losing their liability protection.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The government's Sahyog portal, which coordinates takedown requests between law enforcement, platforms and telecom providers, has faced criticism over the pace at which notices are issued.

Sebagaimana diketahui, meta said it uses automated tools and technologies to detect and review content that may violate its community standards. It also automatically restricts access to certain types of content in India to comply with legal requirements under the IT rules.

Pranesh Prakash, a technology law and policy adviser, said the amended rules allow authorized police officials to notify intermediaries about content they consider unlawful without necessarily filing a formal complaint or initiating other legal proceedings.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "this has led to the worst period of social media censorship that india has ever seen, with digital news media accounts being blocked, cartoonists' accounts being blocked, and even mere discussions of an opposition leader's memoirs being blocked," he said. "Clearly, none of these disclosed any 'unlawful acts. '".

Prakash also raised concerns about the lack of public information on government requests to remove content, saying this made it difficult to assess the scale of restrictions.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the software freedom law center, india (sflc. in), a digital rights organization, said the growing reliance on automated takedowns raised serious concerns about transparency, accountability and due process.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "there is little transparency about the processes through which content is identified, flagged and restricted, or whether there is any meaningful human oversight before a takedown is implemented," sflc. in told DW.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the organization also tested x's verification process by submitting a takedown request against one of its own posts using a fake email address. X registered the request, raising questions about how it verified the identity and authority of those submitting requests.

Sebagaimana diketahui, after sflc. in alerted the company, X introduced email verification codes for people submitting takedown requests.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "a channel that lets anyone pose as a law enforcement official can be misused to silence lawful speech," sflc. in said.

X did not respond to DW's request for a comment.

The Indian government denies that it is censoring online content.

Berdasarkan laporan, while the ministry did not respond to dw's latest request for a comment, in an email response to dw in august, vinod kumar, chief of media and communications at the information technology ministry, said instagram posts by students and protesters following the july cjp protests "are not being taken down as alleged. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa "media enjoys freedom in india. The Government does not censor online content," Kumar said, adding that the government only acts against "objectionable content. ".

Under the Indian IT rules, "unlawful content" generally refers to material which could threaten India's sovereignty and integrity, disturb public order, incite violence, or constitute defamation.

Diungkapkan bahwa however, social media influencers such as university professor madri kakoti, alias dr. Medusa, continue to report restrictions. Kakoti's Instagram account was restricted in India on November 16 without notice, she said, along with that of satirist Shamita Yadav.

Rights groups including Human Rights Watch have warned that expanding content restrictions could chill free expression and encourage self-censorship among journalists, creators and ordinary users.

Acharya, however, said he would continue his work.

Diungkapkan bahwa "the indian constitution gives me the right to draw political cartoons," he said. "It's totally democratic to question and criticize the government in India. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, for tiwari, the issue goes beyond the reach of a single video. It is also about preserving a record of what happened, after the Delhi Police denied allegations of using excessive force during the July 20 protest in front of the Supreme Court.

"We have seen several other videos now, and it's well established why that girl was crying, and that the Delhi Police used force and lied about it," she said.

Berdasarkan laporan, "still, i want that video back up because it needs to stay for posterity. I think that's the larger idea: they want to take this stuff down so it fades from memory, allowing them to categorically deny it later when we have little left to show for what happened. ".

#1218. Pakistan's solar revolution is so successful the national grid is lagging behind

📅 17 Nov 2026

Pakistan's solar revolution is so successful the national grid is lagging behind

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ckvg2n2q3103o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Faizal Shahzad wants to buy several more solar panels to make his home in rural Punjab fully self-sufficient.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, jewellery, glimmering silverware, sofas and an air-conditioning unit. Three months after his wedding, Faisal Shahzad's home in rural Punjab is bursting with gifts from his bride's family, as part of the dowry.

But the most prized possession is tucked under the bed: a 340W solar panel.

Diungkapkan bahwa "in the summer we ran it from 08:00 in the morning until the evening," he says, adding they didn't need to use grid power at all during the day. "We ran our air cooler on it all day. ".

Pakistan has seen a boom in imported solar panels, which glisten from the rooftops of homes and hospitals; from farmers' fields to industrial complexes.

From 2018 to 2025, the share of electricity generated from solar energy in the country rose from 1% to 28%, according to Pakistan-based think tank Renewables First, with some seven million households now owning panels.

Diungkapkan bahwa people used to gift motorbikes or other household items at weddings, shahzad says. It has almost become a must. "Now they give a solar panel and an air cooler. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, alongside the solar panel he still uses the national grid to meet his energy needs, particularly as he lives in a house with his family and brothers' families, who often use multiple appliances simultaneously. But in a country where the average wage is just under 40,000 Pakistani rupees (Â£110; $145) per month, bills are becoming unaffordable, rising to 15,000-18,000 rupees.

Berdasarkan laporan, this year, cop31 is pushing the world to move away from fossil-powered vehicles, boilers and other greenhouse gas-emitting equipment. And while Pakistan has become a poster child for solarisation, the national grid system is experiencing knock-on eï¬ects.

Berdasarkan laporan, the big pivot to solar wasn't driven by government policy but by individual pakistani households. Most people we spoke to said they installed panels to escape soaring electricity prices from an often unreliable national grid.

Electricity tariffs have more than doubled in a few years, says Muhammad Hassan Dajana, industry liaison at Renewables First, while the cost of Chinese solar panels has "decreased by 93%".

Berdasarkan laporan, "people have just found another way to be able to survive," says energy minister awais ahmad leghari. The people have reacted and responded in a very economically viable and efficient manner. We have adapted to the situation. "It's a very healthy thing. ".

While the solar boom brings clear benefits, particularly for a country that imports huge amounts of fuel, there are worries too.

Pakistan needs to avoid the so-called utility death spiral.

Berdasarkan laporan, when people buy less energy from the national grid, fewer customers are left to cover the fixed costs of maintaining it. That can force prices up - which in turn encourages even more people to switch to solar.

Over time, this can lead to a two-tier system in which those who can't afford to buy panels face ever-rising bills, while the national grid becomes an increasing burden on the state.

"You'll have a white elephant in the form of a state-owned enterprise that requires a lot of public funding to just stay afloat," says Dajana.

More and more households are installing solar panels, as seen here in Karachi, but Pakistanis still need energy from the national grid.

Pakistan's government says the costs are already being felt.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "in just the past two years, the exodus from the grid has cost the rest of the consumers more than $500 million [â£378m] a year," says leghari. "That's a very big burden. ".

The government doesn't want to pull people away from solar, he explains, but wants the grid to be more competitive to be able to offer better energy prices.

Diungkapkan bahwa private power producers, which feed into the grid, have been heavily criticised inside pakistan for locking the country into costly, inflexible contracts. Producers themselves point to broader structural problems like poor grid maintenance as contributing to higher bills. Leghari says the government has renegotiated most of the contracts and is now focused on making the grid more efficient with better storage, less waste and more innovation.

Leghari wants the country to run on "up to 90% clean power" by the end of 2036 - including renewables and nuclear - with dependence on imported energy reducing from 26% to 4%.

The solar power boom in Pakistan and the Philippines.

Cheap solar panels, mainly imported from China, are transforming lives and slashing electricity bills across Asia.

But as the government tries to improve the grid, solar is still expanding with widespread adoption in industry.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, kohinoor textiles mills in islamabad, which is powered by a sea of huge blue solar panels, is one example. Utilities manager Sabawoon Khan describes them as his "baby", pointing at construction work levelling the ground for more panels.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when the sun shines, the mills' hundreds of machines are powered entirely by solar energy, khan says. The heavy-furnace-oil engines they once relied on sit mothballed in a warehouse.

Diungkapkan bahwa but there are limits. When it's too cloudy or polluted, and during the night, the company takes more energy from the national grid. In the coming weeks, like other firms, it will start using industrial batteries which can store excess solar energy.

"We needed to reduce our energy costs and this was one way to do it," says Taufique Sayeed Saigol, the mills' CEO, who adds the plan is not to disconnect from the grid altogether.

Berdasarkan laporan, "the state unfortunately doesn't have the resources so we can't really say that we blame everything on the state. We do some of the things ourselves. ".

Rows of large solar panels power this textiles factory in Islamabad for large parts of the day.

Sebagaimana diketahui, critics accuse the government of moving the goalposts on solar power. Previously, households could feed excess electricity into the grid and earn credits, which were then used to offset the cost of grid power when the sun wasn't shining. That policy changed earlier this year.

Diungkapkan bahwa "initially their policy was very helpful," says arif ehsan malik, president of faisalabad's chamber of commerce. "But then the policy changed. Now they have started purchasing at a lower rate and selling back at a higher rate. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa malik says that makes a big difference for small and medium businesses. Leghari counters that the costs of the initial model didn't add up; the electricity the solar producers put into the system was much cheaper than the electricity they ended up taking out of it.

Diungkapkan bahwa "those profits were coming at the cost of the rest of the consumers of the grid. Had we not changed those regulations, the rest of the consumers would have been burdened by at least 150 to 200 billion rupees a year, say, two years from now. ".

Muhammad Hassan Dajana from Renewables First believes that with the right policy, Pakistan could become a global example of a successful energy transition.

Despite admitting that the first wave of solar adoption was a "surprise" to the government, Leghari says he has no fear that solar could outrun their plans, saying it has been incorporated into their 10-year forecasts and the numbers leaving the grid have slowed.

Pakistan has big ambitions for solar; there are plans to open solar battery factories around the country and encourage more electric vehicles.

Berdasarkan laporan, "there are two paths ahead," dajana says. One is a future where solar and the grid work in parallel, demonstrating how a gradual energy transition can succeed. The other is where Pakistan becomes a cautionary tale, burdened with a costly, declining grid.

Shahzad's solar ambitions for his home in rural Punjab certainly have not slowed.

"We plan to get another 10-15 panels and install them on the roof, then connect a full system with batteries and back up.

Diungkapkan bahwa "the plan is to be fully self-sufficient. ".
