#1219. Burnham urges Badenoch to withdraw ‘crass’ comment defending disability cuts on grounds ‘amputees run marathons’ – UK politics live

📅 18 Nov 2026

Burnham urges Badenoch to withdraw ‘crass’ comment defending disability cuts on grounds ‘amputees run marathons’ – UK politics live

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/politics/live/2026/nov/18/shabana-mahmood-andy-burnham-kemi-badenoch-pmqs-latest-news-updates

PM and leader of the opposition clashed at PMQs over welfare.

Berdasarkan laporan, badenoch says that reply makes it sound like burnham is not planning cuts. He says young people cannot wait 10 years. With Burnham, everything takes 10 years, she says.

She says working-age welfare is set to rise.

Diungkapkan bahwa keir starmer could not make welfare cuts because mps now in burnham’s cabinet led a rebellion against it. That shows they are the welfare party.

Burnham says Badenoch only ever asks for cuts.

He says Helen Whately, the shadow DWP secretary, said hundreds of thousands of disabled people would lose benefits under Tory plans.

The biggest rise in Neets came under the Tories, he says.

He says he will give hope to young people.

Policing in England and Wales will be restructured into about 200 local commands, Shabana Mahmood, the home secretary, has said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, under what the home office claims will be “the biggest reforms to policing in 200 years”, the government will set up around 200 new “local police commands” (lpcs). They will deal with routine crime like burglary, vehicle theft and antisocial behaviour.

Announcing the changes, the Home Office said:.

double quotation markSince the government unveiled plans in January to fundamentally restructure the policing model, much focus has been on reducing the number of forces at a regional level.

However, delivering a keynote speech to police leaders today, Shabana Mahmood announced she will build a structure from the bottom up with a larger number of smaller commands that will focus solely on the needs of their local area.

LPCs will be the foundation of the new policing model, focused on keeping neighbourhoods safe and tackling crimes like burglary, vehicle theft, phone theft and antisocial behaviour.

Each one will be situated closer to the areas they serve, with decision making driven by local knowledge and understanding.

Sebagaimana diketahui, broadly aligned to the geographical boundaries of councils, lpcs will cover towns or rural areas. This will also allow police to work in closer partnership with other local services such as probation, health and housing and improve outcomes.

A new local police guarantee will ensure every LPC delivers the same high-quality local policing, no matter where in the country they serve.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the home office said that this move would be the first step towards a wider programme of police reform. There are 43 police forces in England and Wales and in January Mahmood published a white paper setting out plans for some of them to be merged. The Home Office has been looking at plans for a much smaller number of regional police forces, but progress has been held up because how these would fit alongside Andy Burnham’s plans to give mayoral authorities more say over policing remains unresolved.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the home office news release suggests lpcs will be at the bottom of the policing pyramid, and the national police service at the top. It does not say what happens in between.

double quotation markEvery LPC will have a named commander, accountable to their local community and elected officials, with communities able to have a role in setting their local priorities.

Sebagaimana diketahui, above them will sit specialist services that will lead investigations on the most serious and complex crimes. They will be responsible for delivering specialist functions such as public order, forensics and firearms.

This will guarantee that no matter where anyone is, they will have access to expert specialist policing which the current system does not provide.

The new system will also remove the administrative duplication that exists across the existing 43 police headquarters, freeing up thousands of police officers to return to neighbourhood policing.

The final structure within policing would be the National Police Service which will tackle nationwide and international threats.

It will bring together the world-leading capabilities of Counter Terrorism Policing and other agencies, ensuring that policing has the technology, intelligence and resources needed to tackle crime in the 21st century.

Andy Burnham has said that Kemi Badenoch should withdraw her “crass and insensitive” comment justifying cuts to disability benefits on the grounds that “double amputees run marathons”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, after badenoch used this line in a speech last week, the paralympian richard whitehead posted a message on facebook criticising her. He said:.

double quotation markDisability should never be judged through isolated examples of individual achievement, but through an understanding of the barriers people and families face every day.

Diungkapkan bahwa the fact that some double-leg amputees can run marathons does not mean that disability support is unnecessary. Equally, the fact that some people with ADHD thrive despite limited support does not mean that others do not need meaningful assistance.

In subsequent remarks, Whitehead said that Badenoch’s comments were “divisive” and that he was “gobsmacked that somebody’s sporting success would be weaponised in this way”.

At PMQs today, the Labour MP Charlotte Nichols asked Burnham whether he agreed with Whitehead that “the achievements of our sports men and women with disabilities should never be weaponised against others”.

Berdasarkan laporan, double quotation marki thought the comments by richard whitehead do deserve a response from the right honourable lady [badenoch]. They were crass and insensitive, and I think she should withdraw them.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, guardian readers probably don’t need much persuading that pmqs is a terrible forum for reasonable debate, and there was a good example today that shows why. Badenoch is patronising, particularly at PMQs. In his final response to Kemi Badenoch, Burnham accused her of adopting a “patronising tone”. If there were a world championships for being patronising, she would be leading the UK team. This was uncharacteristically personal, and it lit up on social media as about the most interesting line from the exchange, with some commentators implying it was a gaffe. In reality, of course, it was probably one of the least contentious things Burnham said. Yet Burnham will probably conclude that it was a mistake, and something he shouldn’t have said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, why? because it made him look a bit rattled. Burnham came into office determined to pursue “problem solving, not point scoring”, but increasingly that is looking like a lost cause and the centrifugal power of PMQs yanks him back into a slanging match. ) Today, speaking to the Tory leader, he seemed to devote more time than ever to attacking her party’s record, rather than seeking common ground. On the plus side, the points he was making about the Conservatives’ record, and about her policy agenda now consisting of little more than welfare cuts, were forceful. (He is not always like this with opposition backbenchers, but he is – inevitably – with Badenoch. On the negative side, he sounded like someone on the defensive.

Diungkapkan bahwa just as she did last week, badenoch was reasonably good at delivering the sort of broad-brush ‘you’re rubbish’ messaging that would work as a headline for a daily express op ed. But it was hard to discern what particular attack line she wanted to land. There was a time when she would arrive at PMQs with a pre-prepared gotcha question and afterwards, normally following Keir Starmer’s refusal to answer, CCHQ would send out a press release highlighting the alleged implications of the question-dodging. There was none of that today, or last week.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, one of badenoch’s most interesting claims was that burnham is just offering the “vibes” of welfare reform, not the real thing. But that claim is so wide of the mark it is unlikely to work even with a Tory audience. The Milburn plan may have its drawbacks, but it is absurd to dismiss it as just vibes.

Berdasarkan laporan, sky news also set badenoch up for another attack, highlighting alan milburn saying yesterday that some people would lose from the reforms, while burnham said in a separate interview he did not want anyone to lose out. It was a classic case of apples and pears; Milburn was saying people will lose out from the benefit cuts, while Burnham was saying that, because those cuts are part of a strategy intended to divert off benefits into work, in the long run they wouldn’t lose out. Mindful, perhaps, of the ‘if you’re explaining, you’re losing’ theory of political communications, Burnham did not want to clarify this, and he just sidestepped her question. Badenoch then did not pursue the point, which was strange because a follow-up question could have made it much more awkward for him.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, burnham says there was action in the employment rights act to tackle this, but the government could go further, he says. He says they will look to see if this can be extended to freelancers.

Berdasarkan laporan, burnham says he does not know the details. This sounds like an issue for the Tories, he says. But he says he will arrange a meeting for Khan about this.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, andrew george (lib dem) says the budget will reward second home owners who let their homes. They will get a tax benefit. This is public money that could be better spent helping people in housing need.

Berdasarkan laporan, burnham says he asked officials to look seriously at the bill. “It was felt that it wasn’t the best way to address the issues, but we don’t disagree with what he’s trying to do,” he says. He says he will arrange for the housing minister to meet George.

Sebagaimana diketahui, shivani raja (con) says leicestershire police has been “issuing dual identity warrant cards for gender fluid officers”. She says that is absurd, and she urges the government to stop this.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, burnham says the government has been “relentless in tackling violence against women and girls in every single respect”. He says he is not aware of this issue, but will look into it.

Burnham says he would encourage the area to put in an application.

Burnham says he is encouraging the Welsh government to devolve powers further down.

#1220. The seven Anthropic founders who are about to become multi-billionaires

📅 18 Nov 2026

The seven Anthropic founders who are about to become multi-billionaires

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cmd7159vlr85o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Brother and sister Dario and Daniela Amodei.

In the space of just five years, Anthropic has gone from unknown start-up to tech giant, worth more than a trillion dollars.

The company behind the AI platform Claude was formed by seven people who left rival OpenAI in 2021 and, in a matter of hours, will become multi-billionaires - on paper at least.

Anthropic is floating the business on the US stock exchange and will sell its shares at between $70 - $78 each.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if they go for the highest price, the founders' shareholdings will be worth at least $18. 5bn each.

So, who are these people, all in their thirties and forties, who are about to become incredibly wealthy?.

In 2020, Dario Amodei was working for OpenAI, the firm that brought generative artificial intelligence to a mainstream audience, when it launched Chat-GPT.

He decided he wanted to do things his own way, and left, taking his sister Daniela, and five colleagues with him.

Amodei grew up in San Francisco, impressing school friends not just with his academic prowess but also his speed on the running track, and his preoccupation with philosophical and technological questions including the potential of machines to gain consciousness and human longevity.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, initially he studied physics at princeton and stanford. But following his father's death from hepatitis C, he switched to biology and biomedical sciences.

Amodei did stints at the Chinese tech giant Baidu and Google before joining OpenAI.

But he began to worry that some people within the company were putting profit before safety, prompting the decision to jump ship.

Now 43, he is Anthropic's chief executive, and the person who, in his sister's words, makes the company "ambitious".

Berdasarkan laporan, dario and daniela amodei, were close growing up and later shared a flat together in san francisco with other friends. She followed him into OpenAI and joined him when he left to found Anthropic.

She and her brother have always genuinely liked each other, she says, but the only thing she ever did first, was when he followed her in becoming vegetarian.

Amodei studied English Literature at the University of California Santa Cruz, going on to work for Democrat representative Matt Cartwright.

She has also worked at financial services platform Stripe, where she was head of risk operations.

The 39-year-old is president of Anthropic, manages the executive team, and leads the firm's research, engineering, product, governance and commercial work.

Tom Brown, now 39, followed the Amodei siblings when they left to found their new venture.

He led GPT-3 engineering at OpenAI, and prior to that was at Google on its DeepMind project.

Brown established his entrepreneurial credentials co-founding an app called "Grouper" that helps set up drinks between groups of friends.

He has supported US President Donald Trump's stance on datacentres, arguing that they are "an enormous source of prosperity".

Now as chief compute officer at Anthropic he is responsible for how the company secures and uses its computing resources.

Jack Clark, is another arts graduate among the original start-up's founding members and the only one who is not from North America.

Originally from Brighton in the UK, he studied English Literature and Creative Writing at the University of East Anglia and became a technology journalist, writing for publications including ZDNet UK, The Register, and Bloomberg.

He was caught up in the excitement of artificial intelligence and joined OpenAI, where he worked initially in communications, later becoming its policy director.

Sebagaimana diketahui, now, 37, clark is head of public benefit at anthropic. He also leads the Anthropic Institute, an AI think tank.

Sebagaimana diketahui, jared kaplan, 42, is chief science officer at anthropic, and heads its technical research. He is also an associate professor at Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore.

He holds a PhD in physics from Harvard University.

His work on scaling laws - which describe mathematical patterns that show that bigger AI models trained on more data tend to be more consistent - has helped provide AI firms with a framework for predicting AI behaviour, according to Anthropic.

Chris Olah is described as "interpretability research lead" primarily focused on how AI models work with each other.

But according to the New York Times, Olah has spent much of the last year convening meetings with faith leaders from across the religious spectrum.

Described by the newspaper as "boyish" but with "the zeal of an evangelist" the 34-year-old is reportedly exploring the relationship between morality and AI.

He previously led interoperability research at OpenAI, and prior to that was a research scientist at Google Brain.

The Canadian left Toronto University early, but later secured a Thiel Fellowship of $100,000, which is a scholarship to help gifted people move into research without a degree.

Berdasarkan laporan, sam mccandlish, 36, takes less of a public-facing role than the other founders, but like them will own around 1. 6% of the company after its shares go on sale. As a result he too will see his stake crystallise into a hugely valuable asset.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, mccandlish is anthropic's chief architect, and helps shape and implement the company's policy designed to mitigate the risks of ai. Prior to this he worked on safety at OpenAI.

He has a physics PhD from Stanford, and maths and physics degree from Brandeis University outside Boston.

#1221. ICJ to rule on Rohingya genocide case against Myanmar: What to know

📅 18 Nov 2026

ICJ to rule on Rohingya genocide case against Myanmar: What to know

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.dw.com/en/icj-to-rule-on-rohingya-genocide-case-against-myanmar-what-to-know/a-79981434?maca=en-rss-en-all-1573-rdf

The ICJ is set to decide whether Myanmar's military operations in Rakhine State a decade ago were carried out with the intent to destroy the country's Rohingya minority, in whole or in part.

The International Court of Justice (ICJ) will deliver on Thursday its long-awaited judgment in The Gambia's landmark genocide case against Myanmar, seven years after the case was lodged in The Hague.

The Gambia filed the case with the United Nations' top court in November 2019, formally accusing the Southeast Asian nation of breaking its obligations under the 1948 UN Genocide Convention.

In documents and hearings, The Gambia has alleged that Myanmar waged a deliberate campaign of arson, rape and murder in Rakhine State from 2016 to 2017, intending to wipe out the area's ethnic Rohingya minority, in whole or in part.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a un fact-finding mission later concluded that some 10,000 people likely died in the pogroms. Another 700,000 Rohingya fled the country to neighboring Bangladesh, where most of them still live today in the world's largest refugee settlement.

Even before 2016, the predominantly Muslim Rohingya had been subjected to decades of persecution by the Buddhist-majority country's government, with many forced into resettlement camps and most denied citizenship.

Berdasarkan laporan, a number of cases over myanmar's treatment of the rohingya have been filed in courts around the world. The ICJ will be the first to issue a ruling.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "the rohingya people have been waiting for justice for decades for the atrocities and crimes committed against [us]. There were no venues available in [Myanmar]…. International venues were the only hope," said Aung Kyaw Moe, a prominent Rohingya activist whose family was forced to flee the country during the pogroms.

"We've come over many years to a situation where a judgment will be delivered, and the expectation from the Rohingya community is very high," he said.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Berdasarkan laporan, a month after the gambia lodged its case with the icj in 2019, nobel laureate aung san suu kyi, myanmar's de facto civilian leader at the time, traveled to the hague to contest the allegations, calling them "incomplete and incorrect. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa the move tarnished her international reputation as a human rights icon. Many human rights advocates criticized her for defending the very military that had persecuted her for most of her life.

In 2020, ahead of a final judgment, the ICJ issued emergency "provisional measures" ordering Myanmar to take all steps "within its power" to prevent acts of genocide against the Rohingya, an order rights groups say it has blatantly ignored.

Myanmar's military went on to oust the country's democratically elected government the following year, placing Aung San Suu Kyi under arrest and setting off a bloody civil war that continues to rage.

Myanmar also challenged both the court's jurisdiction over the alleged crimes and The Gambia's right to lodge the case, both of which the ICJ rejected in 2022.

Diungkapkan bahwa the icj then held 14 days of hearings this january for myanmar and the gambia to make their arguments before the panel. While Myanmar called one witness, The Gambia called three, as well as an expert.

As The Gambia has accused Myanmar of breaking several articles of the Genocide Convention, Thursday's judgment could be "fairly complicated," said Melanie O'Brien, a professor of international law at the University of Western Australia and past president of the International Association of Genocide Scholars.

Diungkapkan bahwa the convention outlines that states have a duty to prevent and punish genocide and to establish effective penalties for those found responsible. The ICJ could rule in Myanmar's favor on some of these provisions and against it on others.

Diungkapkan bahwa "so, there's quite a lot of layers here. They'll be looking at all of those issues, along with, of course, delving into the facts of the case and the individual crimes of genocide and whether or not Myanmar committed those individual crimes with the intent to destroy the Rohingya," O'Brien said.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Proving Myanmar's intent behind the alleged atrocities is the key question the ICJ is grappling with.

Myanmar argues that its actions were strictly part of a legitimate counterinsurgency and counterterrorism operation, and that those actions could not at the same time be judged as acts of genocide.

Days before the Myanmar military launched its heaviest operations in Rakhine, in August 2017, the Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army, an armed group based in the state, staged a coordinated attack on more than 30 police posts, killing several officers.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the gambia argues that myanmar's actions can qualify as both counterinsurgency and genocide at the same time. It also argues that the sexual violence and killing of children that accompanied the operations are proof that genocide was part of the goal.

"It directly undermines Myanmar's argument that this was a legitimate counterterrorism operation," said Michael Becker, an associate professor of international human rights law at Trinity College Dublin and a former associate legal officer at the ICJ.

"Because evidence of those types of atrocities are very hard to square with the idea that this had some other purpose beyond terrorizing the Rohingya population and indeed taking actions to try to destroy them," he said.

O'Brien and Becker said The Gambia's case against Myanmar is a chance for the ICJ to clarify how it weighs such circumstantial or indirect evidence when judging whether genocide has taken place.

Because investigators were denied access to Rakhine State, they had to rely on interviews with victims and witnesses who had fled Myanmar and on reports by the UN and other groups.

"And how the court deals with that, whether the ICJ accepts or rejects The Gambia's view or Myanmar's view of genocidal intent and how you prove it, this will have major repercussions for other cases," said Becker.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The ICJ is grappling with some of the same questions in cases between the Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda, Ukraine and Russia, and South Africa and Israel.

"I'm sure that the parties in the other cases will pick up on what the court rules in this case and add it to their own cases," said O'Brien.

"And even though this case will only be binding on The Gambia and Myanmar, the court itself may also refer to its own law in their future cases," she added.

The ICJ's judgment may have some effect on not only other cases but other courts as well.

Berdasarkan laporan, the international criminal court — which, unlike the icj, tries individuals and not states — is considering an arrest warrant request for myanmar coup leader min aung hlaing in a trial on alleged crimes against humanity committed against the rohingya. Becker and O'Brien say a finding of genocide by the ICJ could bolster the case for granting the warrant.

What a finding of genocide would actually do for the Rohingya is another key question.

Sebagaimana diketahui, enforcing any reparations or restitution the court may order would rest with the un security council. But with China and Russia, both allies of Min Aung Hlaing's regime, holding veto power on the council, there are serious doubts about whether it would act on any court order on Myanmar.

Aung Kyaw Moe remains hopeful that the Rohingya will one day receive justice.

"Despite these challenges, there are a lot of hopes that we can [move] toward the betterment of the Rohingya people, including compensation, reparations, transitional justice in the domestic setting in the long term," he said.

Berdasarkan laporan, president vladimir v. Putin of Russia touched down in Asia in recent hours. So did two of his nuclear-capable bombers.

Sebagaimana diketahui, mr. Putin arrived early Wednesday in Shenzhen, China, for a regional economic meeting and a trilateral summit with President Trump and President Xi Jinping of China. Satellite images showed that two Russian Tu-95MS strategic nuclear bombers had landed on Tuesday at Da Nang Airport in nearby Vietnam alongside two long-range transport aircraft.

It was the first time that Russian strategic nuclear bombers had deployed to Vietnam since the Soviet era, a pointed demonstration of Russia’s nuclear might and global reach ahead of the high-level talks.

The surprise arrival of the Russian aircraft in the region caused a scramble among American allies in Asia.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, japan dispatched jets after russian planes were detected in japanese airspace near okinoshima, an island in the south of japan, and tokyo registered its discontent with the russian authorities. South Korea also deployed fighter jets; the authorities there said the Russian planes entered South Korea’s Air Defense Identification Zone, where Seoul closely monitors foreign aircraft, but not its sovereign airspace.

Berdasarkan laporan, russia lags both china and the united states significantly in economic output, technological innovation, population size and trade flows, making mr. Putin’s participation in the trilateral summit scheduled for Thursday to some degree conspicuous.

Diungkapkan bahwa but the one critical area where russia has retained its lead is in nuclear weapons. Russia boasts the world’s biggest nuclear arsenal, which Mr. Putin has brandished as a reason the world must continue to accord Moscow a certain level of deference and respect. Russia has also developed a range of new nuclear weapons systems in recent years.

Berdasarkan laporan, the tu-95ms is a nuclear-capable bomber with intercontinental range. Russia has also deployed the bombers in its war against Ukraine to launch conventional missiles.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, taiwan on tuesday said it detected two sorties of russian military aircraft flying in airspace east of the island. Huang Chih-wei, the Vice Chief of the Taiwanese military’s General Staff, said that “the actions of the Russian aircraft undermine regional peace and stability and are detrimental to maintaining the status quo of peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait. Gen. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, the russian and vietnamese authorities did not make any public statements about the arrival of the bombers. Trump and Mr. Putin met with Vietnam’s leader, To Lam, in Shenzhen on Wednesday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, which Mr. Mr. Xi are also attending.

Russia and Vietnam have a longstanding relationship that dates back to the Cold War, and Russia still supplies the vast majority of Vietnam’s military equipment.

Diungkapkan bahwa for vietnam, the decision to welcome the russian nuclear bombers shows china that vietnamese leaders have a range of possible military partners to push back against any aggressive moves by beijing. Vietnam has also deepened its ties with the United States in recent years.

But it is a careful balancing act for the Vietnamese.

Berdasarkan laporan, vietnam allowed russia to refuel its bombers from cam ranh bay in 2014 as they patrolled the area around guam, but the refueling was done midair and the bombers did not land on vietnamese soil. At the time, the United States protested the use of Cam Ranh Bay, a former American and then Soviet base, for the refueling.

Environment secretary Angela Eagle, her ministers and Natural England are breaking the law by failing to intervene to slow the catastrophic decline of Britain’s wild birds, the UK’s environment regulator has said.

New data shows wild bird populations have dropped to their lowest level on record, with almost half – 45% – of 132 native breeding species in decline over a five-year period.

In the last five decades, Britain has lost more than 73 million wild birds from its landscape, according to the British Trust for Ornithology (BTO).

The loss of wild birds includes some of Britain’s best-loved garden birds, including swifts, turtledoves and tree sparrows, as well as wood warblers and bullfinches.

Ministers have legal responsibilities to take action to recover bird populations to healthy levels, as well as specific duties to designate Special Protection Areas (SPAs) where birds and their habitats are legally protected.

But the Office for Environmental Protection (OEP), the independent environmental regulator, said on Wednesday that the environment secretary, her department and Natural England were all breaking the law by failing to protect wild birds.

Eagle has breached environmental law by failing to classify new SPAs, extend existing sites or add new species to those that are protected, the regulator said.

Natural England is in breach of environmental law, according to the OEP, by failing to take the action needed to maintain or restore wild bird populations to appropriate levels and ensure they have sufficient habitats.

The government’s independent nature adviser is also accused of breaching the law by failing to carry out a review of whether there is sufficient habitat for wild birds.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the continued decline in bird populations comes despite evidence that the public’s interest and attention to wild birds is growing. In May, the RSPB reported a 47% increase in the number of people enjoying bird watching over the past eight years.

Helen Venn, chief regulatory officer for the OEP, said there have been continued delays by ministers to protect bird populations.

“As a nation of bird-lovers, and with birds acting as important indicators for the state of our nature more widely, the latest statistics showing declines in the populations of some of our most treasured species are deeply concerning,” said Venn.

“This is why it is important that Defra and Natural England do carry out their legal responsibilities in a reasonable timeframe to deliver nature recovery and in relation to the classification and adaptation of SPAs on land.

The government is legally bound to expand and increase protected areas across the country as part of its 30 by 30 commitment to protect at least 30% of land and seas for nature’s recovery by 2030.

A senior doctor whose evidence helped to convict Lucy Letby and who was held up by prosecutors as a pre-eminent expert was barred from treating patients during the trial over fears he posed a risk to their safety.

Diungkapkan bahwa prof peter hindmarsh, a specialist in hormones in children, was crucial to the crown’s argument that letby had poisoned children by injecting insulin into fluid bags. But a Guardian investigation can reveal he was excluded from clinical practice in March 2023, five months before the end of the trial, by his employer, University College London hospitals trust (UCLH). Diungkapkan bahwa among the reasons for uclh’s decision was that his advice to child patients relating to insulin was not considered safe. A UCLH medical director told the General Medical Council, the doctors’ regulator, that the hospital could not “accept the level of risk Professor Hindmarsh appears to pose to children and young people”.

While Hindmarsh did inform Cheshire constabulary in December 2022 that he was subject to a GMC investigation, and in February 2023 the Crown Prosecution Service told Letby’s defence, her legal team was not made aware that he was later barred from practising on safety grounds.

Had they known, Letby’s defence team might have challenged his credibility as an expert witness and applied for the jury to be told or for his evidence to be dismissed.

Failures of disclosure are recognised as potential grounds for a CCRC referral and for convictions to be overturned.

Berdasarkan laporan, the apparent lack of transparency could mean hindmarsh breached legal rules requiring expert witnesses to disclose to the party instructing them any disciplinary proceedings against them and anything that may be considered to undermine their credibility. Berdasarkan laporan, letby, who was a neonatal nurse at the countess of chester hospital, was convicted of murdering seven babies and attempting to murder seven others, and sentenced to 15 whole-life terms in prison. Court of appeal judges turned down her applications to appeal.

Sebagaimana diketahui, lady justice thirlwall, who chaired a two-year public inquiry after the convictions, refused to consider the experts’ arguments that letby may have suffered a miscarriage of justice, or to wait for the ccrc decision. She produced a report in September making a series of recommendations for the NHS, on the basis that Letby was guilty.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, hindmarsh was presented to the letby jury throughout as a distinguished authority. The lead barrister for the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS), Nick Johnson KC, described him to jurors as “the pre-eminent expert” on insulin.

Hindmarsh was a consultant paediatric endocrinologist – a specialist in hormones, including insulin, in children – at UCLH from 1991, and a professor at UCL, with an eminent reputation.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when johnson introduced hindmarsh at the trial, he asked if he was also an honorary consultant at great ormond street. The jury was not told that four months earlier, in July 2022, Hindmarsh’s contract in that role at the children’s hospital had been terminated.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, hindmarsh asserted in his trial evidence that blood tests and the medical records of two babies being cared for at the countess of chester hospital showed they had been poisoned with insulin, most likely inserted into intravenous fluid bags. The prosecution alleged that Letby injected insulin into the bags, although there was no direct or forensic evidence that she or anybody else had done so.

Berdasarkan laporan, hindmarsh’s evidence alleging insulin poisoning was considered pivotal to the convictions. In summing up, the judge, James Goss, told the jury that if they were sure babies were being deliberately harmed, they could decide other babies were also being harmed, even if they were not sure about the precise cause.

Berdasarkan laporan, johnson presented the two cases of alleged insulin poisoning as incontrovertible evidence. The charges of attempted murder of those two babies were the first on which the jury reached guilty verdicts, and two of only three unanimous guilty verdicts.

The Guardian first revealed in March that the GMC launched an investigation into Hindmarsh on 25 November 2022, the same day he first gave evidence as an expert for the prosecution of Letby.

Diungkapkan bahwa great ormond street hospital had reported “multiple and wide-ranging concerns” to the gmc, including hindmarsh’s “diagnosis and treatment of patients” and “cases where harm to patients has been alleged”. UCLH had been leading a formal investigation of its own into Hindmarsh, and in December 2022 it reported its similar concerns to the GMC.

Then in January 2023, while the Letby trial was still ongoing, a medical tribunal imposed orders that while the GMC investigation continued, Hindmarsh could only work at UCLH, and his clinical work had to be supervised, because otherwise he “may pose a real risk to members of the public”.

Berdasarkan laporan, until now, it has not been publicly known that uclh reported further serious concerns on 15 march 2023, and informed the gmc it had excluded hindmarsh from treating patients at all. This was less than three weeks after Hindmarsh had given his second and final day of evidence at Letby’s trial, on 24 February.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, documents seen by the guardian show that a uclh medical director, dr tim hodgson, informed the gmc of the hospital’s decision. Hodgson wrote that Hindmarsh had breached the supervision order and given independent medical advice relating to three child patients, two involving insulin and diabetes. Hindmarsh’s medical colleagues had submitted “written concerns” about him, Hodgson said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “on the grounds of safety uclh are not presently in a position to allow professor [hindmarsh] to practice clinically even under supervision,” he wrote. “… I do not believe UCLH can accept the level of risk Professor Hindmarsh appears to pose to children and young people even with close clinical supervision. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in two of the cases, hodgson said hindmarsh had independently advised the families that the children stop being given insulin at home. One of the children had an episode of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), a critical, life-threatening complication caused by a severe lack of insulin.

“The patient had an episode of DKA and it’s not clear whether this coincided with the alleged advice from Professor Hindmarsh,” Hodgson wrote.

Diungkapkan bahwa in the two insulin cases, hodgson highlighted concerns that hindmarsh was over-focusing on rare causes of hypoglycaemia (low blood sugar) and diabetes (a cause of high blood sugar). In the first case, his colleagues believed Hindmarsh was not addressing more common causes of diabetes, and in the second, that he was “not treating high glucose levels appropriately”.

Had Letby’s defence team been informed of this, it could have strengthened the case for an application to inform the jury or exclude Hindmarsh’s evidence.

Berdasarkan laporan, experts who have provided reports for letby’s ccrc application have argued that hindmarsh’s opinion that the babies were poisoned via their fluid bags was an extremely unlikely explanation for their condition. They argue that Hindmarsh failed to recognise more common, identifiable medical causes.

Hodgson also said Hindmarsh had questioned the reliability of an insulin antibodies blood test result, sharing “his concern with the family that this was an erroneous, fallible test”.

Berdasarkan laporan, this too could have been significant to letby’s defence. At the trial, Johnson presented results from the immunoassay blood tests as definitive and said there was “no doubt” the two babies were poisoned.

Sign up for the Breaking News UK email to get newsletter alerts direct to your inbox.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, experts supporting letby’s ccrc application say immunoassays are known to be fallible because they can react to antibodies in blood to give a falsely high insulin result. Hodgson’s report suggests Hindmarsh recognised that some blood tests were fallible, but he never made this clear at Letby’s trial.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the gmc responded to these new concerns by applying to the tribunal for hindmarsh’s registration as a doctor to be suspended. Hindmarsh’s barrister argued strongly that although he would not be treating patients because UCLH had excluded him, he should be allowed to continue working as an expert witness. Suspension, she said, would impede his ability to do so.

The barrister argued to the tribunal that Hindmarsh had not breached the supervision order and “no harm has been caused to patients”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the three-person tribunal said it could not determine whether the previous supervision order had “technically” been breached. “However, the tribunal felt that the three cases identified by UCLH did raise concerns about patient safety,” it said.

The tribunal decided that to suspend Hindmarsh would be disproportionate and explicitly allowed him to continue working as an expert witness, saying its order should not “restrict his non-clinical work”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, instead, it imposed a tightening of the supervision requirement so that hindmarsh from then had to be directly supervised when treating patients. This appears to have been a theoretical measure, however, because Hindmarsh was already restricted to only working for UCLH, and the hospital had barred him from treating patients at all.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, expert witnesses have a legal duty under the criminal procedure rules to tell the party instructing them – in hindmarsh’s case, cheshire constabulary – anything “that might reasonably be thought capable of undermining the expert’s opinion or detract from the credibility or impartiality of the expert”. This includes any disciplinary proceedings by a regulatory body.

The rules were introduced in 2014 to improve the reliability of expert evidence and guard against miscarriages of justice, after a series of wrongful convictions in the late 1990s and 2000s.

Lawyers have told the Guardian that under the rules, Hindmarsh should have told the police of the April 2023 tribunal ruling and that his hospital had barred him from clinical practice.

Tim Green KC, a specialist in disclosure, told the Guardian: “Whilst I cannot comment on the facts behind this complex and sensitive case, it is clear that the duty of an expert witness to make disclosure in a criminal or civil case of all material capable of undermining his opinion or detracting from his credibility is a continuous one.

Berdasarkan laporan, “this duty extends after he has given evidence and through to the end of the proceedings. The duty continues through to any appeals, and arguably remains extant now, during the current considerations of the CCRC.

Berdasarkan laporan, “further restrictions imposed by a professional disciplinary tribunal on an expert’s right to practise, like those which can be imposed by the medical practitioners tribunal, are also disclosable in my view. For the same reasons, it also arguable that the information which led the tribunal to impose those restrictions in the first place is also disclosable. Such restrictions are likely to be relevant to an assessment made by a jury or judge of an expert’s opinion evidence, competence and skill. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa lawyers have said hindmarsh may have had a duty to tell the police and cps initially, earlier in 2022, of the investigation into his practice led by uclh, and that great ormond street had terminated his contract. He does not appear to have done so.

Sebagaimana diketahui, when johnson, the lead prosecutor, first introducedhindmarsh in court on 25 november 2022, he sought to clarify that the professor had an eminent position at great ormond street as well as uclh. At that stage, yes. After two questions not answered clearly, Johnson asked Hindmarsh: “Are you an honorary consultant at Great Ormond Street hospital though?” Hindmarsh replied: “Yes. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, hindmarsh did not say his contract at great ormond street had been terminated four months earlier. That point was never clarified to the jury.

Berdasarkan laporan, hindmarsh was first informed of the gmc investigation into him on 30 november 2022. By this point, he had already made his first appearance in the Letby trial.

Diungkapkan bahwa he told cheshire constabulary two weeks later, on 14 december 2022. The CPS was informed two months later and told Letby’s then barrister, Ben Myers KC, on 20 February 2023, just four days before Hindmarsh was due to give his second day of evidence.

Berdasarkan laporan, the cps told myers it would oppose the jury being told, because the gmc investigation into hindmarsh had not reached a final adjudication. Myers did not then make an application to the judge for the jury to be informed.

Diungkapkan bahwa on 23 february 2023, the day before hindmarsh was due to return and give evidence, johnson reminded the jury about him. “Professor Peter Hindmarsh will be here tomorrow to deal with the issue of insulin,” Johnson said. “And because he’s the pre-eminent expert in that narrow field, we will call him first. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa in july 2023, the judge referred to hindmarsh’s evidence in his summing up. He did not mention Great Ormond Street at all, describing Hindmarsh as “emeritus professor of endocrinology at University College London and also a consultant paediatric endocrinologist at University College London hospitals”. Apparently unknown to the judge, UCLH had excluded Hindmarsh from practising as a consultant four months earlier.

Sebagaimana diketahui, letby was convicted in august 2023. In November 2024 Hindmarsh applied to remove himself from registration as a doctor. The GMC investigation into Hindmarsh never reached a final determination. The GMC allowed this, a process known as “voluntary erasure”, which meant the investigation was stopped with no final adjudication.

The CPS has confirmed to the Guardian that it did not disclose to the defence anything relating to Hindmarsh being barred from clinical practice or the April 2023 tribunal ruling, because it had not been made aware of it.

Berdasarkan laporan, cheshire constabulary declined to provide information to the guardian, so it is not clear whether hindmarsh did or did not tell the police. Either way, it was not passed to the CPS, which would have disclosed it to Letby’s defence.

“Cheshire constabulary will not be commenting further in relation to this case,” a spokesperson said.

Diungkapkan bahwa a cps spokesperson said: “the cps met all its disclosure obligations and no objections were raised by the defence at any stage in relation to expert evidence relied on by the prosecution. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the cps’ statement is made on the basis that it disclosed what it knew to the defence, and it had not been told about the tribunal ruling or that hindmarsh was barred from treating patients. Johnson’s representatives did not reply to questions from the Guardian.

Berdasarkan laporan, mcdonald, letby’s lawyer, said: “peter hindmarsh’s evidence was pivotal to the prosecution’s case against lucy letby. The insulin allegations were not simply another part of the prosecution’s case; they were its cornerstone, presented as scientific proof that she had deliberately poisoned babies and was capable of murder.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “it shaped the jury’s perception of lucy and provided the lens through which they were invited to view every other allegation. Its influence permeated the entire trial. If the foundations of the insulin cases are unsafe, the consequences for the safety of the wider convictions cannot be overstated. This was not evidence that could be neatly confined to two convictions. ”.

The Guardian asked Hindmarsh detailed questions about the hospitals’ concerns, UCLH excluding him from clinical practice, and the GMC investigation, and put to him that he appeared not to have made adequate disclosure under the criminal procedure rules.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a representative for hindmarsh replied: “he has no comment in relation to these questions and points. ”.

#1234. Latin America's mega-prisons: Can El Salvador's model work?

📅 18 Nov 2026

Latin America's mega-prisons: Can El Salvador's model work?

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.dw.com/en/latin-america-s-mega-prisons-can-el-salvador-s-model-work/a-79973524?maca=en-rss-en-all-1573-rdf

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, el salvador's mega-prison has become a model for governments across latin america seeking to combat organized crime. But experts question whether the approach is effective, sustainable or compatible with human rights.

Berdasarkan laporan, around 15,000 inmates and a capacity of up to 40,000, prison sentences of up to 1,000 years, strict security measures and an extreme isolation regime. Staged images show inmates with shaved heads and tattoos being subdued by heavily armed guards.

These are just some of the facts circulating about El Salvador's Terrorism Confinement Center (CECOT), a symbol of President Nayib Bukele's security policy and a possible model for other Latin American countries seeking to combat organized crime.

Berdasarkan laporan, more than a dozen governments in the region have proposed building similar "mega-prisons," although most would have a far smaller capacity. A range of experts consulted by DW question the effectiveness and sustainability of these initiatives.

Diungkapkan bahwa de facto mega-prisons — that is, overcrowded prisons with excessive inmate populations — existed in latin america long before bukele, says criminologist jose luis perez guadalupe, former president of the national penitentiary institute and former interior minister in peru. Lurigancho Prison in Lima, for example, designed to hold 3,000 inmates, has housed nearly 11,000 for decades.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but ever since cecot was launched in 2023, the concept of a "mega-prison" has been primarily linked to maximum-security facilities. For Olga Espinoza, an academic specializing in prison systems at the School of Government of the University of Chile, this association is problematic because it implies that the entire prison population requires "extremely severe" punishment.

Berdasarkan laporan, according to espinoza, placing the entire prison population in maximum-security facilities would amount to inefficient and extremely costly "over-intervention. " These facilities require substantial investments in infrastructure, technology, specialized staff, anti-corruption measures and social reintegration programs.

It would also be ineffective because "international evidence indicates that when people with different profiles are placed in the same space, there is a high risk of the spread of criminal behavior," the Chilean expert adds.

Several criminal groups across the region even have their roots in overcrowded prisons: Tren de Aragua in Venezuela; Los Lobos, Los Choneros and Los Tiguerones in Ecuador; and Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC) and Comando Vermelho (CV) in Brazil.

Even when the proposal involves simply building large-scale facilities, investing in a single structure may seem attractive given the difficulties of developing public infrastructure in Latin America.

However, "there is insufficient evidence to support the claim that building mega-prisons is more cost-effective," says Renato Rivera, a senior analyst at the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime (GI-TOC).

The United Nations Standard Minimum Rules for the Treatment of Prisoners, adopted in 1955, "the recommendation has been to build medium-sized prisons housing between 1,000 and 2,000 inmates rather than mega-prisons," explains Perez Guadalupe, a professor at the Universidad del Pacifico in Lima.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "mega-prisons, apart from being impersonal, can become extremely dangerous," says guadalupe. As an example, the GI-TOC's Rivera highlights the widely reported prison massacres in Ecuador in 2021 that took place in the country's largest and most populated facilities.

Diungkapkan bahwa experts acknowledge that mass incarceration has coincided with a dramatic decline in violence in el salvador and has strengthened the public's perception of safety. Despite reports of arbitrary arrests, abuses and more than 500 deaths in state custody in the country, announcements of new mega-prisons project an image of a strong state confronting organized crime across the region.

Sebagaimana diketahui, however, they warn that this political and symbolic impact does not guarantee sustainable results. Achieving them would require a "clear commitment" to external oversight, human rights protections and social reintegration programs, which governments have yet to demonstrate, Espinoza says.

Diungkapkan bahwa perez guadalupe is particularly critical of the salvadoran model, describing it as "pure propaganda. He also argues that the state must demonstrate "moral superiority over those who break the law. " He believes the images released from CECOT violate human dignity. ".

Although transnational organized crime represents a growing challenge across the region, the Peruvian criminologist considers El Salvador's case exceptional.

Sebagaimana diketahui, following the mass arrests carried out under the state of emergency introduced by bukele, the country has one of the highest incarceration rates in the world. CECOT was designed to permanently detain members of gangs such as MS-13 and Barrio 18, which are considered extremely dangerous.

Berdasarkan laporan, however, the reality of other latin american prison systems is different. The question is not where to lock people deprived of their liberty away forever, but rather "how we want them to leave: worse or better," Perez Guadalupe argues, pointing out that most will eventually return to society.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in theory, the official alternative is provided by the un nelson mandela rules for the treatment of prisoners, updated in 2015. They establish principles for modern prison management, including respect for human dignity, an absolute prohibition on torture and degrading treatment and social reintegration as a central goal of imprisonment.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in practice, latin america has developed innovative approaches in this direction. These include the APAC model in Brazil, which operates facilities without guards, weapons or violence; Conflict Prevention and Resolution Committees in Argentina; and the Alternative Criminal Justice Center in the Mexican state of Sonora.

Experts also point to the need for maximum-security prisons for specific inmate profiles, but on a smaller scale and with more precise classification of the prison population.

Sebagaimana diketahui, finally, they emphasize that prisons, including mega-prisons, primarily address the consequences of organized crime rather than its root causes. Poverty, social exclusion and a lack of opportunities require public policies focused on employment, education and social integration to reduce the conditions that enable crime to expand in one of the world's most unequal regions.

This article was originally published in Spanish.

Berdasarkan laporan, as the second world war neared an end, the soon-to-be victors — joseph stalin of the soviet union, winston churchill of britain and president franklin d. Roosevelt — sat down in the Crimean resort of Yalta to discuss the fate of postwar Europe. Their decisions in February 1945 helped shape the global order for the rest of the 20th century, making Yalta synonymous with an era of great-power bargaining by outsize personalities.

Sebagaimana diketahui, on thursday, the leaders of the world’s three largest military powers will meet again. This time it will be President Xi Jinping of China, whose nation has supplanted Britain in military might, hosting President Trump and President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia.

Berdasarkan laporan, the trilateral summit in shenzhen, china — at an uncertain geopolitical moment dogged by wars, climate change and the rise of artificial intelligence — has prompted some analysts to label it “yalta 2. 0. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that parallel has limits, historians say. For one, Yalta was a meeting of allies whose broad objectives overlapped, said Catherine Grace Katz, a historian of 20th century geopolitics and author of a book on that summit. “Or at least ostensibly still allies at the time,” she said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, by february 1945, the three allied powers were united in their fight against hitler’s germany, whose defeat by then seemed inevitable. British and American troops had already stormed through France and Belgium, while the Soviet war machine was steamrolling across Eastern Europe, squeezing Germany from both flanks.

At Yalta, the allies agreed on what the Northern Hemisphere would look like after the dust of war settled.

Berdasarkan laporan, stalin agreed to join the fight against japan in return for territory in the northern pacific. Roosevelt — by then frail, two months from his death and focused on ensuring Japan’s surrender — offered the Soviets broad leeway over Poland’s future. That set the stage for decades of Soviet domination over Eastern Europe.

David Reynolds, a professor of history at the University of Cambridge who specializes in 20th-century diplomacy, argued against overstating what was decided at Yalta.

“‘Yalta’ is a notorious word” that to many conjures the carving up of Europe and selling out to Stalin — but that is based on a misunderstanding, he said.

“The fate of postwar Europe was decided on the battlefield, not at the conference table,” he added.

By the time of the February conference, the Red Army was on the verge of taking Berlin, and both Roosevelt and Churchill had privately conceded the inevitability of Soviet domination of Eastern Europe, Professor Reynolds said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, ms. Katz said, “Short of physically pushing them out of Poland, there was not a lot that the West could do. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, she also pointed out that it was a year earlier, at a meeting in moscow, when churchill and stalin scribbled out their secret “percentages” agreement on a piece of paper. That led to Europe being split between Western and Communist blocs, a division that eventually became the Iron Curtain and persisted until the end of the Cold War.

Diungkapkan bahwa yalta was “not the moment that the world was carved up into these spheres of influence,” she said. “That kind of gets conflated with some of the other meetings that these wartime leaders had. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, that said, she argued, roosevelt missed opportunities to press for greater concessions from stalin at yalta. Professor Reynolds said that several other critical negotiations were also hammered out at Yalta, which is often forgotten.

Diungkapkan bahwa it was the scene of hard-fought bargaining by churchill to secure protections to stop germany from being eviscerated under a future surrender, as stalin had wanted, he said. Diungkapkan bahwa president vladimir v. Putin of Russia touched down in Asia in recent hours. So did two of his nuclear-capable bombers.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, russia lags both china and the united states significantly in economic output, technological innovation, population size and trade flows, making mr. Putin’s participation in the trilateral summit scheduled for Thursday to some degree conspicuous.

Diungkapkan bahwa but the one critical area where russia has retained its lead is in nuclear weapons. Putin has brandished as a reason the world must continue to accord Moscow a certain level of deference and respect. Russia boasts the world’s biggest nuclear arsenal, which Mr. Russia has also developed a range of new nuclear weapons systems in recent years.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the tu-95ms is a nuclear-capable bomber with intercontinental range. Russia has also deployed the bombers in its war against Ukraine to launch conventional missiles.

Diungkapkan bahwa taiwan on tuesday said it detected two sorties of russian military aircraft flying in airspace east of the island. Gen. Huang Chih-wei, the Vice Chief of the Taiwanese military’s General Staff, said that “the actions of the Russian aircraft undermine regional peace and stability and are detrimental to maintaining the status quo of peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait. ”.

Trump and Mr. Mr. Putin met with Vietnam’s leader, To Lam, in Shenzhen on Wednesday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, which Mr. Xi are also attending.

Russia and Vietnam have a longstanding relationship that dates back to the Cold War, and Russia still supplies the vast majority of Vietnam’s military equipment.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for vietnam, the decision to welcome the russian nuclear bombers shows china that vietnamese leaders have a range of possible military partners to push back against any aggressive moves by beijing. Vietnam has also deepened its ties with the United States in recent years.

But it is a careful balancing act for the Vietnamese.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, vietnam allowed russia to refuel its bombers from cam ranh bay in 2014 as they patrolled the area around guam, but the refueling was done midair and the bombers did not land on vietnamese soil. At the time, the United States protested the use of Cam Ranh Bay, a former American and then Soviet base, for the refueling.

World leaders coming to Shenzhen this week are arriving in an almost spotless, ultramodern metropolis, its streets bedecked with pastel banners but mostly emptied of the crowds typical of many Chinese cities.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, shenzhen lies slightly closer to the equator than havana, providing a balmy venue for the asia-pacific economic cooperation gathering. Under sunny skies with mild temperatures, a festive mood prevails in the city, which bears a strong resemblance to Miami — only much larger and with taller, newer high-rises.

Diungkapkan bahwa schools in shenzhen have closed this week, many residents have left town and local authorities have instructed companies to allow those employees who are still here to work from home. m. m. to 9 p. The result has been a holiday atmosphere of sorts in a city with a tech sector known for its punishing “996” work schedules: 9 a. , six days a week.

Sebagaimana diketahui, youthful volunteers — mainly students at local universities — stand on street corners wearing bright red vests, having been offered academic credit in exchange for being trained as guides. Thousands of gawkers have been promenading past the large conference center that will host heads of state from across the Asia Pacific region, taking photos of themselves in front of the flower gardens inside the fence.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, among the crowds walking outside the high steel fences around the conference center was a local resident who had brought her parents and her dog. The resident said that workers had been planting flowers for a year ahead of the summit, and added that a community worker had given her a big package of napkins as a gift after she agreed not to drive her car in the coming week. Shenzhen has halved fares this week on its extensive subway system to help clear the roads for summit buses.

Sebagaimana diketahui, at the same time, however, residents are aware of occasional hassles. “Many friends who live around here plan to travel outside the city because of the inconvenience of transportation — many roads will be closed to traffic,” said the resident, who gave only her family name, Zhang. As is common at high-profile and high-security events in China, she was wary of giving her full name, which can be risky for Chinese citizens.

Berdasarkan laporan, few dare to express any misgivings, however, accepting the disruption with resignation. “Even if we’re unhappy about it, we can’t really say so,” said a resident surnamed Wang. “The government wouldn’t welcome our dissatisfaction. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, while gatherings of world leaders always prompt extensive security, china’s efforts in shenzhen are particularly intensive. Surveillance cameras are ubiquitous along streets in China and not noticeably more common this week in Shenzhen, but there are other, unobtrusive signs of the elaborate security effort underway.

Berdasarkan laporan, xiangmei road, located near the main summit venue and lined with some of china’s costliest condominium towers, was much quieter than usual on monday. A cleaner outside one of the towers who gave only her family name, Li, said that the family employing her has simply left town this week.

Diungkapkan bahwa police have been stationed in apartments on upper floors facing the conference center, drones have been prohibited and the remaining residents have received social media messages urging them to support the gathering, ms. Li said.

Berdasarkan laporan, “this place is usually very crowded,” she said, “but look how quiet it is now. ”.

Ruoxin Zhang and Siyi Zhao contributed research.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the presidents of china, russia and the us have greeted each other amid the apec summit in shenzhen. This comes a day ahead of the trilateral talks between Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump. Follow DW live.

Here are the biggest headlines from Trump's Asia tour on Wednesday, November 18:.

Mexico's Claudia Sheinbaum won praise on Chinese social media for her frugal travel plans this week, taking an economy flight to Shenzhen.

The Mexican president took a South China Airlines flight from Mexico City to Shenzhen, with posts going viral on China's Weibo social media site seemingly showing Sheinbaum chatting with other passengers on board.

She posted a short video on social media showing her being greeted by Chinese officials and schoolchildren after getting off an airport bus, as well as an earlier post showing her waiting in Mexico City's airport departures lounge.

A hashtag on Weibo about her arrival attracted more than 10 million views, with users voicing admiration for her low-cost intercontinental travel.

"It's commendable to spend taxpayer money frugally and ensure it's used where it's most needed, rather than squandering it on luxurious private jets or official travel expenses," the AFP news agency cited one user as saying.

Chinese news agency Xinhua has reported the first comments from Xi Jinping to Donald Trump following his arrival.

#1241. How a green economy could help reverse climate change

📅 18 Nov 2026

How a green economy could help reverse climate change

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.dw.com/en/how-a-green-economy-could-help-reverse-climate-change/a-79874576?maca=en-rss-en-all-1573-rdf

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, green growth promises a future in which economies thrive without destroying the environment. But is this vision realistic?.

Diungkapkan bahwa human civilization is currently profoundly unsustainable. Earth has already crossed seven of the nine planetary boundaries critical for sustaining life, including climate change, ocean acidification and biosphere integrity.

If economies and societies keep to business as usual, the Earth's vital processes will continue to be thrown wildly out of balance, threatening the future of humanity.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it's now largely accepted that if humans are to have any chance of slowing global warming and nature loss, those social and economic models must change. That's where the idea of green growth comes in.

Berdasarkan laporan, its promise is to keep growing the economy while reducing emissions and resource use. That involves, for instance, running factories, businesses and homes on wind, solar and other green energy instead of coal and gas, replacing gas-fired furnaces with heat pumps and  recycling and reusing resources and raw materials.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "basically, the idea is: business as usual, but with more sustainable technologies," said helmut haberl, a social ecology professor at boku university in vienna. Along with his colleagues, he published a major report in 2020 evaluating more than 800 studies on green growth.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in principle, the world's economic output could continue to grow in the long term and generate significantly fewer emissions from the burning of fossil fuels like coal, oil and gas. That's been shown in scenarios modeled by researchers with the UN's Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, or IPCC.

Thanks to renewable energy and green technologies, those scenarios have already become reality in several countries and regions.

Diungkapkan bahwa the economies of developed countries like the united kingdom, the united states, japan and australia have experienced years of growth alongside sinking co2 emissions. That's even when offshore production is included.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in the european union, the bloc-wide economy has grown by more than 70% since 1990. Meanwhile, the EU's carbon emissions have dropped by around 40%.

But such a complete decoupling of growth and emissions is, according to Haberl and his fellow researchers, relatively rare.

Berdasarkan laporan, in india, and in several countries in africa and southeast asia, economies are becoming more efficient. But while economic performance is outpacing emissions growth, emissions are still rising in those countries and globally. This is not compatible with preventing the worst impacts of climate change.

"That doesn't mean, however, that it couldn't work in the future," said Haberl, referring to decoupling of growth and emissions.

And even though economic growth has been shown to be compatible with emissions reduction, eliminating all greenhouse gases from a polluting industry like steel or chemicals is complicated.

These sectors don't just release emissions by burning fossil fuels for energy; carbon is also a key part of the chemical processes used to create their products, notably in the steel industry.

Replacing it with greener substitutes, or an alternative energy source like green hydrogen, requires significant investment.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there's another hurdle: the world's high consumption of resources. A productive economy depends on many raw materials and other products: ores, chemicals, wood, cement, glass and agricultural products.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Many countries are now using green technologies to reduce the amount of resources needed to manufacture a product, for example, and are making their economies more efficient.

Berdasarkan laporan, but that doesn't mean overall fewer resources are being used because falling costs can encourage businesses to produce more things and people to consume more. This can partially offset green savings and is called the rebound effect.

The British economy has been growing for years, emissions have been dropping and efficiency has increased, but the UK still used 7% more resources in 2023 than it did in 2001.

Sebagaimana diketahui, global resource consumption has tripled over the last 50 years. If the world continues on the current pathway, that could increase by another 60% by 2060. It remains unclear whether green growth can deliver the emissions and resource reductions needed to stop climate change and biodiversity loss rapidly enough.

"We really need to move beyond efficiency gains in our existing production practices to look more broadly at what we consume," said Catherine Ganzleben, a sustainability and fair transitions expert at the European Environment Agency.

She told DW that people also need to reconsider how they consume and whether they really need to own everything they use in their daily life — cars, for example.

Diungkapkan bahwa "but we can shift towards models where we share cars, so we pool our resources and have significantly lower resources per person through sharing the goods that we need. ".

Some researchers have concluded that unrestricted economic growth is no longer possible in the long term, even if it's sustainable.

Berdasarkan laporan, instead, they've called for degrowth. This posits slower economic growth, no growth at all or even negative growth, so that the world's ecosystems and the climate have a chance to recover and stabilize.

Berdasarkan laporan, that applies mainly to economies in richer countries, which would need to take targeted steps to reduce their energy and resource use. Poorer countries would continue to grow until their economies and quality of life improve significantly.

Berdasarkan laporan, under the degrowth theory, a society's prosperity is not measured solely by the growth of its gross domestic product, but by values such as quality of life, education and community. The idea is that once countries develop to a certain point, additional growth doesn't translate into greater well-being.

Diungkapkan bahwa ultimately, the concept is based on the idea that human well-being and ecological sustainability is only possible in the long term with a planned, socially just reduction of material production and resource consumption. Degrowth advocates argue this would be preferable to an unplanned and potentially catastrophic economic contraction caused by escalating climate extremes.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

A 2020 study by researchers from the universities of Leeds and Lausanne showed that the concept of degrowth supported the world's climate goals — and that a high quality of life didn't have to be sacrificed in exchange for a significantly lower consumption of energy and resources.

However, there is still no conclusive evidence that an entire modern economy could continue to function entirely on the degrowth principles in the long term.

Nevertheless, Haberl doesn't assume that an environmentally friendly economic model automatically goes hand in hand with sacrifice, arguing instead for a needs-based economy.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "a society isn't necessarily better off when it's producing more goods and services," he said. It all depends on how prosperity and quality of life are measured in the future, and how states decide to do business.

Sebagaimana diketahui, today, a successful economy is measured by the growth of a country's gross domestic product — put simply, the worth of all of its goods and services. This calculation doesn't account for income distribution, unpaid work, quality of life or environmental damage.

Diungkapkan bahwa "the highest possible real incomes for every individual would probably not be compatible with ecological goals in the long term," said haberl. "On the other hand, an increase in prosperity — related to a higher quality of life — would be. ".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Sebagaimana diketahui, an analysis by the european environment agency (eea) pointed out that the idea of steady growth is part of the world's economic cycle, and deeply anchored in our institutions, norms and societal discourse. The job market and tax system are also closely tied to gross domestic product growth. A shrinking economy would therefore require a fundamental shift in our way of thinking.

Sebagaimana diketahui, countries face a dilemma: a steadily growing economy is not compatible with ecological goals, according to the eea. On the other side, a sharp decline in growth could trigger enormous social upheaval.

Sebagaimana diketahui, and the correlation is much more complex than the idea of "less is more," as highlighted by an eea study in november 2021. "The fact that GDP growth has been harmful for the environment does not necessarily mean that declining GDP would be good for the environment," noted the report.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, achieving green growth while respecting environmental limits would require an "unprecedented decoupling of economic activity from environmental and climate pressures. Whether this is feasible is currently uncertain. ".

This article was originally written in German.
