Watch: Inside the gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war with Russia.

There's a new front in the war in Ukraine, and it is underground.

For the past seven months Ukrainian forces have been living and fighting Russian troops in an old Soviet gas pipeline in the north-eastern Kharkiv region.

Berdasarkan laporan, with a diameter of just over a metre there is enough room only to crawl. But it is relatively safe from the drones that now saturate the skies above the front line â and make it nigh-on impossible for either side to advance.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, going underground is now the "only option", says zanuda, who has helped plan ukraine's tunnel operation and calls it a new world of fighting. But, he acknowledges, it is hard.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "on the surface you always have some room to manoeuvre, but here you can only engage the enemy head-on. ".

The journey to get to this subterranean battleground in the Kharkiv region only reinforced the dangers on the ground: a high-speed move by vehicle across open fields, followed by a long march across muddy ground â accompanied by Ukrainian troops with their weapons loaded, ready to shoot down Russian drones.

Arriving at the tunnel entrance, the first thing to hit you is the lingering smell of gas and fetid air.

Berdasarkan laporan, both sides use openings in the pipeline to get to the surface, where most of the fighting takes place. They have made breaches in the ground, and used welding tools to break through the thick steel.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the russians were the first to exploit the pipe to infiltrate the nearby city of kupyansk in september 2025. They have used underground pipelines before, during the capture of the city of Avdiivka in 2024, and last year in their bid to recapture areas of Russia's Kursk region.

But Ukrainian forces have slowly turned the tables.

Troops move through the tunnel on special sleds - they call it the Kupyansk metro.

A specially designed electric cart transports troops and supplies through the pipeline.

Sebagaimana diketahui, they call it the kupyansk metro. There is a regular bump as you cross the welded sections of the pipe. We travelled on it for 40 minutes, heads bowed and legs crossed. It occasionally breaks down. It is like an austere fairground ride, without the fun.

Berdasarkan laporan, our destination was a break in the pipeline where ukrainian troops have built dug-outs to store ammunition and equipment, with just enough room to stand. It is where the man they call Musician conducts the movement of troops and supplies. He has been living like a mole, his face engrained with dirt and earth.

Sebagaimana diketahui, musician tells me he has spent the past three months there, with a few brief visits above ground to clean up or go to the toilet. Musician tells me we are close to the line of contact: "But it's safe underground. From time to time we can hear the thuds of artillery rounds above. ".

Ukrainian troops like Musician rarely see the sun - but they say they feel safer underground.

Berdasarkan laporan, the cart continues its journey into the bowels of the earth. It returns about half an hour later with more troops covered in dirt. They have been fighting in positions on the surface.

There is a look of relief on their dust-caked faces.

"It's more comfortable in the pipe because drones don't fly here, and neither do artillery shells or glide bombs," says Vovochka, who has been fighting on the ground for the past three weeks.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but there has been fighting in the pipeline, too. Operation Veles, named after a mythical Slavic god of the underworld, began in April. Since then Ukraine has advanced 15km (9. 3 miles) along the pipeline.

It has been painstaking, backbreaking work â with the ever-present fear of coming into contact with the enemy.

Berdasarkan laporan, back above ground we meet a few of the soldiers, from the 13th khartiia brigade of ukraine's national guard, who have taken part in the mission. Their first task was to clear the detritus, water and Russian barricades inside the pipeline.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the ukrainian troops say some of the barriers were boobytrapped or piled with russian bodies. "When we moved them or climbed over them, we had no idea what was underneath," says Chyzh.

Diungkapkan bahwa the other danger, he said, was the ricochets from gunfire when they tried to advance. "You never know where a bullet is going to go or how it will bounce. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, his comrade kort says "we were all firing, we were pushing them back". "Yes, there were bodies," says Kort. "I even had to sleep right next to them. Over the course of the operation Ukraine says it killed more than 100 Russian soldiers and took 30 prisoners. ".

The men live and fight in very tight quarters - but have managed to clear 15km of the pipe.

Their commander's former life as a miner helped prepare them for the physical and psychological challenges of operating underground.

Berdasarkan laporan, from a building on the surface, biashym keeps in regular contact with his men still in the pipeline. Behind him is a cabinet full of medicine.

Berdasarkan laporan, soldiers in the pipeline spend much of their time on their knees and suffer abrasions. Biashym admits some have had panic attacks from living in such a confined space. Others have struggled to breathe.

Hundreds of Colombian volunteers have also been involved in the operation, part of the RUG 23rd Assault Regiment.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, foreign fighters have helped boost ukraine's depleted ranks. One of the Colombians, whose call sign is Gecko, tells me it took them 30 days to just clear 500m.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "it was difficult, it was hot and i had fear inside the pipe," he said. "But at some point I just thought, OK, just deal with it and let's advance. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa russian forces, like ukraine's, have built fortified positions inside the pipeline. They still try to infiltrate Ukrainian positions, burrowing their way in and out of the pipe. From a control room above ground we watched Ukrainian drones target another Russian attempt to outflank them.

Berdasarkan laporan, while some of the fighting taking place underground, there are still battles on the surface and in the air. It has been a combined operation.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but zanuda, who is chief of the planning section of the 13th khartiia brigade, believes it is the best way to fight in the future. "Ground operations are now nearly impossible," he said, adding that "everyone understands, for now, the only way to fight is underground".

Sebagaimana diketahui, there'll be more missions like this, he believes. "Pipelines run everywhere," he said. "You have to remember, back in the Soviet times, oil, gas and ammonia were being transported to Europe, with the entire transit route running through Ukraine. ".

In reality it has been brutal, gruelling and dangerous work in the harshest of conditions.

It has taken Ukraine seven months to clear 15km of the pipeline.

Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky has hailed it as a success.

It has helped retake lost territory and been a boost for morale, but on its own it has not changed the course of the war.

#1270. Myanmar faces historic genocide verdict at UN court over Rohingya massacres

📅 18 Nov 2026

Myanmar faces historic genocide verdict at UN court over Rohingya massacres

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c5m2l90ez144o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

When the judges of the International Court of Justice read out their verdict in the seven-year-old genocide case filed by The Gambia against Myanmar on Thursday, they could make history.

In the years since the Genocide Convention was signed in 1948, after the Nazi Holocaust, dozens of individuals have been successfully prosecuted for the crime of genocide, in conflicts such as those in Rwanda and the former Yugoslavia.

But no state has ever been found guilty by an international court of committing genocide.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "it would be a judgment of landmark importance if the gambia were to win this case," says arsalan suleman, the lawyer leading the case against myanmar at the court. "It would give renewed vitality to the 1948 Genocide Convention and to the notion of international legal accountability for crimes committed by a state. ".

The mass expulsion of the Rohingya population of Rakhine State in August and September 2017 was without question a military operation of exceptional brutality.

I was among a very small number of journalists who witnessed the deliberate burning of Rohingya villages in Rakhine, and also the dreadful human suffering of the hundreds of thousands who fled to neighbouring Bangladesh.

Their accounts of killing, torture and mass rape by Burmese soldiers have been thoroughly documented by human rights groups and a United Nations fact-finding mission, external.

I have on many occasions interviewed ethnic Rakhine people about their animosity towards the Muslim population, and I have documented the systematic obliteration of what remained of Rohingya villages by the Myanmar state.

But the question posed at the UN's top court, the ICJ, is whether all of this amounted to genocide.

Hundreds of thousands of Rohingya fled across the Myanmar border in 2017 as attacks on them grew.

Diungkapkan bahwa the icj was established in 1945 to help settle disputes between states, not to try international crimes. However, it was chosen to address the attacks on Rohingyas in Myanmar because there were few other avenues of redress for the victims.

Myanmar authorities have denied accusations of ethnic cleansing or genocide, saying they were only responding to terrorist actions by Rohingya militants with so-called military "clearance operations".

Diungkapkan bahwa a un report in 2018, based on hundreds of interviews, said the army's tactics were "grossly disproportionate to actual security threats". It said top military figures in Myanmar must be investigated for genocide in Rakhine State and crimes against humanity in other areas. Myanmar rejected the report.

As Myanmar was not a signatory to the International Criminal Court, it was not possible to file a case there against the officials accused of atrocities in Rakhine State.

Instead in November 2019 The Gambia, backed by the Organisation of Islamic Co-operation, filed a case at the ICJ, arguing that all states are bound by the Genocide Convention, so all have an interest in upholding it.

It accused the state in Myanmar, not just the military, of genocide.

This was a novelty in international law; a state not directly affected by an act, arguing that it had legal standing to make a complaint because it was indirectly affected by any violations of such an important convention.

Myanmar objected to this argument, but the ICJ judges ruled that The Gambia was eligible to file the case.

Min Aung Hlaing, the general who now runs Myanmar, was responsible for the military's operations in 2017.

The case drew even more attention when the Nobel laureate Aung San Suu Kyi, who at the time headed the elected government in Myanmar, chose to lead the initial legal defence of her country at The Hague in person, for which she was widely criticised.

She had very limited influence over the actions of the Myanmar military in Rakhine State, but her refusal to condemn them dismayed many of those who until then had admired her courage and adherence to democratic principles.

Since she was deposed by a coup in 2021 and placed under arrest the defence has been led by a new team appointed by the military.

Diungkapkan bahwa historically, proving that genocide has been committed has been very difficult. Judges apply a high bar to this.

Typically, where there is no explicitly genocidal programme, like that of the Nazis, the judges require that the evidence presented at court must be such that the only reasonable inference from the actions of the defendants is that they had genocidal intent.

When Bosnia-Herzegovina filed a genocide case against Serbia at the ICJ in 1993, it took the court 14 years to conclude that while incidents like the 1995 massacre at Srebrenica did amount to genocide, there was not sufficient proof that the state of Serbia had genocidal intent, though it was found to have failed to prevent genocide.

Myanmar's lawyers and Aung San Suu Kyi have argued something similar.

Suu Kyi said that The Gambia's team mischaracterised a complex conflict and military operation, and that while she accepted that war crimes may have been committed against the Rohingyas, that is not proof of genocidal intent.

Aung San Suu Kyi's refusal to condemn the Myanmar military's actions in Rakhine State dismayed her admirers.

But Arsalan Suleman believes the weight of evidence his team gathered is enough to meet that high bar.

"What we presented to the court was the long history of discrimination targeting the Rohingya, and how that history, and the policies connected with it, provide a background to understand the government's language, rhetoric, propaganda, and policies that were part of the 2017 'clearance operations'," Suleman said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "we discussed the 1982 citizenship law, and the tightening noose of discriminatory laws that restricted access to education, healthcare, livelihoods, and travel - all of which made life really impossible for the rohingya and, we argued, was one of several indicators of genocidal intent. ".

What happens if the court does find in favour of The Gambia?.

Myanmar would then find itself tarnished by having committed "the crime of crimes", as sitting on the same bench as Nazi Germany, the Rwandan Hutu militants and the Bosnian Serbs at Srebrenica.

That might seem a setback for Min Aung Hlaing, the general who now runs Myanmar, who above all was responsible for the military's operations in 2017, and who has been trying to improve his dismal international image in recent months.

Diungkapkan bahwa there is no right of appeal against an icj verdict. However, there is also no penalty that follows an ICJ verdict.

The Burmese coup leader is focused mostly on rebuilding relations with neighbouring Asian countries, who are unlikely to pay too much attention to such a verdict, and much less on rebuilding relations with Western countries who do care.

Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh's Cox's Bazar mark the ninth anniversary of their exodus from Myanmar.

But for the huge Rohingya diaspora this verdict matters a great deal.

"This is like formal recognition of our suffering," says Mohammed Nowkim, a Rohingya who was driven out of the Rakhine town of Buthidaung in 2017 and now lives in Canada.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "for the rohingya, this trial is a moment of acknowledgement of our suffering after years of denial. The Rohingya have been waiting for justice for decades, not just this year. ".

He and other Rohingya activists hope that a ruling in favour of The Gambia will prompt more co-ordinated action by other countries to find a resolution which allows them to go home to Rakhine State, in safety.

More than a million are stuck in wretched camps in Bangladesh, barred from employment as international funding dries up.

But the obstacles to realising this hope are formidable.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, rakhine state has been ravaged by a conflict between the military and the insurgent arakan army, which now controls most of the territory. It is supported by the indigenous Rakhine population who are very hostile to the idea of the Rohingyas coming back.

Sebagaimana diketahui, many rohingya villages have been completely destroyed. And international support for them has faded over the years. Even an unprecedented genocide verdict at the world's highest court cannot change that reality.

Berdasarkan laporan, myanmar's army massacred rohingyas. Now it wants their help.

Seeing through the official story in Myanmar.

#1274. Claude-maker Anthropic poised for $1.4tn stock market debut

📅 18 Nov 2026

Claude-maker Anthropic poised for $1.4tn stock market debut

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6742m39xgzxo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has quickly become one of the most notable names in the technology industry.

Berdasarkan laporan, anthropic is poised to hit a value of at least $1. 4 trillion (Â£1. 1 trillion) when it debuts on the public stock market.

The artificial intelligence (AI) company behind the popular chatbot Claude said it will price shares at $83 each when it lists on Thursday on the Nasdaq, a tech-focused stock exchange based in New York.

That price will make it one of the most highly valued companies in the world.

It will be the first US company focused exclusively on AI to go public, marking a crucial test for the fast-growing industry.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the ai firm said earlier this month it would likely offer its shares for between $70 and $78 each, which valued the company at up to $1. 3tn.

But demand for Anthropic's stock debut - commonly referred to as its initial public offering, or IPO - is very high, according to one early investor in the company who spoke with the BBC on condition of anonymity.

If that turns out to be the case, Anthropic's valuation could quickly blow past its target on Thursday when trading begins.

Sebagaimana diketahui, depending on how strong that demand is, anthropic could even exceed the early market valuation of elon musk's spacex, which was the world's most highly valued stock debut when it went public with a value of $2. 2tn in June.

However, in the weeks that followed, SpaceX shares fell significantly in price.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as it stands, anthropic's listing will see the firm raise more than $68bn from its initial investors. It is also expecting another $26bn from private placements. So the total amount the company will raise is expected to be $94bn.

The amount of cash Anthropic has raised from its listing is already more than SpaceX raised in June.

OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT and Anthropic's biggest rival, is expected to go public next year.

Until then, Anthropic will be the only public company in the US that is considered a true AI company, or one that was founded and built around AI tools and products for consumers and businesses.

There is excitement around Anthropic's listing, but also some concern from investors around its ability to generate revenue and profits going forward.

Yang Wang, a principle financial analyst with Counterpoint Research, said the central issue for Anthropic is whether its business "can keep pace" as hundreds of billions of dollars in financial obligations come due in the next couple of years.

"Nevertheless, it is not an everyday occurrence for public investors to gain direct exposure to a frontier-model developer with the potential to shape the next stage of productivity," Wang said.

Diungkapkan bahwa while nearly every other major tech company is pouring huge amounts of money into the technology and infrastructure required for their own ai tools, they are built around social media or online retail or online search. AI tools and applications are secondary.

"Anthropic going public gives us a whole new window into what AI demand looks like," Marta Norton, who heads investment strategy at investment firm Empower, told the BBC.

The seven Anthropic founders who are about to become multi-billionaires.

Anthropic was started by a group of co-founders, led by siblings Dario Amodei and Daniela Amodei, all of whom left their work at OpenAI to start a new AI firm.

The company has carved itself out in the ongoing AI race as more focused on building the technology with safety top of mind.

Diungkapkan bahwa it refused to comply with a demand by the us department of defense that anthropic's tools be used in an essentially unrestricted way. And Dario Amodei has been outspoken in his belief that AI tools may soon be so powerful that they present a threat to human existence.

Nonetheless, the company is looking to grow quickly and gain more access to financing through the public markets in order to do so.

Norton said Anthropic going public now, in a time of market volatility comes down to the simple fact that the company needs access to more money.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "ai is financially demanding," norton said. "The public markets open up the financial spigot a little bit more, and so the time has come. ".

But broader anxieties have started to grow about the AI industry's business model, which is built on expensive, reliant on in-demand computer chips, controversial data centres, and deals with other tech companies.

The Federal Reserve Bank has expressed concern about the rapid growth of AI-related debt being financed through "complex and opaque" structures, according to minutes from its October meeting to discuss a potential rate rise.

A few of the meeting's participants also noted that "AI-related exposures were becoming increasingly concentrated among a small number of firms".

#1277. Israeli military launches rare ground operation in Gaza beyond Yellow Line

Israeli military launches rare ground operation in Gaza beyond Yellow Line

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cw8r7510degno?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Residents fled the area near Nuseirat and Bureij refugee camps following the Israeli evacuation order.

Israeli ground forces have launched a rare operation in part of the central Gaza Strip outside their control, after issuing evacuation orders for residents.

Witnesses said tanks advanced east of Nuseirat refugee camp and rolled onto the territory's main north to south road under the cover of artillery strikes.

The Israeli military said the "targeted" operation aimed to dismantle a "terror tunnel" west of the so-called Yellow Line, which marks the more than 60% of Gaza's territory occupied by Israel.

The Palestinian armed group Hamas, which controls the rest of Gaza, accused Israel of a "flagrant violation" of the October 2025 ceasefire agreement.

Sebagaimana diketahui, violence has continued in gaza over the past 13 months, with near-daily israeli strikes, and living conditions for the 2. 1 million people there remain dire.

Early on Wednesday afternoon, Israeli military body Cogat's Arabic spokesperson announced the start of the incursion and warned Palestinians living in an area north of Nuseirat and Bureij refugee camp to stay away for their own safety.

It also said a section of the north to south Salah al-Din road that passed through the area would be closed to traffic.

Later, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said it had begun a joint operation with the Shin Bet security service "to dismantle a terror tunnel west of the Yellow Line that posed an immediate and direct threat to IDF troops".

"IDF troops under the Southern Command are deployed in the area in accordance with the ceasefire agreement and will continue to operate to remove any immediate threat and thwart attempts by the Hamas terrorist organisation to harm Israeli civilians or IDF troops, or to violate the agreement," it added.

Hamas warned in a statement that the advance of Israeli military vehicles beyond the Yellow Line and the evacuation of residents constituted "a dangerous development and a flagrant violation of the ceasefire agreement".

Footage published by Palestinian media outlets and on social media showed families fleeing areas near Nuseirat camp following the announcement.

Berdasarkan laporan, in one video verified by bbc verify, a man can be seen ducking after hearing artillery fire and then running along salah al-din road, about 1. 9 miles) west of the Yellow Line. 5km (0. "The Israeli occupation now is firing randomly near the houses and tents of people," he says.

Automatic gunfire can be heard in another video filmed just to the south-east.

Berdasarkan laporan, a resident of nuseirat who was forced to flee told bbc arabic's middle east daily programme: "the situation is now extremely dire, with israeli forces firing indiscriminately at areas where displaced people have sought shelter. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa "we couldn't take any of our belongings with us - not even our blankets, pillows, or clothes. We had no choice but to leave everything behind. ".

A second resident also reported "indiscriminate gunfire and shelling" and said there had been "numerous casualties, including fatalities".

Asked about reported fatalities, the IDF sent a general statement about the operation.

Israel building new land barriers in Gaza and displacing families.

Israel moves Yellow Line deeper into Gaza, satellite images show.

Gaza's Hamas-run Civil Defence agency said three people were killed and others were wounded in three separate Israeli drone strikes on Wednesday.

One man was killed in Nuseirat, the second to the north in Gaza City, and the third in the central town of Deir al-Balah, it added.

The IDF told the BBC that it had "struck several military operatives".

At least 1,658 people have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza since the ceasefire began last year, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.

The Israeli military says six of its soldiers have been killed over the same period.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, meanwhile, more than 1. 9 million people - about 90% of Gaza's population - remain displaced, with 1. 4 million of them living in tents or makeshift shelters, according to the UN.

Reconstruction has yet to begin in Gaza, where an estimated 82% of all structures have been destroyed or damaged during the war, as US President Donald Trump's peace plan has largely stalled.

The disarmament of Hamas has been a key sticking point.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the group has agreed to give up its weapons in exchange for a phased withdrawal of israeli troops from the 60% of gaza they currently occupy. But Israel has insisted that Hamas must fully disarm before any pullout.

The war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.

Since then, more than 74,700 people have been killed in Gaza, the health ministry says.

UK and allies call on Israel to allow rapid humanitarian access to Gaza.

Israel kills Hamas commander in strike on Gaza camp, officials say.

Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills six Palestinians, health ministry says.

#1281. Russian man accused of spying on US tech defence company that assists Ukraine

Russian man accused of spying on US tech defence company that assists Ukraine

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cq20xg80ly47o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

The alleged foreign agent was discovered with two Russian passports.

US investigators have arrested a Russian man who they say was recruited by Moscow to spy on employees of a technology and defence firm in California's Silicon Valley that has links to Ukraine.

Igor D'iu is accused of acting as an agent of a foreign government to conduct a spying operation in Palo Alto, near San Francisco.

He is also accused of stalking employees of the company and possessing falsified identity documents.

Diungkapkan bahwa the company is not named in charging documents, but is described as a publicly traded technology and defence company that produces software used by ukraine in its war with russia. US prosecutors say the company was targeted by Russia due to its assistance to Kyiv.

"The allegations in this case describe a state-sponsored operation to target and harass employees of an American technology and defense company because of that company's assistance to Ukraine in its war with Russia," said US Attorney for the Northern District of California Craig Missakian.

Berdasarkan laporan, "we will not tolerate any efforts - by foreign governments or otherwise - to turn silicon valley into a base for foreign intelligence operations. ".

Prosecutors say that D'iu entered the US unlawfully via the Mexico border, after travelling there from Istanbul in June.

Berdasarkan laporan, he was allegedly recruited through the telegram encrypted messaging app. His handlers referred to Russia as "'the Motherland' and directed D'iu to gather information about the company because it was supplying weapons used against Russia in Ukraine".

On their instruction, he purchased computers, phones, wireless networking equipment and remote access software - tools he needed for his spy mission.

He then went to a coffee shop located near the company's offices in Palo Alto, where he photographed laptop screens of employees who were working there.

His handlers also allegedly "instructed him to position his laptop at designated locations near the company so they could remotely access it and attempt to collect information from company employees in the vicinity".

The suspect allegedly took photos of employees screens at a cafe near the office.

Diungkapkan bahwa according to cbs news, the bbc's us partner, the company in question is palantir technologies. Palantir did not reply to a BBC request for comment.

D'iu also allegedly conducted surveillance of employees and their residences.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, on 3 september, he followed a vehicle driven by one senior executive for nearly 30 miles. He fled after she drove to a police station. Police later obtained evidence that he had followed other employees' cars on previous days.

During the investigation, officials discovered identity cards that had been falsified - including a US passport, California ID card, and a Social Security card with the fake name "Hugo Landry Johns".

A raid on his home in October in East Palo Alto turned up two Russian passports, and a handwritten notebook that contained numerous home addresses of employees "family members' names, educational and employment histories, and assessments of their strengths and weaknesses", prosecutors say.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, he faces two charges related his alleged work as a foreign agent, one charge of interstate stalking, and one count of fraud related to his identity documents. He faces over 15 years in prison if found guilty.

The suspect was found with forged identification documents including a US passport.

Ukraine's long-range drones using Western tech to hit Russia.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, he has been held in jail since 2 november. It is unclear whether he has hired a lawyer who can speak on his behalf.

The arrest comes as espionage allegations roil the US tech industry, amid the news that Nvidia ex-CEO Jensen Huang had a romantic affair with a woman suspected of spying for China.

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6lyw490z14jo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

The mother of a four-year-old girl killed in central France and found along a motorway almost 40 years ago has been sentenced to 20 years in prison.

Halima El Bakhti, 72, was found guilty on Tuesday of "torture and acts of barbarity resulting in death without the intent to kill", French media reports.

The girl's father, 74-year-old Ahmed Touloub, was handed a 15-year sentence as an accomplice.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, four-year-old inass touloub was found along the a10 road in suã¨vres in the loir-et-cher department on 11 august 1987. Her body bore multiple marks of abuse, including human bite marks, broken bones and burns with an iron.

Sebagaimana diketahui, she was buried in an unmarked grave near the location where her body was found. Unidentified for three decades, she was known only as the "Little Martyr of the A10".

Then, in 2018, she was identified after the DNA of her brother â tested in an unrelated case â matched with hers, leading to the arrest of their parents.

The trial took place in Loir-et-Cher Assize Court from 2 November, with the verdict delivered on Tuesday after several hours of deliberation.

During the trial, prosecutor AnaÃ¯s Allio emphasised that "not a single part of Inass's body was spared", and recalled the "sense of vertigo that overcame us all" upon viewing the "unbearable photographs" from the autopsy, France Info reports.

The jury concluded that the child's mother was suffering from impaired judgement at the time of the girl's death, which reduced the maximum potential sentence.

French media outlet France Info described the two defendants as sitting stoically in chairs before the court with their heads bowed as the reasoning behind the verdict was read out.

El Bakhti and Touloub have 10 days to appeal the verdict.

Inass's death sparked one of France's biggest ever investigations, with the girl's photograph posted in public places and an alert sent to more than 30 countries.

Grand Theft Auto VI released as gamers rejoice globally

Tanggal: 19 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.dw.com/en/grand-theft-auto-vi-released-as-gamers-rejoice-globally/a-79986461?maca=en-rss-en-all-1573-rdf

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, after 13 years of waiting, fans around the world will get to play the latest installment in the blockbuster video game series. In focus: A tale of crime and violence in a fictionalized version of Miami.

Grand Theft Auto VI will be officially launched Thursday, ending a 13-year wait for one of the most anticipated games ever.

The game will become playable at midnight local time (CET) on a wide range of platforms, including PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X, meaning gamers in Asia will get to play the game ahead of users in the US and Europe.

In New Zealand, one of the first countries worldwide where the game became available, the release prompted internet providers to prepare for a spike in internet usage at midnight.

This comes due to the game's size of 212 gigabytes, more than a quarter of the average New Zealand household's usage in a month.

Rockstar Games, the company behind the GTA franchise, faces high expectation after 13 years of anticipation, with the previous versions having become commercial and cultural hits around the world.

GTA games sold 470 million units worldwide, and the fifth installment generated $1 billion in retail sales in just three days after its release in 2013.

Take-Two Interactive, Rockstar Games' parent company, saw its shares rise by more than eight percent the day before the game's release.

The game takes place in Vice City, a fictional version of Miami.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it follows lucia caminos and jason duval, a couple drawn into criminal networks while trying to secure a better life. GTA games are often criticized for including excessive violence and for glorifying crimes and drug use.

Lucia, a former prisoner, and Jason, an ex-military man, experience a series of criminal jobs that go wrong in the drug-trafficking world of Leonida, a fictional state based on Florida.

According to Rockstar, Leonida is the company's most detailed open world so far, extending beyond Vice City into smaller communities and nightlife hotspots inspired by locations in South Florida.

Music has been an intrinsic part of the GTA experience, and the latest game is expected to feature a soundtrack including artists like Tame Impala and SZA.

#1289. Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries to be US Speaker of the House

📅 18 Nov 2026

Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries to be US Speaker of the House

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cmy49873dn95o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Democrats in the US House of Representatives officially nominated Hakeem Jeffries to be Speaker, setting him on the path to become the first black lawmaker to lead the chamber.

The House will elect its new Speaker on 3 January, when the next term begins and Democrats will be in the majority.

Berdasarkan laporan, his election to the powerful position - the speaker is in line to succeed the president after the vice-president - is widely expected. Should he win, Jeffries will preside over his party's largest House majority in years and benefit from the Senate also being under Democrats' control.

Jeffries told reporters after the vote that the nomination was "a high honour and a distinct privilege".

Diungkapkan bahwa as of wednesday, democrats will hold at least 257 seats in the house next year, which is well beyond the 218 needed for a majority. Seven races from the recent midterm elections are still uncalled.

Diungkapkan bahwa jeffries, who represents a district in new york, was re-elected as the party leader in a 251-11 closed-door vote on wednesday. He has served as minority leader since 2023.

The Congressional Black Caucus, currently made up of only Democratic House members, noted the potential history-making moment when Jeffries takes the helm of the House.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "the american people, largely driven by turnout among black communities, particularly across the south, have trusted us to make washington work for them," said the committee's chair, yvette clarke, in a statement. "Now, it is our charge and responsibility to do all we can to deliver on their faith. ".

Despite overwhelming support in Wednesday's vote , Jeffries faced a handful of holdouts from new members in the party's left wing, who have said the party's sweeping victory in the midterm elections is a sign voters want change.

"While we have seen meaningful progress, there is still work to be done to ensure that the direction our party takes in this coming Congress reflects what our constituents are demanding of our leadership," seven incoming lawmakers, including fellow New Yorkers Darializa Avila Chevalier and Claire Valdez, said in a statement.

All congressional Democrats are gearing up for clashes with the White House once they officially take control in January.

President Donald Trump, a Republican, has signalled a willingness to work with Democrats on some issues, but has also pledged to use his veto power to reject legislation he does not like.

Trump's opposition could make it hard for Democrats to deliver on their campaign promises to address affordability and pass other reforms.

At a news conference following the vote on Wednesday, Jeffries pledged that House Democrats would "fight to lower the high costs of groceries and gas and housing", and "make healthcare affordable for every single American".

Though the party will have a large enough majority to weather defections on must-pass legislation, Jeffries will still have to navigate internal ideological divisions that have grown particularly sharp over US support of Israel and Americans' rising healthcare costs.

Many incoming Democrats, including members of the Democratic Socialists of America, won their elections by challenging the party establishment.

The Congressional Progressive Caucus, from the party's left wing, congratulated Jeffries on the nomination, adding they would "continue conversations with Leader Jeffries to ensure Democrats deliver a bold agenda for working people".

Along with shepherding legislation, Jeffries as Speaker will also have to manage the complex array of investigations that Democrats plan to launch into Trump, his family, and cabinet members now that they have regained control of the chamber's oversight powers.

Rounding out their party leadership team, House Democrats also elected Katherine Clark of Massachusetts as majority leader, Pete Aguilar of California as majority whip, and Joe Neguse of Colorado as assistant speaker.

#1291. What the Crimean bridge attack means for Russia

📅 19 Nov 2026

What the Crimean bridge attack means for Russia

Tanggal: 19 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.dw.com/en/what-the-crimean-bridge-attack-means-for-russia/a-79985991?maca=en-rss-en-all-1573-rdf

Berdasarkan laporan, ukraine's latest strike on the kerch bridge has disrupted a key transport link between russia and crimea. Beyond the damage, the attack could have serious consequences for Russian military logistics and Putin's prestige.

It had been a year and a half since Ukraine last attacked the 19-kilometer-long Kerch Bridge connecting Russian-annexed Crimea with Russia's Krasnodar region.

Berdasarkan laporan, now, ukraine has struck again. The attack during the night of November 17 caused the highway section of the bridge to collapse into the sea. As a result, shipping traffic between the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov has also been disrupted.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, russia's ministry of transport announced a "temporary suspension" of road and rail traffic on the bridge, though later, rail services were resumed. Russian authorities have launched a criminal investigation into what they are calling a "terrorist attack. " It was only after this announcement that the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) confirmed the attack.

Berdasarkan laporan, the kerch strait bridge is considered one of russian president vladimir putin's most prestigious projects. Its construction began after Russia's 2014 annexation of the Ukrainian Crimea peninsula, an act considered illegal under international law. The Kerch Bridge was completed four years later.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it has been targeted by ukraine on several occasions since russia's 2022 full-scale invasion. The most well-known strike occurred in October 2022, when an explosives-laden truck detonated on the bridge, causing extensive damage and several months of traffic restrictions. The most recent attack took place in June 2025, when the SBU reported that an underwater support structure was blown up.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the latest ukrainian operation lasted about a month, and consisted of seven distinct phases. "First, the SBU and armed forces systematically neutralized the enemy's air defense system. After that, the direct attack on the bridge began," says the SBU Telegram channel.

Some Russian military bloggers claim that the attack was carried out with the support of Ukraine's Western allies, or at least using their equipment and weapons.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ukraine has not confirmed this. It has instead pointed out that various Ukrainian-made weapons were used in the attack, ranging from a variety of drones, to FP-5 Flamingo and R-360 Neptun missiles. British daily The Times has cited Ukrainian military sources, saying that Ukraine attacked the bridge without the support of SpaceX's satellite network system Starlink. There has been no confirmation of this so far.

Sebagaimana diketahui, ukrainian president volodymyr zelenskyy, meanwhile, described the strike as a response to russian attacks: "russia is attacking our infrastructure every day, particularly bridges in zaporizhzhia, dnipro, kyiv, and the odesa region. " He said "we are rebuilding our infrastructure, but we also remind Russia that the war always returns to where it began. ".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, after the attack, pictures and videos of the bridge were shared on social media. The Krimskij Veter Telegram channel has highlighted damage to the railroad link and questioned why Russian authorities have opted to resume train services.

Diungkapkan bahwa the kerch strait shipping channel is also completely blocked by debris. "This brings road traffic to a standstill, but also shipping between the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov," the channel writes.

Diungkapkan bahwa indeed, the kerch strait navigational channel is merely 120 meters wide, writes mychajlo hontschar of the ukrainian center for global studies "strategy xxi" on facebook. "The strait is shallow, only three to five meters deep. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as early as the 19th century, the seabed was dredged to allow heavier ships to pass from the black sea to the sea of azov and vice versa. "Now, Vladimir Putin's bridge-building efforts have brought shipping to an indefinite standstill," Hontschar said.

Not only will river-sea vessels no longer be able to leave the waters of the Sea of Azov, the Don, and the Volga, but boats and small ships from the Black Sea fleet and the Caspian flotilla based in Novorossiysk will also be unable to do so.

Many pro-Kremlin Telegram channels have been quick to claim that the bridge does not play an important role in the Russian army's logistics or in supplying Crimea.

Berdasarkan laporan, the dva mayora (two majors) channel quotes the "deputy president of the republic of crimea," olga kurlayeva, who described the bridge as a "purely civilian structure. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa ukrainian military experts interviewed by dw, on the other hand, point to the systematic disruption of russian logistics. These efforts also included regular attacks on the R-80 highway leading through Russian-occupied territories of the Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia, and Kherson regions.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, russia cannot replace the kerch bridge with any other land connection, says oleksandr kovalenko, a ukrainian military expert with the information resistance group that seeks to counter disinformation. He expects the damaged bridge will cause supply problems for the Russian armed forces: "If there is a resource shortage during attacks or in defense, then either the attacks or the defense will fail. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, that is why he does not rule out a decline in attacks from occupied crimea on the rest of ukraine. And while they don't originate in Crimea, they are brought over via the Kerch Bridge. "From there, many drones are launched toward Odesa, Mykolaiv, and the right bank of the Dnipro River in the Kherson region. Then there are attacks using Iskander-M ballistic missiles, as well as Zircon and Oniks missiles, guided missiles, and glide bombs. "There are many launch pads for kamikaze drones in Crimea — in the Hvardijsk area, at Cape Chauda and in Balaklava," Kovalenko told DW. They also fly over Crimea en route toward Ukraine. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, kovalenko says the bridge strike has dealt a serious blow to vladimir putin's standing. It comes at a sensitive time as Putin is about to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, China.

Sebagaimana diketahui, memes and witty comments about the bridge abound on x. Meanwhile, the Russian president's spokesperson Dmitry Peskov has promised to rebuild the bridge and assured that it will be "even better than before. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, andrii korezkyj of the kyiv university of transportation, however, says this is not likely to happen anytime soon. "All in all, I would estimate that it would take between one and a half and three years [to rebuild]," Korezkyj told DW, adding, "I don't think they'll let the Russians build another [bridge] arch like that near the Ukrainian border without interference. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa pro-russian commentators, known as z-bloggers, agree with this view. "Unlike in 2022 and 2023, the Ukrainian armed forces are now able to launch strikes against floating cranes and repair teams. ".

"Even installing a pre-assembled arch under these conditions would constitute a challenging task," writes the pro-Kremlin Rybar Telegram channel.

#1292. EU ‘to close door’ to talks on long-term UK ties until Burnham has decided on Brexit

📅 18 Nov 2026

EU ‘to close door’ to talks on long-term UK ties until Burnham has decided on Brexit

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/18/eu-uk-reset-summit-talks-burnham-brexit

Diplomats say piecemeal approach of resets is coming to an end and Europe wants clarity on whether Britain wants to reverse its exit.

The EU will shut the door to discussions with Andy Burnham about the UK’s longer-term relationship with the bloc until the government has decided whether it wants to proceed with reversing Brexit, diplomats have said.

European capitals are also warning they have reached the end of the line for piecemeal “reset” summits with the UK and want the prime minister to focus on his next steps domestically before they proceed.

But they suggested a joint statement after a summit this Friday would signal that further discussions would follow on the UK’s entry to the EU’s energy single markets, irregular migration and a closer defence and security relationship.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “clarity is what we need more than anything from the uk. Don’t come back until you know what you want. Work out what your options really are and then come to negotiate,” one EU diplomat said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “the prime minister needs to bring the public with him. We can’t have another negotiation based on just half the country. We’ll only put the effort in if we know it’s not going to change down the line. ”.

Burnham is expected to set out his own next steps after the summit on Monday, including his hopes for a “national conversation” on what a closer relationship might look like.

Sebagaimana diketahui, with less than 48 hours before the brussels summit, negotiators were still racing to finalise friday’s agreement. A leaked draft seen by the Guardian shows continued disagreement over demands by the EU that the UK commit to aligning with the bloc’s trade defence measures, such as tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles, in exchange for inclusion in Made in Europe legislation.

The text shows the UK is pushing for a weaker commitment, only promising an “aim to protect supply chains consistently across our markets and guard against potential risks of circumvention”.

A Cabinet Office source said Made in Europe language was “the highest jeopardy” in the negotiations, while an EU official suggested it was the part of the discussions most likely to go “down to the wire” on Friday.

Though there is a formal commitment to annual reset summits, senior EU diplomats say the current approach, designed by Keir Starmer, will quickly “reach its limits” and more “mini deals” do not make sense.

One said the “piecemeal approach is coming to an end” and that Burnham’s intentions for the UK’s long-term relationship created a natural juncture for the EU too.

Sebagaimana diketahui, another said: “it is like a buffet: you can choose to nibble on one or two dishes to start, but at a certain point you have to go for the whole of the buffet. ”.

One EU diplomat said there would be a “pause for reflection” after the Friday summit.

Burnham has said there is no rush to decide on the longer-term relationship, as he comes under pressure from within his own party to slow the pace of pursuing of closer ties.

He is not now expected to set out the full range of options for the future relationship – the status quo, customs union, single market or full rejoin – until he announces his 10-year plan in December.

Sources said the government was considering holding a year-long “national conversation” in 2027, including town halls and citizens assemblies, before deciding which route to pursue in advance of the next election.

However, the potential length of that debate has alarmed Brussels officials, who were caught off-guard by the launch of the new pro-Brexit campaign group Stay Out, set up by architects of the Vote Leave campaign.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one eu diplomat said: “the government would spend the year making evidence-based arguments about each of the four options, while boris johnson and michael gove and nigel farage will spend it shouting about traitors. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, after the reset deal is agreed on friday, it will be enacted by the european partnership bill, covering the deals on food and agriculture, emissions trading and youth mobility. It is expected to be introduced before Christmas, with legislation laid possibly as soon as next week.

Sebagaimana diketahui, eu diplomats said the two sides were expected to settle on a quota of about 100,000 people a year being allowed to work, travel or study in each other’s territories. Originally, the UK had pitched for 50,000 and then 80,000, while Brussels has consistently sought a higher number.

Both sides have agreed that tuition fees for European students coming to the UK should be discussed at a later date, although there have been attempts by some member states to link the debate to the ratification of the whole reset deal.

Sebagaimana diketahui, senior labour figures are already beginning their push to have a full rejoining on the table. The former business secretary Peter Kyle said Burnham should fight the next election on a promise to rejoin the EU, with voters given a referendum on the outcome of any deal.

Kyle, who was a key member of Starmer’s cabinet, said the “only way through” the challenges of the domestic political debate was for the government to offer voters the choice to accept or reject any agreement.

He is the latest senior Labour MP to publicly wade into the Brexit debate, after the former foreign secretary David Lammy said the party should go into the next election clear that its intention was to rejoin.

Rachel Reeves, the former chancellor, has also said Britain’s future should be back in the bloc, arguing that leaving had made the UK “poorer, weaker and less secure”.

#1293. The leave campaign has been resurrected, so how should Burnham respond?

📅 18 Nov 2026

The leave campaign has been resurrected, so how should Burnham respond?

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/18/pro-brexit-stay-out-same-playbook-analysis

No 10 is confident the PM can make the case for closer EU ties, while others worry about leaving the campaign solely in his hands.

The launch of a pro-Brexit campaign was one of the few genuine surprises this week in Westminster, even if the arguments were straight out of a familiar playbook.

The video launched on X over the weekend, with scenes of riots in France, champagne flowing in Brussels, and European politicians saying how desperate they were for Britain’s cash.

Sebagaimana diketahui, among westminster’s anti-brexit veterans, there was immediate chatter about whether a counteroffensive was needed. “I think the immediate reaction was – are they off to the races while we are still putting our pants on?” one said.

For now, the rebuttal of Stay Out’s claims – including that returning to the EU would cost £750m a week – is mostly being done on social media by interested pro-rejoin freelancers, without any kind of central organisation.

One MP said: “It is hard for us to begin any kind of new pro-rejoin campaign until we know exactly the direction the government is heading.

Berdasarkan laporan, “there are organisations that exist already, like best for britain, but i think making the case to the public would need a fresh movement. I think we want to stay away from the kind of marches that People’s Vote movement did with the blue berets if we can possibly avoid it. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, inside no 10, there is a confidence that andy burnham can make his own case for a closer relationship with europe, without the need for any external pressure group. Stay Out – which is run by the former deputy chief Brexit negotiator Oliver Lewis – will be dubbed “the status quo campaign”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there is reason to be confident. Strategists have seen Labour polling that shows almost three-quarters – 71% – of all voters support a closer relationship with Europe if it helps bring down prices and grow the economy.

It will be the prime minister, they say, who can front any campaigning that is needed, who can argue that Brexit has done more harm than good, damaging the economy, making it harder for British people to travel and businesses to trade and fuelling the small boats crisis.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, however, there will be some fears that this has been tried before when david cameron attempted to make the case for remain in 2016. “Cameron could not make this kind of emotional connection with people, it was business leaders, facts and figures, and he was arguing for the status quo,” one said. “We are the change campaign now. But Labour strategists say this is a fundamentally different political moment. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, while some cabinet members urged caution last week over burnham’s uncertain direction on europe, most trust the prime minister can set out a viable post-summit plan. “All of us, honestly, are slightly running to catch up with a different way of doing things,” one said. “We all easily lapse into the worries about leave-voting seats.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “but there is obviously an argument to be made that the old rules don’t apply. And we have to believe in that as the way to affect public sentiment. And Andy’s way of doing things is laying out political argument. ”.

Sign up for the Breaking News UK email to get newsletter alerts direct to your inbox.

Berdasarkan laporan, there are some close to labour who worry about leaving the argument solely to burnham. “You do need rebuttal out there and people ready to go out and fight and say, this is bollocks. And it felt like that infrastructure is not there yet. “Can they do this from the bowels of Downing Street?” one asked. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, another veteran of the remain campaign said there was concern about being “left out on a limb” if a rejoin campaign was resurrected. They have people willing to help but it’s not organised in any way. “I think whether they like it or not, there will be an apolitical campaign trying to push the maximalist position on Europe. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa many of those who worked on the remain campaign and the subsequent people’s vote are scarred by the experience, particular the final months which descended into bitter infighting. But the same is also true for some of the most high-profile veterans of Vote Leave – who also want to steer clear of Stay Out.

Sebagaimana diketahui, as in the pro-brexit campaigns, there are often willing funders to push pro-european campaigning. “But you could not pay me any money to go back to that issue. “It will happen because there will be money for it,” one campaign veteran said. ”.

#1296. Julio Iglesias facing court investigation over alleged sexual offences

📅 18 Nov 2026

Julio Iglesias facing court investigation over alleged sexual offences

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6x284pnn4e2o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Singer Julio Iglesias is facing an investigation by Spain's national court over allegations he sexually abused and assaulted two female former staff members.

Two women, who worked for the 83-year-old in the Caribbean, have accused him of abuse which they say took place in the Bahamas and the Dominican Republic in 2021.

The announcement comes after Spanish prosecutors dropped an inquiry into the claims earlier this year after concluding that they lacked jurisdiction because the alleged crimes took place abroad.

Iglesias, who has been a household name in Spain since the 1960s and has sold millions of records worldwide, has previously denied the allegations.

But in a statement published on Wednesday, external (in Spanish), national court Judge Antonio PiÃ±a said the account given in the complaint, alongside preliminary evidence provided, justified opening criminal proceedings.

He added that the investigation would cover parts of the complaint relating to potential crimes against sexual freedom, as well as assault and degrading treatment.

Berdasarkan laporan, but the court will not investigate claims made in the lawsuit of human trafficking or crimes against workers' rights. PiÃ±a said these allegations were dismissed after he looked into the hiring of the women and found there was "no deception or artifice involved".

PiÃ±a said the former employees had been summoned to testify in person on 3 February.

The announcement comes after Spain's public prosecutor's office shifted its position last month, saying it now believed the court had jurisdiction to investigate the allegations.

In its statement, the national court said Spanish law sets out that courts can hear cases of crimes committed abroad by Spanish citizens provided certain conditions are met.

The allegations against Iglesias first emerged in a joint three-year investigation between Spanish newspaper El Diario, external and television network Univision news, published in January.

In that investigation, the two women were identified as a domestic worker and a physical therapist, who described alleged sexual abuse and degrading working conditions.

The domestic worker, whose name was changed to Rebeca in the reports, said Iglesias would regularly call her to his room at the end of the day and would touch her inappropriately without consent.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, rebeca, a dominican who was 22 when the alleged events took place, also alleged that iglesias had forced her to take part in threesomes with another female member of staff. She also described the singer slapping her in the face and grabbing her genitals.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the other woman, a venezuelan physical therapist named as laura in the article, said iglesias had touched her breasts and kissed her on the mouth against her will. She added that he constantly threatened to fire her, controlled how much food she ate and asked her about when her period was due.

Rebeca and Laura filed an initial legal complaint in January against Iglesias for sexual assault and human trafficking.

Diungkapkan bahwa in a response to the allegations in january, iglesias said, external: "i deny having abused, coerced, or disrespected any woman. These accusations are absolutely false and deeply sadden me. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa on wednesday, the court said the lawsuit had been accepted based on evidence provided in the complaint. This included a photograph of one of the complainants, showing a bruise on her arm that was "consistent with the possibility of her being grabbed forcefully".

It added that the same photo showed "two marks on one of her thighs that could correspond to a human bite", which the complainant said were "a consequence of her forced participation in acts of a sexual nature".

WhatsApp message exchanges, including New Year's greetings, which suggest an "affectionate" relationship between the women and Iglesias, will also be considered, the court said.

But it added that the seemingly cordial tone, which presents "an apparent discrepancy with certain aspects of the narrative", would be clarified through a "complete and contextualised examination of the communications".

The claim over violations of workers' rights could not be investigated because there is no comparable criminal offence in the Bahamas and the Dominican Republic, where the alleged crimes took place, it said.

Iglesias is one of the most successful Latin artists of all time, having sold more than 300 million records in a career spanning decades.

He is also the father of fellow music superstar Enrique Iglesias.

#1297. Cheese, pet passports and youth mobility: what’s in the UK-EU ‘relationship reset’ draft?

📅 18 Nov 2026

Cheese, pet passports and youth mobility: what’s in the UK-EU ‘relationship reset’ draft?

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/18/uk-eu-relationship-reset-draft-explainer

Leaked text of 72-paragraph second draft shows agreement has largely been reached before expected signoff on Friday.

The UK-EU “relationship reset” agreement, which began in earnest under Keir Starmer, is expected to be signed off by Andy Burnham in Brussels on Friday.

A leaked text of the second draft shows an agreement has largely been reached with some outstanding points.

Here’s what is and isn’t addressed in the 72-paragraph joint communique, from pet passports and cheese imports to student fees and artist touring visas.

Berdasarkan laporan, you may not make it. The deal states it will “allow people from the EU and the UK to reside for up to three years to engage in activities such as work, studies, au pairing, volunteering, or simply travelling”.

But the deal may not be active until 2030 because work permits are the preserve of national governments, not something Brussels can solve.

“We aim to apply this agreement no later than 2028 and endeavour to ensure that opportunities under the scheme will be available to our young people no later than January 2030,” the draft says.

Diungkapkan bahwa this has yet to be agreed. The two options in the draft text are a halfway house between international and home fees, or a concession from the UK to allow EU citizens pay the same as British students (or Irish ones, who are also eligible for home fees under a separate longstanding agreement).

The choices, according to the draft, are “significantly reduced undergraduate” or “equal treatment” with UK nationals on tuition fees.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the british government wants to cap youth mobility at between 50,000 and 80,000 places to reduce impact on overall migration numbers. The EU is pushing for at least 100,000.

Some EU states, including Germany, are open to the idea of allowing unlimited numbers of British young people to work, live or study in their countries regardless of UK reciprocation.

Elton John has long been among those demanding the government fix a flaw in the Brexit deal which saw gigging bands or theatre groups unable to tour Europe without major bureaucracy (and its associated cost) since 2021.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the eu has resisted negotiating on the issue because, like youth mobility, it touches on work permits which are a national remit. But in what appears to be a win for the UK, touring artists do feature in the draft text.

No deal been reached, but it has been agreed that “the EU and the UK should explore further mutually beneficial solutions” for “touring artists”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, not yet. The draft agreement says the sanitary and phyto-sanitary (SPS) agreement will not be implemented until 1 March 2028.

This takes into account primary legislation that is needed on the UK side to dynamically align with EU standards.

Diungkapkan bahwa no. These are tied to the SPS deal, meaning British travellers will still have to fork out up to £200 every time they take their dog or cat to an EU country.

Travel and transport officials are hoping relevant changes to the SPS agreement can be brought forward.

Berdasarkan laporan, “around 15% of our customers have pets with them. For them it will make a huge difference,” Yann Leriche, the chief executive of Getlink, the owner of Eurotunnel, told the Guardian.

Diungkapkan bahwa no. The EU has pressed the UK to follow its trade defence measures which include quotas on Chinese hybrid-electric cars and tariffs on fully electric cars.

The UK has said it will not be coerced into a decision but is demanding that British manufacturers are not locked out of the upcoming Made in Europe legislation in exchange for forming a kind of trade club with the EU on autos.

Berdasarkan laporan, both sides agree to protectionist measures in “a particular supply chain” but there is no agreement yet on how that will apply. The UK’s proposed text says: “We will aim to protect supply chains consistently across our markets and guard against potential risks of circumvention. According to the text, the EU proposes that “the UK would be bound to ensure in its policies and national legal order the same outcomes” as measures imposed by the EU. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa it’s gone. Instead of a vague “trusted partnership”, both sides commit to a “partnership for economic resilience”.

The language in the latest draft agreement has also been tightened up in a concession to the UK, say diplomats.

Berdasarkan laporan, the uk wants to restore pre-brexit access to eu databases but this will not be agreed on friday. The EU will instead explore giving the UK access to its proposed Prüm International scheme “on data exchange for police cooperation to chosen third-country partners”.

There is no mention of Eurodac, the database that stores biometrics of asylum seekers in the EU, and diplomats say sharing this data, which was not collected for law enforcement purposes, could be tricky.

But according to the draft, the EU will “continue exploring ways to reinforce mutual and reciprocal exchanges of data on criminal records of third-country nationals”.

#1300. Fiona the hippo undergoing care after swallowing a hat at Cincinnati Zoo

📅 18 Nov 2026

Fiona the hippo undergoing care after swallowing a hat at Cincinnati Zoo

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cm2d93z0e9gjo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Watch: Fiona the hippo under observation after eating hat.

The Cincinnati Zoo in Ohio says its beloved hippopotamus Fiona is undergoing emergency medical care after swallowing a knit hat that slipped into her enclosure.

The Zoo said that Fiona had swallowed the hat about nine days ago and was asymptomatic at first, adding that she was "large enough that a small-ish hat should be passing through".

But a few days later, her appetite started to decrease, and the zoo staff were trying to encourage Fiona to eat to help push the hat through her digestive system.

Berdasarkan laporan, fiona rose to fame when she was born premature at the cincinnati zoo and at first struggled to survive. Her story inspired an ice cream flavour as well as a character in Cincinnati's ballet.

Michelle Curley, a spokesperson for the zoo, told US media that the hat got into Fiona's enclosure by accident, after a visitor tossed it in the air and it caught on a ceiling fan that flung it through a small opening.

"We probably couldn't make [it] happen again if we tried," Curley said.

Zoo staff have been providing a series of supportive measures like fluids and ultrasounds to help Fiona recover.

The latest ultrasound showed the hat passing through Fiona's small intestine, the staff said, adding that she is still a bit dehydrated.

"Surgery isn't an option for full-grown hippos and our best chance for success with Fiona would be if she could pass this on her own," one of the zookeepers said in an update.

Fiona was born six weeks early to 17-year-old hippo Bibi on 24 January 2017.

At birth she weighed 13 kg (29 lbs), which the zoo said was about half the previous lowest recorded birth weight for her species.

The zoo said staff were "rooting for her and hoping that she proves to be as strong and resilient as she was at the beginning of her life".

#1302. US Pentagon chief Hegseth signs military deal in Venezuela

📅 19 Nov 2026

US Pentagon chief Hegseth signs military deal in Venezuela

Tanggal: 19 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.dw.com/en/us-pentagon-chief-hegseth-signs-military-deal-in-venezuela/a-79985607?maca=en-rss-en-all-1573-rdf

Diungkapkan bahwa on a visit to caracas, pete hegseth signed a deal that signifies the "reestablishment of our defense partnership. " US-Venezuela ties were strained for years until US troops ousted ex-President Nicolas Maduro in January.

US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth visited Venezuela on Wednesday, met with the country's interim authorities and also signed a military cooperation deal with the Latin American country.

The Pentagon did not release any information on Hegseth's trip or confirm the visit, although it was broadcast on Venezuelan state media.

Berdasarkan laporan, the visit comes after us forces in january ousted former venezuelan president nicolas maduro and took him along with his wife to new york to face drug trafficking charges. Since then, US President Donald Trump has backed acting President Delcy Rodriguez to lead the country.

Both Rodriguez and Hegseth touted the new military agreement between the two countries at the presidential palace in Caracas.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, rodriguez said the deal would strengthen training for the venezuelan military while facilitating access to new technologies. She said this would allow the two nations to "face common threats. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, hegseth said the us sees the deal "as a reestablishment of our defense partnership and the opportunity to work together between our two great militaries. ".

The agreement includes intelligence sharing between the two nations in addition to joint training.

Berdasarkan laporan, the pentagon chief said the us seeks "to ensure the venezuelan people are not threatened by foreign actors or narco-terrorists or criminals and that they are safe and secure inside sovereign borders. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, hegseth said wednesday that since maduro's ouster, venezuela "has gone from our most aggressive regional threat to a compliant security partner. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, us-venezuela relations were strained under maduro, who had taken office in 2013. In 2019, Maduro cut off Venezuela's formal diplomatic relations with the US after Trump's first administration recognized Venezuelan opposition leader Juan Guaido as the country's interim president.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Diungkapkan bahwa after the ouster of maduro, the trump administration urged venezuela to comply with demands such as us access to the venezuelan oil market. Trump had threatened Rodriguez, who was Venezuela's vice president, with a "fate worse than Maduro" if she didn't cooperate with Washington.

Berdasarkan laporan, trump has later praised rodriguez as a "terrific person" who is doing a "great job. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa under rodriguez, venezuela has released political prisoners and facilitated the shipments of oil to the us, with the us then controlling the proceeds and returning the money under an energy deal. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has been overseeing Venezuela's transition and is in close contact with Rodriguez.

Berdasarkan laporan, elections after maduro's ouster are expected at some point in venezuela, but with rodriguez's government acting favorably towards the us, it's unclear whether they would happen anytime soon. Nobel Prize winner and opposition leader Maria Corina Machado recently urged elections after arriving in Venezuela.
