#1303. Can Anthropic's record breaking IPO stop the AI bubble bursting?

📅 18 Nov 2026

Can Anthropic's record breaking IPO stop the AI bubble bursting?

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cj4gnpzll020o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Can Anthropic's record breaking IPO stop the AI bubble bursting?.

It was during November 2020 that somewhere in San Francisco, a woman called Daniela Amodei phoned a friend, asking for advice.

Daniela oversaw safety and policy at OpenAI, one of the most talked-about AI companies in the world.

But Daniela and her brother Dario - who worked there too - had misgivings over safety levels at OpenAI and thought it could be time to walk away.

Berdasarkan laporan, so she did what many do when we can't make a decision about something, she phoned a friend. You already know the answer. The friend's reply was direct and to the point: "You don't need to be on the phone with me. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, the amodei siblings and a handful of other colleagues quit. Together, they set up a rival â Anthropic.

Six years on and Anthropic, the maker of leading AI model Claude, has predicted revenues of $52bn in 2026 and $135bn in 2027, according to analyst estimates.

Diungkapkan bahwa it is about to sell shares to the public for the first time in what's known as an initial public offering or ipo, aiming for a valuation of an estimated $1. 4tn (Â£1tn), which would propel it straight into the top 10 of the most valuable US companies.

The sale comes at a crucial time when many are wondering whether, amid increasing concern about the potential of AI, the industry's bubble is showing signs of bursting.

Where once investors were "all in" on a technological revolution to rival the railroads, the car, electricity and the internet, some are now hedging their bets, amid arguments that AI prices will be driven down as the technology becomes more common and concerns that a hefty wedge of the AI investment is tech giants investing in each other.

Shares in companies that supply the raw computing power behind AI, like Coreweave and Nebius, have seen their value cut in half while even the mighty Nvidia has lost its crown as the world's most valuable company with its shares down 30% - a staggering $2tn fall in value.

So could the Anthropic IPO reinflate the bubble or will it be remembered as the last gasp of a boom that is heading for a bust?.

At an event last week, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei told JPMorgan Chase's CEO Jamie Dimon that his guiding principle was to "never let your company be worth a single dollar more than it's worth".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the company is selling roughly $65bn worth of shares to the general public and a further $26bn on to other big tech companies. It is comfortably the single biggest money raising event in US corporate history.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it's an old adage that during a gold rush you should buy companies that sell the picks and shovels as opposed to those staking everything on striking gold. In AI's case that's the chip makers, the data centre builders, the energy providers. But Anthropic is arguably the gold itself and this IPO will see what value people put on it, according to Fiona Cincotta.

Berdasarkan laporan, "i think the reason that this ipo is so important is basically it's the first ability for the public investors to access a pure play ai trade," she says, adding that previous offerings have been about "other parts of the ecosystem, which are, the semiconductors, the chips, the, data centres. But this is the first time that we were actually able to access the AI provider. ".

Daniela Amodei helped set up a rival company to OpenAI.

What a company is worth depends almost entirely on predicted future earnings.

It's that calculation that many think presents the sharpest needle to the AI bubble.

Will current and future users of AI be prepared to pay enough to justify the trillions being spent on the chips, data centres, energy and employees, some of whom can command annual salaries of over $100m?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "ai is certainly in a financial bubble. While LLMs [large language models] offer genuine utility and are undoubtedly here to stay, the economics don't add up," said Gary Marcus, Professor Emeritus at New York University and author of Taming Silicon Valley, speaking earlier this year.

Berdasarkan laporan, "[the] more companies build ai models, the [more the] technology becomes commoditised, eliminating meaningful competitive advantages and driving down prices. ".

So far, the growth rates in Anthropic revenue are extraordinary.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but these explosive growth rates hide a potential problem. Around a quarter of that revenue came from just a handful of companies, among them Google and Amazon.

It's also concentrated in the US which accounts for two-thirds of its revenue.

Diungkapkan bahwa there is also the staggering network of circular financing found in the ai world. For example, Anthropic has agreements to buy or lease hundreds of billions of dollars worth of chips and computing power from a handful of companies including Broadcom, Google, Amazon. Many of those firms are also investors in Anthropic and major customers of its products.

Diungkapkan bahwa it's not just some wall street investors questioning whether the ai boom is all it's cracked up to be. Out on Main Street, ordinary Americans have concerns too.

With the US driving so much of global AI growth, a growing public backlash against a technology that threatens to replace millions of jobs and hoover up vast amounts of energy and water became a factor in the recent midterm elections in the US.

Sebagaimana diketahui, many areas in the us have passed moratoriums on data centre development and many candidates deemed too close to big tech found that association a political liability rather than an asset. Many Democrat candidates publicly opposed data centre development and won.

Added to that, the Pied Piper of AI, chip maker Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang, resigned last week after admitting to having been "unfaithful" to his wife after reports he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, Alice Huang.

Dario Amodei is one of Silicon Valley's big beasts.

Huang's spectacular fall from grace and Nvidia's 30% fall in value from its peak have left AI investors looking for a new champion for the AI boom that has underpinned the US stock market and arguably much of its entire economy for the last two years.

If Anthropic â and its CEO are to be AI's new Pied Piper, he will be playing a different tune to the relentlessly upbeat, leather jacket-clad talisman Huang.

While Huang wanted AI development to continue full throttle, Anthropic was built on misgivings over the levels of safety and responsibility the OpenAI leavers felt were being exercised over the development of society-changing technology.

Amodei has warned that AI capabilities could enable biological weapon development, mass surveillance, authoritarianism and the replacement of millions of white-collar, tax-paying workers.

He has called for a slowdown in its development as its powers are growing at such an exponential rate that it could very soon elude any human oversight.

That said, his paternalistic overtures have been sceptically received by those who point out that the pace of Anthropic's development of new more powerful models has shown no sign of the slowdown he's advocating for the rest of the industry.

But for all the concerns, just as with Elon Musk's SpaceX before it â the hype and the FOMO (fear of missing out) on an undoubtedly profound moment in technological and perhaps human development â means that buying interest is high.

It's reported that orders to buy shares exceed the number on offer by over six times.

With demand outstripping supply by such a margin, a first-day jump is likely given the oversubscription, but it doesn't tell you much about long-run return.

Sebagaimana diketahui, using spacex as an example again, shares initially rose nearly 70% from its ipo sale price of $135 to $225. Shares in SpaceX are currently back to $145.

The Anthropic IPO could be wildly successful and blow a bit of fresh new air into what some maintain still looks a lot like a bubble.

Eileen Burbidge, founder of tech investors Passion Capital, is one of those who reject the notion that AI is a bubble about to burst.

Diungkapkan bahwa "maybe the growth of the bubble has slowed down a little bit, but actually i wouldn't be willing to say that it's about to burst yet," says burbidge. "I think this IPO could actually mean everyone could be off to the races again. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, fiona cincotta believes anthropic's ipo is about far more than just anthropic. "I think what's going to be really interesting here is I think it can actually be used as a valuation benchmark for the entire AI ecosystem," she says.

Diungkapkan bahwa "that's why i don't think this is just going to affect the share price of anthropic. I think this is going to have much wider implications across the whole AI trade. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, two things can be true at the same time. The Anthropic IPO could be wildly successful - FOMO is a powerful emotion in financial markets. But its probable success won't soothe the unease in some quarters that not every company, every investor and every citizen will think of AI as the answer to humanity's problems.

#1304. Alexander Zverev notified of abuse lawsuit by ex-partner during ATP Finals

📅 18 Nov 2026

Alexander Zverev notified of abuse lawsuit by ex-partner during ATP Finals

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/nov/18/alexander-zverev-abuse-lawsuit-atp-finals-finals-brenda-patea

Men’s world No 1 allegedly violated terms of settlement.

Lawyers say Zverev will ‘defend himself against lawsuit’.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, alexander zverev was officially notified of a lawsuit filed by his former partner during the middle of the season-ending atp finals on wednesday. The latest legal case against the men’s world No 1 brought by the mother of the former couple’s daughter alleges that Zverev violated the terms of an out-of-court settlement between the pair after the woman accused him of assaulting her.

The lawsuit brought by Brenda Patea in Germany takes issue with Zverev reportedly saying in an interview with the French sports daily L’Equipe earlier this year that “it has been proven that the accusations were false” and “my innocence has been proven”.

Zverev’s Berlin-based lawyers, Christian Schertz and Anna Sophie Heuchemer, confirmed in a statement that they were formally served with Patea’s lawsuit on Wednesday.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “our client will defend himself against the lawsuit,” zverev’s lawyers said. “If the statement attributed to him was indeed made in the form alleged, we consider it to be a permissible expression of opinion” – which would be protected by the German constitution. They said there had been no breach of any contractual obligations.

Diungkapkan bahwa patea’s lawyer, michael scheele, said that zverev’s claim over his innocence “triggered a veritable storm of criticism against our client”. He said the backlash was damaging to her business as an influencer and that she also felt her honour had been violated.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “quite apart from the fact that zverev’s claim is false, he was not permitted to make any public statements whatsoever, in any form,” he said. “Both Brenda Patea and Alexander Zverev had agreed to this in a settlement. ”.

Patea is seeking that Zverev be ordered not to repeat such comments and that he be fined up to €250,000 (£208,500) every time if he does.

Berdasarkan laporan, zverev faced a charge of causing bodily harm to patea during an argument in berlin in may 2020. The case officially declared no verdict and the settlement entailed no acknowledgment of guilt on Zverev’s part. The case ended in a district court in Berlin in 2024 after the settlement. He always denied any wrongdoing. Zverev agreed to pay fines to the state and charitable organisations.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the german player this month ascended to the world no 1 ranking for the first time. He also won his first two grand slam titles this year and is competing this week at the ATP Finals in Turin.

Tanggal: 18 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/israeli-tanks-cross-yellow-line-boundary-into-hamas-controlled-central-gaza

First incursion across boundary since ceasefire deal comes as Eisenkot seeks to form government without Netanyahu.

The Israeli military crossed into Hamas-controlled central Gaza on Wednesday in its first ground operation across the “yellow line” boundary since a fragile ceasefire was agreed last October, forcing dozens of displaced Palestinians to flee their tents.

Israeli tanks rolled along the Salah al-Din road, Gaza’s main north-south route, a day after the US-backed Board of Peace, a body overseeing the ceasefire, accused Israel and Hamas of failing to honour their commitments to end hostilities.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in separate incidents on wednesday, palestinian medics said two people were killed by israeli fire, one in deir al-balah and the other in gaza city. The Israeli military said it was unaware of any incident in Deir al-Balah and had struck a militant in Gaza City.

Diungkapkan bahwa israel has stepped up its attacks on hamas, which it says has been regrouping and rearming. Hamas has accused Israel of trying to derail the US-brokered ceasefire agreed in October 2025.

Israeli strikes have continued since the ceasefire, and Hamas remains armed.

Last week, an Israeli airstrike on Nasser hospital in southern Gaza killed six people, including a surgeon and a disabled man, and wounded 28 others, according to the hospital director.

The body overseeing Donald Trump’s plan to end the war in Gaza has accused Israel and Hamas of failing to honour their commitments to end hostilities, leaving Palestinians in dire conditions and the ceasefire at risk of collapse.

Berdasarkan laporan, in its second report to the un security council since the truce began 13 months ago, the trump-led board of peace said the gap between what was agreed and what was happening on the ground remained the biggest threat to the deal. The report, seen by Reuters, warned that “a ceasefire that delivers nothing visible cannot be sustained indefinitely”.

Diungkapkan bahwa gaza’s health authorities say at least 1,600 palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire came into effect. The Israeli military says five of its soldiers have been killed over the same period.

Palestinian authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed in Gaza since Israel launched its military campaign in response to the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, in which about 1,200 people were killed.

".

Leaseholders in England and Wales will have their ground rent capped in 2028, the housing minister has said as he publishes a bill that will eventually ban virtually all new leasehold properties.

Matthew Pennycook will introduce the government’s leasehold reform bill on Thursday, including measures to cap charges, end the sale of new leasehold flats and make it easier to extend and buy out leases.

He said one of the first elements of the bill to come into force would be the long-promised £250 cap on annual ground rent – though it will not be enacted as quickly as some MPs have pushed for.

Berdasarkan laporan, “the ground rent can be expected fairly early,” he said. “I think it will be a really historic moment … leasehold denies individuals control over the homes they live in and have paid for.

“It then allows freeholders and managing agents acting on their behalf to extract excessive amounts of money from them, whether that’s unreasonable or extortionate charges, punitive and escalating ground rents, unjustified administration and permission fees – you name it.

Berdasarkan laporan, “leasehold is an anachronism in the 21st century. I really do think that the bill that we’re introducing tomorrow [Thursday] marks the beginning of the end for the feudal leasehold system. ”.

Pennycook and his Conservative predecessors promised to end the leasehold system, which exists in only a few countries worldwide and dates back to feudal property laws.

Berdasarkan laporan, thursday’s bill will mark the biggest step towards making those promises a reality, extending the ban on leasehold for new houses to flats, which make up the bulk of leasehold properties. Pennycook has previously said he expects the ban to come into force after the next election.

It will also make it easier for those in leasehold properties to switch to a collective system known as commonhold, ensuring that such a move can be made with the agreement of half the residents in a block rather than all of them.

And it will end freeholders’ right to evict leaseholders for relatively small unpaid bills.

One of the first changes to become law will be the £250 cap on ground rent.

Sebagaimana diketahui, mps on the housing select committee had urged pennycook to introduce it as soon as next year, but he insisted it was not possible because of the “technical process” of beginning its enforcement. The 2028 date would not be explicitly included in the bill but ministers would enact it through secondary legislation, he said.

He also said many other leaseholders’ demands would have to come in a second law to be introduced later in the parliament.

They include establishing an independent regulator for property management agents and changing the rates that determine how much it costs to extend or buy out a lease.

Pennycook said that wrestling with the legal technicalities of property law had slowed the process of drafting the bill, arguing that doing so had minimised the risk of the government having to go back and rewrite parts of it.

“This is by far and away the most complex and technical piece of legislation I have ever dealt with,” he said.

“We are undertaking the most ambitious overhaul of land and property law in a century, if not longer … it is just ferociously complex.

“We’re taking on some big vested interests, and those vested interests have very deep pockets.

Diungkapkan bahwa “leasehold law is extremely litigious – we’ve had challenges brought to the 2024 act … [and] we will get challenges to this piece of legislation as well, almost certainly. ”.

The campaign group Raise the Colours has been temporarily banned from placing union jacks on lamp-posts and roundabouts in Birmingham after a legal challenge by the local council.

The high court judge Emma Kelly granted an interim injunction banning the placing of all flags on council-owned street furniture without prior permission in a judgment issued on Wednesday, Birmingham city council said.

The council, run by a minority coalition led by the Liberal Democrats, sought the injunction against seven people identified as supporting or participating in the affixing of flags in the city, including Ryan Bridge, a co-founder of Raise the Colours, and “persons unknown”.

The application for an injunction, which attracted national attention and follows similar action by Oxfordshire county council, argued the actions of the flag activists had caused danger, alarm and distress.

People associated with Raise the Colours, which describes itself as a grassroots movement, have been placing union jacks and St George’s flags on public infrastructure across the country since August last year.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the group’s website states it is a “campaign to cover britain in symbols of unity and patriotism”. However, others have accused the group of racism and spreading anti-immigration rhetoric – claims it has previously denied.

In its claim to the high court, Birmingham city council said the defendants had travelled across the city “unlawfully affixing flags” and had confronted residents who attempted to remove them.

“In doing so, they are engaging in tortious and criminal behaviour, which is both antisocial and dangerous,” the claim read, adding that the behaviour had caused “danger” and “alarm” to residents.

The council said residents of Birmingham had suffered “fear, anxiety, intimidation, harassment,” been put at “serious risk of harm”, and some had suffered physical injuries, including a broken leg.

The case was adjourned in early September after the judge said she was “troubled by the lack of clarity” from the council “against the individual defendants”, and a further hearing was scheduled at the end of September.

Berdasarkan laporan, bridge opposed the injunction and read a written statement to the court. He said: “For me, the union flag represents home, identity, belonging, national identity, British culture and patriotism. ”.

His lawyer, Liam Wells, argued that the injunction would have a “chilling effect” on human rights and that erecting union jacks and St George’s flags was an expression of his political views.

Wells said the interim injunction would risk “silencing people in their political views and expression of political opinions” and the council had failed to prove Bridge had acted unlawfully.

Three local residents, Adam Biggs, Mark Hudson and Tony Kaye, joined the case representing ‘persons unknown’ opposing the injunction bid, and expressed concerns it would ban people flying flags for pride and other campaigns.

The council’s cabinet member for equalities, communities and social justice, Jane Baston, said on Wednesday the local authority was grateful for the judgment and it was an “important step”.

Diungkapkan bahwa “we have taken a proportionate and evidence-led approach throughout this case. Our priority has always been to protect public safety, supporting the welfare of our staff and contractors, maintaining community cohesion and ensuring public funds are used responsibly,” she said.

Sign up for the Breaking News UK email to get newsletter alerts direct to your inbox.

In a video uploaded to Facebook, Bridge said he was “gutted” and “devastated” by the decision, including the fact that the injunction granted power of arrest against him and others.

He said Raise the Colours was “not about race, colour, creed” but about opposing “illegal invaders breaking in our country, jeopardising our borders, on the rubber dinghies”.

At the Reform UK conference in Birmingham in September, Nigel Farage promised to help Bridge in his legal fight if the party was able to do so.

In response to the judgment, Reform’s leader in Birmingham, Jex Parkin, said the council had its “priorities entirely wrong” and had pursued an “ideologically driven case against residents proudly displaying our national flags – at huge public expense”.

The leader of the local Conservatives, Robert Alden, also criticised the injunction and said the council was “punishing ordinary Birmingham residents who simply want to show pride in where they live”.

Berdasarkan laporan, he said: “amidst a 23-month bin strike, loss of roads funding, and mounting litter on our streets, the council has chosen to make this court action a priority. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, the group brummies united against racism, which campaigned for the injunction, welcomed the judgment. Members of the group told the Guardian earlier this year they had presented evidence of incidents involving Raise the Colours to the police and council officers.

Berdasarkan laporan, the group said it was “not opposed to this country’s flag” and many of its supporters “see the flag as a symbol of celebration and unity”. “However, we are firmly opposed to those who seek to use the flag to further an agenda of hate and who dress up racism as patriotism,” a statement read.

A further hearing in the case will take place on Thursday.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, speaking in abu dhabi, he said: "if europe could identify one person to speak on their behalf, that would be a bigger achievement than getting the russians to include them in the negotiations. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, government spokesperson hille responded on monday: "europe's strength lies precisely in the unity and cohesion of many countries. We should not allow ourselves to be drawn into debates that others want to frame around this question. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa hille emphasized that the situation remained unchanged: peace in ukraine could only be achieved step by step. Europe, too, would need stamina, perseverance and a willingness to undertake the painstaking work required to bring it about.

Sebagaimana diketahui, european supporters of ukraine are also under pressure as public opinion on the issue is shifting, including in germany. While a broad majority favored helping defend the country in the immediate aftermath of Russia's invasion in the spring of 2022, support has since fallen markedly.

Sebagaimana diketahui, according to the latest deutschlandtrend survey on the issue, conducted or german public broadcaster ard in september 2026, 52% of eligible voters still support weapons deliveries to ukraine, while 42% believe such support has gone too far. That is the highest level of opposition recorded since the start of the war.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a further study conducted for public broadcaster wdr in november 2026 found that support for ukraine has become a more polarizing issue in germany than immigration. According to the survey, 54% of respondents favor continued support for Ukraine, while just under 29% would prefer a rapprochement with Russia, despite its war of aggression against Ukraine.

This article was originally written in German.
